# Chapter 582: (1): Only Drinkers Leave Their Marks

Sword of Coming

Autumn passed, and winter arrived, time strolling by at a leisurely
pace.

If it weren\'t for the fact that Chen Ping\'an could see the silhouette
of the southern end of the Sword Qi Great Wall when he looked up, he
would have almost mistakenly thought that he was at the White Paper
Blessed Land, or perhaps at the Golden Millet Blessed Land after
drinking some Forgetting Sorrow Wine.

Even though Chen Ping\'an cultivated diligently without slacking off ---
in fact, he could be described as very busy --- he still felt like this
wasn\'t enough. Thus, he asked Grandma Bai to spar with him, yet Grandma
Bai was unwilling to unleash deadly power, no matter what, and at most
taught him some fist stances. Not satiated by the fist technique
training sessions, Chen Ping\'an could only invite Grandpa Nalan to the
training ground in the Minute Small World, allowing him to familiarize
himself with the deadly power of an Unpolished Jade Tier sword
cultivator\'s flying sword.

At the same time, Chen Ping\'an also learned some elementary stealth
techniques from the so-called assassin who had fallen from the Immortal
Tier. There were many exquisite movements that pertained to the
fundamental principles of cultivation, yet these movements could only be
performed by sword cultivators. This left Chen Ping\'an feeling slightly
disappointed.

Besides cultivation, Chen Ping\'an would try his best to visit the wine
shop whenever he had free time. He would stay for around two hours each
time, though he wouldn\'t help much when it came to selling wine.
Instead, he would sit amidst a large group of young children, continuing
to play the role of a storyteller. At most, he would also teach them
some characters and recite some poems and essays, ones that didn\'t
pertain to any particular teachings or principles.

Even though Chen Ping\'an was delegating all of his responsibilities,
Shopkeeper Die Zhang didn\'t have any complaints at all. This was
because the money-making strategies of the wine shop had all been
devised by Assistant Shopkeeper Chen, so it was only reasonable for him
to slack off now. Die Zhang admitted that she had only invested some
money and provided some ordinary labor, and in any case, Chen Ping\'an
had done many more things following the successful opening of the wine
shop. For example, he had plastered a brand new horizontal scroll above
the entrance to complement the original couplet.

\"Those who drink my wine can advance.\"

The shopkeepers of the other restaurants and wine shops on the street
were nearing the brink of collapse. Not only had this new wine shop
stolen a large chunk of their business, but most importantly, it clearly
exuded a more impressive aura. This led to the restaurants and wine
shops in the Sword Qi Great Wall clamoring to put up couplets and
horizontal scrolls.

Looking around and comparing, however, many alcoholic sword cultivators
ultimately felt like the couplet at the new wine shop was the most
appealing. Or to put it bluntly, it was the most shameless.

After almost every single wine shop in the Sword Qi Great Wall started
to put up couplets, the new wine shop promptly came up with a new
marketing strategy.

There were many small wooden tablets in the shape of Peace and Safety
Tablets hanging around the shop, each with an inscription by a sword
cultivator customer of the wine shop. Die Zhang would ask the customers
to inscribe their names and some calligraphy works on the small wooden
tablets, after which she would hang them on the wall as auspicious good
luck charms.

These wooden tablets weren\'t placed according to the customers\'
cultivation bases, and they were instead hung up by the customers
themselves. The front side of these tablets would always be the
customers\' names, while the backside would be whatever they wanted to
write. The wine shop didn\'t place any limit on how much or how little
they could write.

Of the customers that had already hung wooden tablets in the wine shop,
four were surprisingly sword immortals at the Upper Five Tiers. There
was Wei Jin of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent\'s Wind Snow Temple,
Gao Kui of the Sword Qi Great Wall, Yuan Qingshu of the Southern Whirl
Continent, and the Unpolished Jade Tier Tao Wen of the Northern Complete
Reed Continent, who had visited the wine shop alone late one night.

All of them had left inscriptions on the backside of the wooden tablets,
but this hadn\'t been by choice. They had initially inscribed their
names on the front side only, but Chen Ping\'an had found opportunities
to pester all of them afterward, forcing them to leave inscriptions on
the backside as well. He had all kinds of methods to force compliance,
and this had been an eye-opening experience for the embarrassed Die
Zhang. As it turned out, businesses could also be run like this.

And thus, Wei Jin\'s inscription read: *Troubled by love, sword unable
to be drawn.*

Gao Kui, the rugged-looking man with a single eye and a large beard,
left the inscription: *May the flowers bloom, the moon be round, and
people enjoy longevity.*

The elegant and carefree Yuan Qingshu had inscribed: This world should
know that I, Yuan Qingshu, am a sword immortal.

Sword Immortal Tao Wen was the most understanding, and after hearing
that he could receive a free pot of Bamboo Sea Small World Wine, he
immediately wrote: *The wine here is affordable and delicious, and it
would be even better if buying on credit were allowed.*

Casting one\'s gaze over the youngest generation of prodigious sword
cultivators, the wine shop had been graced with the presence of Pang
Yuanji, Yan Zhuo, Chen Sanqiu, Dong Huafu, and a dozen or so others. Of
course, there was also the young girl, Guo Zhujiu, and apart from
writing her name and her nickname, Lü Duan, she had also made a secret
inscription on the back, reading: *Master sells wine, and this disciple
buys wine, the relationship between master and disciple warms the heart
and lasts for eternity.*

There were also quite a number of earth immortal sword cultivators who
were too embarrassed to turn down the request of inscribing their names
on the small wooden tablets, but many of them only inscribed their names
and left the backsides blank. In any case, Chen Ping\'an seldom worked
at the wine shop, while Die Zhang was truly at a loss regarding how to
ask the customers for this favor. Chen Ping\'an felt like this wasn\'t
sustainable, so he handed Die Zhang a few paper slips, saying that she
could hand these over to Nascent Tier sword cultivators who appeared
suitable and were actually willing to inscribe the small wooden tablets,
but simply didn\'t know what to inscribe on the backside. She could hand
over a paper slip when they paid.

And thus, an old and abrasive Nascent Tier sword cultivator who had no
experience with calligraphy had initially put on airs and turned down
Shopkeeper Die Zhang\'s request, but after seeing one of the paper
slips, he had unexpectedly changed his attitude straight away and
secretly put away the slip, telling Die Zhang to make haste and hand him
a small wooden tablet.

Appearing serious as if he were facing a great demon, the old sword
cultivator had left an inscription according to the poetry line on the
paper slip. When leaving, he had even purchased an additional slip of
the most expensive Azure Divine Mountain Wine. Purposely suppressing his
sword qi as he drank to his heart\'s content, he had sung loudly while
stumbling down the street. He repeated the same line again and again,
the line of poetry that had suddenly come to him like a stroke of
inspiration. \"Past glories not worth boasting about, countless battles
fought over the years. Drunk and satisfied, my sword becomes my pillow,
dreaming that the Azure God visits to pour me wine.\"

One day later, this Nascent Tier sword cultivator who mysteriously
learned how to compose poems became extremely famous among the
alcoholics and gambling addicts of the Sword Qi Great Wall.

However, he was eventually struck by a Sword Immortal\'s flying sword
from some unknown place, causing him to lie in a sickbed for several
days.

There was also a Nascent Tier sword cultivator from the Northern
Complete Reed Continent who could still be considered young, and he
regarded himself as someone who would occasionally attain enlightenment
when drinking under the moonlight. The inscription on his wooden tablet
read: *Half of the sword immortals in the world are my friends, which
fine lady in the world isn\'t demure? I wash my sword with fine wine,
who doth say I\'m not a free spirit?*

The Bamboo Sea Small World Wine sold by the wine shop came in three
grades, with the lowest grade costing one snowflake coin a pot and
tasting the blandest.

Medium-grade Bamboo Sea Small World Wine tasted slightly better and cost
five snowflake coins a pot, and the wine shop announced that one
extremely valuable bamboo leaf from the Bamboo Sea Small World would be
hidden in each one hundred pots. Sword Immortal Wei Jin and Guo Zhujiu
could both attest to this.

High-grade Azure Divine Mountain Wine cost ten snowflake coins a pot,
and there was no guarantee that customers would be able to purchase it,
given that the wine shop would only sell a single pot a day. If a
customer missed out, then they could only try again tomorrow.

The small wine shop was always packed to the brim now, but after the
initial popularity, there was no longer the sight of sword cultivators
fighting to buy wine and squatting down on the streets to drink wine.
Even so, the six tables would always be full.

Die Zhang was already very satisfied with the income of the wine shop,
but she couldn\'t help but feel a slight sense of disappointment at the
same time. Just like Chen Ping\'an had anticipated, purchasing wine
became exceedingly difficult following the hugely successful opening of
the wine shop. Many restaurants and wine shops would rather pay
compensation to Die Zhang than continue to sell her raw wine, making it
abundantly clear that they wanted to see this new wine shop hung out to
dry. If their customers were left empty-handed a few times, it wouldn\'t
be long before their business started to tumble downhill. Indeed, being
popular for a short while and then betraying customer expectations was
no way to run a business long-term.

Even Die Zhang was aware of this problem, so the assistant shopkeeper
who liked to delegate work would naturally be even more aware of it.
However, Chen Ping\'an never commented about this, and whenever he was
at the wine shop, he would either chat with some regular customers and
drink some free wine or mingle with the children at the alley corner and
act like a storyteller. Die Zhang didn\'t want to trouble Chen Ping\'an
with everything, so she could only mull over the potential solutions
herself.

Late at night, Chen Ping\'an and Ning Yao arrived at the wine shop that
was about to close. There were no customers in the shop.

Die Zhang retrieved the account book, and Chen Ping\'an sat to the side
and retrieved one snowflake coin, purchasing a pot of the cheapest wine.
This was the rule here --- even the shopkeepers needed to pay for wine.

Chen Ping\'an carefully looked over the account book as he drank wine.

Yan Zhuo and the others had also agreed beforehand that they would drink
together today, the reason being that Chen Ping\'an was actually willing
to treat them in a rare display.

Chen Ping\'an and Ning Yao were sitting on the same bench.

Yan Zhuo sat on a bench by himself, while Dong Huafu and Chen Sanqiu
shared a bench.

Yan Zhuo looked at Chen Ping\'an, who was carefully flipping over the
account book, before glancing at Die Zhang, who was sitting nearby. He
couldn\'t help but ask, \"Die Zhang, you won\'t feel like Chen Ping\'an
doesn\'t trust you, right?\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled knowingly, not looking up to say anything. Instead,
he raised his wine bowl and took a sip of wine, essentially admitting
guilt and thus willingly drinking in punishment.

\"What nonsense are you speaking?\" Die Zhang snapped. \"Is this not the
required rigour when doing business? We\'re running this business
together because we\'re friends, so would our friendship end simply
because we\'re double-checking the account books to make sure everything
is correct? Who doesn\'t make mistakes? If these mistakes aren\'t picked
up and corrected, then whose fault will it be in the future? Will
everything be fine if we simply ignore the mistakes? If we carelessly
and foolishly ignore each other\'s mistakes, won\'t we be throwing money
away when the business starts to fall apart?\"

\"Your favoritism is showing far too clearly, Die Zhang. Why does it
become friends doing business together when you talk about Chen
Ping\'an? Then didn\'t I get beaten up for nothing in the past?\" Yan
Zhuo lamented in an aggrieved voice.

\"Didn\'t I apologize to you already?\" Die Zhang replied with a smile.

\"I was quite happy to hear you apologize back then, but now, I can\'t
help but feel that you weren\'t sincere enough,\" Yan Zhuo said sulkily.

Chen Ping\'an flipped a page of the account book and remarked in
amusement, \"It always feels frustrating when your friend makes a new
friend.\"

Yan Zhuo waved a hand and corrected, \"This isn\'t my point at all.\"

Chen Ping\'an raised his wine bowl and touched it with Yan Zhuo\'s,
saying with a smile, \"I\'m not making a casual comment about Young
Master Yan because you\'re so large and seemingly able to carry money
everywhere. However, you stingily buy the cheapest wine every time,
spending even less than the young girl, Miss Lü Duan.\"

Die Zhang appeared slightly hesitant, but she eventually mustered her
courage and said, \"Yan Zhuo, Sanqiu, can I discuss something with the
two of you?\"

Yan Zhuo was slightly puzzled, but Chen Sanqiu had seemingly guessed the
reason already. He smiled and replied with a nod, \"Of course.\"

Yan Zhuo\'s eyes lit up as he asked, \"Are you inviting the two of us
into this business venture? So, my curiosity was correct. I took a
glance at the wine vats at your residence, and taking into account the
number of customers served at the wine shop each day, I knew that you
would be running very low on wine. And now, the competing restaurants
and wine shops are also very envious of your success, so trying to find
a source of wine has become a colossal problem, right?

\"No stress. This problem is easily solved. There\'s no need to even
involve Sanqiu, seeing that he\'s a young master who never needs to put
in any hard work. He\'s accustomed to lying down and enjoying good
fortune, so he doesn\'t understand these kinds of matters at all.
However, I\'m different, and I assist with a good number of businesses
in my clan. As such, how difficult can it be to hook you up with some
suppliers of cheap wine? Rest assured, Die Zhang, we\'ll follow the
rules as you\'ve stated, and I won\'t affect the Yan Clan\'s business
too much either. I\'ll try to make a small profit while also helping you
earn some more.\"

There was a complicated expression on Die Zhang\'s face.

Chen Ping\'an appeared slightly exasperated as he closed the account
book and chuckled. \"There are two types of happiness for Shopkeeper Die
Zhang when she makes money, with the first type of happiness coming from
immortal coins landing in her pockets as she works the abacus and
calculates the earnings at the end of each day. The other type of
happiness comes from the ability to earn money despite the challenges.

\"Say, Fatty Yan, does this not sound reasonable? If you carry a sack of
silver to the wine shop, I presume that Die Zhang won\'t even be willing
to plan ahead and check the accounts in the future. Fatty Yan, won\'t it
be easier for you to directly give us a number?\"

Yan Zhuo was struck by realization as he replied, \"Ah, you could have
told me earlier. Die Zhang, I would have understood your intentions if
you were this direct earlier, no?\"

\"You\'re blaming me?\" Die Zhang fumed.

Yan Zhuo drank wine and begged for forgiveness, saying, \"No, it\'s all
my fault. My fault.\"

Chen Ping\'an changed the topic, telling Die Zhang what the key
watchouts were regarding these profits and losses.

In reality, it wasn\'t the case that Die Zhang didn\'t understand these
principles, and she had most likely understood them a long time ago.
However, some of these matters pertained to rifts between friends, ones
that could be big, small, existent, or non-existent. There were some
unintentional words that had hurt other people, but she was unwilling to
explain herself, lest she appear too deliberate. Or perhaps she was too
embarrassed to explain herself. Things would be okay if she were lucky,
and she would be able to delay these matters for a lifetime. These were
only small matters, after all, so she could make up for them by doing
well at bigger matters. If she were unlucky, however, then friends would
be lost, and it would no longer matter whether she explained herself or
not.

Every single person, including those sitting in the wine shop right now
and including Ning Yao, needed to overcome the barrier in their heart.
This wasn\'t a unique challenge for Die Zhang, the only person among the
original friend group who had grown up in an impoverished alley.

Chen Ping\'an was merely borrowing this opportunity to gently touch on
the problem as a bystander, helping the two people face the problem
head-on. He couldn\'t have mentioned this problem too early, or else he
would have put himself in a very awkward position. If he left it until
it was too late --- for example, when both Yan Zhuo and Die Zhang felt
like he was one of their best friends --- then the timing would become a
little inappropriate.

Chen Ping\'an couldn\'t speak these thoughts out loud, or else it would
be like transforming fine wine into bland water. Thus, he could only
mull over it himself, at times making him feel like he was manipulating
people too much. The past Chen Ping\'an would have felt guilty and been
riddled with self-doubt, but this was no longer the case.

Each good intent needed to be protected and cherished by a greater good
intent. Chen Ping\'an believed in good people being blessed with good
karma, and this was a sincere and adamant belief. However, people
couldn\'t place all of their hopes in the heavens alone. Living in this
world and interacting with other people, each person could actually be
viewed as a so-called heaven. In this sense, there was no need to always
seek outside help and seek help from loftier entities.

*Many thoughts weigh on my mind as I observe the world, and it appears
as if I\'m not treating other people with enough sincerity. However, if
I adhere to the rules and ultimately cause no harm to others with my
actions, perhaps even bring a certain degree of benefits to the world,
then I shouldn\'t constrain myself due to self-doubt.*

*I can examine my conscience after my actions, slowly tempering my heart
against my conscience. This is a process of cultivating the heart. This
is what my master, the Scholarly Sage, suggested by telling me to think
more about all kinds of different matters. Even if I discover afterward
that my thoughts and actions were simply traveling in circles and
returning to the same spot, this is still a top-notch cultivation
method. I ask nothing from heaven and earth, yet heaven and earth gains
a person who seeks to do good, a person who can protect himself and also
benefit other people. Is this not delightful? Is this not good?*

The singularity of heaven and earth was eternally unchanging, with only
the human heart forever shifting.

The philosophies of the Three Teachings and the Hundred Schools of
Thought were fundamentally looking at this notion and striving to
influence the human heart.

After finishing the business discussions, they were once again just
friends enjoying a drink with each other.

# Chapter 582: (2): Only Drinkers Leave Their Marks

Sword of Coming

Chen Sanqiu revealed a rumor, saying that another sword immortal from
the Northern Complete Reed Continent was going to arrive at the Sword Qi
Great Wall very soon. In fact, this sword immortal had seemingly arrived
at Stalactite Mountain already. However, some sword immortals at the
Sword Qi Great Wall were also going to return home soon.

This was often the case for sword cultivators from the Northern Complete
Reed Continent. They would usually return home after participating in
one large-scale battle.

However, two large-scale battles breaking out within a timespan of ten
years had caught everyone off guard. As such, the large majority of
sword cultivators from the Northern Complete Reed Continent had chosen
to stay behind at the Sword Qi Great Wall, deciding to take part in
another battle.

There were naturally some sword immortals and earth immortal sword
cultivators who had to leave the Sword Qi Great Wall for various
reasons, given that they needed to deal with matters at their own sects.
The Sword Qi Great Wall never uttered any nonsense regarding these
decisions, and not only that, but there was even an unwritten rule that
pertained to these outsider sword immortals as they prepared to leave.
The local sword immortals, who were well-acquainted with these outsider
sword immortals, needed to treat the latter to some wine and bid them
farewell. This could be viewed as a gift of gratitude from the Sword Qi
Great Wall.

Chen Ping\'an and Ning Yao turned around and looked toward the street in
unison.

Six people were walking over, all of them sword immortals!

Not only did Chen Ping\'an recognize one of the female sword immortals,
but he was even quite familiar with her. She was none other than Li Cai,
the sect leader of the Northern Complete Reed Continent\'s Duckweed
Sword Lake.

She had once said that she would come to the Sword Qi Great Wall after
challenging the newly advanced Sword Immortal Liu Jinglong to a sword
duel. Apart from fulfilling her promise to Li Yu, her good friend from
Profound Dawn Mountain, she also needed to kill an additional great
demon to commemorate Li Yu, who had already passed away after failing to
break through to the next cultivation tier.

Chen Ping\'an only recognized one of the five remaining people, the tall
and sturdy elder with white hair and a white beard walking at the front
of the group. This old man genuinely had a bad temper, and this was
something Chen Ping\'an had personally witnessed and heard when he had
stood atop the city wall in the past. The old man had directly uttered
the old great sword immortal\'s name, loudly questioning Chen Qingdu\'s
decision to kill Dong Guanpu. Afterward, the clan leader of the Dong
Clan had almost clashed physically with Chen Qingdu, eventually
exclaiming, \"Others are all afraid of you, Chen Qingdu, but I\'m not
afraid!\"

This left a deep impression on Chen Ping\'an, and he also became
slightly curious about Dong Guanpu, the person whom the old great sword
immortal had killed with a single sword strike. This was because,
according to Ning Yao\'s explanation, Dong Guanpu, or Grandpa Little
Dong, was actually a very good person.

He could only attribute this to every clan having its own burden to
bear.

There were far too many extraordinary sword immortals at the Sword Qi
Great Wall, but there was even more unrest to worry about.

Dong Sangeng, Li Cai, who had just arrived at the Sword Qi Great Wall,
and the other sword immortals were seemingly making their way straight
to the small wine shop.

Seeing this, Chen Ping\'an stole an extra glance at the four other sword
immortals, managing to guess the identities of two of them. There was
Sect Leader Han Huaizi of the Great Emblem Sword Sect and Huang Tong,
the disciplinary elder of the ancestral hall.

Chen Ping\'an and his companions had already stood up.

After greeting his old ancestor, Dong Huafu said, \"This wine shop
doesn\'t sell wine on credit.\"

Dong Sangeng shot a glare at him and asked, \"Don\'t you have money on
you?\"

\"I never pay for my wine,\" Dong Huafu replied with a shake of his
head.

Dong Sangeng laughed heartily and remarked, \"As expected of a
descendant of my Dong Clan. Looking across the entire Sword Qi Great
Wall, only sons from the Dong Clan can act so shamelessly, yet appear so
reasonable.\"

Die Zhang inevitably felt uneasy and fearful.

After all, this old man was Dong Sangeng, the clan leader of the Dong
Clan.

He was the old sword immortal who had inscribed the character \"Dong\"
onto the great wall!

In the past, A\'Liang had hated nothing more than sword technique
sparring sessions with Dong Sangeng, avoiding this whenever he could. If
he couldn\'t avoid it, then he would ask Dong Sangeng to give him money.
If Dong Sangeng refused, then A\'Liang would obediently stand beside the
thatched cottage on the city wall and accept a beating. If he didn\'t go
to the city wall to disturb Chen Qingdu\'s rest, then he would instead
lie down on the rooftop of the Dong Clan\'s ancestral hall.

Dong Sangeng waved a hand and put two tables together, saying to the
youths, \"Don\'t come over here to speak nonsense. Just focus on serving
wine.\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded in acknowledgment at Li Cai, who also smiled and
nodded in response.

Old Ancestor Huang Tong of the Great Emblem Sword Sect unexpectedly
smiled at Chen Ping\'an, leaving him with no option but to cup his fists
and bow in respect. However, he didn\'t say anything to the sword
immortal.

After sitting down, Dong Sangeng glanced at the couplets and horizontal
scroll plastered around the shop door, clicking his tongue in wonder and
remarking, \"How truly daring. Thankfully, the characters are written
quite well, much better than A\'Liang\'s worm-like characters.\"

Beads of sweat involuntarily formed on Die Zhang\'s forehead.

Chen Sanqiu and Yan Zhuo also felt a little anxious.

This couldn\'t be helped. They were too insignificant to even be scolded
by Dong Sangeng, whereas most of the sword immortal seniors in their
clan had suffered genuine beatings at the hands of Dong Sangeng.

Perhaps only Ning Yao and Chen Ping\'an could be regarded as calm and
composed at this moment.

Dong Sangeng stood up and left after drinking a pot of wine, and the two
other local sword immortals from the Sword Qi Great Wall also bade
farewell and left.

Meanwhile, Han Huaizi, Huang Tong, and Li Cai, the three sword immortals
from the Northern Complete Reed Continent, all stayed behind.

Chen Ping\'an told Die Zhang to retrieve an extra pot of fine wine from
the shop, following which he accepted it and brought it to the table
himself, saying, \"Junior Chen Ping\'an pays his respects to Sect Leader
Han, Sect Leader Li, and Sword Immortal Huang.\"

Li Cai smiled widely and commented, \"Did you hear that, Huang Tong? My
name came before yours. This is the consequence of you not becoming a
sect leader.\"

Chen Ping\'an felt a little exasperated upon hearing this.

Sword Immortal Li Cai was completely going against the justice and
morality of the martial world.

Unexpectedly, however, Huang Tong smiled and said, \"I\'m doing very
well behind Sect Leader Li. In fact, being on top or under Sect Leader
Li will also be okay.\"

Chen Ping\'an had just sat down, yet he almost fell off his chair after
hearing this. He didn\'t have time to worry about etiquette anymore, and
he hurriedly drank some wine to suppress his shock.

When traveling across the Northern Complete Reed Continent before, he
had never heard about this sword immortal from the Great Emblem Sword
Sect being such a direct and unrestrained person.

Why hadn\'t Qi Jinglong mentioned this at all? To avoid disrespecting
his lofty seniors?

Li Cai chuckled coldly and responded, \"Here\'s wishing you misfortune
when you travel on the intercontinental ship, drowning halfway and
becoming fish feed.\"

Huang Tong laughed loudly, not appearing angry and instead looking quite
delighted.

Han Huaizi was a very composed and mature person, possessing the
demeanor of a lofty sword immortal. He smiled faintly at Chen Ping\'an
and said, \"You can ignore their nonsense.\"

Huang Tong retracted his smile, no longer appearing immature as he said,
\"Stalactite Mountain is keeping an extremely close eye on the origins,
destinations, and contents of every single messenger flying sword in the
area now. In fact, Stalactite Mountain has unilaterally locked up a
large number of messenger flying swords, and there\'s no way to speak
reason with them.

\"Thankfully, Qi Jinglong wrote his letter in a very smart manner,
preventing his messenger flying sword from being blocked and taken.
Since Chen Ping\'an is good friends with Liu Jinglong, and seeing that
Li Cai is also a sword cultivator from the Northern Complete Reed
Continent, the four of us can all be regarded as one big family.

\"Firstly, I need to thank Li Cai for being the first to challenge Qi
Jinglong, helping him get off to a good start. That person who has a
good relationship with the Confucian academy came immediately afterward,
forcing the old geezer, Bai Shang, to act shamelessly. It was thanks to
this that Qi Jinglong was not only able to solidify his position as a
sword immortal in the Northern Complete Reed Continent, but he was even
able to improve his Sword Dao through the three consecutive battles. The
Great Emblem Sword Sect owes Li Cai a huge favor regarding this.\"

After saying this, Huang Tong smiled faintly and continued, \"So, Sect
Leader Li can feel free to choose the front or the back. I won\'t say a
single word, and I won\'t be a man if I so much as frown!\"

Li Cai pursed her lips and said, \"I have some good news for you. Jiang
Shangzhen has already advanced to the Immortal Tier.\"

\"I\'m a mighty sword immortal, and this is already enough. So what if
I\'m not man enough?\" Huang Tong immediately said.

That godforsaken Jiang Shangzhen was like a shared nightmare for the
cultivators of the Northern Complete Reed Continent. He was already able
to use his golden core as a nascent soul in the past, and he was
renowned for being able to unleash the power of an Immortal Tier
cultivator as an Unpolished Jade Tier cultivator afterward. So, what
could he achieve now that he had advanced to the Immortal Tier?

Disregarding Jiang Shangzhen\'s cultivation, who wanted to interact with
a person who was metaphorically running around with a bucket of shit?
Throwing a punch or launching a sword strike at Jiang Shangzhen would
genuinely grant them piss and shit in return. Most importantly, Jiang
Shangzhen liked to bear grudges and was also very good at running away.
Thus, even Huang Tong wasn\'t willing to provoke him.

In the past, an elderly Nascent Tier cultivator from the Northern
Complete Reed Continent hadn\'t believed these facts about Jiang
Shangzhen, going as far as to spend twenty years of his life trying to
hunt down and kill him, determined to exterminate this vermin that
everyone wanted dead, but no one was able to kill. However, he failed to
make many inroads, and his immortal force was subject to great misery.

Jiang Shangzhen had fabricated a mountain of stories about the chaotic,
romantic, and hostile relationships of the immortal force, managing to
compile them into several large books and even including pictures. Not
only that, but Jiang Shangzhen even gave these books away for free,
sometimes even paying people to accept them. And once people accepted
these books, they would at least read a few pages, no?

Han Huaizi smiled and said, \"Senior Brother, there\'s a junior present,
so even if you don\'t care about your own image, you should at least
look after Jinglong\'s image, right?\"

Huang Tong cleared his throat and drank a sip of wine, continuing,
\"Let\'s discuss some proper matters, Li Cai. The customs and traditions
at the Sword Qi Great Wall appear similar to those of the Northern
Complete Reed Continent, but in reality, the difference is actually
quite big. Indeed, the deadly clashes on the battlefield to the south of
the city wall couldn\'t be more different than the one-on-one duels
we\'re familiar with. Many cultivators from other continents are prone
to dying during the first few days of battle, suffering death if
they\'re careless for even a second. People shouldn\'t become conceited
because of their status as an Unpolished Jade Tier sword cultivator or
whatnot, what with the battlefield being a place of deadly tricks and
schemes. The demon tribe also has some incredibly sly and cunning
members.\"

Huang Tong flicked his wrist and retrieved three books from his
minimization treasure, two old and one new. He pushed them toward Li
Cai, who was sitting opposite him, and said, \"These two books were
printed in the Sword Qi Great Wall, with one introducing the demon tribe
and one being similar to a military book. I wrote these books from
personal experience after being involved in two large-scale battles. I
suggest that you familiarize yourself with these three books and
memorize them, or else I\'ll honor you with a cup of wine right now.
That way, I won\'t need to raise a cup in your honor when I return to
the Northern Complete Reed Continent\'s Great Emblem Sword Sect in the
future and hear about Li Cai dying in battle. After all, that would be a
case of you seeking death, so it absolutely wouldn\'t be deserving of me
drawing my sword to pay homage!\"

Li Cai accepted the three books and nodded in response, replying, \"This
is a matter of life and death, so I wouldn\'t dare to be conceited and
careless.\"

Huang Tong sighed and looked at his junior brother, the sect leader of
the Great Emblem Sword Sect, saying, \"Miss Li had no option but to
personally travel here due to having no other capable cultivators in her
sect. However, the Great Emblem Sword Sect still has me, Huang Tong, to
represent the sect, no? Junior Brother, I\'m not good at dealing with
miscellaneous matters, and you\'re also aware that it would be better
for you to return to the Northern Complete Reed Continent to further
help Jinglong ascend even higher. It\'s not like there won\'t be any
representatives of the Great Emblem Sword Sect at the Sword Qi Great
Wall after you leave --- there\'s still me!\"

Han Huaizi shook his head and said, \"We already reached an agreement
before. There\'s no use trying to change my mind.\"

\"Agreement my ass!\" Huang Tong fumed. \"I\'m only pissing off back to
the Northern Complete Reed Continent because I can\'t defeat you in
battle.\"

\"You can practice sword techniques in earnest when you return to the
Great Emblem Sword Sect,\" Han Huaizi said in a calm voice.

Huang Tong felt extremely anxious as he drank a large bowl of wine and
said, \"But you\'re ultimately the leader of a sect. Our Great Emblem
Sword Sect can maintain a clear conscience even if you leave and I
remain.\"

\"I\'ll suffer a guilty conscience,\" Han Huaizi replied. \"Ever since
its founding, not a single sect leader of the Great Emblem Sword Sect
has battled to death at the Sword Qi Great Wall, nor has a single
Ascension Tier sword immortal. We can potentially achieve the latter
with Liu Jinglong\'s talent, so I can feel at ease and complete the
former first.\"

Huang Tong cut a dejected figure as he left.

However, he visited the wine shop before he left for Stalactite
Mountain, using a wisp of sword qi to inscribe his name on a wooden
tablet and writing another sentence on the backside: *The old man leaves
in desolation, devoid of a sword immortal\'s spirit.*

Li Cai was filled with spirit and vigor after hearing about the wine
shop\'s rules, but she only inscribed her name on the so-called safety
tablet and didn\'t inscribe anything on the backside. She said she would
return and inscribe the backside after she killed two Upper Five Tier
demons.

Han Huaizi inscribed both his name and a message.

\"Han Huaizi, fourth sect leader of the Great Emblem Sword Sect. I have
no major regrets in this life.\"

Chen Ping\'an quietly drank wine by himself during this time.

Only when Li Cai and Han Huaizi, two sect leaders from the Northern
Complete Reed Continent, left together and walked along the deserted
street at night did Chen Ping\'an stand up and call out, \"Sect
leaders.\"

\"Don\'t look back,\" Han Huaizi said with a soft chuckle.

However, Li Cai had already turned around and asked, \"Is something the
matter?\"

\"Wine money,\" Chen Ping\'an responded with a smile.

Li Cai looked at Han Huaizi in puzzlement, asking, \"We need to pay for
wine at the Sword Qi Great Wall?\"

\"I don\'t know,\" Han Huaizi replied with a relaxed expression.

Li Cai frowned and said, \"Feel free to keep the tab under Jiang
Shangzhen\'s name. You can record one snowflake coin as one lesser heat
coin!\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and nodded in response.

The two sword immortals slowly walked along the street.

Li Cai found this slightly strange. With Chen Ping\'an\'s temperament,
it didn\'t make sense for him to do something like this. Thinking of
this, she turned around and looked back.

The young man was holding his hands inside his opposite sleeves as he
stood there and looked at them. Only when Li Cai looked back did he
return to the wine table and sit down.

Han Huaizi used his mind\'s lake to chuckle and explain, \"This young
man is just making conversation for the sake of it. He most likely
thinks that even exchanging a few more words with us is a good thing.\"

\"What kind of interaction is this?\" Li Cai asked in exasperation.

Han Huaizi thought for a moment before surprisingly giving an answer.
\"This is an interaction between sword cultivators.\"

[]{#chapter-46.xhtml}

# Chapter 583: (1): Come Here for a Beating

Sword of Coming

Compared to before, Chen Ping\'an was the only additional person at the
Ning Residence. It hadn\'t become that much livelier.

The reason behind the Ning Residence\'s sombreness was far too solemn
and heavy.

Following Ning Yao\'s birth, the Ning Residence initially had a chance
to become a top-notch clan like the Dong, Qi, and Chen clans. Now,
however, that was nothing more than a past glory. Yet, there also
existed a dark haze that couldn\'t be shooed away.

Elsewhere, business at Die Zhang\'s wine shop had initially been on the
verge of going downhill, but thanks to Sword Immortal Huang Tong from
the Great Emblem Sword Sect visiting his hometown to drink and Old Sword
Immortal Dong Sangeng personally visiting the wine shop, as well as four
other sword immortals visiting with them and three leaving inscriptions
on the safety tablets, business immediately started to boom again.

The wine shop was unbelievably busy, with a large number of people
squatting on the ground to drink. At the same time, the wine shop
promoted a new and unique pickled vegetable dish, giving it away for
free whenever someone purchased a pot of wine. It was a perfect match
with the slightly bland Bamboo Sea Small World Wine, with the crunchy
pickles a perfect complement for each sip of wine.

Chen Ping\'an maintained a very disciplined schedule while he stayed at
the Ning Residence, and apart from refining Qi for twelve hours at the
pavilion on Dragon Slaying Cliff every single day, he would often spend
one hour sweeping the courtyard in the morning with Grandma Bai. During
this time, he would ask detailed questions about matters pertaining to
fist techniques. Li Er had explained things clearly enough during Chen
Ping\'an\'s training sessions at Lion Peak, but when it came to
grandmasters at the peak, the fundamentals of their fist principles
would generally be connected, but the paths they took afterward would be
completely different.

Grandma Bai would often give demonstrations when she got into the fine
details, allowing Chen Ping\'an to emulate her movements. In fact,
Grandma Bai felt especially happy and content because Chen Ping\'an had
already used her fist stance during his battles on the street. Bai
Lianshuang\'s fist techniques were completely different from most in the
world, focusing most on retracting one\'s fist and containing one\'s
intent. Only when one tempered one\'s fist intent to a state of fullness
and flawlessness could one think about throwing punches at one\'s
opponents.

At noon every day, Chen Ping\'an would enter the training ground in the
Minute Small World with Nalan Yexing, spending approximately one hour to
familiarize himself with the flying sword of an Unpolished Jade Tier
sword cultivator.

There would be another training session at midnight, one that Nalan
Yexing had suggested, saying that the four hours at midnight would be
the best time to learn his two completely different sword intent
essences.

Learning sword techniques from Nalan Yexing was completely different
from learning fist techniques from Grandma Bai, with Chen Ping\'an often
suffering injuries in the process. Nalan Yexing already controlled his
sword strikes very well, and Chen Ping\'an would only appear like he was
bloodied and riddled with wounds. In reality, however, these were
nothing more than minor cuts. Even so, Grandma Bai would feel pained and
worried every time she saw this.

Chen Ping\'an had suffered slightly heavier wounds one time, and when
drinking wine with Nalan Yexing after the training session, as they
always did, Grandma Bai had severely scolded Nalan Yexing, unleashing a
torrent of abuse at him. Nalan Yexing hadn\'t dared to talk back, and he
could only sit there and hold onto his wine cup.

Chen Ping\'an had already explained the situation to Grandma Bai, as had
Ning Yao, with both of them telling Grandma Bai that she didn\'t need to
worry. For some unknown reason, however, the knowledgeable and capable
old woman was quite stubborn and unreasonable regarding this matter,
leading to pain and suffering for Nalan Yexing.

After hearing that Chen Ping\'an\'s barrier for the Eighteen Stops
Technique was loosening and showing signs of breakthrough, Grandma Bai
finally suppressed her worry and let Nalan Yexing off the hook. He
needed to be given credit for his hard work, even if he wasn\'t given
credit for his achievements.

Regarding the Eighteen Stops Technique that A\'Liang had modified, Chen
Ping\'an privately asked Ning Yao why A\'Liang had only taught it to so
few people.

Ning Yao\'s expression became solemn as she explained that it wasn\'t
the case that A\'Liang didn\'t want to teach the modified Eighteen Stops
Technique to more people, but rather, he didn\'t dare to.

Sitting inside the pavilion, Chen Ping\'an suddenly jolted awake at this
realization, so terrified that he surprisingly broke into a cold sweat.

If A\'Liang had taught this modified technique to too many people, then
it was inevitable that the younger generation of demon tribe sword
cultivators in the Savage World would manage to elevate their Sword Dao
to the next level!

Ning Yao looked at Chen Ping\'an.

\"I\'ve only taught the technique to a single person --- Pei Qian,\"
Chen Ping\'an said.

\"Then it\'s okay,\" Ning Yao replied with a nod.

Afterward, Chen Ping\'an asked whether, with the exception of the two
published books, there were any other books by sword immortals available
in the markets. It didn\'t matter whether the sword immortal was local
or not, nor did it matter whether the book was about battles at the
Sword Qi Great Wall or travels through the Savage World.

Ning Yao replied that the Ning Residence didn\'t have many such books in
its collection, with most of the books in the scripture library
belonging to the Three Teachings and the Hundred Schools of Thought.
However, Chen Ping\'an could try his luck at Mirage Market located in
the north of the city.

Chen Ping\'an became quite hesitant.

This market was extremely strange, with its foundation genuinely being a
mirage. Moreover, this mirage had remained tangible and condensed for a
long time, not dispersing into thin air. The buildings were majestic and
imposing, appearing much like immortal residences, and the forty or so
structures of various styles could hold several thousand people at once.

The Sword Qi Great Wall was tightly guarded, making it difficult for
outsiders to enter and exit. Thus, the large businesses that had
frequent dealings between the Majestic World and the Sword Qi Great Wall
would all set up shop at Mirage Market, selling all kinds of strange and
wonderful artifacts, ancient curios, immortal treasures, and everything
in between. However, Mirage Market would fade once every one hundred
years, during which the cultivators and people residing there would need
to exit and wait for the market to condense into a tangible form again.
Only then could they return.

Ning Yao had once faced an assassination attempt at Mirage Market.

It was also over there that Grandma Bai had fallen from the tenth tier
of martial arts to the ninth tier, the Mountain Summit Tier. One had to
realize that, unlike Qi refiners, it was quite rare for pure martial
artists to drop cultivation bases. From this, it was abundantly clear
just how dangerous and brutal the assassination attempt on Ning Yao had
been.

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t agree with Ning Yao\'s suggestion to visit Mirage
Market together, and he instead planned to ask someone to help him
purchase the books. This was simply a matter of spending money, money
that he had worked hard to earn and spend.

Disregarding their combat power and only focusing on their cultivation
speed, Chen Ping\'an could compare himself to Die Zhang, Chen Sanqiu,
and the others, even if he didn\'t compare himself to Ning Yao. Even so,
Chen Ping\'an still sincerely felt like he wasn\'t at their level.

One time at the training ground, Yan Zhuo had joked that he would teach
in the stead of Chen Ping\'an, passing down the unparalleled fist
technique to Guo Zhujiu. Chen Ping\'an had squatted down nearby and
ignored their nonsense. However, when he looked up and glanced at the
sight of Chen Sanqiu and Dong Huafu refining Qi in the pavilion, using
their bridges of immortality to form links with heaven and earth, he saw
that their speed of channeling spiritual energy was even quicker than
the eye could follow. This caused Chen Ping\'an to feel slightly vexed,
feeling like he was wasting the top-notch environment of Dragon Slaying
Cliff by cultivating there every day.

Ning Yao stood beside Chen Ping\'an and consoled, \"Your bridge of
immortality isn\'t fully constructed yet, and the two of them are
already Golden Core Tier cultivators, so that\'s why you feel like there
exists such a huge gulf. Things will be different when you obtain all
five bonded items of the Five Elements, with each bonded item supporting
the others. You only have three bonded items right now, but the quality
of the water seal, the soil of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent\'s
Five Mountains, and the wooden divine statue are all good enough, able
to form the shell of a small world. You have to realize that even here
at the Sword Qi Great Wall, the large majority of earth immortal sword
cultivators don\'t possess such complicated core abodes.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and remarked, \"It\'s enough for sword cultivators
to have a decently good bonded sword. It doesn\'t need to be supported
by so many bonded items.\"

\"Aren\'t I just trying to comfort you?\" Ning Yao asked.

\"I appreciate it,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a smile.

He then recalled something and asked, \"Die Zhang is busy with her store
and wine shop every day --- will this truly not affect her
cultivation?\"

Ning Yao shook her head and replied, \"No, it won\'t. Apart from when
she advanced to the Abode Tier and the Golden Core Tier at the Ning
Residence, she has relied on herself for all of her other breakthroughs.
She can advance very quickly each time she hones herself on the
battlefield, and she\'s a cultivation prodigy who\'s naturally built for
large-scale battles. You didn\'t see her full sparring session with Dong
Huafu last time, but you\'ll understand what I mean when you fight
alongside her on the battlefield in the future. You\'ll understand why
Chen Sanqiu and the others treat her as a friend until death. Every time
a large-scale battle concludes, Chen Sanqiu will ask Fatty Yan and Dong
Huafu whether they saw the back of Die Zhang\'s head or not, and whether
it\'s beautiful or not.\"

Ning Yao paused for a moment before continuing, \"Because of this, the
seniors in the Dong Clan and the Chen Clan have always been thoroughly
impressed by Die Zhang, who doesn\'t hail from a very good background.
This is especially so for the Chen Clan, which even intends to have a
young prodigy get married to Die Zhang. Chen Sanqiu\'s older brother
agreed to this suggestion, but Die Zhang herself didn\'t agree to it.

\"Grandpa Dong\'s willingness to see the Great Emblem Sword Sect\'s
Sword Immortal Huang Tong off at Die Zhang\'s shop had nothing to do
with you, but it had everything to do with Die Zhang saving Dong
Huafu\'s life in the past. Die Zhang once said, \'There\'s no need to
save me if my death is inevitable,\' and this was a statement greatly
appreciated by Grandpa Dong.\"

Ning Yao smiled and said, \"I didn\'t discuss these matters in much
detail with Die Zhang, seeing that she always likes to overthink things.
I\'m afraid that she\'ll end up getting distracted. She holds far too
much admiration for those senior sword immortals with outstanding
military merit, so much so that it\'s become a detriment. You would have
most likely noticed the situation at the wine shop just then. Regardless
of whether it was Zuo You, Grandpa Dong, Han Huaizi, Li Cai, or the
others, Die Zhang would feel extremely tense and nervous whenever she
saw any of them.\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded and replied, \"I did notice this. If you\'re okay
with it, I can chat with her about this matter later. I have some
experience regarding these things.\"

Ning Yao glared at Chen Ping\'an and asked, \"Why would I not be okay
with this? Perhaps you view me as a cold-hearted person?\"

Chen Ping\'an reached forward and pinched Ning Yao\'s cheeks, replying,
\"Of course not.\"

Fatty Yan had his eyes peeled and his ears open the entire time, and in
a moment of carelessness, he was kicked in the face by the young girl
who was learning martial arts from him. Yan Zhuo was completely unfazed,
and he used his eyes to signal to Guo Zhujiu, who turned around and
immediately drew a sharp breath. Her master was truly courageous! Sure
enough, those who were capable would become more courageous. At the same
time, she was also incredibly smart and fortunate, having found herself
such a brilliant master. She was definitely going to benefit from this!

Ning Yao stood still and didn\'t move, allowing Chen Ping\'an to pinch
her cheeks as she remarked, \"How very capable of you. Why don\'t I
accompany you for a sparring session in the Minute Small World?\"

Chen Ping\'an hurriedly retracted his hands, clasping one hand behind
his back and gesturing toward the training ground with his other hand as
he replied with a faint smile, \"After you.\"

Ning Yao raised an eyebrow and dashed into the Minute Small World
located near the south of the training ground, gracefully coming to a
stop before lightly flexing her wrists.

However, Chen Ping\'an had already fled into the distance, disappearing
without a trace.

Ning Yao didn\'t chase after him, instead summoning her flying sword and
casually strolling around the Minute Small World. This couldn\'t be
regarded as practicing sword techniques, and she was simply giving her
flying sword some fresh air, having not summoned it for a long time.

Cultivation was truly not worth a mention for Ning Yao.

Guo Zhujiu appeared slightly dazed as she praised, \"Assessing the
situation and knowing when to advance and when to yield\... My master is
truly a man of greatness.\"

\"Lü Duan, I\'ll teach you fist techniques, and you can teach me the art
of flattery. How does that sound?\" Yan Zhuo asked.

Copying her master\'s pose from when he had stood on the street and
faced his opponents before, the young girl clasped one hand behind her
back and clenched her other hand into a fist, appearing confident and at
ease as she shook her head and replied, \"Your heart isn\'t sincere, and
your talent is even worse.\"

Yan Zhuo was slightly dumbfounded.

Ning Yao beckoned with her hand and said, \"Lü Duan, come here for a
beating.\"

\"Alrighty!\" Guo Zhujiu shouted in reply.

She then turned around to flee, and soaring through the sky wasn\'t a
difficult task given that she was already a Middle Five Tier sword
cultivator. However, her escape wasn\'t as smooth as her master\'s.

This didn\'t matter, and a disciple didn\'t need to worry about being
inferior to their master.

However, it was a shame that Ning Yao reached forward and made a
grabbing motion, using a perfectly weighted wisp of sword qi to wrap
around Guo Zhujiu and casually drag her back.

Guo Zhujiu stumbled and stood still, giving a soft shout before putting
her hands together and interlocking her fingers, exclaiming, \"Heed my
call, heaven and earth, make me invisible to Big Sister Ning, and make
her punches and kicks not hurt at all!\"

Yan Zhuo cupped his face and started to violently massage it, muttering
to himself, \"I would rather become Lü Duan\'s disciple than to take her
as my disciple.\"

Guo Zhujiu was severely underestimating Ning Yao if she felt like her
prayers would help her escape punishment.

The young girl\'s face was black and blue as she skipped out of the Ning
Residence, and before leaving, she even asked Big Sister Ning whether
she wanted to eat some desserts. At the same time, she patted her chest
and promised that she had simply faceplanted due to walking too
carelessly. However, Big Sister Ning mysteriously grabbed her head and
thumped it against the door several times.

The slightly dizzy Guo Zhujiu left the holy land of fist technique
training by herself, touching her face as she pitifully walked along the
street. Blood from her nose covered her palm, but she casually wiped the
blood onto her clothes. She then slowly walked forward with her head
held high, thinking to herself that learning fist techniques truly
wasn\'t easy. However, this was a good thing! After all, what kind of
peerless fist technique could be learned so easily?

When she achieved seventy to eighty percent mastery of the fist
technique, she wouldn\'t do anything to Big Sister Ning. She was
Master\'s wife, so Master wouldn\'t necessarily be willing to side with
his disciple. Guo Zhujiu would tolerate her behavior. However, Dong
Bude, the old girl who couldn\'t find herself a partner, would need to
be careful when she walked around at night in the future.

The young girl, who had a lush green inkstone hanging by her waist,
gazed up at the clear blue sky, nodding lightly to herself and thinking
that today was a good day.

Chen Ping\'an and Ning Yao went for a walk to Die Zhang\'s wine shop.

In the past, they would each have their own rest time between Qi
refinement, and these rest times wouldn\'t necessarily line up. Thus, it
was often Chen Ping\'an who went to the wine shop by himself.

It was clear that Ning Yao had purposely cut her cultivation short today
so that she could accompany Chen Ping\'an.

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t think much about this.

When walking past the wine shops that were nowhere near as popular as
his own, Chen Ping\'an looked at the many couplets and horizontal
scrolls and said to Ning Yao in a soft voice, \"Their calligraphy skills
aren\'t as good as mine, and even the contents of their couplets and
horizontal scrolls are nowhere near as good as mine, don\'t you think?\"

\"One of the big restaurants recruited an unofficial disciple of a
Confucian sage, the sage of an academy, to personally write their
couplet and horizontal scroll,\" Ning Yao replied.

Chen Ping\'an smiled and said, \"They\'ve only taken a small and shallow
leaf out of my book, so this won\'t do them any good. I dare wager that
the restaurant owner will need to offer incense and thank the heavens if
business at his restaurant doesn\'t become worse. He doesn\'t need to
dream about the wine drinkers appreciating the couplet and horizontal
scroll. There are seventy-odd restaurants and wine shops competing here,
and there are one hundred or so types of immortal wine produced in the
Majestic World, so it isn\'t difficult at all to find wine to drink. At
the end of the day, however, what is actually being sold?\"

\"What?\" Ning Yao asked.

Chen Ping\'an smiled and didn\'t say anything, continuing to take in the
contents of the couplets and horizontal scrolls that were like shy young
ladies.

\"You can piss off if you don\'t want to say,\" Ning Yao snapped.

\"We, of course, want the customers who drink our wine to feel like
sword immortals even if they aren\'t sword immortals,\" Chen Ping\'an
hurriedly explained. \"If they\'re already sword immortals, then we want
them to feel even greater than sword immortals. Our wine shop is small,
and the tables and chairs are crude, yet it\'s unexpectedly
unrestrained, with the small wine cups containing colossal worlds. Which
is why Die Zhang\'s suggestion of copying those big and fancy
restaurants and swapping out our current tables and chairs now that
we\'ve made some money is completely unacceptable.

\"Fatty Yan suggested using his own money to make an investment,
offering up a large silk shop that\'s under his name but isn\'t doing
too well. However, I directly turned down his offer. Firstly, moving
locations will damage the feng shui of the wine shop, stripping away the
unique atmosphere and charm of our current wine shop for nothing in
return. Secondly, this city isn\'t small, with tens of thousands of
people living here, and we can estimate that half of the population is
female. That being the case, will silk and satin truly not sell?

\"So, I plan to have a good chat with Fatty Yan, and I\'ll tell him not
to invest in our wine shop. Rather, we\'ll invest in his silk shop.
Casting our gaze across the city, which group is genuinely willing to
spend money apart from sword cultivators who like to drink? It\'s
naturally women who like to make themselves more beautiful. With this in
mind, I\'ve already drafted up a new couplet for the silk shop\...\"

\"A\'Liang once said that men practicing sword techniques can rely on
just their talent to become sword immortals,\" Ning Yao said slowly.
\"However, a person can\'t dream about becoming a kind and considerate
man like him if they haven\'t been pierced in the heart by the incisive
words of women that are like flying swords, suffered the emotional pain
of women walking away and not looking back, and had to drink hundreds
upon thousands of liters of lingering dream wine.\"

Chen Ping\'an turned around to face Ning Yao, winking and saying,
\"You\'re right about that. For the past ten years, the person on my
mind has been extremely far away, so far away that even the flying
swords of immortals can barely reach her. I could only drink wine and
practice fist techniques to wash away my worries.\"

He suddenly became panicked and flustered in the next moment.

Ning Yao didn\'t conceal anything as her expression turned into one of
despondence.

It was as if her eyes wanted to convey something, but she couldn\'t help
but hesitate. She wasn\'t good at speaking, so she always chose to
remain silent. This was because she didn\'t know how to speak in a
romantic manner.

In the past, the young boy wearing straw sandals --- who had only
arrived at Stalactite Mountain after throwing one million punches ---
had been just as awkward as her when it came to speaking to others. As
such, she didn\'t feel bad about anything, and she felt like this was
only natural. Everything was communicated silently between the two of
them.

Chen Ping\'an extended a thumb and gently brushed it across Ning Yao\'s
eyebrow, saying in a soft voice, \"Don\'t be unhappy. You need to relax
your frown.\"

\"I\'m not unhappy,\" Ning Yao replied.

Chen Ping\'an bent down and lifted Ning Yao up before sprinting away.

Ning Yao was at a complete loss.

Carrying Ning Yao in his arms, Chen Ping\'an ran all the way to Die
Zhang\'s wine shop. The several dozen customers sitting at the tables
and squatting on the ground were all stupefied by what they saw.

There were quite a number of young women at the wine shop, most of them
from large clans and visiting the wine shop due to its fame. They
weren\'t shocked by this sight, and their eyes instead lit up. In fact,
some of the bolder women even drank a large swig of wine and whistled
loudly and adeptly.

Chen Ping\'an put Ning Yao down and waved an arm, announcing, \"Those
who haven\'t paid yet will all get ten percent off!\"

He then added, \"The words of the Second Shopkeeper might not count, so
everything will be subject to Shopkeeper Die Zhang\'s final approval.\"

The customers immediately turned their heads toward Die Zhang, who
smiled and said with a nod, \"Let\'s give everyone ten percent off.\"

Cheers and claps instantly rang out around the wine shop.

Bloody hell\... Being able to get a discount from this Second Shopkeeper
truly wasn\'t an easy feat.

Chen Ping\'an grabbed a small stool and was just about to go to the
intersection between the street and the alley to become a storyteller
again. He looked at Ning Yao, who nodded to give her approval.

Die Zhang walked over to Ning Yao\'s side and asked in a quiet voice,
\"What\'s going on today? Chen Ping\'an never acted like this in the
past, and judging by his behavior, it won\'t be long before he starts
beating drums and gongs on the street.\"

Ning Yao shot a sideways glance at a table of young women in the
distance who were engaged in spirited chatter, smiling and not saying
anything.

Die Zhang suppressed a smile. She had once secretly mentioned to Ning
Yao that females would often visit the wine shop to drink now, yet their
purpose for patronizing the shop wasn\'t for the wine. Instead, they
were naturally visiting because of the renowned Second Shopkeeper. There
were two shameless customers who had not only purchased wine but had
also inscribed their names and messages on the safety tablets hanging
around the walls.

If Die Zhang weren\'t the shopkeeper, she would have felt a strong urge
to remove these safety tablets. Ning Yao had also flipped the two safety
tablets around to read their messages before, and she had quietly
flipped them back after taking a quick glance.
