# Chapter 587: Piss Off Further, Chen Qingdu

Sword of Coming

Chen Ping\'an felt slightly unconscionable as he drank wine and looked
at the busy shopkeeper. He swirled the wine pot around, estimating that
there were still two bowls of wine remaining. The wine bowls at the shop
indeed weren\'t very big.

Chen Ping\'an raised a hand and beckoned Die Zhang over to drink
together, pouring her a bowl of wine after she walked over and sat down.
He smiled and said, \"I don\'t come to the wine shop often, so I\'ll
take the opportunity today to say a few things to you. Fan Dache is only
a friend of a friend, and what he wanted to hear today wasn\'t actually
principles or reason. He feels far too depressed, and he needed an
outlet to vent his emotions.

\"However, Chen Sanqiu and the others didn\'t know what to say
specifically because they\'re Fan Dache\'s friends. When buried for a
long time, the sweetness and mellowness of aged wine are most
intoxicating when suddenly opened. There\'s a big chance that Fan Dache
will die the next time he travels south to fight, and he\'ll most likely
think that he can live in her heart forever this way. Of course, this is
only my speculation, and I always like to think of the worst-case
scenario.

\"In any case, I was scolded severely by Fan Dache for no reason, and he
even shattered a bowl of our wine shop --- I need to have Chen Sanqiu
pay up for this in the future. You\'re different, Die Zhang, and not
only are you Ning Yao\'s friend, but you\'re my friend as well. So, I\'m
not going to hold back too much regarding what I say next.\"

\"Rest assured, I\'m not Fan Dache, so I won\'t go on a drunken rampage.
I can\'t bear to shatter a wine bowl and lose money either,\" Die Zhang
replied in a joking manner.

\"How do you feel about sword immortals?\" Chen Ping\'an asked directly.
\"Some unleash sword strikes in the distance, while some visit this shop
to drink wine. Do you feel the same way about them? Or?\"

Die Zhang thought for a moment before replying, \"I feel respect toward
them.\"

She hesitated for a moment before adding, \"This all comes down to fear.
I suffered at the hands of some low-level sword cultivators when I was
young, and to put things simply, those were very miserable experiences.
At that time, those low-level sword cultivators already appeared like
lofty immortals in my eyes. You might find this comical, but I couldn\'t
help but shake and go pale whenever I walked past them when I was
little. This only improved slightly after I became acquainted with
A\'Liang.

\"I naturally want to become a sword immortal, and I won\'t regret it if
I die on the path to becoming a sword immortal. Rest assured, from
becoming a Nascent Tier cultivator to becoming a sword immortal, I\'ve
already considered what I need to do at each cultivation base. At the
very least, I can purchase a large residence many years earlier than
planned. This is thanks to you.\"

Chen Ping\'an raised his wine bowl and drank with Die Zhang, after which
he smiled and said, \"Okay, I feel like the issue isn\'t big. You admire
the strong, but you can also sympathize with the weak, allowing you to
walk a middle path. Not only were Ning Yao and I worried, but Chen
Sanqiu and the others were also worried about you fighting too
ferociously in the large-scale battles, caring too little about your own
life.

\"There was a misunderstanding between you and Fatty Yan in the past, so
he doesn\'t dare to say too much. As for the others, they\'re also
afraid of saying too much, similar to the situation with Chen Sanqiu and
Fan Dache. Speaking truthfully, however, don\'t trivialize the matter of
life and death. Don\'t die if you can avoid it.

\"Forget about it, these types of things are often out of our control.
I\'ve gone through the same troubles, so I don\'t have the right to
lecture you. In any case, I\'ll do the same thing as Fatty Yan and the
others the next time we leave the city wall, and I\'ll strive to take a
few extra glances at your back. Come, let\'s raise a toast to your back,
shopkeeper.\"

Die Zhang raised her wine bowl and lightly touched it with Chen
Ping\'an\'s before downing its contents.

Chen Ping\'an smiled and said, \"My next question might be asking for a
beating, so you need to promise me this first: I\'ll still be the second
shopkeeper afterward, and we\'ll still be friends afterward.\"

Die Zhang smiled and replied, \"Just ask your question first. Promises
are useless, and women reneging on promises is even quicker than men
downing wine.\"

Chen Ping\'an felt slightly exasperated as he asked, \"You like the
Confucian noble scholar who took with him the sword, Righteous Aura, but
do you only like his character, or did you somewhat like his status as a
virtuous scholar as well? Do you hope that he can one day bring you out
of the Sword Qi Great Wall and take you to Stalactite Mountain and the
Majestic World?\"

Die Zhang blushed slightly, and she nodded in response before replying
in a low voice, \"I liked both aspects of him. I liked his character and
demeanor, and I especially liked his bookish aura. He was a virtuous
scholar! Just how impressive is that? And he\'s even become a noble
scholar now, so I naturally care about this a lot! In any case, I\'ve
always wanted to travel to the Majestic World ever since meeting
A\'Liang and Ning Yao, and it would obviously be best if I could do so
together with him!\"

Die Zhang was in high spirits as she continued, \"If there truly comes a
day when he reciprocates my feelings, then I\'ll travel to the Majestic
World only when I become a sword immortal! Otherwise, I won\'t leave the
Sword Qi Great Wall even if he begs me to.\"

Chen Ping\'an clicked his tongue in wonder and remarked, \"It\'s
difficult to say whether he likes you or not, yet you\'re already
thinking this far ahead?\"

Die Zhang took a large swig of wine, wiping her mouth with the back of
her hand before replying in exuberance, \"Is it illegal to simply think
about this?!\"

Chen Ping\'an hesitated for a moment before saying, \"Let me tell you a
story. This isn\'t hearsay, nor is it something I personally witnessed.
You can treat this as a story from some book, and after listening to it,
you can, at the very least, avoid the worst-case scenario. It isn\'t
very useful for much else, and many aspects of this story aren\'t
necessarily relevant to you and that noble scholar.\"

This was a story about a lovestruck scholar and a female ghost wearing a
wedding dress.

Those who had strong emotions would often be weighed down by pain, and
those who were lovestruck would often be hit with disappointment.

Naturally, Chen Ping\'an didn\'t hope that Die Zhang and the noble
scholar would suffer such a fate, and he hoped that all of the lovers in
the world could ultimately hold hands and enjoy life together.

There was a condition to this, of course, that being one didn\'t blindly
fall in love with the wrong person. This blindness didn\'t just pertain
to whether the other person was worthy of one\'s romantic feelings, but
it actually pertained more to one\'s own understanding. The most pitiful
people were those who failed to understand from the beginning to the end
why the person whom they loved reciprocated the love in the beginning,
yet didn\'t love them anymore in the end.

This was the reason behind Chen Ping\'an\'s question to Fan Dache,
subtly asking him whether Yu Qia knew about his borrowing money from his
friends to buy presents for her. Was Fan Dache aware of her thoughts and
mindset? Would he still accept her attitude if he were fully aware? If
he did, and if he were able to properly deal with the troublesome
branches on this path, then that would be a reflection of his abilities.

If Fan Dache were truly unaware and muddleheaded from the beginning to
the end, then he definitely wouldn\'t have become so embarrassed and
angry at the wine shop. Indeed, it was abundantly clear that Fan Dache
was aware of Yu Qia\'s knowledge of him borrowing money from Chen
Sanqiu, whether he had realized it from the beginning or only realized
it much later.

Even so, Yu Qia had chosen to accept Fan Dache\'s effort and sacrifice,
continuing to ask him for more. Did Fan Dache truly understand what this
signified? Clearly not. Perhaps he had a vague feeling that her actions
were wrong and hurtful, but he was ultimately unable to come up with a
proper solution.

Fan Dache only knew that the two of them would grow further and further
apart following their breakup. He drank wine to wash away his sorrows,
feeling like he should dig his heart out to show Yu Qiao his true
feelings.

Was it wrong for Fan Dache to unreservedly love a person in this manner?
Of course not. How could it be wrong for a man to sincerely love a
woman, willing to completely open himself up to her? Delving deeper,
however, was it possible for there to truly be no wrong? Being so deeply
in love with someone, should a person not, first and foremost,
understand who they were in love with?

Chen Ping\'an was an outsider, but he had immediately seen through Yu
Qia\'s strong ambitions after seeing her from afar two times, also
noticing how she subtly separated Fan Dache\'s friends into different
categories. She was filled with fighting spirit and lofty ambitions, and
simply guaranteeing food and shelter with a wealthy descendant like Fan
Dache was far from enough.

Yu Qia hoped that she could one day be invited on her own merit to those
wine tables that were filled with sword immortals. Not only that, but
she definitely wouldn\'t be satisfied with being a mere accompanying
guest at the end of the table. Rather, people definitely needed to
voluntarily walk over to respectfully raise a toast to her after she sat
down! She would sit up straight and wait for other people to pay
respects to her!

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t like this type of woman, but he definitely didn\'t
detest them either. He simply understood them and respected their choice
among the many different paths in the world.

Did Fan Dache understand these things? No, he didn\'t understand them at
all.

His relationship had fallen apart, but he could perhaps try his luck and
find a suitable and like-minded partner in the future, becoming immortal
Dao partners with her. If he were unlucky, however, then he would only
suffer the same disappointment again.

Die Zhang felt righteous indignation when she heard the story\'s
conclusion, and she asked, \"Was the scholar simply yearning to become a
noble scholar of Lake View Academy and yearning to legitimately marry
that female ghost and carry her on an eight-person sedan chair?\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded and replied, \"That was always his unwavering
ambition, and it was because of this that he was forced to jump into the
lake and commit suicide. However, the female ghost mistakenly thought
that the scholar had betrayed her deep feelings the entire time.\"

The rims of Die Zhang\'s eyes surprisingly became red as she murmured,
\"How could the ending be like this? His companions at the Confucian
academy were also scholars, so how could they be so wicked?\"

\"Scholars never use swords to attack their foes,\" Chen Ping\'an said.
\"The reason I told you this story is that I want you to think more. The
Majestic World is vast, and the number of scholars is great, so is it
possible for every single one of them to be a good person who lives up
to the standards of the sagely scriptures? If that\'s the case, then
would the Sword Qi Great Wall be in this current state?\"

Die Zhang looked up at Chen Ping\'an with a strange expression.

\"I try my best to understand these matters and think more about
everything. I observe more, think more, and contemplate more, not for
the sake of becoming them, but quite the contrary, for the sake of never
becoming like them,\" Chen Ping\'an continued with a smile.

He raised his wine bowl and said, \"If there truly comes a day when the
romantic feelings between you and that noble scholar are mutual, and
you\'re also a sword immortal at that time and decide to travel to the
Majestic World, then you definitely need to invite Ning Yao and me over.
I\'ll help you stay guarded against those scholars who are no better
than dogs.

\"No matter if it\'s that noble scholar\'s so-called friends,
companions, seniors, or teachers, it\'s naturally best if these people
are reasonable to deal with. I also trust that the people around him are
mainly good. Those who are alike tend to gather together, after all.

\"However, it\'s inevitable for some bad people to slip through the
cracks, and I know what kind of repulsive principles they\'ll spew once
they open their mouths. I\'m the Scholarly Sage\'s final disciple, so
when it comes to arguing with other people, I was at least able to learn
some of the fundamental essence.

\"What do friends mean? It means that some unpleasant words and
mood-killing words have to be said, just like some difficult tasks have
to be undertaken. I\'m actually praising myself by saying this. Come on,
let\'s drink some wine!\"

It was rare for Die Zhang to smile so brightly, but her expression
quickly became downcast just as she was about to raise her bowl to drink
some wine. She shot a glance at her missing arm.

\"These things won\'t matter if the feelings between the two of you are
genuine. Otherwise, it won\'t make a difference even if you gain two
extra arms,\" Chen Ping\'an said.

Die Zhang chuckled in irritation and huffed, \"Is it a good thing to
have three arms?\"

\"You have a point. My shortcoming is not being very good at speaking
reason,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a smile.

Die Zhang\'s mood improved again, and she was just about to touch her
wine bowl with Chen Ping\'an\'s. However, Chen Ping\'an suddenly killed
the atmosphere again, saying, \"In any case, there\'s no relationship
between you and that noble scholar to speak of right now, so don\'t get
too ahead of yourself and daydream about a perfect future.

\"Otherwise, you\'ll only be setting yourself up for disappointment in
the future. At that time, this wine shop will earn boatloads of money
from you as you drink to wash away your sorrows, and as the second
shopkeeper, this won\'t sit right with me.\"

Die Zhang\'s expression immediately became dark.

Chen Ping\'an sighed with emotion and remarked, \"The truth often hurts,
and it\'s difficult to be friends.\"

Die Zhang suddenly smiled and said, \"You\'ve already described both the
best-case scenario and the worst-case scenario. Thank you for this.\"

She grabbed the wine pot, and she quickly discovered that there was only
a single bowl of wine remaining.

Chen Ping\'an waved his hand and said, \"I won\'t drink any more. Ning
Yao is quite strict about these things.\"

Die Zhang didn\'t hold back, pouring herself the remaining wine and
starting to drink slowly.

If a customer hollered for more wine, Die Zhang would tell them to grab
wine or grab food by themselves. This was the good thing about regular
customers --- there was no need to be too polite with them after
becoming familiar.

Die Zhang had been worried about providing insufficient service at the
beginning, so she had personally attended to all aspects of the wine
shop. It was only after seeing Chen Ping\'an act like this --- chatting
and bantering with customers and even asking them to help grab wine and
food, yet still managing to keep them happy --- that she had emulated
him and started to do the same.

She looked at Chen Ping\'an, and she noticed that he was gazing toward
the corner of the alley. In the past, he would always spend the majority
of his time sitting over there and playing the role of a storyteller.

Today, however, the children no longer gathered around the small stool.

Die Zhang knew that Chen Ping\'an would inevitably feel downcast.

Even so, she still didn\'t fully understand why Chen Ping\'an cared so
much about these matters. Perhaps it was because he had come from an
impoverished alley in that small town in the Jewel Small World? Even
though he was already an immortal in the eyes of many people, he still
had a soft spot for impoverished alleys?

However, sword cultivators who grew up in the impoverished alleys of the
Sword Qi Great Wall all dreamed about becoming neighbors with those
powerful families and wealthy clans, no longer needing to return to the
small alleys where roosters crowed and dogs barked. Die Zhang also had
the same mindset.

Chen Ping\'an said he wouldn\'t drink anymore, but looking at Die Zhang
leisurely drinking by herself, he couldn\'t help but glance at the pot
of wine on the table that he planned to give to Senior Nalan. A battle
took place in his mind, and Die Zhang pretended that she couldn\'t see
anything. To say nothing of the customers finding it extremely difficult
to get any benefits from the second shopkeeper, even she, the
shopkeeper, found it extremely difficult.

Just when Die Zhang thought that Chen Ping\'an would definitely pay up
today, he thought of a brilliant solution and stood up, giddily
shuffling over to another table with his wine bowl. After making some
small talk with the sword cultivators there, he was able to get himself
a bowl of free wine, which he promptly finished drinking. When he
returned to Die Zhang\'s table, he surprisingly had half a bowl of wine
again.

After sitting down, Chen Ping\'an sighed with emotion and remarked,
\"They\'re far too enthusiastic and kind. I couldn\'t turn down their
goodwill, and they wouldn\'t take no for an answer.\"

\"Chen Ping\'an, you\'re actually a successful disciple of
Commercialism, aren\'t you?\" Die Zhang asked in an exasperated voice.

\"There are countless people in the world, and who isn\'t a business
person?\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a smile.

Die Zhang glanced at Chen Ping\'an drinking and said in amusement, \"You
said just then that Ning Yao is quite strict about these things?\"

Chen Ping\'an had already enjoyed quite a few bowls of wine today, and
he replied with a chuckle, \"Am I a lofty fourth tier Qi refiner for
nothing? A burst of spiritual energy dissipates the alcohol and
astonishes the world.\"

Die Zhang chuckled in response, deciding that she would definitely
tattle on him to Ning Yao.

Chen Ping\'an looked down the street, thinking to himself that business
at the other restaurants and wine shops was truly quite mediocre.

When seeing the booming business of the new wine shop before, the owners
and attendants of these businesses had all stood outside their front
doors to loudly and enthusiastically advertise themselves and attract
customers. Yet, they couldn\'t keep this up, could they? Meanwhile, he
hadn\'t even used one hundred percent of his power yet.

Die Zhang continued to serve the guests after drinking wine. She
ultimately couldn\'t bring herself to act as shamelessly as the second
shopkeeper.

Chen Ping\'an slowly sipped his half a bowl of wine.

Seeing this, Die Zhang directly gave him a pair of chopsticks and a
plate of picked vegetables.

Chen Ping\'an sat cross-legged and slowly chipped away at the wine and
food.

More and more customers arrived, so Chen Ping\'an returned the table and
squatted down on the side of the street. Of course, he didn\'t forget to
take the pot of unopened wine with him.

Die Zhang glanced at the wine bowl that was almost empty, yet still
unfinished after such a long time, and she said with an angry chuckle,
\"Can you tell me straight if you want me to treat you to some wine?\"

She couldn\'t help but feel a little perplexed. He was genuinely willing
to offer two celestial tools as a marriage gift, yet he was also miserly
to such an extreme degree?

Ning Yao\'s eyebrows had been slender and attractive when privately
telling Die Zhang about this, almost causing Die Zhang\'s heart to
flutter as well.

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and said, \"You\'re truly mistaken about my
intentions.\"

And thus, he walked over to another table to get half a bowl of wine for
free, not forgetting to raise it in front of Die Zhang to prove his
innocence.

Die Zhang busily served the customers for a long while, and she
discovered that Chen Ping\'an was still squatting on the side of the
street.

She couldn\'t help but walk over and ask, \"Is something on your mind?\"

Chen Ping\'an shook his head, but he nodded afterward and gazed into the
distance, replying, \"There are things on my mind, and they\'re all good
things. I always feel like I\'m dreaming, and this was especially the
case when I saw Fan Dache.\"

Chen Ping\'an ate some pickled vegetables and drank a sip of wine,
smiling widely as he did so.

Die Zhang carried a stool over and sat beside him.

\"Second Shopkeeper, don\'t you dare have any impure thoughts about Miss
Die Zhang. Although it\'s not a big deal if you do, and you simply need
to treat me to a pot of wine --- the five snowflake coin variant --- as
hush money,\" one customer chuckled and said.

Chen Ping\'an raised a middle finger high into the air.

Die Zhang didn\'t care about this at all. Indeed, people at the Sword Qi
Great Wall genuinely didn\'t have any reservations about these matters.
Die Zhang wouldn\'t feel embarrassed or awkward regardless of how
sensitive she was, and feeling these ways would only prove that she had
something to hide.

Moreover, she had never come across someone more measured than Chen
Ping\'an among those in the same generation.

In reality, everyone could see the strong feelings between Chen Ping\'an
and Ning Yao, regardless of whether they were friend or foe. Chen
Ping\'an had traveled a great distance to come here from the Majestic
World, and this was his second time doing so. Not only that, but he also
planned to leave the city wall and fight alongside Ning Yao in the next
large-scale battle. Perhaps some people would gossip and spread rumors
behind their backs, purposely putting a negative spin on things.
However, the large majority of people were clearly aware of the reality.

Chen Ping\'an genuinely drank quite a lot of wine today.

\"If we\'re conceited and oblivious to the people, the matters, and the
world around us, then we\'ll often find it difficult to help ourselves,
liberate ourselves, and cherish things when it comes to the joys,
sorrows, reunions, and partings around us.

\"Those who are young can learn, and they don\'t need to be afraid of
making mistakes. They can right their wrongs, and they can strive to
make the good better. What is there to be afraid of? What\'s scary is
that people like Fan Dache become completely stupefied after a blow to
their heart, after which they start to blame the heavens and complain
about other people.

\"Do you know why Fan Dache insisted on inviting me over to drink with
him? And insisted on asking for my opinion? Why didn\'t he ask for the
opinions of Chen Sanqiu and the others? That\'s because he can live with
not coming to this wine shop to drink in the future, but he can\'t live
with losing true friends like Chen Sanqiu and the others.\"

Upon hearing this, Die Zhang asked, \"Do you have a terrible impression
of Fan Dache?\"

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and replied, \"You have it the wrong way
around. Judging by how sincere his love for that young woman was, Fan
Dache won\'t draw hate from other people. It\'s precisely because of
this that I was willing to play the role of the villain and speak the
unpleasant truth. Otherwise, would I not know what to say to comfort
him? Was I so bored that I provoked him on purpose?

\"Meticulously examining a person\'s heart is no comfortable matter. The
more meticulous we are, the tougher things will become.

\"However, if this initial discomfort can allow those around us to live
better and more peaceful lives, then we\'ll eventually become more
comfortable and relaxed in the end as well. Knowing this, it\'s very
important for us to take responsibility for ourselves first. In this
way, treating our opponents with respect and seriousness is also one
aspect of taking responsibility for ourselves.\"

Die Zhang wholeheartedly agreed with this, but she still said,
\"Alright, I get it. I\'ll treat you to some wine!\"

Chen Ping\'an chuckled in speechlessness, putting his chopsticks down
beside the plate and walking away with the unopened pot of wine.

As he walked, he suddenly turned his gaze toward the city wall, but the
strange feeling disappeared as quickly as it had arrived. Chen Ping\'an
didn\'t think too much about this.

------------

Chen Qingdu\'s brows were knitted in a deep frown as he slowly walked
out of his thatched cottage and forcefully stomped his foot, unleashing
even more power than when the Scholarly Sage had visited the Sword Qi
Great Wall just then.

A figure in white swayed elusively above the city wall.

This was an extremely tall woman standing with her back to the north and
her face to the south, a sword in one hand.

Looking at her wavering figure, Chen Qingdu knew that she couldn\'t
remain here for too long. This allowed him to breathe a sigh of relief.

However, an uncharacteristic expression of seriousness and reminiscence
appeared on the face of the old great sword immortal who had already
guarded this city wall for ten thousand years.

He slowly walked over to the parapet where she was standing and asked in
curiosity, \"Why have you come here?\"

\"I\'ve come here to visit my master,\" she replied in a calm voice.

Chen Qingdu was stunned into silence for a long time before exclaiming
in disbelief, \"What?!\"

She then continued, \"So you can piss off further, Chen Qingdu.\"

# Chapter 588: Sword Techniques from the Heavens

Sword of Coming

Thankfully, the flow of time had already ground to a halt at the Sword
Qi Great Wall, or else the tall woman\'s words would have shaken the
sword hearts of a great many sword immortals.

Of course, the nearby Zuo You and the slightly further Hidden Official
and Dong Sangeng could remain unrestrained, but they were still unable
to detect what was going on around Chen Qingdu. If anyone dared to
wantonly challenge the barrier erected by Chen Qingdu, that would
essentially be an act of challenging the old great sword immortal to a
sword duel. Chen Qingdu never went easy on other people, and the number
of sword immortals who had died at his hands was more than just the
solitary Dong Guanpu from ten years ago.

Only sword immortals were able to witness Chen Qingdu\'s sword strikes
--- this wasn\'t a baseless statement.

Chen Qingdu wasn\'t angered by the tall woman\'s words at all, and he
smiled as he jumped onto the parapet and sat down cross-legged, gazing
at the vast expanse of land to the south as he asked, \"How did the
Confucian temple dare to let you stand here? These sages most certainly
won\'t be oblivious to the consequences. Perhaps the old scholar vouched
for you? Indeed, he just made a huge contribution for no compensation to
speak of. He\'s truly willing to use up his merit for the sake of his
closing disciple.\"

One was standing on the parapet while the other was sitting,
highlighting a clear distinction between their seniority.

The tall woman frowned and commented slowly, \"Chen Qingdu, your courage
has also grown considerably after ten thousand years of cultivation.\"

Chen Qingdu smiled and replied, \"It\'s been a long time since I last
spoke with you, Senior. This is a rare opportunity, so what does it
matter if I\'m scolded a bit?\"

The tall woman had only stood here for a brief moment, yet she had
already become aware of some secrets that perhaps even the sages of the
Three Teachings and the many sword immortals were unable to gain
knowledge of. She shook her head and said, \"How pitiful. Why act like
that if you knew things would turn out like this? Do you feel any
regret?\"

Chen Qingdu nodded and replied, \"Focusing on just myself, I do indeed
have many regrets. Back then, I actually had other paths in front of me,
allowing me to be unrestrained amid heaven and earth, perhaps even more
than most gods and deities. However, I still brandished my sword and
ascended higher, continuing to fight alongside many like-minded people
in the human world, pointing my blade at the heavens. Those who died
didn\'t feel any regret, so whether or not I feel regret isn\'t
important at all.\"

Chen Qingdu looked up and asked, \"Does Senior feel any regret?\"

The tall woman was leaning against her sword, her palms resting on its
hilt. She fell silent for a moment before sidestepping the question and
asking, \"You wouldn\'t have missed the three wisps of sword qi in his
acupoints, would you?\"

\"I noticed some traces, but I didn\'t dare to believe it,\" Chen Qingdu
replied. \"At the same time, I was also worried about this being a
profound scheme of the Confucian Sect.\"

Chen Qingdu gazed up at the sky, sighing with emotion before continuing,
\"Prior to that child, just how lofty and peerless were the individuals
accompanying you, Senior? A sword strike here and a sword strike there,
and they could casually leave in their wake a mountain of deity corpses
and a trail of shattered blessed lands.

\"Following them, however, the ordinary young boy only possessed the
aptitude to become an earth immortal, yet his bridge of immortality was
shattered, and he was only a\... third or fourth tier martial artist at
the time. How could I believe my eyes, Senior? Even until now, I\'m
still unable to comprehend why you decided to choose Chen Ping\'an.

\"So, I purposely turned a blind eye to this, waiting for this day to
arrive. I hope that the moment I attain enlightenment is when I meet
you, and I hope that the last sight before my death is to take another
look at those wisps of sword qi.\"

There was a faint smile on Chen Qingdu\'s face as he put his index
finger and middle finger together, lightly drawing them through the air
and instantly causing a river of sword qi to light up far in the
distance. This wasn\'t a perfectly straight river; it was instead a
winding river, seemingly gazing down at the human world from the
heavens.

\"This is the first sword technique that I learned,\" Chen Qingdu said
with a smile. \"Truth be told, the sword cultivators nowadays have murky
sword hearts and wavering Dao Hearts, with their aptitudes truly
inferior to those from our generation. All it took was a single glance
for us to identify our Great Dao.\"

This sword strike would presumably cause significant commotion if it
landed in the Savage World close to the Sword Qi Great Wall.

For example, was Chen Qingdu going to leave the Sword Qi Great Wall and
challenge the entire Savage World for the first time after ten thousand
years?

\"Are you flaunting these trifling techniques in front of me?\" the tall
woman asked.

\"I wouldn\'t dare to,\" Chen Qingdu replied with a smile.

After saying this, the extremely old man --- the old great sword
immortal in the eyes of everyone at the Sword Qi Great Wall --- finally
rediscovered the spirit expected of him, saying, \"In any case, this
junior\'s sword techniques truly can\'t be regarded as low-level
anymore. I naturally wouldn\'t have stood a chance if I fought against
you ten thousand years ago, Senior, but if I get another opportunity to
travel against the flow of time and return to the past with my sword,
going to that battlefield\...\"

The tall woman seemingly didn\'t move, but her sword was already
hovering in the air, with its tip pointing at the seated Chen Qingdu.

Chen Qingdu remained upright and unfazed despite the blade being just
three inches from his head, and he formed a tiny speck of light at the
tip of the sword.

\"Others might not be able to deal with you at the Sword Qi Great Wall,
Chen Qingdu, but I\'m an exception,\" the tall woman said.

In the beginning, the sword techniques in the world split into four
lineages, with Chen Qingdu representing one at the Sword Qi Great Wall,
the heavenly masters representing one at Mount Longhu, the Daoist sword
immortals representing one at the Mystery Capital Temple, and the
Buddhists representing one at the Lotus Flower Buddhist Nation.

This was the extremely hidden inheritance of the sword technique
orthodoxies over the past ten thousand years, unknown to almost everyone
in the world. In fact, many sword immortals from the Northern Complete
Reed Continent were completely oblivious to this piece of history as
well, only knowing that there existed four immortal swords in the large
worlds.

Each of the four sword technique lineages had its own focus, but in
terms of destructive ability alone, the lineage represented by the Sword
Qi Great Wall\'s Chen Qingdu was undisputedly number one.

Chen Qingdu naturally wasn\'t afraid of the tall woman beside him,
someone who was far away from reaching the pinnacle of the Sword Dao.
Rather, he simply respected her.

This was a feeling of respect even greater than heaven and earth.

However, even though he didn\'t fear her, how could he truly not feel
worried at all? Just like she had mentioned, if they disregarded combat
power and cultivation base for the moment, Chen Qingdu\'s sword
techniques would never be the loftiest in front of her, regardless of
how lofty they were.

This remark from her was actually even more astonishing than her quip
for Chen Qingdu to piss off.

One had to realize that Chen Qingdu would legitimately be peerless at
the Sword Qi Great Wall unless the sages of the Three Teachings
personally visited the great wall with the tokens of their teachings.
Even the Daoist second disciple, armed with an immortal sword, would
stand no chance against Chen Qingdu.

Why did Stalactite Mountain exist? Why was there a Catch and Release
Pavilion at Stalactite Mountain? The Daoist second disciple had already
arrived at Stalactite Mountain back then, so why hadn\'t he taken
another step forward? He was someone who liked to battle against heaven
and earth, so why had he visited the Majestic World with an immortal
sword, yet returned to the Heavenly World without unleashing a single
sword strike?

After all, the Daoist second disciple\'s initial intention had been to
stand on the largest mountain seal in the world and engage in an all-out
battle against the Sword Qi Great Wall\'s Chen Qingdu! He wanted to
prove that not only was his Dao power profound, hence half of the White
Jade Capital being crafted by his hands, but his sword techniques had
also opened a new chapter for the world, establishing a fifth lineage of
sword technique orthodoxy!

In the end, however, the Daoist second disciple ultimately didn\'t
unleash a sword strike in his first and only visit to the Majestic
World.

The tall woman and Chen Qingdu both gazed into the distance, with the
former never sparing so much as a single glance for the latter.

Looking at the southern wall of the Sword Qi Great Wall, dust started to
rustle and fall from the strokes that made up the humongous characters.
Some of the earth immortal sword cultivators over there swayed back and
forth as a result, yet they didn\'t notice this at all.

\"Senior, this is enough, no?\" Chen Qingdu asked with a faint smile.

\"Are you aware that your inaction back then caused my master\'s
cultivation speed to become significantly slower? He should have
overcome the barriers of the Sword Qi Eighteen Stops Technique a long
time ago,\" the tall woman replied.

\"Is it a big deal for young people to progress more slowly and face
some additional hardships?\" Chen Qingdu asked. \"Progressing too fast,
ascending to the pinnacle too early, and having your company as well,
won\'t necessarily be a good thing for the world. Zuo You\'s comments to
Wei Jin about wielding a sword were absolutely spot on, and he should
explain this same concept to his junior brother.

\"If Chen Ping\'an is unable to truly become your master, then my
opinion is that he should walk even slower on the path of cultivation.
It\'s best that he\'s never able to wield a sword, and the slower he
reaches the pinnacle, the better. If he one day becomes fond of
unleashing sword strikes on a whim, then I\'ll truly regret ever letting
him enter the Lotus Flower Blessed Land to train and temper himself,
giving him an opportunity to rebuild his bridge of immortality.

\"If I remember correctly, that blessed land borders a small world that
was shattered by your emanating sword qi when you killed a genuine deity
back then, yes, Senior?\"

The tall woman didn\'t offer a response.

The tiny speck of light on the tip of her sword suddenly expanded to the
size of a fist, causing Chen Qingdu\'s hair to slowly float and sway in
the air. Some strands of his hair were severed, carried away by the
wind, and astonishingly sliced apart the frozen river of time with ease.

\"Chen Qingdu, I\'m giving you face, so you need to cherish this
leniency!\"

Her expression was cold, and the depths of her eyes housed a radiance
even brighter than the sun and the moon. \"My previous master from ten
thousand years ago felt pity for you people, the ants on the ground, and
you people accepted their pity. Ten thousand years later, I\'ve already
fallen significantly, while your Sword Dao has risen several notches.
However, this is no excuse for you to speak to me like this. The old
scholar was alarmed and anxious while taking me here, and he told me a
whole load of nonsense. This wasn\'t without reason.\"

Chen Qingdu smiled bitterly and asked, \"The old scholar didn\'t tell
you about the marriage proposal, did he? Are you squabbling with me
because of this? That old man is truly miserly! He\'s never willing to
accept even the smallest of losses!\"

He reached over and grabbed the orb of light on the sword tip,
continuing, \"I can\'t offer any more than this. Senior, you can feel
free to take this pure sword intent, and you can treat this as
compensation for me delaying the tempering of your sword.\"

The tall woman frowned and withdrew her sword, with the orb of light
instantly disappearing from its tip and slowly flowing through the
blade. She once again rested her hands on the hilt and leaned against
the sword like before.

Chen Qingdu turned around and asked with a smile, \"What do you think
when looking at the human world again?\"

\"It\'s too small,\" the tall woman replied coldly.

Chen Qingdu nodded and concurred, \"Indeed. Even the sun, the moon, and
the stars lost their radiance before your sword light in the past, or to
be more precise, it was your existence that created the dazzling
galaxies we see now.\"

The tens of thousands of stars in the sky were all floating corpses.

Chen Qingdu stood up, hunchbacked as if he were unable to withstand the
weight, unable to truly straighten his back throughout the past ten
thousand years.

Apart from a small number of great sword immortals, all of the sword
cultivators in the world had already become oblivious to the fact that,
looking back to the foundation, all of the sword techniques in the world
originated from the heavens. It was from those fundamental sword
techniques that tens of thousands of mystical abilities had sprouted,
struck by swords from the human world, and knocked to the ground
alongside the many deities. These mystical abilities were then collected
by the measly humans who had initially lived a life of struggle,
allowing them to cultivate and become immortals atop the mountains.

Initially, puppets raised as livestock by the many deities, lowly
puppets to offer incense, these measly humans gradually transformed
themselves and became rulers of the world. That was an extremely long
and arduous process.

Chen Qingdu was one of the first people to learn sword techniques in the
world, making him one of the most experienced founders of sword
cultivation and eventually allowing him to open the heavens with the
others. Why were swords the way they were, and why did sword cultivators
possess the greatest destructive ability, even surpassing heaven and
earth? These were the reasons.

During the late stages of that earth-shattering great war, however,
disagreement and conflict flared up among the humans, resulting in the
sword cultivators becoming prisoners who were exiled to the Sword Qi
Great Wall. At the same time, the demon tribe was also exiled to the
desolate land of barbarians.

Afterward, the Majestic World established the Confucian temple in the
Middle Earth Divine Continent and constructed the nine Mighty
Suppressing Pagodas that towered between heaven and earth. The young
Daoist priest riding atop the ox had traveled far to the Heavenly World,
building the White Jade Capital as his base. Meanwhile, Buddha had
trodden upon lotus flowers and allowed his divine light to grace the
vast lands.

Compared to this, was the extermination of flood dragons eight thousand
years ago not just a measly matter?

\"Why were you willing to choose that child, Senior?\" Chen Qingdu asked
in a quiet voice.

\"Qi Jingchun said that a one-in-a-million chance for some people is a
certainty, so he told me to give this a try,\" the tall woman replied.

\"Have you been disappointed again?\" Chen Qingdu asked.

The tall woman casually raised her sword and thrust forward, piercing
Chen Qinqdu\'s head. Golden light poured from her sword, appearing like
a small Milky Way hovering in the human world.

Chen Qingdu remained unfazed and unmoving, simply sighing with emotion
and remarking, \"Senior, your temper is still as bad as always.\"

\"It\'s already improved a lot,\" the tall woman replied.

Chen Qingdu shifted several steps to the side, avoiding her sword as he
smiled and asked, \"Then why did you split apart Stalactite Mountain
with a single slash before?\"

If it weren\'t for the Second Sage personally stopping her and appearing
at the Confucian temple in a rare display, then Stalactite Mountain
might have already collapsed and ceased to exist a long time ago.

\"Master was unconscious at the time, so I was able to act as I
pleased,\" the tall woman responded.

\"I would have never imagined that your master would be Chen Ping\'an,\"
Chen Qingdu said in helplessness. \"Thinking about this a bit more,
however, no one else seems to be more suitable. If it were anyone else,
it would be difficult to say whether they were the master or you were
the master.\"

Chen Qingdu suddenly chuckled and remarked, \"Just how divine was Qi
Jingchun\'s final move on the Go board?\"

The tall woman made a casual grabbing motion, drawing the golden light
from her sword and regathering it into a dazzling orb of light that
landed in her palm. She casually squeezed down, shattering the orb and
saying with a cold chuckle, \"Offering me sword intent? From you, Chen
Qingdu?\"

Chen Qingdu smiled and nodded in response.

The tall woman held her index finger and middle finger together, saying
with a faint smile, \"I\'ll extract it myself.\"

Specks of golden light started to materialize around the entire Sword Qi
Great Wall.

Chen Qingdu\'s expression changed slightly, and he heaved a soft sigh.
He could stop her if he truly wanted to, but the price to pay would be
far too great. In any case, he genuinely didn\'t understand her
temperament right now, so he could only use his trump card.

And thus, the young man in azure who had shaken away the effects of the
alcohol and was just about to arrive at the Ning Residence, suddenly
turned around and stumbled his way to the city wall, arriving beside the
tall woman.

There was puzzlement and delight on Chen Ping\'an\'s face as he
exclaimed in a soft voice, \"Big Sister Immortal?\"

The tall woman flicked her sleeve and caused the specks of golden light
to disperse, with the sword in her hand also vanishing from sight. She
turned around and smiled, pulling Chen Ping\'an into an embrace. Chen
Ping\'an was slightly flustered, and he spread his arms and turned
around to look at Chen Qingdu with an innocent expression. However, the
tall woman placed a hand on his head and pulled it forward.

Chen Qingdu closed his eyes and opened them again. No, he truly wasn\'t
seeing things.

The old great sword immortal reached up and massaged his temples. The
sword strike from before naturally hurt.

Chen Ping\'an flushed beet red. The tall woman had thankfully let go of
him already, and she bent down slightly to gaze at him. She smiled
widely and said in a gentle voice, \"Master, you have grown taller
again.\"

Seeing her reach over again, Chen Ping\'an hurriedly extended his hands
and lightly placed them on her arms, saying with a bitter smile, \"I\'m
dead meat if Ning Yao sees this.\"

There was a tragic expression on the tall woman\'s face as she clutched
her heart and asked, \"Are you not afraid of me dying of heartbreak
first?\"

There was a peculiar glimmer in Chen Ping\'an\'s eyes as he smiled
widely and gazed up at the sky. He raised his arm, pointing at the three
moons as he asked, \"Big Sister Immortal, I\'ve heard that this world
will be fine even if two of the three moons go missing. The cycle of the
four seasons will continue as normal, and the growth of all matters will
progress without impediment. That being the case, can we perhaps hack
one of the moons down to take home in the future? For example, we can
secretly place a moon inside the Lotus Root Blessed Land.\"

The tall woman looked up and replied with a faint smile, \"This isn\'t
possible right now, but it won\'t be difficult in the future.\"

Chen Qingdu was almost stifled to death as he stood beside them and
listened on.

The tall woman shot a sideways glance at him, and the old great sword
immortal took his leave upon seeing this.

Before leaving, however, Chen Qingdu said in a seemingly casual manner,
\"Rest assured, I won\'t tell Little Ning about this.\"

Chen Ping\'an turned around and said with a limpid gaze, \"I\'ll tell
her myself.\"

The tall woman continued to smile widely as she stood beside Chen
Ping\'an.

However, three words instantly exploded in Chen Qingdu\'s mind\'s lake,
\"Fuck off further.\"

Chen Qingdu clasped his hands behind his back as he slowly walked away.

Chen Ping\'an placed his hands inside his opposite sleeves as he walked
alongside the sword spirit.

He was extremely familiar with the river of time, so not only did he not
feel uncomfortable as he walked along it, but he even took to it like a
fish in water. His shuddering soul wasn\'t an issue at all. If he
didn\'t care about face, and if the sword spirit weren\'t present, he
could have easily sprinted along the river of time. After all, it was an
incredibly rare opportunity to enter a frozen river of time and reap its
corresponding benefits.

He turned around and asked with a smile, \"Why have you come here? Did
my master visit the Dragon Spring Prefecture?\"

The sword spirit nodded in response.

The old scholar was still worried about the safety of his closing
disciple at the Sword Qi Great Wall. Of course, he had also said frankly
to her that so be it if Chen Qingdu, that old geezer, didn\'t give him
face, but how could he not give Chen Ping\'an\'s master face? Was this
acceptable? Was this not the same as refusing to give face to his
disciple, who was also her master? Who gave Chen Qingdu such wanton
courage?

\"I initially thought I could only see you again after a few decades,\"
Chen Ping\'an said.

\"Regarding the matter of sharpening the sword, the Dragon Slaying
Platform at the Wind Snow Temple has already been completely consumed,\"
the sword spirit said with a smile. \"Rest assured, Master, I still
spoke reason with them. The Wind Snow Temple was absolutely terrified
when they noticed something amiss in the beginning, and none of the
sword cultivators guarding the Dragon Slaying Platform dared to act
rashly.

\"Afterward, a baby-faced little child secretly made his way to
Dragonspine Mountain and adhered to all of the etiquette, so I decided
to see him and teach him a sword technique as compensation for the Wind
Snow Temple. The little child was quite happy, especially since this
sword technique could help him advance his cultivation base.

\"Following this was Ruan Qiong\'s Dragon Slaying Platform, and he also
agreed to my request. It\'s because of this that the Great Li Empire is
especially choosing another site for the Dragon Spring Sword Sect now.
Ruan Qiong was fairly smart and didn\'t make any requests, so I became
happy and taught him a sword-forging technique. Otherwise, his dreams
and ambitions would have been nothing but just that with his crappy
cultivation base.

\"As for the Dragon Slaying Platform owned by True Martial Mountain\...
It\'s best to forget about that. It has far too many ties and
implications, and touching it could easily cause trouble. I don\'t mind
trouble at all, but it would have caused a huge headache for you,
Master.\"

There were some things she wasn\'t incapable of doing, but, as with Chen
Qingdu\'s concern about the master-subordinate dynamic involving her,
she was also worried about causing trouble for Chen Ping\'an.

Chen Qingdu had genuinely raised some good points, but she simply felt
like a measly Chen Qingdu didn\'t have the right to lecture her.

Chen Ping\'an held his hands inside his opposite sleeves and said in a
calm voice, \"There will eventually come a day when troubles are nothing
more than measly troubles for me.\"

The sword spirit was extremely happy.

There were many twists and turns, and she had initially thought that
their affinity would drift further and further apart, eventually leaving
a huge chasm between them. She wouldn\'t necessarily have felt
disappointed, but she would have somewhat felt that the situation was a
pity. In the end, however, he unexpectedly matched her ideal image and
became the perfect person to wield the sword.

\"What kind of person do you want to become if you are able to keep
ascending higher, Master?\" the sword spirit asked with a smile.

\"Someone who speaks with reason, and someone who acts with principle,\"
Chen Ping\'an replied without hesitation. \"And when I launch a sword
strike beyond the heavens and throw a punch toward the earth, all of the
martial artists in the world will feel like divine might has been
unleashed.\"

[]{#chapter-57.xhtml}

# Chapter 589: (1): Child in the Corner

Sword of Coming

\"Why must you live for the sake of other people?\" the sword spirit
asked with a sigh.

When it came to practicing martial arts and training fist techniques,
Cui Cheng\'s influence on Chen Ping\'an was unfathomably big.

Half of his remark just then clearly resonated with the deceased Cui
Cheng. It was a solemn promise, one that linked the two of them despite
the barrier of life and death.

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and explained, \"This isn\'t the case.
I\'ve always been living for myself, but I\'ll inevitably develop
relationships and find things I care about as I walk along this path.
Those whom I respect should live eternally in my heart, and even if the
world forgets them, they\'ll still live on in my memory. If the
opportunity arises, I\'ll even strive to reawaken the world\'s memory of
these people.\"

The sword spirit fell deep into thought, recalling some matters from
long, long ago.

After walking for a while, Chen Ping\'an turned around and retraced his
steps.

The sword spirit also turned around and retraced her steps.

This was the path of no wrong that Chen Ping\'an pursued, preventing the
sword spirit from traveling too broadly along the river of time and
potentially triggering unexpected consequences.

There were far too many surprises and accidents in the world, with
people powerless to stop them. They could only accept their fates.

But at the very least, Chen Ping\'an would avoid causing too many
surprises and accidents due to his own carelessness.

Mr. Qi knew Chen Ping\'an the best, yet he had already passed away
because of Chen Ping\'an.

The sword spirit and Chen Ping\'an sat on the parapet, just like they
had sat on the golden arch bridge in the past.

\"Are you about to leave?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

\"I can stay, but the old scholar who\'s waiting painfully at Stalactite
Mountain might have to visit the Confucian temple to apologize,\" the
sword spirit replied.

\"A brief parting is no issue, but please don\'t leave without ever
returning again. I might be able to stand this, but I\'ll inevitably
feel very distressed. Yet, I won\'t be able to say anything, and I can
only suffer distress in silence,\" Chen Ping\'an said.

\"Master, you and I shall share life and death for eternity,\" the sword
spirit said with a smile.

Chen Ping\'an turned around and extended a palm.

The sword spirit raised her hand, not high-fiving Chen Ping\'an, but
instead holding his hand and giving it a gentle shake. \"This is the
second promise between us.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and nodded. \"I\'ll definitely honor my promises.\"

The sword spirit retracted her hand and lightly tapped her knees, gazing
at the barren lands of the Savage World as she said with a cold chuckle,
\"There appear to be a few undying old friends still.\"

\"Then I\'ll take extra caution,\" Chen Ping\'an said.

\"If I appear, then these sneaky primordial beings won\'t dare to kill
you. At most, they\'ll only dare to shatter your bridge of immortality
again, forcing you to step onto an ancient path with me,\" the sword
spirit said.

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and replied, \"Regardless of what I\'ll
think in the future and whether I\'ll change my mind or not, I most
definitely won\'t leave at this moment.\"

\"Okay, okay,\" the sword spirit said with a smile.

\"Do you know what\'s most impressive about me?\" Chen Ping\'an suddenly
asked, smiling.

The sword spirit thought about this for a moment before replying, \"You
dare to make trade-offs.\"

For example, Chen Ping\'an had made a trade-off between her and Ning Yao
when he had unleashed a sword strike toward Tassel Mountain in the old
scholar\'s picture scroll.

If he had chosen incorrectly, then things would have progressed in a
drastically different direction.

A person who acted obsequiously toward so-called power and influence
didn\'t deserve to unleash a sword strike toward the heavens in her
stead.

Ten thousand years had passed, and how many people in the human world
had buckled at the knees and gone weak in the back? Countless. These
people truly needed to take a look at how their ancestors had struggled
through difficult times and climbed to greater heights with their
swords, courting death for the sake of creating a better world for
future generations.

Following the heroic death of this generation, however, the radiance of
humanity --- which was vastly different from that of divinity --- also
started to change. More accurately, it was covered.

The gods and deities had crafted these ants in the past, and they were
regarded as ants because of their innate shortcomings, which pertained
to more than just their short lifespan. It was precisely because of
these shortcomings that the lofty gods in the heavens had viewed the
humans as measly ants who could never rebel, only being able to offer
endless amounts of incense to them for all eternity. Their lives were
completely worthless.

At that time, some of the lofty gods peering down at the world had
noticed the transformations in the humans. However, they were reaping
unimaginable benefits through forming and tempering their godly bodies
using incense offerings from the human world, something that was linked
to the foundation of their longevity, so some of the gods turned a blind
eye to changes in the human world.

They wanted to maintain the status quo and continue to draw on the
bottomless source of power. Meanwhile, some of the gods thought nothing
of this transformation, convinced that they could crush these measly
ants with ease if they wanted to.

Reality had ultimately proven otherwise, propelled by many so-called
coincidental inevitabilities. For example, the conflict between fire and
water.

Most unexpected of all was the fact that her previous master, as well as
a few deities, had been willing to regard a small handful of people as
genuinely like-minded individuals.

That was the catalyst behind the growth of sword techniques and a myriad
of other techniques in the human world.

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and said in a soft voice, \"My heart is
free.\"

He then smiled and continued, \"People didn\'t say this in the past
because they had never even considered it before.\"

She then repeated the four words spoken by Chen Ping\'an.

\"My heart is free,\" she murmured.

------------

The old great sword immortal tossed Chen Ping\'an back inside the city.
Nalan Yexing was already waiting at the entrance, and the two of them
entered the Ning Residence together, with Nalan Yexing asking in a quiet
voice, \"Did the old great sword immortal drag you over?\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded in response, not saying anything else.

Nalan Yexing hadn\'t been especially worried to begin with, and he felt
even more at ease after learning that it was indeed the old great sword
immortal\'s doing.

However, Chen Ping\'an used his mind\'s lake to say, \"Grandpa Nalan,
can you please pass on a message to Grandma Bai? I have some matters to
discuss with her at the Minute Small World.\"

\"A meeting with Young Mistress?\" Nalan Yexing asked with a serious
expression.

\"Yes, together,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a smile.

The four of them convened at the training ground.

Chen Ping\'an roughly explained the situation regarding the sword
spirit, only giving a general overview of the current situation and not
touching upon the more fundamental matters.

Nalan Yexing and Bai Lianshuang exchanged glances with each other as if
they were listening to something unfathomable.

A true spirit nurtured and born from an immortal sword?

One of the four legendary immortal swords that had possessed the
greatest destructive power ten thousand years ago? A true spirit that
could be regarded as an old friend of Old Great Sword Immortal Chen
Qingdu?

Ning Yao fared okay, with her expression remaining calm and unfazed.

A ripple appeared at the training ground, from which a tall woman in
white stepped out and stood beside Chen Ping\'an. She looked around
before eventually settling her gaze on Ning Yao.

Ning Yao raised an eyebrow.

\"Rest assured, I\'m going to leave very soon,\" the sword spirit said
with a smile.

\"And so what if you don\'t leave?\" Ning Yao asked.

The sword spirit looked at Ning Yao\'s glabella and remarked with a
faint smile, \"That\'s fairly interesting. You\'re worthy of my
master.\"

Chen Ping\'an knew that things were about to go south, and sure enough,
Ning Yao chuckled coldly and said, \"And would I be unworthy if I
didn\'t possess that? Does your opinion matter regarding whether I\'m
worthy or not?\"

Beads of sweat formed on Nalan Yexing\'s forehead. Bai Lianshuang was
also tense with anxiety.

The sword spirit smiled and replied, \"No, it doesn\'t matter at all.
Happy?\"

Ning Yao replied with a cold chuckle.

Chen Ping\'an looked down and kept quiet, unable to use any of his
abilities at this moment. Even speaking a single word would be wrong.

\"Alright, I\'m going to leave now,\" the sword spirit said with a yawn.

Her figure, which was already shimmering and unstable to begin with,
gradually faded away, eventually breaking through the sky of the Sword
Qi Great Wall under Chen Qingdu\'s escort. After arriving at the
Majestic World, the old scholar helped to conceal her aura as they
traveled to the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.

As they traveled, the old scholar smiled and asked, \"How was it?\"

\"She\'s not exactly a very beautiful girl,\" the sword spirit replied.

The old scholar rubbed his hands together and said with an awkward
expression, \"I wasn\'t asking about that.\"

\"Oh, you were asking about Chen Qingdu? It\'s been ten thousand years,
so our brief chat and reminiscence went quite well,\" the tall woman
responded.

The old scholar scrunched up his face, feeling like now was not a
suitable time to ask too many questions.

The sword spirit glanced down at Stalactite Mountain and said casually,
\"Chen Qingdu has agreed to let one more person through, to make a total
of three people. You can satisfy the Confucian temple\'s request now.\"

\"What? Senior, your lofty status was only worth one additional
person?!\" the old scholar fumed. \"Is Chen Qingdu trying to revolt?!
What utter impudence!\"

\"I can instruct Chen Qingdu not to let a single person through. That
way, my lofty status will be worth four people, no?\" the sword spirit
replied.

\"How can I possibly ask you to travel to the Sword Qi Great Wall again,
Senior?\" the old scholar said in a righteous voice. \"Three people is
also fine. Chen Qingdu might be stingy, but righteous scholars like me
still need to uphold propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of
shame.\"

The sword spirit looked down again, glancing at the Flood Dragon Trench.
The old scholar also glanced down, and he huffed, \"I say we forget
about them. There are only some small fry left.\"

A streak of white light and a puff of azure smoke disappeared in a
flash, instantly traveling thousands of kilometers on the way from
Stalactite Mountain to the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. To say
nothing of sword immortals soaring through the skies on their swords,
even intercontinental messenger flying swords couldn\'t travel at such
an astonishing speed.

The sword spirit raised a hand and moved her fingers slightly.

The old scholar craned his neck and glanced over, feeling slightly
uneasy as he asked in an uncertain voice, \"What are you doing?\"

\"Recording things,\" the sword spirit replied in an apathetic voice.

\"Recording what?\" the old scholar asked carefully. \"Recording the
crimes of Lu Chen? Or recording the crimes of that stinky Daoist priest
from the Observing Dao Temple?\"

\"Recording how many times you call me \'Senior,\'\" the sword spirit
replied with a faint smile.

\"How could you do that?\" the old scholar exclaimed in a pained voice.
\"I\'m not very old, but have I ever cared about other old geezers
referring to me as an old scholar? Referring to others as \'Senior\' is
out of respect, while referring to me as an old scholar or impoverished
scholar is something of a joke. How many people respectfully refer to me
as the Scholarly Sage? Who can I vent my pain and frustration to\...?\"

The sword spirit retracted her hand and glanced down at the sect located
in the sea, the one with both a deity statue representing a formal rain
god and a divine general statue representing an official of the Heavenly
Court\'s Northern Heavenly Gate, asking, \"How has Bai Ze chosen?\"

The old scholar smiled and replied, \"He made a good choice, saying that
he wanted to wait for a while longer.\"

\"And the resulting merit from this choice?\" the sword spirit asked.

\"It won\'t count. How can it count, and who can it count towards? He\'s
no longer with us,\" the old scholar said with a shake of his head.

\"Scholars are quite good at keeping tabs and accounts,\" the sword
spirit commented with a snicker.

The old scholar nodded and concurred, \"You\'re right about that. It\'s
quite mentally tiring, to be honest with you.\"

The sword spirit turned around and said, \"No, something\'s not right.\"

The old scholar huffed and said, \"It was too risky for you to go to the
Sword Qi Great Wall. I suggested that I could make a promise with my
life, but those bloody criminals at the Confucian temple refused to
accept my proposal, no matter what. As a result, a portion of merit that
should have belonged to my closing disciple was used up.

\"There are few generous scholars belonging to the lineage of the Second
Sage, and all of them are as miserly as can be. Can stingy sages be
regarded as true sages? If my divine statue were still enshrined at the
Confucian temple, standing there in boredom with the old geezers, then I
would have expounded some reason to the crappy lineage of the Second
Sage a long time ago.

\"I guess this is all my fault. Back when I was still respected and
revered, those at the Confucian schools and academies tried everything
they could to invite me over to give lectures. However, I was
thin-skinned and liked to put on airs, so I didn\'t give anywhere near
as many lectures as I should have. Otherwise, if I had visited more of
those schools and academies back then, Little Ping\'an would have many
more seniors who weren\'t technically senior brothers, but perhaps even
better than senior brothers.\"

The sword spirit was surprisingly unfazed about the old scholar using up
her master\'s merit. It appeared as if this action suited her tastes.

As for the old scholar\'s remark about making a promise with his life,
she couldn\'t help but feel embarrassed by his shamelessness. The
impoverished scholar was unlike a human, unlike a ghost, and unlike a
deity, and was he not aware of this awkward situation himself? Who in
the Majestic World was capable of killing him now?

The Paramount Sage definitely wouldn\'t make a move, and the same was
true for the Etiquette Sage. Meanwhile, the battle between the Second
Sage and the Scholarly Sage only pertained to their Great Dao, and it
had absolutely nothing to do with any private grievances.

The old scholar nodded to himself and continued, \"It would have been a
waste not to use this merit, and the earlier it\'s used up, the better,
lest my disciple feel upset after learning of its existence. Being
entangled with this merit wasn\'t a good thing to begin with. I\'m not
trying to boast or anything, but those belonging to my lineage are all
ambitious and knowledgeable, possessing exemplary characters and
displaying great generosity.

\"Little Ping\'an has visited three continents and traveled far and
wide, yet he hasn\'t visited a single Confucian academy. This is a clear
reflection of his attitude toward our scholarly temples, schools, and
academies. He feels frustration and anger in his heart, and I view this
as a very good thing. This is the way it should be.\"

\"What about Cui Chan?\" the sword spirit asked with a smile.

\"Have I ever taken this person as my disciple before? I only recall
having a grand-disciple by the name of Cui Dongshan,\" the old scholar
replied with a baffled expression.

\"I feel like Cui Chan\'s demeanor is the closest to those human
ancestors,\" the sword spirit stated.

\"Who said it wasn\'t?\" the old scholar replied with an adrift look.

He paused for a moment before murmuring, \"I also made mistakes, but
it\'s a shame that I no longer have the opportunity to right my wrongs.
This is life. The ability to identify mistakes and make positive changes
is a great virtue; the ability to identify mistakes but not have the
opportunity to make changes is a great regret, a great pain.\"

However, the old scholar quickly wiped away the dark fog in his mind,
tugging at his beard as he smiled. The past couldn\'t be chased, but the
future could be pursued. Indeed, hadn\'t he found himself a closing
disciple?

Senior? What senior?

He was indeed younger, but the two of them possessed the same seniority.

[]{#chapter-58.xhtml}

# Chapter 589: (2): Child in the Corner

Sword of Coming

It was evening, and Die Zhang couldn\'t help but feel slightly puzzled
as she stood in the wine shop. Chen Ping\'an had just left in the
morning, so why was he already back for more wine?

Business was quite good, and to say nothing of empty tables, there
wasn\'t even an empty chair at the wine spot. This caused Chen
Ping\'an\'s mood to improve as he purchased wine.

Die Zhang handed over a pot of the cheapest wine and asked, \"What\'s
this all about?\"

\"I encountered some matters, and Ning Yao told me she wasn\'t angry.
She adamantly stated that she wasn\'t angry, but I have a nagging
feeling that this isn\'t the case,\" Chen Ping\'an replied in
helplessness.

Die Zhang didn\'t take pleasure in his misfortune, and she consoled him
by saying, \"Ning Yao always speaks frankly, so she definitely isn\'t
angry if she says so. You\'re overthinking things.\"

\"Shopkeeper, am I a better judge of people, or are you a better judge
of people?\" Chen Ping\'an replied in a gloomy voice.

Die Zhang could feel at ease and take pleasure in Chen Ping\'an\'s
misfortune now, and she replied, \"Then, Second Shopkeeper, you can
drink some more wine. Our wine shop will provide as much wine as you
want, and as per the rules, regular customers can\'t drink on credit
unless they\'ve just broken through.\"

Chen Ping\'an squatted on the side of the street with a pot of wine and
a dish of pickled vegetables, and squatting beside him was an alcoholic
sword cultivator who often visited the wine shop, the type who would die
if he didn\'t drink for a single day. He was at the Dragon Gate Tier,
and his name was Han Rong. Just like Chen Ping\'an, he would only drink
Bamboo Sea Small World Wine when he visited, the cheapest wine at one
snowflake coin per pot.

At first, Chen Ping\'an told Die Zhang that attracting this type of
customer was most important and that treating them well was crucial,
leaving her a little baffled. Seeing this, Chen Ping\'an was left with
no option but to patiently explain the reason. The friends of alcoholics
were generally alcoholics as well, and these alcoholics liked to always
drink at the same place.

Compared to those people who would occasionally drink a pot of fine wine
by themselves, these alcoholics, who would feel a strong urge to return
and order another pot of wine immediately after leaving, were the best
customers to attract. Recurring business was always better than one-off
transactions.

At the time, Die Zhang had surprisingly recorded these words in the
accounts book, regarding them as priceless words of wisdom, which made
Chen Ping\'an extremely anxious. The shopkeeper was truly not cut out
for doing business. In fact, how had she managed to run her
miscellaneous shop for more than ten years? Yet, he had only worked as a
wandering merchant for several years. Perhaps he genuinely had some
aptitude when it came to doing business?

Han Rong smiled and asked, \"Second Shopkeeper, are you drinking to
drown your sorrows? What happened? Were you kicked out of home for being
too touchy? It\'s okay. I\'m experienced with women, so let me teach you
a brilliant tactic. How about this, you can treat this as payment for
the wine. This is a great deal for you!\"

Chen Ping\'an ate some pickled vegetables and took a sip of wine,
replying in a leisurely voice, \"Listening to your suggestions will
truly cause me to become irritated and shameless. In any case, I\'m
simply here to drink and relax, and are we not aware of who should be
teaching whom? What did Brother Han write on the safety tablet on the
wall? Have you forgotten after drinking so much?

\"There\'s something I don\'t understand. There are so many safety
tablets in the wine shop, but only a single one is hanging with its name
side facing the wall. Say, Brother Han, are you treating this wine shop
as a place to confess? Will that young lady dare to visit our wine shop
to drink in the future? You need to pay double for today\'s wine.\"

\"Don\'t haggle with me, okay? Brothers speaking about money is a
surefire way to hurt the relationship,\" Han Rong said.

He slowly took a swig of wine before sighing with emotion and remarking,
\"There are countless single men here, but there are few men as loyal
and lovestruck as I am. If I truly succeed in the future and end up with
that beautiful woman, then I\'ll regard it as your wine shop bestowing
blessings on me. I\'ll definitely visit to return the favor at that
time, and I\'ll directly order two pots of wine that cost five snowflake
coins each.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and said, \"Easy done. I\'ll even throw in an extra
pot of wine for free at that time.\"

\"For real?\" Han Rong asked.

Chen Ping\'an nodded and replied, \"Yes, but the type that costs one
snowflake coin each.\"

\"That\'s far too casual,\" Han Rong exclaimed in disappointment.
\"Second Shopkeeper is young and successful, having outstanding
achievements and being regarded as a prodigy among prodigies in the
younger generation\...\"

\"Hold it right there, Brother Han. Are you going to compensate me if I
throw up my wine?\" Chen Ping\'an asked in mock anger.

Die Zhang was completely won over by Chen Ping\'an\'s business nous as
she stood in the distance and watched the second shopkeeper enjoy a
spirited conversation with the customer.

Chen Ping\'an had also said before that he genuinely liked to drink at
the Sword Qi Great Wall. This was because at the Majestic World, many
wine shops would discriminate based on the status of the customers, with
powerful individuals receiving more wine and less powerful individuals
receiving less wine.

Han Rong chuckled giddily, suddenly recalling a matter and saying,
\"Second Shopkeeper, you\'ve read a lot of books, so can you think of a
few cringey poems? They don\'t need to be good poems, and something like
\'dreaming that the Azure God visits to pour me wine\' will do. The
young lady whom I like is somehow fond of these poems, so you need to
help your brother out with this. Regardless of whether this works out or
not, I promise that I\'ll drag an entire table of alcoholics over as
thanks. I\'ll adopt your surname if we don\'t finish ten pots of wine.\"

\"Do you think pretentious poems are like wine, served bowl after bowl
as long as one is rich? Sorry, but you can keep dreaming.\" Chen
Ping\'an shook his head and continued, \"In any case, I\'m not married
yet, so I\'m not accepting any sons.\"

Han Rong raised his wine bowl and said, \"Us brothers have a good
relationship, so why don\'t we take a swig of wine first? You should at
least come up with one poem for your brother, and even one or two lines
will suffice. If I don\'t become your son, can I become your grandson
instead?\"

Chen Ping\'an raised his wine bowl and replied, \"How about I mull over
this afterward? However, to be completely honest with you, whether or
not I gain inspiration to compose a poem depends entirely on whether I
have enough wine to drink or not.\"

Han Rong immediately turned around and shouted to Die Zhang,
\"Shopkeeper, I\'ll grab the bill for Second Shopkeeper\'s pot of
wine!\"

Die Zhang nodded in response, and she felt that if Chen Ping\'an were to
focus on selling wine, he could expand the wine shop to the city wall in
just a few years\' time.

A tall and slender woman gracefully walked over, arriving in front of
the second shopkeeper, who was currently explaining the meaning of
\"fleeting time\" to Han Rong. She smiled and asked, \"May I please
trouble Young Master Chen for a brief moment?\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and nodded in response, turning around and saying
to Han Rong, \"It\'s not important if you don\'t understand, and the
most important thing is that she understands.\"

He then walked along the street with the young woman and said with a
smile, \"Thank you for reaching out, Miss Yu.\"

The young woman was none other than Yu Qia, who had left Fan Dache
completely heartbroken.

Yu Qia\'s expression was slightly unnatural, but it wasn\'t long before
she said slowly in a soft and gentle voice, \"I heard about the events
that night, and even though I\'m no longer in a relationship with Fan
Dache, I still have to apologize to you, Young Master Chen. After all,
this happened because of me, and I caused you to suffer.

\"Perhaps it isn\'t suitable for me to say this, and you might even feel
like my apology is shallow and insincere. No matter what, I still hope
that you can sympathize with Fan Dache. He\'s truly a very good person,
and I\'m the one who has wronged him.\"

\"I wouldn\'t have tolerated a scolding from Fan Dache if he weren\'t a
good person,\" Chen Ping\'an said. \"Who hasn\'t become drunk before? If
a man murmurs a woman\'s name when he\'s drunk, then he definitely has
sincere feelings for that woman. As for scolding others when they\'re
drunk? Their words shouldn\'t be taken seriously at all.\"

Yu Qia curtsied and said, \"Thank you, Young Master Chen. Then I won\'t
disturb you and your friend anymore.\"

Following Yu Qia\'s departure, Chen Ping\'an returned to the wine shop
and squatted down, continuing to drink by himself. Han Rong had already
left, and he naturally hadn\'t forgotten to pay for Chen Ping\'an\'s
wine.

\"What was that all about?\" Die Zhang shuffled over and asked.

\"Yu Qia came to apologize for Fan Dache\'s outburst,\" Chen Ping\'an
explained with a smile.

Die Zhang pursed her lips before saying, \"And that\'s only because
she\'s afraid of offending Chen Sanqiu, the leader among the group of
young masters that includes Fan Dache and the others. If Chen Sanqiu
truly criticizes Yu Qia and gives her a bad reputation, then she
doesn\'t need to dream about hanging out with them in the future.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and didn\'t say anything.

Things naturally weren\'t so simple.

\"Why don\'t we make a bet about whether Fan Dache will appear here or
not?\" Chen Ping\'an suddenly suggested.

\"I wager that he\'ll appear,\" Die Zhang said with a nod.

Chen Ping\'an smiled and was just about to nod in confirmation.

Seeing this, Die Zhang changed her mind and said, \"Actually, forget
about the bet.\"

Chen Ping\'an had an expression of regret, and Die Zhang felt like she
had made the correct decision to pull out of the bet. Unexpectedly,
however, Fan Dache turned up after less than fifteen minutes.

Die Zhang rolled her eyes.

Fan Dache was extremely hesitant after he arrived at the wine shop, but
in the end, he still purchased a pot of wine and squatted down beside
Chen Ping\'an.

Chen Ping\'an smiled and said, \"Miss Yu said that she was the one who
has done wrong by you.\"

Fan Dache lowered his head, and tears immediately streamed down his
cheeks. He didn\'t drink, and he held his wine bowl just like that.

Chen Ping\'an raised his wine bowl and lightly touched it against the
white bowl in Fan Dache\'s hand, saying, \"Don\'t get too hung up on
this, so much so that you yearn for war to start tomorrow, feeling like
dying on the battlefield to the south of the Sword Qi Great Wall is a
form of liberation.\"

Fan Dache took a large swig of wine and asked, \"How did you know?\"
