# Chapter 595: (1): The Top Ten Sword Immortals of the Sword Qi Great Wall

Sword of Coming

On this day, Fan Dache\'s entire body was riddled with small gashes, and
he was drinking at the wine shop with a dazed expression.

Chen Sanqiu wasn\'t in much better condition.

The five of them had joined forces to battle Nalan Yexing in the Minute
Small World on the Ning Residence\'s training grounds, but aside from
Chen Ping\'an, the four others, namely Chen Sanqiu, Yan Zhuo, Dong
Huafu, and Fan Dache, had all been made to suffer for their decision to
challenge the old sword immortal.

Fatty Yan had returned home to continue his training, while Dong Huafu
had gone somewhere to wander around on a shopping spree. Everything
would be put on Yan Zhuo and Chen Sanqiu\'s tab, so he didn\'t have to
worry about budgetary restrictions.

\"Sanqiu, I\'m suddenly a little afraid to become a Golden Core Tier
swordsman,\" Fan Dache admitted. \"Once I reach the Golden Core Tier, I
won\'t have any guardian swordsmen anymore.\"

\"That\'s *your* problem,\" Chen Sanqiu said with a grin. \"I come from
a wealthy clan, so even after I reach the Golden Core Tier, I\'ll still
have swordsmen from my clan to protect me on the battlefield. What a
reassuring thought that is! I should have a drink to that.\"

And so he did, raising his cup to take a sip of wine.

At this point, Chen Sanqiu had realized that when dealing with a friend
like Fan Dache, the direct and straightforward approach was always the
best, and that there was no need to be overly considerate of Fan
Dache\'s feelings.

\"Chen Ping\'an has agreed for me to accompany all of you onto the
battlefield during the next battle, so he\'s going to be my guardian
swordsman,\" Fan Dache declared with a grin of his own.

Even if Fan Dache were a complete fool, Chen Ping\'an\'s intentions
would\'ve still become abundantly clear to him after so many sparring
and training sessions together. On one hand, he was trying to enhance
Fan Dache\'s cultivation base, but he also had a secondary objective,
which was to hone everyone\'s cohesion and teamwork as a unit. Ideally,
they would all survive the next battle and slay many demons in the
process.

Chen Sanqiu raised his bowl of wine, then gently touched it to Fan
Dache\'s as he remarked, \"You\'re a lucky man, Fan Dache. Not everyone
gets to have Chen Ping\'an as their guardian swordsman.\"

Fan Dache poured himself another bowl of wine as he mused, \"If I think
about it that way, I\'m suddenly looking forward to becoming a Golden
Core Tier swordsman again. Right now, Chen Ping\'an is a fifth tier
cultivator, and he just so happened to make his breakthrough on the
Sword Qi Great Wall, so why isn\'t he here to celebrate with us?\"

\"He\'s probably too embarrassed to make a fuss,\" Chen Sanqiu chuckled.
\"After all, he still hasn\'t even reached the Abode Tier yet.\"

\"He\'s not one to get embarrassed over something like that,\" Fan Dache
disagreed with a shake of his head.

Earlier, when they were drinking together here, Chen Ping\'an had stood
up, raised a toast to everyone, and delivered an address, encouraging
everyone to make breakthroughs of their own. He told them not to be shy
about it, and that they had no excuse not to make breakthroughs,
considering they were able to enjoy the cheapest wine and the finest
yangchun noodles on the Sword Qi Great Wall, in addition to free pickled
vegetables.

According to him, they were unworthy of drinking his wine if they
couldn\'t make breakthroughs in their cultivation, and he declared that
he was going to raise his wine prices for those who took too long to
make breakthroughs.

At the time, all of the patrons of the wine shop had fallen into a
bewildered silence. They felt like something wasn\'t right, but at the
same time, it didn\'t really feel worth it to confront Chen Ping\'an
over his provocative remarks.

However, what was much more infuriating to everyone was the betting
station that had been arranged to take bets on whether Dong Huafu would
take the initiative to treat everyone. In the end, almost everyone lost.
In the beginning, no one felt particularly disgruntled by this outcome.
After all, both the second shopkeeper and Yan Zhuo had also suffered
heavy losses along with everyone else.

The only one who had officially won money on the bet was Pang Yuanji,
and after the event, he came to drink at the wine shop with a rather
smug grin. That was when some people began to realize that they had been
duped. Furthermore, the bookmaker of the betting station was none other
than the Nascent Tier old fart who had inexplicably written a poem
earlier.

It was an extremely familiar scam!

Thus, Chen Ping\'an didn\'t accompany Chen Sanqiu and Fan Dache to the
shop to drink. Instead, he paid a visit to the Sword Qi Great Wall.

After splitting the spoils, Chen Ping\'an had made a profit of quite a
few grain rain coins. On the way to the Sword Qi Great Wall, he decided
that he had to find a new bookmaker next time. For example, Sword
Immortal Tao Wen seemed like a very honest and trustworthy guy.

Instead of traveling directly to Zuo You using his talismanic boat, Chen
Ping\'an chose to walk an extra few dozen kilometers.

Along the way, he encountered a bunch of children of the Lower Five
Tiers practicing sword techniques under the tutelage of a Nascent Tier
swordsman. It wasn\'t considered taboo to spectate this type of
training, so Chen Ping\'an sat down atop the city wall to watch from
afar.

There was also a group of children arguing nearby, seemingly debating
how many Lin Junbis it would take to defeat a single shopkeeper.

All of the children who were able to play on top of the Sword Qi Great
Wall had to be remarkable in some way, either coming from affluent clans
or possessing an innate aptitude for swordsmanship.

The children from places like Yanchi Alley and Spirit Rhino Alley would
never come here. The city was too far away from the Sword Qi Great Wall,
and it was simply too long a journey for the average child to make on
foot. Additionally, there was very heavy sword intent and immense sword
qi on the Sword Qi Great Wall, creating an unforgiving, inhospitable
environment for children with frail constitutions. Such was life. Some
were born with everything, while others found themselves in worse and
worse situations as they progressed through life.

One of the children spotted Chen Ping\'an, and he immediately yelled,
\"You tell them, Second Shopkeeper! Surely you can beat up five Lin
Junbis with just a single hand! If you say yes, then you\'ll be my
friend! My name is Yuan Zaohua!\"

Chen Ping\'an merely waved a dismissive hand in his direction,
indicating for him to go away.

The boy refused to give up, lowering his expectations a little as he
asked, \"How about three? Surely you can deal with three!\"

\"I wouldn\'t know. I\'ve never fought him before,\" Chen Ping\'an
replied with a smile.

\"How about I issue an official challenge for you?\" Yuan Zaohua
offered. \"I\'ll tell everyone that you can beat up Lin Junbi, Yan Lü,
and Jiang Guancheng with just one hand!\"

Chen Ping\'an stood up and made his way over to the boy. Only up close
did he discover, to his surprise, that it was actually a girl, but she
was a tomboy through and through.

He gave her a light kick on the backside as he scoffed, \"Get outta
here! Do you even know how to write? How is an illiterate little brat
like you going to write an official challenge?\"

\"Of course I know how to write! I\'m way smarter than you!\" Yuan
Zaohua snapped with an indignant expression.

\"Alright, in that case, how do you write Chen Ping\'an?\" Chen Ping\'an
asked with a smile.

\"I know how to write your name, but I\'m not going to!\" Yuan Zaohua
replied. \"You must\'ve forgotten how to write your own name, and you
want to trick me into teaching you, right? You\'re not fooling me that
easily!\"

Clearly, she was the leader of this group of children, and all of the
other kids were eager to back her up.

Chen Ping\'an sat down facing the city in the north, then pulled out a
bamboo leaf before using it as a makeshift instrument to play a tune.

\"That doesn\'t sound good at all!\" Yuan Zaohua scoffed disdainfully.

All of the other children could only nod in agreement.

Chen Ping\'an merely ignored her, and that left her feeling a little
disappointed. He continued to sit in silence, gently patting his own
knee in an absentminded fashion as he looked out at the distant city.

All of a sudden, Chen Ping\'an smiled and asked, \"Who do you all think
are the current ten most powerful sword immortals? It doesn\'t have to
be in order.\"

\"What\'s the point if you don\'t assign an order to them?\" Yuan Zaohua
scoffed with a roll of her eyes. \"That would be just saying a bunch of
names with no purpose.\"

Chen Ping\'an stood up and prepared to depart.

\"Chen Ping\'an, I\'ll tell you my top ten if you give me a folding
fan,\" Yuan Zaohua negotiated as she extended a hand toward him.

Chen Ping\'an chuckled. \"Well, aren\'t you a tricky little customer!\"

Yuan Zaohua spread her arms open wide to block Chen Ping\'an\'s path,
and she insisted with a stubborn expression, \"Hurry up! You have to
give me a folding fan with the best calligraphy and the most characters
on it!\"

Chen Ping\'an was initially planning to ignore her, but a thought then
suddenly occurred to him, and he sat down as he prompted, \"Go ahead and
tell me your top ten first. I\'ll decide whether I want to give you a
folding fan afterward.\"

\"The old great sword immortal, Dong Sangeng, A\'Liang, Lord Hidden
Official, Chen Xi, Qi Tingji, Zuo You, Nalan Shaowei, the old deaf guy,
and Lu Zhi! That\'s my top ten!\" Yuan Zaohua declared, rattling off the
entire list of names in a single breath. \"Give me the folding fan!\"

Chen Ping\'an rose to his feet again, and he really did pick out a jade
bamboo folding fan from his minimization treasure before slapping it
down onto Yuan Zaohua\'s hand.

\"Make sure you don\'t lose it; this thing\'s worth quite a bit of
money.\"

Yuan Zaohua opened the folding fan with a gleeful expression, but there
weren\'t many characters on it, and she barely recognized any of them.

\"Gimme another one! I want one with more characters on it!\" she
demanded.

Chen Ping\'an gave her another light kick on the backside as he
chuckled, \"I suggest you don\'t push your luck! Otherwise, I\'m going
to change my mind.\"

Yuan Zaohua closed the folding fan and tucked it behind herself, then
extended her other hand toward Chen Ping\'an as she declared, \"In that
case, I\'ll buy the folding fan with the most number of characters from
you!\"

\"How\'re you going to pay for it?\" Chen Ping\'an asked with an amused
smile.

\"The old great sword immortal, Dong Sangeng, A\'Liang, Lord Hidden
Official, Chen Xi, Qi Tingji, Zuo You, Nalan Shaowei, the old deaf guy,
and Lu Zhi,\" she repeated with a serious expression. \"From now on,
I\'ll add Chen Ping\'an to my list! You will be the eleventh most
powerful sword immortal on our Sword Qi Great Wall! How about that?\"

Chen Ping\'an burst into laughter, and he gave her another fan, this one
with many more characters on it.

\"Very impressive, little girl,\" he praised with an amused smile.
\"You\'re the only one on the Sword Qi Great Wall that\'s been able to
swindle me out of money.\"

Yuan Zaohua was very pleased with her spoils, but she still wanted more.

\"If you give me another one, I can include you in my top ten, or even
my top five! It\'s fine if this one doesn\'t have as many characters on
it,\" she negotiated.

Unfortunately for her, Chen Ping\'an didn\'t take the bait.

However, prior to his departure, he pulled out a small seal and told
Yuan Zaohua to hand him the folding fan that had fewer characters on it.
He gently imprinted his seal onto the fan, then returned it to Yuan
Zaohua, while all of the other children looked on with wide eyes.

By the time the Nascent Tier sword immortal concluded his lesson, Chen
Ping\'an was already long gone, and the old sword immortal made his way
over to Yuan Zaohua and the children.

At this moment, Yuan Zaohua was resting her chin on top of the city wall
with the two folding fans splayed out before her, doing her best to
identify any characters that she recognized. Of course, she preferred
the one with more characters on it, and in her eyes, it had to be far
more valuable than the other one.

However, the old sword immortal\'s attention was drawn to the folding
fan bearing fewer characters, and he was quite amused by what he saw.

*Most good things aren\'t meant to last; precious jewels soon become
relics past.*

*But lost jewels may still be unearthed someday, perhaps gaining in
value; who\'s to say?*

The first sentence came from an extremely renowned piece of poetry in
the Majestic World, whereas the second half was complete nonsense, most
likely something that Chen Ping\'an had made up himself.

Having said that, it did put a positive twist on things, invoking a
sense of hope when the original piece of poetry contained a rather
sobering message.

All of a sudden, the old sword immortal\'s attention was drawn to the
seal imprinted on the fan, and an intrigued look appeared on his face.

The inscription in the seal read: \"Life is fraught with separations,
but even shattered mirrors can be mended.\"

The old sword immortal then thought of Yuan Zaohua\'s background. Her
father was a bright talent who had high hopes of reaching the Upper Five
Tiers, but ultimately perished on the southern battlefields before he
could reach his full potential, leaving behind only Yuan Zaohua and her
mother. The old sword immortal turned his gaze in the direction that
Chen Ping\'an had departed.

It had to be said that he was a little different from the academics from
schools and ones that the old sword immortal had encountered in the
past.

Meanwhile, Chen Ping\'an had already met up with Zuo You.

\"I see you\'ve already made a breakthrough,\" Zuo You remarked.

\"That\'s right. I am now a fifth tier Qi refiner,\" Chen Ping\'an
confirmed with a nod.

\"Make sure you don\'t slack off in your studies and mental
cultivation,\" Zuo You cautioned.

Zuo You was probably the only senior brother under the heavens who was
concerned that their junior brother was making breakthroughs too
quickly, rather than worried that their junior brother\'s cultivation
base was too low.

\"With you keeping a constant eye on me, I wouldn\'t dare to slack off
even if I wanted to,\" Chen Ping\'an said in a resigned manner.

\"Why didn\'t you say that you couldn\'t die to my sword qi a few more
times even if you wanted to?\" Zuo You sneered.

Chen Ping\'an immediately knew that he was in for a lot of suffering.

\*\*\*

Osmanthus Girl Jin Su on the Osmanthus Island was actually Lady Gui\'s
only direct disciple, and her cultivation base remained the same as it
had been ten years ago. This was no surprise, given that bottlenecks
were difficult to overcome. Hence, upon the Osmanthus Island\'s arrival
at Stalactite Mountain, Lady Gui encouraged her to go and explore
Stalactite Mountain to take her mind off things. In close proximity to
both the mountain and the sea, Stalactite Mountain was an exceptional
place to see and visit.

Lady Gui had even given Jin Su an allowance of one grain rain coin as
spending money, jokingly remarking to her disciple that if she
encountered the same beloved items that had been on her mind for close
to the past twenty years, then she shouldn\'t hesitate to purchase them
this time. This gave Jin Su a massive fright, and she tried to refuse,
but Lady Gui brushed her off with a dismissive wave. At the same time,
she told Jin Su that this was the first time both Mr. Qi and his
disciple were visiting Stalactite Mountain, so she should help them out
wherever she could.

Jin Su didn\'t think much about it.

Neither Qi Jinglong nor Bai Shou had revealed their sect of origin, so
Jin Su merely treated them as if they were a traveling Confucian scholar
and his scholarly attendant. The Northern Complete Reed Continent was
renowned for its abundance of swordsmen, yet neither of them was
carrying swords.

They had traveled to Stalactite Mountain on Osmanthus Island on this
occasion because they were apparently friends of Chen Ping\'an\'s, and
they were staying in the Guimai courtyard, which was under Chen
Ping\'an\'s name. Jin Su hadn\'t had many interactions with Qi Jinglong
and Bai Shou. Occasionally, she would visit their courtyard with Lady
Gui to have some tea.

All Jin Su knew was that Qi Jinglong came from the Northern Complete
Reed Continent, and that he had traveled southward on the Flax Robe
Sect\'s immortal ship. Along the way, he made a stop in the Dragon
Spring Prefecture, then went straight to Old Dragon City from there. It
just so happened that the Osmanthus Island was traveling to Stalactite
Mountain, so he moved into the vacant Guimai courtyard.

Lady Gui never revealed Qi Jinglong\'s cultivation base, and Jin Su
didn\'t ask, merely regarding Qi Jinglong as an ordinary passenger on
their ship, the type that she would never meet again.

His background, his cultivation base, his personality\... What did any
of that have to do with her?

However, Jin Su didn\'t dare to ignore her mistress\'s orders. On this
occasion, Osmanthus Island was once again harbored near the Catch and
Release Pavilion, and she began introducing the origins of the pavilion
to Qi Jinglong. His disciple, Bai Shou, immediately lost interest in the
pavilion upon seeing the plaque personally inscribed by the Daoist
second disciple. In contrast, Qi Jinglong insisted on paying the
pavilion a visit.

Jin Su didn\'t care either way, but Bai Shou was feeling really
disgruntled at having to wait for Qi Jinglong as he slowly squeezed
through the crowd, then stood within the crowded Catch and Release
Pavilion for quite some time. Among the eight most prominent attractions
of Stalactite Mountain, the Catch and Release Pavilion was the least
interesting one, yet even upon his departure, Qi Jinglong took some time
to stare up at the plaque, as if he could really see something special
about it.

All the while, Jin Su had been watching with disdain, feeling as if Qi
Jinglong were being too pretentious and putting on an act to make
himself appear more cultured and sophisticated.

Thankfully, Jin Su perpetually had a rather cold expression to begin
with, so her disdain wasn\'t displayed through her face.

Furthermore, several other osmanthus girls she was quite close with
stood next to her, and they would be traveling together for the next
three days. The thought of that, combined with the grain rain coin that
she had carefully tucked away, brought a hint of a smile to her face.

In her eyes, Bai Shou wasn\'t much better than Qi Jinglong. He was
constantly complaining and whinging, going on and on about how \"Liu\"
Jinglong was delaying his trip to the Lightning Lake Platform. He
didn\'t refer to Qi Jinglong respectfully as Master or Mr. Qi, instead
seemingly adamant that his master had the Liu surname instead, something
that Jin Su felt rather strange, but she didn\'t care to ask questions.

What Jin Su felt to be even stranger was that Qi Jinglong was willing to
bring such a rude and uncouth disciple with him on his journey.

[]{#chapter-71.xhtml}

# Chapter 595: (2): The Top Ten Sword Immortals of the Sword Qi Great Wall

Sword of Coming

After leaving the crowded Catch and Release Pavilion, Jin Su routinely
asked Qi Jinglong if there was any particular inn where he would like to
stay. She told him that the Ganoderma Inn had the best scenery, but it
was quite expensive. As a result, many of the Osmanthus Island\'s
regular passengers, including Chen Ping\'an, generally preferred to stay
in the Stork Inn.

However, the inn wasn\'t very big, and it was tucked away deep in a
small alley. It wasn\'t a particularly great inn, but it certainly had
the advantage of low prices. Qi Jinglong smiled and politely requested
that Jin Su take them to the Stork Inn, but that was immediately met
with opposition from Bai Shou.

He was just about to complain when Qi Jinglong turned and gave him a
warning glance, so he could only swallow his gripes and sulk in silence.

The group made its way to the Stork Inn, and sure enough, it really was
tucked away deep in a small alley, just as Jin Su described. Looking at
the vibrant smile on the young innkeeper\'s face, Bai Shou couldn\'t
help but feel as if they were clueless pigs being taken to the
slaughter.

As soon as they sat down in their room, Bai Shou immediately began to
complain.

\"Don\'t all of the swordsmen of our Northern Complete Reed Continent
stay in the Spring Banner Inn when they come to Stalactite Mountain? Why
are we staying in this shoddy little inn instead? Are you lusting after
those osmanthus girls or something?\"

Qi Jinglong poured two cups of tea, and Bai Shou took his cup before
downing its contents in one go, then continued, \"Let\'s have a
heart-to-heart here, Liu Jinglong. Jin Su is the prettiest one out of
those osmanthus girls, but even she loses to Celestial Maiden Lu in the
looks department, does she not?

"Apparently, the owner of the Spring Banner Inn almost became Dao
partners with Celestial Maiden Lu\'s grandmaster in the past, so did you
choose not to stay in the Spring Banner Inn because you were afraid that
someone there would tip off Celestial Maiden Lu, and she would come all
the way here to find you? I\'m sure she wouldn\'t do that; it\'s not
like she\'s Sun Qing of the Rainbow Sparrow Residence.

"Out of all of the women who like you, I\'d say Celestial Maiden Lu is
inarguably the most beautiful. Personality-wise, I like Sun Qing the
most. She\'s really confident and straightforward, but also just a
little bit shy. The one at the Three Official Attendant Temple is a
little bit too passionate. She looks at you like a parched alcoholic
looking at a flagon of fine wine, and I could immediately tell as soon
as I saw her that the two of you weren\'t meant to be.\"

\"How about we make another trip to Downtrodden Mountain once we return
to the Great Emblem Sword Sect?\" Qi Jinglong proposed with a smile.

Bai Shou immediately shut his mouth and pretended not to have heard Qi
Jinglong. He then felt like it wasn\'t good enough just to ignore Qi
Jinglong\'s suggestion, so he even respectfully poured the latter a cup
of tea.

On the subject of Downtrodden Mountain, it was always much better to be
safe than sorry. Just the mere thought of having to deal with Pei Qian
was enough to give him a splitting headache.

*To think that I, the great Sword Immortal Bai Shou, would already have
my reputation swept to the ground on my first-ever journey, before I\'ve
even made a name for myself! I\'m never going to Downtrodden Mountain
ever again!*

Downtrodden Mountain was clearly a place that went against his eight
characters, meaning that misfortune was sure to befall him whenever he
went there. Furthermore, it was clear just from its name that it was an
inauspicious place, so he was determined never to go there again.

Meanwhile, Qi Jinglong was feeling a little sad as he thought about some
personal matters.

One of the reasons why he had left the Northern Complete Reed Continent
on this occasion was that he didn\'t have anything to do for now. He had
successfully weathered the challenges from the three sword immortals in
the wake of his breakthrough, so he decided to go on a journey to the
other eight continents of the Majestic World.

In addition, he had also been secretly informed by Huang Shi that the
sect leader had ordered him to make an immediate trip to the Sword Qi
Great Wall. Qi Jinglong was well aware of the sect leader\'s intentions.
Clearly, he wanted Qi Jinglong to capitalize on this period of relative
peace to visit the Sword Qi Great Wall right away, and once there,
perhaps he would even pass down his position of sect leader to him.

If that were to happen, then Qi Jinglong wouldn\'t have to take part in
the battles to defend the Sword Qi Great Wall as a new sword immortal of
the Northern Complete Reed Continent for at least the next century.

All of the Great Emblem Sword Sect\'s other affairs could simply be left
to Han Huaizi to manage.

Bai Shou didn\'t dare to comment on Qi Jinglong\'s romantic affairs
anymore, so he changed the subject and asked, \"Can we really not go
stay in the Spring Banner Inn? I really wanted to see that gourd vine.
Back in the sect, I promised a bunch of my junior brothers and junior
nephews that I would go and see the future Sword Nurturing Gourds on
their behalf.

"It would be really embarrassing for me if I had to go back and tell
them that I couldn\'t follow through on my promise. What am I supposed
to do? Hide on the Graceful Peak after I get back to avoid them? Think
about it. If I\'m being embarrassed, then you\'re also going to be
embarrassed by association!\"

The Spring Banner Inn was one of the top four private residences of
Stalactite Mountain.

The most renowned one of the four was naturally the Ape Rub Residence,
which belonged to the so-called god of riches of the Pure White
Continent. The entire residence might as well have been constructed from
immortal coins, and the past differences between the residence\'s owner
in his younger days and the Daoist Great Heavenly Lord made for a
popular story that was still enjoyed by many.

Then there was the Plum Blossom Garden constructed by cultivators of the
Middle Earth Divine Continent. It was said that the garden was home to
an Upper Five Tiers spirit that had lived for countless years. The owner
of the garden had booked out an entire intercontinental ship to ensure
that the ancestral plum tree was transported smoothly from his hometown
to Stalactite Mountain, and that had undoubtedly been an extremely
costly maneuver.

The Spring Banner Inn had been constructed by a disillusioned sword
immortal of the Northern Complete Reed Continent. It was very popular
with other swordsmen from the Northern Complete Reed Continent, but its
owner never showed himself in public.

The final one of the four residences was the Water Essence Residence,
which had been constructed by an immortal sect that was situated out at
sea. Apparently, it was able to gather up the remnants of the Flood
Dragon Trench thanks to its close proximity, and the sect was enhanced
significantly as a result.

People like Sect Leader Han Huaizi and Disciplinary Elder Huang Tong of
the Great Emblem Sword Sect, as well as Sect Leader Li Cai of Duckweed
Sword Lake, had all previously stayed in the Spring Banner Inn when
visiting Stalactite Mountain.

Planted in the Spring Banner Inn was a gourd vine that had been nurtured
by generations of unfathomable immortals, and after it came into the
possession of the owner of the Spring Banner Inn, it had continued to be
nurtured with spiritual energy for over a thousand years. At this point,
it had already produced fourteen gourds of different sizes that had
hopes of being crafted into Sword Nurturing Gourds.

As long as the refinement process was successful, each gourd would at
least start off as an immortal treasure, and it was said that if the
finest of the fourteen gourds were ever refined into a Sword Nurturing
Gourd, it would become a pseudo-celestial tool right away.

In the immortal world, there existed immense disparities in value even
among treasures of the same caliber.

A pseudo-celestial Sword Nurturing Gourd was almost comparable to a
Sword Nurturing Gourd left behind by the Dao Ancestor, and as a result,
they were regarded as celestial tools.

That sword immortal from the Northern Complete Reed Continent had made
an extremely wise decision to bring the gourd vine all the way here. The
Spring Banner Inn was under the protection of Stalactite Mountain, and
by extension, the gourd vine was also able to benefit from Stalactite
Mountain\'s protection.

However, out of the fourteen gourds that were still yet to completely
ripen, it would already be a very impressive return if even half of them
could ultimately be successfully refined into Sword Nurturing Gourds.

Not only would the Spring Banner Inn be able to gain a tremendous
reputation and enormous wealth from those seven Sword Nurturing Gourds,
but even more importantly, they would also be able to establish close
ties with seven sword immortals. Perhaps those connections alone would
be enough for the owner of the Spring Banner Inn to establish a sect on
whichever continent in the Majestic World that he pleased.

This was why Bai Shou was so keen to visit the Spring Banner Inn.

He had been extremely envious after finding out that Chen Ping\'an\'s
red wine gourd was actually a legendary Sword Nurturing Gourd, and he
was very much looking forward to the day when he could get his own Sword
Nurturing Gourd.

How cool would it be if he could travel the world while using a Sword
Nurturing Gourd as a container for wine, just as Chen Ping\'an did?

He had suggested that Chen Ping\'an engrave the words \"Sword Nurturing
Gourd\" onto his wine gourd, but Chen Ping\'an had turned down the
shameless suggestion.

\"We\'ll go there after we\'ve visited the seven other attractions
first,\" Qi Jinglong said. \"Right now, it\'s extremely difficult for
outsiders to travel from Stalactite Mountain to the Sword Qi Great Wall,
so we\'re going to need the Spring Banner Inn to vouch for us.\"

Bai Shou\'s eyes instantly lit up with excitement, and he asked, \"Can
you reserve a Spring Banner Inn Sword Nurturing Gourd for me? Even the
worst one of the bunch is fine! That can serve as your
disciple-recruiting gift to me. The Great Emblem Sword Sect is such a
massive and reputable sect, and you\'re now an Unpolished Jade Tier
swordsman; you\'d be bringing shame to both yourself and your sect if
you give me too shoddy a disciple-recruiting gift!

"You should take a leaf out of Brother Chen\'s book. He gave out so many
gifts after the Downtrodden Mountain Ancestral Hall was established, and
all of them were extremely valuable!\"

In truth, Bai Shou was only running his mouth, and he had no realistic
expectations that Liu Jinglong would accept his request. Sword Nurturing
Gourds were priceless treasures that even some sword immortals didn\'t
possess. This was because, compared with things like pocket treasures
and minimization treasures, Sword Nurturing Gourds were rather awkward.

If the caliber of a Sword Nurturing Gourd couldn\'t match up to a
swordsman\'s cultivation base, then it would only hamper the nurturing
of the swordsman\'s bonded flying sword. However, Sword Nurturing Gourds
of a sufficient caliber to catch a sword immortal\'s eye were
exceedingly rare.

However, to Bai Shou\'s surprise, Qi Jinglong nodded as he replied,
\"I\'ll make a request for you, but I can\'t make any promises on
whether it\'ll work out or not.\"

Bai Shou was ecstatic to hear this, and he exclaimed, \"Really? You\'re
really willing to put in a request for me?\"

In his eyes, Liu Jinglong had a whole host of terrible qualities, but if
there was one good thing about him, then it was that he always kept his
word.

\"You accepted me as your master in the ancestral hall, so it\'s only
right that I give you a disciple-recruiting gift,\" Qi Jinglong said.
\"Right now, you are a direct disciple of our Great Emblem Sword Sect\'s
ancestral hall, and it would benefit you immensely to own a Sword
Nurturing Gourd of a high caliber.

"It would allow you to nurture your sword faster, and that way, you\'ll
have more time to spend on mental cultivation, so why would I not be
willing to make the request for you? It\'s not like I\'m going to barge
my way into the Spring Banner Inn and force them to sell me a Sword
Nurturing Gourd.\"

\"I just didn\'t expect you to be so generous, seeing as you never even
bring money with you wherever you go,\" Bai Shou murmured.

\"A person\'s generosity isn\'t solely reflected in how they handle
money,\" Qi Jinglong said with a smile. \"It\'s never a good thing to go
to extremes or to be too narrow-minded in any regard. I\'m not saying
this to make excuses for myself. Instead, I\'m telling you this because
I want you to always think more when you meet people outside of me.
Otherwise, you run the risk of passing up worthy friends and making
friends with those who are unworthy.\"

\"Hold on a second! Could it be that you know that the Spring Banner Inn
isn\'t going to sell you a Sword Nurturing Gourd, so you\'re just using
this as an opportunity to preach to me?\" Bai Shou asked with a
skeptical expression.

\"Cultivators like you and I can live far longer than the average
person, so as long as you\'re willing to look, the truth will always
come out eventually. Do you need to ask my true intentions? Even if I
tell you what my true intentions are, would you believe me?\" Qi
Jinglong countered with a smile.

\"Stop! My head hurts!\" Bai Shou wailed as he frantically clasped his
hands over his ears to keep out Qi Jinglong\'s insufferable preaching.

Qi Jinglong was unbothered, and his smile remained unchanged as he
continued to sip on his tea.

\"Are we going to have to keep traveling with Jin Su and the others?\"
Bai Shou suddenly asked. \"They're even more hard-working in their
shopping than we are in our cultivation! It\'s exhausting having to
travel with them!\"

\"The immortal ship of Old Dragon City\'s Fu Clan just so happens to be
harbored at Stalactite Mountain as well, so I\'m assuming Lady Gui is
worried that they could run into trouble while sightseeing on Stalactite
Mountain,\" Qi Jinglong explained. \"The people of the Fu Clan tend to
be very reckless and self-centered, thinking that they can get away with
anything. We saw that ourselves back in Old Dragon City. The Fan Clan
didn\'t charge us even a single snowflake coin on this journey, so we
have to reciprocate their goodwill.\"

Bai Shou crossed his arms and replied, \"In that case, I suppose we\'ll
just have to keep them company for a while longer. If the people from
the Fu Clan try to get up to some shady business, then I\'m gonna have
to do something about it.\"

\"Oh? What exactly are you going to do about it? I\'m intrigued now,\"
Qi Jinglong said with a chuckle.

Bai Shou had been brimming with confidence just like this before the
Flax Robe Sect\'s immortal ship harbored at the Ox Horn Mountain ferry
station. He had still been full of confidence after spotting the three
children on top of the stone steps on Downtrodden Mountain, convinced
that he could easily beat them in a fight.

Bai Shou could tell what Qi Jinglong was alluding to, and he immediately
flew into a rage. \"Stop making fun of me, Liu Jinglong! Am I your
disciple or not?!\"

However, a hint of dejection then appeared on his face.

Pei Qian was Chen Ping\'an\'s first-ever disciple, while he was
technically Liu Jinglong\'s only direct disciple.

Chen Ping\'an\'s cultivation base as a Qi refiner was still far below
Liu Jinglong\'s, yet Bai Shou had been utterly embarrassed by Pei Qian
on Downtrodden Mountain.

Liu Jinglong had never blamed him for this, but Bai Shou still felt he
had put Liu Jinglong to shame with his inept display.

\"I\'ve never felt like my disciple is inferior to others,\" Qi Jinglong
reassured.

Bai Shou\'s cheeks instantly became flushed as he snapped, \"Who\'re you
calling your disciple?! I\'ve never truly thought of you as my master!\"

\"If you compete with others, there will always be people better than
you, but if you compete with yourself, then you\'ll always win; it\'s
just a matter of your margin of victory. Which one do you think is the
superior path to take, Bai Shou?\" Qi Jinglong asked with a serious
expression.

Bai Shou lay down on the table in a dramatic fashion as he let loose an
almighty groan. He felt extremely envious of Pei Qian because her master
was always absent, so she barely ever had anyone preaching to her.

What was most concerning to Bai Shou was that as they parted ways last
time, Pei Qian told him that she was perhaps also going to make a trip
to the Sword Qi Great Wall to visit her master, and that the timing of
her trip was only dependent on when Zhong Qiu planned to embark on his
journey.

She had decided that the next time they met, they would only engage in a
verbal battle rather than a physical contest. Of course, Bai Shou had no
say in the matter, and it wasn\'t like she cared about his opinion
anyway.

Whenever Bai Shou thought of this, he would immediately be overcome with
a sense of frustration.

\*\*\*

Ning Yao was still in seclusion.

Whenever Chen Ping\'an took a break from his Qi refinement, he would
spar with Nalan Yexing on the training grounds.

Without Fan Dache and the others present, Chen Ping\'an was able to go
all-out, and he seemed like an entirely different person in the Minute
Small World.

Granny Bai would always watch their sparring matches from the pergola,
and the more she saw, the more convinced she became that Chen Ping\'an
was the most handsome and talented young man on the entire Sword Qi
Great Wall. In her eyes, his martial arts aptitude was unmatched, and
she wasn\'t concerned at all about his relatively lacking cultivation
base as a Qi refiner.

Clearly, he was the type to build a solid foundation before making rapid
progress, and sure enough, he had already made a breakthrough to the
fifth tier. In fact, she was so confident in Chen Ping\'an that she
deemed his aptitude for cultivation to be almost on par with that of
Ning Yao.

On this day, Chen Ping\'an was sitting on a little stool not far away
from the wine shop, eating some sunflower seeds. He had finally finished
telling the story of the wine-loving Sword Immortal Qi.

Feng Kangle was still eager to hear more, so he asked Chen Ping\'an if
there were any other noteworthy stories about Sword Immortal Qi. Chen
Ping\'an thought about it and decided that he could make up a few more,
so he continued his storytelling. The next story began as the young
sword immortal arrived at an ancient monastery in the wilderness while
out on a journey.

He lit a campfire and was just about to begin drinking when several
beautiful women drifted into the monastery, leaving a trail of alluring
fragrance and tinkling laughter in their wake. The young sword
immortal\'s brows instantly furrowed slightly at the sight of the women
because, as a cultivator, he was able to see fox tails trailing along
behind them. Thus, the young sword immortal rose to his feet after
downing a flagon of wine.

Right as Feng Kangle was being drawn into the story, Chen Ping\'an left
things on a cliffhanger, declaring that he would tell the rest of the
story next time.

Even after making his way to the wine shop, Chen Ping\'an didn\'t ask
for a drink. Fan Dache and the others weren\'t around, and the remaining
gamblers were all glowering at him with rather hostile expressions, so
it was going to be difficult for him to get a free bowl of wine or two.
He squatted down by the side of the street and had a bowl of yangchun
noodles.

As he did so, he suddenly felt a pang of guilt toward Qi Jinglong. He
felt like his stories weren\'t spectacular enough to do Qi Jinglong
justice, but there was nothing more that he could do. After all, he
wasn\'t a true storyteller, and he had already done his best.

[]{#chapter-72.xhtml}

# Chapter 596: (1): Someone Has Challenged Chen Ping\'an

Sword of Coming

In Chen Ping\'an\'s mind, this was not a matter of wine, but one of
principle. He was running this wine shop, yet he couldn\'t even get a
bowl of free wine here, and that was absurd to him!

Hence, Chen Ping\'an decided to make a deal with a pair of swordsmen
that he was familiar with. The two men had been glowering resentfully at
him even as they enjoyed their meal of noodles and wine, and it took a
lot of convincing, but Chen Ping\'an managed to win them over. He
implied to the two men that the next time someone ran a shady betting
station, he would make sure that they were in on it and would get a
share of the profits.

The attitudes of the two swordsmen instantly took a drastic turn at such
an alluring proposition, and they insisted on treating Chen Ping\'an to
some wine. Furthermore, they weren\'t willing to settle for the cheapest
Bamboo Sea Small World wine. Even though they were both struggling
financially, they insisted on scrounging together five snowflake coins
to buy a flagon of the shop\'s most expensive wine. They told Chen
Ping\'an that he had to drink it. Otherwise, he would no longer be their
friend.

Chen Ping\'an sat at the table, waiting for the wine to be brought to
him, feeling a little lonely. With so many friends, it was difficult not
to be treated to wine.

The list of the top ten sword immortals of the Sword Qi Great Wall that
Yuan Zaohua had provided earlier on the city walls was not much
different from Chen Ping\'an\'s list: the old great sword immortal, Dong
Sangeng, A\'Liang, Lord Hidden Official, Chen Xi, Qi Tingji, Zuo You,
Nalan Shaowei, the old deaf guy, and Lu Zhi.

No one knew the full extent of Chen Qingdu\'s power, and aside from the
imaginative and heavily romanticized stories told by children, there
were no real tales of his feats, either.

The Dong Clan had been dealt a rather heavy blow after Dong Guanpu was
personally slain by the old great sword immortal for colluding with the
demon tribe, and in the wake of that incident, Dong Sangeng had kept a
very low profile. His previous public appearance was when he gave a
send-off to Sword Immortal Huang Tong of the Great Emblem Sword Sect.

A\'Liang was already long gone from the Sword Qi Great Wall. He had
scammed a donkey and a white Sword Nurturing Gourd off Wei Jin, and
during his travels, he ran into Chen Ping\'an and Li Baoping.

The Hidden Official was undoubtedly one of the most powerful people on
the Sword Qi Great Wall, but just like the old great sword immortal, the
full extent of her powers was unclear. To this day, no one had seen her
bonded flying sword, and at the very least, Chen Ping\'an hadn\'t even
heard any mention of her bonded flying sword. If one were to listen
closely to the stories told about the Hidden Official, it would occur to
them that she was the sword immortal who seemed least like a swordsman
on the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Chen Xi was the current leader of the Chen Clan, but he was perpetually
made to feel unworthy in the face of the old great sword immortal.
Whenever he was in Chen Qingdu\'s presence, it always felt like he was
still just a child. Hence, among all of the prominent clans on the Sword
Qi Great Wall, the people of the Chen Clan were the ones most averse to
visiting the city walls.

Chen Ping\'an had met Qi Tingji while practicing his fist techniques on
the city walls during his first visit to the Sword Qi Great Wall. He was
a handsome, youthful-looking sword immortal and the leader of the Qi
Clan.

As for Zuo You, he required no further introduction.

Nalan Shaowei had already been in seclusion for a very long time. Even
though the Nalan Clan was one of the most powerful clans on the Sword Qi
Great Wall, it was often forgotten about due to Nalan Shaowei\'s
prolonged absence. As for whether Nalan Yexing was a member of the Nalan
Clan, that was something that Chen Ping\'an had never asked about. It
was important to be critical and ask questions, but it simply wasn\'t
appropriate to pry into some matters.

The old deaf guy was the old swordsman who was rumored to be a demon,
and he was overseeing the prison where many great demons were being held
captive.

When it came to Lu Zhi, just about everyone had already forgotten about
her time in the Majestic World. She had arrived on the Sword Qi Great
Wall at the Golden Core Tier, and she made one breakthrough after
another, performing many glorious feats on the battlefield in the
process.

Each time a battle was waged to defend the city, she would be sure to
put her life on the line.

A\'Liang had once invited her out for a drink, and he had said something
rather interesting to her that had somehow been leaked, even though
there had been no one else present at the time.

He had said, \"All those who reside alone away from others are either
wild beasts or deities.\"

Lu Zhi was the sword immortal whom Dong Bude and Die Zhang admired the
most.

After learning that what he had said to Lu Zhi had somehow been made
public knowledge, A\'Liang had been furious, denouncing the culprit for
shamelessly eavesdropping on them. How could they have leaked something
that he had said in private to a woman? Granted, what he had said had
been self-admittedly extremely profound, insightful, and classy, but had
the culprit asked for his and Lu Zhi\'s approval before leaking the
contents of their conversation for the entire world to hear?

Chen Ping\'an was drinking his free wine, and he felt like he was doing
quite well for himself, considering he was already ranked eleventh in
Yuan Zaohua\'s eyes at such a young age.

\"Hey, Second Shopkeeper, I hear you have a sword immortal friend on the
Northern Complete Reed Continent who\'s really good in a fight and even
better at drinking, is that right?\" a drunkard asked.

Chen Ping\'an rubbed his chin as he mulled over the question carefully,
then nodded as he replied, \"I\'d say he could beat all of you at once
with ease.\"

Of course, no one believed him.

Amid the hustle and bustle, Zhang Jiazhen was looking at Chen Ping\'an,
who was staring into the distance in a daze.

Right at this moment, a smile appeared on Chen Ping\'an\'s face as he
turned to the street with a reminiscent expression.

He felt like he could see Qi Jinglong and Cao Qinglang walking along
side by side.

Chen Ping\'an finished the wine in his bowl in one go, then rose to his
feet as he declared, \"Everyone, I have an announcement to make!\"

Everyone instantly fell silent, waiting with bated breath for him to
continue.

*Could it be that he\'s about to pay for everyone\'s wine?!*

Chen Ping\'an smiled as he concluded, \"Don\'t forget to pay!\"

\*\*\*

Over the next three days, Liu Jinglong continued to keep Jin Su and the
other osmanthus girls company as they visited all of Stalactite
Mountain\'s most noteworthy attractions. Bai Shou didn\'t have any
interest in the Incense Offering Tower or the Ganoderma Inn, nor did he
feel much desire to visit the Sword Reverence Pagoda, which was laden
with the portraits of many sword immortals. Ultimately, he still didn\'t
truly see himself as a swordsman.

Out of all of the attractions on Stalactite Mountain, the Lightning Lake
Platform was the one that captivated him the most. The flashing
lightning and rumbling thunder made for a riveting visual and auditory
experience, and he had heard that the martial goddess from the Middle
Earth Divine Continent had refined her sword there not long ago.

Unfortunately, they only made a brief trip to the Lightning Lake
Platform, and even then, the osmanthus girls had stayed a bit longer
than they otherwise would\'ve out of consideration for Bai Shou. After
that brief visit to the Lightning Lake Platform, they went to the Milu
Cliff, and upon their arrival, the osmanthus girls immediately began
chatting spiritedly with one another.

At the foot of the Milu Cliff was an entire street full of shops that
were clearly heavily catered to the female demographic. Even the
relatively more inexpressive and steadfast Jin Su was like a kid in a
candy shop as she waltzed excitedly from one shop to another, while Bai
Shou was left rolling his eyes in exasperation.

Qi Jinglong continued to trail along behind them at a leisurely pace,
carefully inspecting every single attraction that they visited. Even
when they visited the shops at the foot of the Milu Cliff, he remained
as dutiful and watchful as ever, occasionally even offering his opinion
on items that the osmanthus girls brought to him.

Bai Shou could tell that at least two of the osmanthus girls had become
quite fond of him, and whenever they spoke to him, they made sure to
speak in a very soft and gentle tone while observing him with keen
attention.

This was very perplexing to Bai Shou. They had no idea who he was, nor
were they aware of his connection to the Great Emblem Sword Sect, and
they certainly didn\'t know that he was the so-called Terrestrial Flood
Dragon of the Northern Complete Reed Continent. From their perspective,
he should\'ve been nothing more than a pedantic scholar with not even a
single snowflake coin to his name, so why were they attracted to him?

Could it be that his bonded flying sword had some type of innate ability
to capture the hearts of women? If that were the case, then Bai Shou
would feel much more motivated to learn swordsmanship from him.

The day passed by in an uneventful fashion.

Qi Jinglong didn\'t bother to reveal to Bai Shou that they had been
followed by two separate groups of people in secret, but Qi Jinglong had
scared them off on both occasions.

On the first occasion, Qi Jinglong had only displayed the aura of a
Golden Core Tier swordsman. Whoever had been following them in secret
was unwilling to give up, and they returned with reinforcements. Qi
Jinglong could only elevate his cultivation base by an additional tier,
and after that, no one else came to bother them.

Bai Shou spent the entire day hanging around near the osmanthus girls,
putting on a display of boredom as he carried the spoils from their
shopping trip. However, despite his perceived casual, lazy demeanor, he
had actually been extremely vigilant the entire time, constantly
observing his surroundings, just like he used to as an assassin of Deer
Cutter Mountain.

Qi Jinglong was quite pleased to see this.

With Qi Jinglong accompanying the osmanthus girls, there was no way that
he would allow any harm to befall them at the hands of the people from
the Fu Clan. Hence, Bai Shou could\'ve easily grown lazy and complacent,
knowing that his services weren\'t required anyway.

Even in the Great Emblem Sword Sect, there were many direct disciples
who, unbeknownst to even themselves, underwent minute changes in
personality after they attained their status as direct disciples. They
still spoke and behaved as they usually did, maintaining a respectful
demeanor while continuing to abide by the rules, but deep down, they
were already ever so slightly different from the people they had once
been.

Over time, these minute differences would be magnified, and they would
turn into drastically different individuals. Outside of his own
cultivation, Qi Jinglong would do his best to help his juniors of the
Great Emblem Sword Sect remain steadfast and true to themselves, but
there were certain matters that he simply couldn\'t speak on as they
concerned the foundation of their Great Daos.

Jin Su and the other osmanthus girls returned to the Osmanthus Island,
satisfied with the spoils from their shopping trip. Over the few days
that they had spent together, Jin Su\'s impression of Qi Jinglong had
improved significantly, and she thanked him in earnest as they parted
ways.

Qi Jinglong escorted them all the way to the Catch and Release Pavilion,
and only then did he take Bai Shou to pay the bill at the Stork Inn.
From there, they were planning to go and stay in the Spring Banner Inn,
but upon their return to the Stork Inn, Bai Shou was immediately
overcome by a sense of immense schadenfreude.

As it turned out, a familiar woman was waiting for them there. It was
none other than Celestial Maiden Lu Sui of Water Scripture Mountain.

\"Jinglong, the people at the Spring Banner Inn heard that you and Bai
Shou have already been on Stalactite Mountain for three days, so they
asked me to come here and extend an invitation to you,\" Lu Sui
explained in a gentle voice. \"I\'ve already paid the bill for you. You
don\'t blame me for that, do you?\"

Qi Jinglong shook his head with a wry smile. It felt like it would be
the wrong answer regardless of whether he blamed her or not, so he
simply chose not to speak.

It was at times like this when Qi Jinglong began to miss Chen Ping\'an.

The innkeeper of the Stork Inn was very intrigued. Who was this young
outsider to warrant an invitation from the Spring Banner Inn?

The people at the renowned private residences like the Spring Banner Inn
and the Ape Rub Residence were extremely selective with their guests,
and generally speaking, no cultivator below the Upper Five Tiers would
even be permitted to set foot inside.

Qi Jinglong smiled and bade farewell to the innkeeper, who responded
with a smile and a nod of his own.

He was just the innkeeper of a tiny inn, and there was no need to be
overly polite to someone so far above him. Even if he did everything in
his power to appease the young man, it wasn\'t going to amount to
anything, and he had never been one to suck up to others anyway. All he
wanted was to enjoy a peaceful life and earn enough money to get by, and
he didn\'t harbor any lofty ambitions.

Having said that, he certainly wasn\'t averse to meeting mysterious and
unfathomable young men like Chen Ping\'an and Qi Jinglong every once in
a while. Perhaps once they forged resounding reputations for themselves,
more and more business would be drawn to the Stork Inn by association.

However, it was not going to be easy to earn a reputation in a place
that was teeming with power and talent like Stalactite Mountain.

On the way to the Spring Banner Inn, Bai Shou eagerly struck up a
conversation with Lu Sui. He was very keen on visiting Water Scripture
Mountain as there were many pretty big sisters there.

Bai Shou wasn\'t actually a playboy. Instead, he simply liked it when
girls liked him.

On this occasion, Lu Sui was clearly much more talkative than the usual
cold and unapproachable Celestial Maiden Lu, who was focused solely on
her cultivation.

Bai Shou was feeling very indignant on Celestial Maiden Lu\'s behalf. If
such an exceptional woman couldn\'t even capture Liu Jinglong\'s heart,
then he deserved to be single for life and be forced to drink to death
by Xu Xingjiu!

The owner of the Spring Banner Inn made a rare appearance to personally
welcome Qi Jinglong.

Lu Sui brewed some tea for the two sword immortals, while Bai Shou was
feeling rather uneasy.

In the past, Bai Shou hadn\'t felt much respect or veneration for the
Great Emblem Sword Sect, and he certainly wasn\'t afraid of Liu
Jinglong, but for some reason, that began to change after his meeting
with Disciplinary Elder Huang Tong.

He didn\'t want to admit it, but he was even more afraid of the prospect
of having to meet Sect Leader Han Huaizi on this trip.

Similarly, Bai Shou was feeling very tense and uneasy in the presence of
Shao Yunyan, the owner of the Spring Banner Inn.

These were all legendary sword immortals, almighty figures who stood at
the very top of the mountain summit, even on the Northern Complete Reed
Continent, where swordsmen were as common as copper coins.

As for why he was so comfortable around Liu Jinglong, even though the
latter was also a sword immortal, that was a question that Bai Shou had
never really pondered.

In his eyes, it seemed like his master treated the sword immortal owner
of the Spring Banner Inn no differently from the much lesser cultivators
on the Osmanthus Island.

Bai Shou accepted the cup of tea offered to him by Lu Sui with both
hands, and after taking a sip, he began to feel a bit more settled and
composed.

Qi Jinglong asked if he could reserve a Sword Nurturing Gourd, and Shao
Yunyan accepted his request with a smile, offering him a very fair
price.

Qi Jinglong expressed his gratitude, while Bai Shou began sweating
profusely after hearing the exorbitant number of grain rain coins that
the Sword Nurturing Gourd was going to cost.

\"Outside of this deal, the Great Emblem Sword Sect doesn\'t owe me
anything, but you owe me a favor, Fellow Cultivator Qi,\" Shao Yunyan
said. \"To tell you the truth, if these fourteen gourds can ultimately
be successfully refined into seven Sword Nurturing Gourds, then all
seven have already been reserved well in advance in irrevocable deals.
However, one of them is not going to be able to fulfill the agreement
and make the purchase, so you\'re in luck.

"Otherwise, I\'m afraid I would\'ve had no choice but to turn you down.
In repayment for this favor, all that I ask is that you go into battle
for me once at my request within the next one thousand years. Rest
assured, it will be in a situation where you\'re fully justified to draw
your sword, and I won\'t try to force you to compromise on your morals
and values.\"

\"That\'s not a problem,\" Qi Jinglong replied with a smile.

He then hesitated momentarily before asking, \"If it turns out that more
than seven of the gourds are successfully refined into Sword Nurturing
Gourds, then can I reserve another one?\"

\"If there are additional Sword Nurturing Gourds beyond the projected
seven, then the extra ones will be sold to the highest bidders, so it\'s
probably going to be very difficult for you to get your hands on one,\"
Shao Yunyan replied with a smile.

There were some things that Shao Yunyan had chosen not to reveal to Qi
Jinglong. Even though one of the previously reserved Sword Nurturing
Gourds had become available, it was certainly not just available to
anyone.

As for why Qi Jinglong had been able to claim the Sword Nurturing Gourd,
there were three reasons for this. Firstly, Shao Yunyan and the Spring
Banner Inn had faith in Qi Jinglong\'s potential and were confident that
he would reach even higher heights in the future.

Secondly, there was a very good chance that Qi Jinglong was going to
become the next leader of the Great Emblem Sword Sect. Thirdly, Shao
Yunyan had also originally come from the Northern Complete Reed
Continent, so there was a bit of a connection between the two in that
regard.

Shao Yunyan didn\'t see the need to articulate all of this because he
knew that Qi Jinglong was already aware of all of these underlying
reasons.

\"It seems like I was hoping for a little too much,\" Qi Jinglong said.

\"It\'s only thanks to your presence here that I\'ve gotten a chance to
drink tea brewed by Lu Sui, Fellow Cultivator Qi,\" Shao Yunyan
chuckled.

Lu Sui was the most prized direct disciple of the Water Scripture
Mountain sect leader, and the only one that Shao Yunyan had ever been
indebted to in his life was Lu Sui\'s mistress.

The two of them had obtained the gourd vine that currently resided in
the Spring Banner Inn by chance together, and she was actually the one
who had made the greater contribution in the process. However, for
various reasons, the two of them were ultimately unable to become Dao
partners. Despite this, she had gladly given him sole ownership of the
gourd vine, and she had never expressed any regret or changed her mind
on this decision.

However, this only made him feel even more indebted to her. Hence, with
no children of his own, he treated her most prized disciple, Lu Sui,
like his own daughter. Lu Sui\'s devotion and infatuation toward Liu
Jinglong was very reminiscent of how her mistress had once felt about
Shao Yunyan.

It was a little off-putting for Bai Shou to hear Shao Yunyan refer to
Liu Jinglong as Qi Jinglong, just like Chen Ping\'an did.

Regarding this matter, Bai Shou had heard some rumors on the Graceful
Peak. Apparently, Liu Jinglong\'s surname was originally Qi, but after
entering the Great Emblem Sword Sect to cultivate, his name had been
marked down as Liu Jinglong in the ancestral hall.

After finalizing the deal on the Sword Nurturing Gourd, Shao Yunyan had
some more tea before promptly departing, but Lu Sui stayed and continued
to brew tea.

Bai Shou was watching her elegant and masterful tea-brewing technique,
and it was certainly a sight for sore eyes.

\"Have you seen through some of the secrets on Stalactite Mountain yet,
Jinglong?\" she asked with a smile.

Qi Jinglong nodded as he replied, \"The eight attractions on the
mountain are all eyes of a formation. Stalactite Mountain is not just a
mountain seal. Instead, it\'s a celestial weapon with both offensive and
defensive capabilities, one that\'s been refined countless times over.
As for the origins of the formation, I presume it comes from one of the
three ancient techniques left behind by the Master of Three Mountains
and Nine Lords.

"The most remarkable aspect of the formation is that it uses mountains
to refine water and turn the heavens. Once it\'s activated, it\'s
capable of turning heaven and earth on their heads.\"

Lu Sui\'s eyes were brimming with affection, and even though she only
took a quick glance at Liu Jinglong before returning her attention to
the tea that she was brewing, that fleeting glance alone would\'ve been
enough to captivate countless men.

However, Qi Jinglong was completely oblivious, still lost in his own
thoughts as he pondered the complexities of the Stalactite Mountain
formation.

Bai Shou was struck by the urge to give him a slap to the head.

A thought seemed to have occurred to Lu Sui, and she said, \"My mistress
is good friends with Sword Immortal Li, and she can accompany you to the
Sword Qi Great Wall. Lingcong is here with me on Stalactite Mountain.
I\'m sure you\'ve met her before, Jinglong. I came with her to visit
Stalactite Mountain on this occasion.\"

Qi Jinglong nodded in response, not questioning Lu Sui\'s alibi in the
slightest.

Bai Shou was growing more and more exasperated by the second, and he
could only chug down his cup of tea to drown his frustration.

*What the hell are you nodding for, you idiot?! Do you not realize that
Celestial Maiden Lu is only making up that story? She\'s not here with
Lingcong or whatever; she\'s here to see* you*! I don\'t mean to make
unfair comparisons, but Brother Chen is miles ahead of you when it comes
to stuff like this! Forget it, I\'ll just have to tell Brother Chen
about this the next time we meet and get him to teach you some of his
tricks.*

However, Lu Sui was already accustomed to this, and while refilling Qi
Jinglong\'s cup, she said, \"I heard that a martial arts prodigy from
the Middle Earth Divine Continent recently arrived at the Water Essence
Palace. She progressed to the Vajra Body Tier as the strongest sixth
tier martial artist under the heavens, and she made her breakthrough on
the Golden Armor Continent, where she received a lot of guidance from
Cao Ci.

"She came to the Sword Qi Great Wall on this occasion because she wants
to practice her fist techniques on the city walls for a few years, just
as Cao Ci once did.\"

\"I have a friend who\'s currently also practicing his fist techniques
on the Sword Qi Great Wall,\" Qi Jinglong said with a smile. \"Maybe
they\'ll run into each other at some point.\"

After his ordeal with Pei Qian, Bai Shou couldn\'t help but feel a
little uneasy whenever he heard mention of a female pure martial artist.

\"Is it Chen Ping\'an from the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent?\" Lu
Sui asked with a curious expression.

Qi Jinglong had mentioned this name last time at the Three Official
Attendant Temple. It seemed that Chen Ping\'an was the reason why Qi
Jinglong had gone on a shopping trip to Hatred Sword Mountain and the
Three Official Attendant Temple before facing his three challenges, so
the name had left quite a deep impression on Lu Sui.

Qi Jinglong smiled and nodded in confirmation.

\"Even I\'m starting to get a little curious about this Chen Ping\'an,\"
Lu Sui mused. \"I wonder what it is about him that\'s made him such a
close friend of yours.\"

Qi Jinglong didn\'t offer any explanation.

Unable to remain silent any longer, Bai Shou interjected, \"Brother Chen
doesn\'t really have any good qualities, but his ability to convince
people to drink wine is unmatched!\"

Qi Jinglong turned to Bai Shou with a smile, and the latter immediately
put on a serious expression as he amended, \"That is Chen Ping\'an\'s
worst quality of all! He\'s a compulsive drunkard, and I\'m both furious
and embarrassed to have a brother like him!\"

Lu Sui was struck by a combination of amusement and exasperation, and
she couldn\'t help but wonder why Liu Jinglong had decided to take on
such an erratic disciple.

# Chapter 596: (2): Someone Has Challenged Chen Ping\'an

Sword of Coming

On top of the city wall, Sword Immortal Ku Xia was instructing Lin
Junbi, Yan Lü, and the others in their swordsmanship. Ku Xia was
teaching a set of sword techniques that were permitted to be taught to
outsiders on the Sword Qi Great Wall. Everyone sat on cushions,
listening intently to Ku Xia\'s guidance.

First, Ku Xia provided a rough breakdown of the meaning behind the sword
mantra, then went into extremely meticulous detail about several other
elements, including the route of spiritual energy circulation through
the key acupoints, and the method that one should use to draw upon and
recycle their spiritual energy.

After that, he took questions from everyone, but instead of answering
them himself, he left the task to Lin Junbi, who possessed the greatest
aptitude and learning ability among the students present. Only when Lin
Junbi\'s answers proved inadequate would Ku Xia make some additional
remarks.

What was strange about this set of top-tier sword techniques was that
they could only be used to their full potential in a place like the
Sword Qi Great Wall, a small world that was teeming with sword qi. One
could still use them in the Majestic World, but they would be much less
effective there. Most of the outsiders who had the opportunity to learn
these sword techniques generally weren\'t missing top-tier sword
techniques anyway, so there wasn\'t much point for them in learning
these sword techniques.

To put it in simpler terms, these sword techniques were too situational,
and even for an exceptional prodigy like Lin Junbi, who was blessed with
the fortune of an entire nation, he would only be able to make any
meaningful progress in the sword techniques in question on the Sword Qi
Great Wall.

Ku Xia was actually quite reluctant to teach this lesson, as the
instructor on this occasion was actually supposed to be the native sword
immortal, Sun Juyuan. However, Sun Juyuan was so disdainful of these
future pillars of the Shaoyuan Empire that he simply shirked his
responsibilities and refused to come. Ku Xia was quite a stubborn man,
and he initially wasn\'t willing to compromise and take Sun Juyuan\'s
place.

Eventually, Sun Juyuan became sick of his constant pestering, and he
delivered an ultimatum to Ku Xia, telling him that if the Shaoyuan
Empire still wanted the people they sent to the Sword Qi Great Wall to
be able to stay in the Sun Manor in the future, then they had best not
force him to do anything against his will.

Ku Xia took a glance at his direct disciple, Jiang Guancheng, and he
couldn\'t help but heave an internal sigh.

He was concerned about how simple-minded and straightforward his
disciple was, but he also didn\'t want his disciple to become too much
like Lin Junbi in his cultivation and personality. Besides, he much
preferred Jiang Guancheng to some of the petty and calculating young men
and women around him.

Ku Xia naturally had his reasons for choosing Jiang Guancheng as his
disciple, and one of his main considerations was that the Great Dao they
each pursued was quite close in nature. However, Jiang Guancheng was
like a rough gemstone that would require much more honing and refining.

Even though Lin Junbi was currently only seated on a cushion, with his
hands folded over one another on his lap and a relaxed and composed
smile on his face, he still had the appearance of an elegant and refined
immortal.

Yan Lü had been constantly and meticulously learning from Lin Junbi,
whether it be in the way that he treated others or the way in which he
regarded and interacted with the world around him. Even though Lin Junbi
was younger than him, Yan Lü felt like he had much to learn from him.

In the past, Yan Lü had adopted a very simple approach to how he saw
others. He either saw someone as smart or stupid. As for their morals
and values, he didn\'t care about those things at all. Those who were
useful to him were friends, while those who he couldn\'t make use of
were of no interest to him.

There were no stupid people among his peers on this journey; only those
who were smart enough or not quite there.

The ones who were not quite there included Jiang Guancheng and the
clueless girl who was infatuated with Lin Junbi, while those who were
smart enough included the group of \"foolish individuals\" who had
previously stood up for Lin Junbi.

It seemed like they were twisting the truth, but were those people
really oblivious to reality? What were their true intentions? Their
objective was simply to say meaningless things to appease Lin Junbi.

Even if it didn\'t work, it wasn\'t like they stood to lose anything.
Deep down, there was a very good chance they were hoping their support
would get to Lin Junbi\'s head, giving him a rush of blood to the head
and convincing him to challenge Chen Ping\'an to a battle to the death.
Even if neither side perished in battle, ideally, Lin Junbi would be
outmatched by Chen Ping\'an and suffer a setback to his Dao Heart as a
result of his defeat.

On the path of cultivation, Lin Junbi was undoubtedly going to be a
fierce competitor of theirs, so if they could use Chen Ping\'an to get
rid of him, then that would certainly be a desirable end result.

There were extremely complex networks of relationships in the Shaoyuan
Empire, and Lin Junbi had put on a far too spectacular display on this
trip thus far. Even though everyone had come from the Shaoyuan Empire,
they had all realized one thing, which was that if Lin Junbi were
allowed to fulfill his potential, then for at least the next few
centuries, all of the swordsmen of the Shaoyuan Empire would be put in
an awkward position where they would only be able to fight over second
place.

Lin Junbi of the Shaoyuan Empire was going to be the equivalent of Cao
Ci of the Middle Earth Divine Continent in the martial arts world, and
all of his contemporaries would be completely outshone by his
brilliance.

Aside from those people, Zhu Mei and Jin Zhenmeng fell into another
category of their own, and they were relatively less calculating.

However, Yan Lü didn\'t like to deal with people like them.

As opposed to Zhu Mei and Jin Zhenmeng, Yan Lü much preferred to try and
win over the calculating scoundrels who were constantly plotting the
downfalls of those around them.

Zhu Mei\'s background was not inferior to his own, while Jin Zhenmeng
was someone who possessed a resolute Dao Heart and pure sword intent. In
order to try to win them over, Yan Lü would have to give up many things
he was unwilling or unable to give up.

While serving as half a Dao mentor to his peers, Lin Junbi\'s mind was
already elsewhere.

There were sword immortals situated at set intervals along these city
walls.

As for those around him, Lin Junbi had never regarded them as his own
contemporaries, and that included even Yan Lü. In his eyes, they were
too weak in mental fortitude, too lacking in aptitude, and too pitiful
in intelligence.

Hence, their backers and backgrounds meant nothing. There were even
times when Lin Junbi was struck with the urge to laugh and tell them
that they should cherish this precious opportunity to travel and
cultivate alongside him. At the very least, he had still not left them
so far behind on the path of cultivation that he was completely out of
sight, and they were certainly very fortunate to be sitting with him as
equals atop these city walls.

Bian Jing wasn\'t attending Ku Xia\'s lesson with everyone else.
Instead, he had gone to the Mirage Market. There was what was supposedly
a sparring arena there, but in reality, it was more like the Northern
Complete Reed Continent\'s Temper Mountain, where all battles were to
the death.

However, it was also different from Temper Mountain in that only
individuals of the same cultivation base could face off against each
other in this sparring arena. Both combatants put their lives on the
line, and the winner would obtain the loser\'s entire wealth, as well as
a considerable cut of the gambling profits generated from the battle.

Battles between swordsmen were generally not the most spectacular, and
they didn\'t happen here all that often. Unless there was a sworn
vendetta between two swordsmen, they generally wouldn\'t come here to
settle their differences. Furthermore, battles between swordsmen often
ended instantaneously, so there really wasn\'t much to be seen.

The truly spectacular battles were the ones between swordsmen and other
Qi refiners, and of course, the best outcome for the spectators would be
if the Qi refiner were fortunate enough to take down a swordsman of the
same cultivation base at the cost of their own life.

A small group of swordsmen would come here to frequently do battle, and
some did so to hone themselves by placing themselves in life-threatening
peril, while others were simply here to earn money in order to better
nurture their flying swords.

As for why other Qi refiners were willing to set foot in the sparring
arena even at the risk of their own lives, that was naturally not
because they all had a death wish. Instead, they simply had no choice in
the matter. Almost all of these Qi refiners had been transported here in
secret on intercontinental ships, and they were vagrant cultivators from
all of the Majestic World\'s continents, or survivors from destroyed
immortal sects.

If they could win three battles against other Qi refiners of the same
cultivation base, then they would get to live. If they still dared to
participate in more battles after that, they would be able to win money
in accordance with the rules. If they could kill a swordsman, then that
single victory alone would be enough to grant them their freedom.

Certain Confucians had once expressed vehement opposition to this
arrangement, regarding it as a horrific violation of human rights. They
questioned why the Sword Qi Great Wall didn\'t enforce regulations to
stamp out this practice, instead allowing vagrant cultivators to be
transported there by the shipful just to lose their lives.

There was even once a woman from a wealthy clan on the Middle Earth
Divine Continent who had come to Stalactite Mountain on her clan\'s
intercontinental ship to stay at the Ape Rub Residence. She had
extremely powerful backers, and she went on an extravagant shopping
spree at the Ganoderma Inn, attracting a great deal of attention in the
process.

She was accompanied by two servants, a ninth tier martial artist who was
constantly with her, and an Upper Five Tiers Militarian cultivator who
protected her from the shadows. After watching the battles that took
place in the Mirage Market\'s sparring arena, she felt not only
sympathetic toward the Qi refiners who had been abducted to the Sword Qi
Great Wall from the Majestic World, but also the swordsmen from the
demon tribe who were being used as \"whetstones.\"

In her eyes, they had taken on human forms, so they were already humans,
and it was entirely far too inhumane to be treating them with such
cruelty and brutality. Thus, she kicked up a big fuss at the sparring
arena before departing in a proud fashion, feeling as if she had come
out on top.

That same day, her Militarian cultivator servant was brutally beaten by
a native sword immortal, while the ninth tier martial artist didn\'t
even dare to get involved because there were clearly more sword
immortals eagerly waiting in the wings.

The woman had no choice but to turn to Sword Immortal Sun Juyuan, who
was on good terms with her clan, but wasn\'t even able to secure an
audience with him. All of her belongings were thrown onto the street
outside the Sun Manor, and Sun Juyuan had dismissed her with a very
concise and to-the-point message. \"Piss off.\"

The woman was distraught and left the Sword Qi Great Wall in tears with
her servants. After returning to the Majestic World, she used the power
and wealth of her clan to gather up a bunch of prestigious scholars in
the literati world, calling upon them to openly denounce the Sword Qi
Great Wall\'s savage customs and traditions.

In her words, \"How are the swordsmen of the Sword Qi Great Wall any
different from the demons of the Savage World?\" In the wake of her
shenanigans, no one from her clan, her sect, and her entire empire was
ever permitted to set foot on Stalactite Mountain again. Indeed, not
just the Sword Qi Great Wall, but even Stalactite Mountain had been made
off-limits.

Anyone who was discovered trying to step onto Stalactite Mountain in
secret would be instantly struck down into the sea by the gatekeeper
sword immortal, and whether they lived or died would be entirely up to
the will of the heavens.

This had been a massive incident at the time, but the old great sword
immortal never said anything, so the Dong Clan had been very confident
in their handling of the matter, taking the old great sword immortal\'s
silence as a sign of approval for them to do as they pleased.

Not only did Bian Jing spectate some of the battles in the sparring
arena, but he had also placed some bets. There were different things
that one could bet on, most notably the outcomes of the battles and
which combatants would live or die. There normally wasn\'t much profit
to be made betting on the outcomes of the battles.

The regular gamblers here all possessed extremely keen eyes, so their
success rates at guessing the outcomes of battles were extremely high.
Hence, the bets that one could really stand to win or lose large sums of
money on were the bets on how long it would take for one or both of the
combatants to perish.

If one were fortunate enough to correctly guess that both combatants
would lose their lives, then they would often win enough money to cover
their wine costs for two or three years. This was quite a significant
sum, considering how expensive the immortal wine on the Sword Qi Great
Wall was.

Bian Jing was sitting in a corner of the packed spectator stands,
