drinking some wine as he waited in silence for the next battle to
commence.

The first combatant was a Sea Observation Tier swordsman who had come
here from the Majestic World for training purposes, and his opponent was
a demonic swordsman of the same cultivation base. The latter\'s clothes
were in tatters, and his entire body was riddled with injuries.

However, that didn\'t seem to affect his combat prowess at all. Demons
were extremely physically resilient to begin with, and those injuries
seemed to have only ignited his savage nature, working to further
enhance his powers as a swordsman.

This was not a common match-up.

Bian Jing had heard that in the Savage World, anyone who was able to
become a swordsman was referred to as a Great Dao talent, much like the
scholarly talents of the Majestic World.

Apparently, this demonic swordsman had secretly ventured onto a
battlefield in the wake of a major battle to try his luck at picking up
some broken swords. In the process, he was captured by the patrolling
swordsmen of the Sword Qi Great Wall and taken back here to be
imprisoned.

From there, he ended up just like many of the other captured demons,
thrown into the arena to provide entertainment to the spectators. If he
died, then that would be that, and if he lived, then he would be taken
back to the prison to recover from his injuries and await his next
battle.

Bian Jing was not surprised at all that many of the people who traveled
here from the Majestic World felt sympathetic toward these demonic
prisoners.

He wondered if those so-called kind-hearted people would still be
feeling sympathetic toward the demons when they breached the Sword Qi
Great Wall\'s defenses and took over the Majestic World.

Bian Jing\'s mind was entirely immersed in his internal small world, and
there was a being that was capable of seeing all of his thoughts lurking
deep within his mind\'s lake. The being grinned after reading Bian
Jing\'s thoughts, and its entire body was filled with an unmatched aura
of savagery.

Even though Bian Jing was a swordsman at the Golden Core Tier
bottleneck, just that slight grin from that almighty being was enough to
create a massive disturbance in his internal small world, causing all of
the spiritual energy in his acupoints to bubble and churn like boiling
water. Thankfully, even without Bian Jing\'s intervention, the being
suppressed its aura in order to avoid being detected.

If it were exposed in a place like this, then it would undoubtedly be
surrounded and killed by a whole host of sword immortals. If these sword
immortals were just some Unpolished Jade Tier small fry, then they
wouldn\'t be a concern at all, as the being would be able to gobble them
up with ease. Instead, what the being was worried about was the
possibility of being confronted by those old farts from the Dong, Qi,
and Chen Clans.

The being began communicating with Bian Jing through his mind\'s lake,
declaring, \"Once we succeed, my contribution will be enough for you to
secure a certain celestial weapon. On top of that, I\'ll fulfill our
earlier agreement and ensure that you become an Immortal Tier sword
immortal. As for whether you can reach the Ascension Tier, that will be
up to you.

"Once you reach the Ascension Tier and obtain a good sword, who cares
about the Majestic World or the Savage World? You\'ll be able to go
anywhere you please, and anywhere you go, the mountain summit will be
beneath your feet! When that time comes, the likes of Lin Junbi and Chen
Ping\'an will be nothing more than mere ants that won\'t even be worthy
of you to look down on.\"

\*\*\*

At the moment, there were two gates that granted passage between
Stalactite Mountain and the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Qi Jinglong and Bai Shou entered the Sword Qi Great Wall together with
Lu Sui and Ren Lingcong.

Bai Shou was so dizzy that he felt as if the entire world were spinning
around him, and he was resting on his haunches, dry-retching
incessantly, while Qi Jinglong gently held onto his shoulders to steady
him.

Ren Lingcong wasn\'t faring much better, but she was forcing herself to
maintain a composed facade. Lu Sui was holding onto her hand, helping
her stabilize the spiritual energy in her acupoints, and only then did
some color return to her deathly pale complexion.

At almost the exact same time, a woman left the Water Essence Palace on
her own through another gate to arrive on the Sword Qi Great Wall. As
soon as she arrived, her fist intent immediately began to flow over her
entire body, and she felt no discomfort whatsoever from the pervasive
aura of oppression and subjugation on the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Her original intention for this trip to the Sword Qi Great Wall was to
follow in Cao Ci\'s footsteps, staying in the thatched cottage that he
had constructed atop the city walls to hone her Vajra Body Tier
cultivation base. Her ultimate objective was to progress to the Far
Roaming Tier as the strongest seventh tier martial artist under the
heavens.

However, after hearing some things in the Water Essence Palace, she felt
like the will of the heavens was urging her to change her plans. Thus,
her current goal was to seek out the man that Cao Ci and Liu Youzhou had
mentioned on multiple occasions and challenge him. She was going to make
him lose three battles in a row once again!

[]{#chapter-74.xhtml}

# Chapter 597: (1): Peril Even Before the Battle

Sword of Coming

Bai Shou was still looking rather lethargic and sickly, temporarily
unable to acclimate himself to the environment on the Sword Qi Great
Wall, and Ren Lingcong was in a similar state.

This was why no Qi refiners below earth immortals liked to stay for long
periods of time on the Sword Qi Great Wall; the environment was simply
too inhospitable for them to bear. A young swordsman would fare much
better. Over time, they would ultimately stand to benefit from the
environment on the Sword Qi Great Wall, receiving nourishment to both
their soul and their flying swords.

However, for all Qi refiners outside of swordsmen, just the process of
expelling the sword intent from their internal small worlds was
extremely grueling and painstaking. Throughout history, there had been
no lack of cocky young Qi refiners who had visited the Sword Qi Great
Wall during periods of relative peace between battles.

They would trudge arduously to the Sword Qi Great Wall from Stalactite
Mountain, and by the time they were carried back to the gate on the
backs of their servants, they would\'ve already suffered a drop in
cultivation base.

\"If your friend is in the city, then how about you come with me to the
White Vein Residence on Taixiang Street? Sword Immortal Song Lü has some
deep connections to our Northern Complete Reed Continent, so I\'m sure
we\'ll be welcome there,\" Lu Sui suggested.

Lu Sui was aware that this proposal of hers was a little unreasonable,
but she was afraid that after parting ways with Liu Jinglong here, the
latter would become completely absorbed in his cultivation and forget
all about her.

She had come all the way to Stalactite Mountain to meet him, yet their
time together had been so short. If they were to part ways here, perhaps
they would only meet again when she visited him to bid farewell as she
prepared to return to Stalactite Mountain.

However, if they were to stay in Sword Immortal Song Lü\'s White Vein
Residence together, then even if Liu Jinglong went into seclusion and
refused to entertain any guests, at the very least, they would still be
under the same roof. Regardless of the weather outside, they would be
seeing the same piece of scenery, and that would give her some sense of
solace.

\"That sounds like a great idea!\" Bai Shou agreed. \"We can go pester
Sword Immortal Song Lü rather than disturb our sect leader\'s
cultivation.\"

Bai Shou felt rather apprehensive about meeting Sect Leader Han Huaizi
of the Great Emblem Sword Sect for the first time. On Graceful Peak, he
had overheard from conversations between many of his peers that Han
Huaizi was an extremely strict old man, and everyone spoke of him with a
sense of awe and veneration. In contrast, Disciplinary Elder Huang Tong
was a much less intimidating individual, but the problem was that Bai
Shou felt just as fearful and uneasy whenever he was in Huang Tong\'s
presence.

If Huang Tong were already so menacing and oppressive, Bai Shou was
worried that Han Huaizi would banish him from the ancestral hall before
he could even get a word in. Liu Jinglong was extremely respectful of
his seniors, so if Han Huaizi ordered him to expel Bai Shou from the
ancestral hall, then he would have no choice but to oblige.

It wasn\'t that Bai Shou cherished his status as Liu Jinglong\'s
disciple. Instead, he simply felt like it would be quite a waste to have
to leave behind the glory and authority that he had earned for himself
on Graceful Peak.

Qi Jinglong shook his head and said, \"I don\'t know Sword Immortal Song
Lü personally, so it would be inappropriate to suddenly show up on his
doorstep. It would also require Ms. Lu and her sect to redeem a favor
with Sword Immortal Song Lü in exchange for our accommodation, and that
would be too much to ask.

\"Besides, it\'s only right that we visit our sect leader before anyone
else. I also have to pay a visit to Senior Li to express my gratitude to
her. After our sparring match in the Great Emblem Sword Sect, she left
in quite a hurry, so I didn\'t get a chance to thank her.\"

There were many vacant private residences in the city where foreign
sword immortals could stay. They could choose any one of those vacant
residences to stay in, then simply notify Zhu An and Luo Shan. Of
course, they could also be invited to stay with native sword immortals,
and they were more than welcome to station themselves atop the city
walls if that was what they wished to do.

Han Huaizi and Huang Tong had slain many demons between them on the
southern battlefield, and their contributions on the battlefield had
earned the Great Emblem Sword Sect quite a large manor by the name of
the Armory. Thus, all of the disciples of the Great Emblem Sword Sect
had a place to stay on the Sword Qi Great Wall, and they wouldn\'t have
to arrange accommodation for themselves separately.

In contrast, Sect Leader Li Cai of Duckweed Sword Lake had only just
arrived, and she had no friends or acquaintances among the native sword
immortals, so she had chosen to stay in the Myriad Ravine Residence, the
residence previously occupied by the sword immortal from the Northern
Complete Reed Continent who had recently perished in battle.

She didn\'t fear the negative connotations of staying in such a
residence at all, and that had earned her some respect from many of the
native sword immortals.

\"In that case, I\'ll go and visit Sect Leader Han if I get the
chance,\" Lu Sui said with a smile.

\"That would be great,\" Qi Jinglong replied with a nod. \"Our sect
leader thinks very highly of you, and I\'m sure he\'d be very happy to
have you as a guest.\"

A wide and affectionate smile appeared on Lu Sui\'s face, while Ren
Lingcong took a deep breath and averted her gaze. She would be unable to
suppress her temper if she looked at the lovestruck Lu Sui and the
oblivious Liu Jinglong for too long.

Bai Shou was also feeling furious with Liu Jinglong.

*Does Celestial Maiden Lu care if the leader of our Great Emblem Sword
Sect would be happy to have her as a guest? Do you not see the way
she\'s looking at you? Surely she would\'ve been able to convey her
feelings properly even to a blind man at this point! Are you really that
oblivious, or are you just a really good actor?*

After the two duos parted ways, Qi Jinglong and Bai Shou set off for the
Armory. Qi Jinglong chose to make the journey on foot in order to cater
to Bai Shou, allowing the latter to take some time to familiarize
himself with the flow of the sword intent in this place.

All of a sudden, Qi Jinglong seemed to have realized something, and he
asked, \"Did I say anything to Ms. Lu just now that could be construed
as a little impersonal?\"

\"Are you kidding me right now?\" Bai Shou snapped.

Qi Jinglong heaved a sigh of relief. It seemed like he had done a fine
job.

\"There was not a single thing you said that *wasn\'t* impersonal!\" Bai
Shou concluded.

\"Oh, I see,\" Qi Jinglong mused.

\"Why do you not like Big Sister Lu, Liu Jinglong?\" Bai Shou asked.
\"There are a million good things about her and nothing bad! There are
countless handsome young prodigies on our Northern Complete Reed
Continent who are in love with her, yet why is it that she likes you,
and why do you not like her?\"

\"I don\'t know. There\'s no reason for it,\" Qi Jinglong replied in a
resigned manner.

The two of them traveled southward along the edge of the city for close
to a hundred kilometers before finally arriving at the Armory.

For cultivators of their caliber, even if they didn\'t fly atop their
flying swords, a journey of this length was still far from a lengthy
undertaking. Even though Bai Shou was not yet fully accustomed to the
oppressive aura of the Sword Qi Great Wall, he was still able to travel
much faster than the average layman.

The residences that they passed by on the way here mostly belonged to
sword immortals of the Upper Five Tiers, or were temporarily inhabited
by foreign sword immortals.

Sect Leader Han Huaizi of the Great Emblem Sword Sect was standing at
the entrance, and Qi Jinglong extended a respectful bow as he greeted,
\"Liu Jinglong of Graceful Peak pays his respects to Sect Leader Han
Huaizi.\"

Bai Shou gulped nervously, then imitated Liu Jinglong, extended a deep
bow as he greeted in a trembling voice, \"Sixteenth-generation direct
disciple of the Great Emblem Sword Sect\'s ancestral hall, Bai Shou of
Graceful Peak pays his respects to Sect Leader Han Huaizi!\"

Han Huaizi was the fourth leader of the Great Emblem Sword Sect, but the
heritage of the ancestral hall went back far further than that.

The Great Emblem Sword Sect didn\'t have a particularly long history on
the Northern Complete Reed Continent, but every single one of its
leaders had been sword immortals, and they almost always had a
complementary sword immortal like Huan Tong by their side, thereby
allowing them to maintain a solid position near the mountain summit of
the Northern Complete Reed Continent.

Furthermore, the sect had never been short on talent, even among some of
its lower-ranking members. For example, Liu Jinglong was far from a
senior figure in the sect because his master was only a
fourteenth-generation direct disciple of the ancestral hall, which was
why Bai Shou was only a sixteenth-generation disciple. However, in the
Majestic World, whenever the position of leader was passed down within a
sect, there was always a shift in the seniority hierarchy that followed.

If Liu Jinglong were to become the next sect leader, then his entire
branch in the ancestral hall\'s genealogical records would be
significantly elevated in status. As the first disciple of Graceful
Peak, Bai Shou would be automatically elevated into a sixth-generation
grandmaster of the Great Emblem Sword Sect thanks to his connection to
Liu Jinglong.

\"No need for formalities,\" Han Huaizi said with a smile. \"From now
on, wherever we go, we should follow the local customs and traditions.
There are only three of us in this residence anyway, so we don\'t have
to keep up appearances for anyone, isn\'t that right, Bai Shou?\"

Bai Shou had no idea how to respond. *Yes? No, surely that wasn\'t the
right answer. No? That\'s even more incorrect!*

He could only turn to Liu Jinglong for help with a pitiable look on his
face.

\"What\'s wrong?\" Qi Jinglong chuckled. \"I thought you weren\'t afraid
of anything or anyone; why has your courage suddenly dwindled to the
size of a grain of rice in front of our sect leader?\"

Bai Shou immediately regained his courage when regarding Liu Jinglong,
and he blurted out, \"That\'s what they named that little water monster
on Downtrodden Mountain!\"\[1\]

He then immediately recalled that he was still in the presence of the
sect leader, and he began sweating profusely as he implored, \"I\'m
sorry, Sect Leader! I shouldn\'t have said that! Please don\'t kick me
out of the Great Emblem Sword Sect!\"

Han Huaizi was both amused and exasperated. Thankfully, Liu Jinglong had
already informed him of Bai Shou\'s rather erratic nature in his letter.
Otherwise, Han Huaizi would've truly been caught a little off guard.

\"There are indeed many things that you can\'t say on the Sword Qi Great
Wall, so don\'t think that you\'re untouchable just because you\'re a
swordsman of the Great Emblem Sword Sect and Liu Jinglong\'s direct
disciple. Having said that, there\'s no need to be overly rigid and
restrained here in our sect\'s own residence. While cultivating here,
make sure to think lots and ask many questions,\" Han Huaizi said with a
smile.

Bai Shou was very much taken aback. This was completely different from
the stern and authoritative Sect Leader Han Huaizi that he had imagined.

\"This is when you should say \'Yes, Sect Leader,\'\" Qi Jinglong said
with an amused smile.

\"Yes, Sect Leader!\" Bai Shou hurriedly repeated.

Qi Jinglong could only shake his head in exasperation. Never had he seen
such an obedient Bai Shou.

After some more small talk, Han Huaizi led the duo into the Armory while
telling them about the history of this residence, including which sword
immortals had previously resided here, when they had died in battle, and
how they had died.

A sense of awe and veneration arose in Bai Shou\'s heart, and he
unconsciously slowed down his breathing and footsteps because he felt
like every breath that he took and every step that he walked was
disturbing the rest of the eternally slumbering sword immortals.

Han Huaizi took a subtle glance at Bai Shou\'s demeanor and expression,
then turned and gave Qi Jinglong a slight nod of approval.

\*\*\*

There was a young woman who was intentionally using her fist intent to
draw in hostile sword qi. She was wearing a pair of straw sandals and a
red robe, and her hair had been arranged into a neat and tight bun.

All she was carrying with her was a bag that contained some dry rations.
As opposed to entering the city, she went straight to the Sword Qi Great
Wall. She began rushing ahead at full speed when she was still some
distance away from the city walls, then sprang high up into the air,
landing over a hundred feet up the wall before continuing to rush her
way up its vertical surface.

With one final, forceful step, she launched herself upward, covering the
final few dozen feet in a single stride before drifting down onto the
top of the city wall.

From there, she made her way to the left. According to Cao Ci, the two
thatched cottages should be no more than fifteen kilometers apart from
each other.

Along the way, she didn\'t encounter any of the sword immortals because,
given the close proximity of this section of the city wall to the two
thatched huts, there was no need for any sword immortals to be stationed
here. With the old great sword immortal stationed nearby, no demon would
be able to set foot on this section of the city wall and hope to return
to the Savage World alive.

All of a sudden, the young woman\'s brows furrowed slightly as she
detected the immense sword qi on this section of the city wall.

It had to have been coming from Zuo You, the strange and reclusive sword
immortal who had shattered the Dao Hearts of countless prodigious
swordsmen before going out to sea.

However, as she drew close to the thatched cottage, she noticed that
there was a sword immortal with a youthful appearance standing in her
path, and they had already turned to observe her.

She continued onward without pause, taking a glance at the nearby
thatched cottage before turning her gaze back to the sword immortal,
then cupped her fist in a salute as she asked, \"Are you staying in this
thatched cottage, Senior?\"

\"If you don\'t mind, I can move out of this thatched cottage,\" Wei Jin
replied with a smile and a nod.

\"I *do* mind, so feel free to stay as you please, Senior,\" she said,
then stopped in her tracks before sitting down with her legs crossed.

She removed the bag of dry rations from her back, then pulled out a
piece of flatbread and began devouring it.

Wei Jin wasn\'t bothered, and he closed his eyes and resumed his
cultivation.

After eating the piece of flatbread, the young woman took a sip of
water, then asked, \"Would you happen to know where Sword Immortal Ku
Xia of the Shaoyuan Empire currently is on the city wall, Senior?\"

Wei Jin opened his eyes, then replied, \"The place where Sword Immortal
Ku Xia is stationed is about four hundred kilometers away from here.
Barring any mishaps, he should currently be teaching a lesson in
swordsmanship right now.\"

\"Thank you, Senior,\" the woman replied with a nod, then stood up and
hoisted her bag onto her back.

She began practicing her walking meditation alongside her fist
techniques as she set off in search of Ku Xia. She was frequently
covering a distance of several dozen feet with a single stride, but at
the same time, she was performing her fist techniques extremely slowly.

Along the way, she saw a giant golden bird that broke through the sea of
clouds above to cast an enormous shadow onto the city wall, and it was
as if day had suddenly transitioned into night. It descended next to a
white-robed sword immortal, and by the time it reached him, it had
already shrunk down to the size of a sparrow, allowing it to perch on
its owner\'s shoulder.

The sword immortal in question was lying lazily on his side on a bed,
facing the south while drinking some wine.

The woman only took a single glance at him before averting her gaze.

Meanwhile, Sword Immortal Ku Xia was seated on a cushion, while Lin
Junbi and the other young swordsmen were meditating with their eyes
closed, trying to harness the erratic and rapidly flowing pure sword
intent between heaven and earth. For them, harnessing the sword intent
in the environment was a much higher priority than absorbing the
spiritual energy in the air. However, Lin Junbi was the only one who was
making any significant progress.

Aside from him, even Yan Lü was struggling to find a reliable method to
harness the sword intent, only able to do so through blind luck. During
this time, someone was fortunate enough to capture a wisp of sword
intent and was ecstatic, but as soon as they became distracted by their
elation, that wisp of sword intent immediately began wreaking havoc in
their body. Sword Immortal Ku Xia was forced to intervene, using his
flying sword to expel the sword intent from the young swordsman\'s
internal small world in order to ensure their safety.

The young swordsman almost had the foundation of his Great Dao
compromised, and his complexion had turned deathly pale.

Ku Xia spoke to him through his mind\'s lake in a calm, soothing manner
to help the young man regain his composure and consolidate his sword
heart. As for the state of turmoil and unrest of the spiritual energy in
his acupoints, that was only a minor concern, and the young man could
resolve that problem on his own without Ku Xia\'s assistance.

These were all outstanding young talents who had been chosen from the
Shaoyuan Empire to travel to the Sword Qi Great Wall. If they couldn\'t
even take care of such a minor issue by themselves, then they may as
well pack their bags and return to Stalactite Mountain right away. In
any case, they would always be able to stay at the Plum Blossom Garden,
and they could wait there for everyone else before returning to the
Shaoyuan Empire together.

All of a sudden, Ku Xia rose to his feet and turned his gaze in a
certain direction. Upon spotting the young woman who was approaching
from a distance, a rare smile appeared on his face, and he stood up to
welcome her.

The young woman was a prolific traveler, and she had used many aliases
during her travels, but she had only one true name, and that was the one
recorded in the genealogical records of her clan\'s ancestral hall.

1\. A reminder that the Mili in Zhou Mili\'s name literally translates
to a grain of rice. ☜

[]{#chapter-75.xhtml}

# Chapter 597: (2): Peril Even Before the Battle

Sword of Coming

Her name was Yu Juanfu.

The Yu Clan of the Middle Earth Divine Continent was a top-tier clan
with an extremely long history.

It had once single-handedly given rise to the Great Clear Empire, an
empire even more powerful than the Shaoyuan Empire. After the fall of
the Great Clear Empire, it took no more than a hundred years for the Yu
Clan to support the founding of the even more massive Profound Secret
Empire.

Yu Juanfu and her fiance, Huai Qian, were both among a small handful of
the Middle Earth Divine Continent\'s top young prodigies, and both of
them had rather interesting stories. In order to escape her marriage
arrangement with Huai Qian, Yu Juanfu had fled to a set of ancient ruins
on the Golden Armor Continent, where she had practiced her fist
techniques on her own for many years.

Huai Qian had also gone out of his way to avoid the marriage
arrangement, traveling to the Northern Complete Reed Continent
specifically to hunt earth immortal swordsmen and collect their bonded
flying swords. Apparently, the patriarch of the Huai Clan had made a
rare appearance last year to seek out a good friend of his, who was also
one of the top ten cultivators of the Middle Earth Divine Continent, but
the reason for this was unclear.

Ku Xia\'s senior uncle, Zhou Shenzhi, was also among the top ten
cultivators of the Middle Earth Divine Continent, and he was even ranked
ahead of the patriarch of the Huai Clan. He was said to be someone whose
arrogance was outmatched only by his swordsmanship. On the Middle Earth
Divine Continent, Zhou Shenzhi was renowned for being a pain to deal
with. Even as his junior nephew, Ku Xia was still treated with nothing
more than disdain and hostility.

Their branch had been on very good terms with the Yu Clan for
generations, and Yu Juanfu was the junior whom Ku Xia liked most,
without exception.

Zhou Shenzhi had once candidly declared that all of the descendants of
his clan were utterly useless, and that not even a single one of them
could hope to match Yu Juanfu.

This was quite a scathing remark, considering the abundance of
exceptional prodigies among Zhou Shenzhi\'s descendants.

Zhou Shenzhi was so fond of Yu Juanfu that during the latter\'s first
three-year-long journey on the Middle Earth Divine Continent, Zhou
Shenzhi had secretly accompanied her the entire time, serving as her Dao
guardian. Unsurprisingly, her direct and foolhardy personality
eventually got her into big trouble, and she was targeted by an Immortal
Tier cultivator.

Zhou Shenzhi immediately intervened, severing one of the Immortal Tier
cultivator\'s hands, and the latter was forced to flee back to his
ancestral hall, where he sought refuge in a small world and refused to
come out. Zhou Shenzhi casually followed him back to his sect and forced
the entire sect to kneel before him.

He then strolled his way to the mountain summit from the foot of the
mountain, and along the way, anyone who dared to speak, raise their
heads, or display even the slightest hint of anger or indignation was
instantly killed.

However, not only was Yu Juanfu not grateful to Zhou Shenzhi for
standing up for her, but she also complained that he had gone overboard.
She told him that it would\'ve sufficed for him to simply scare off the
enemy, and that she should be the one to settle her own vendettas. Not
only was Zhou Shenzhi not enraged by her ingratitude, but he also
continued to escort her all the way to the Golden Armor Continent before
finally returning to the Middle Earth Divine Continent.

In the face of the approaching Ku Xia, Yu Juanfu stopped in her tracks,
then cupped her fist in a salute as she greeted, \"Yu Juanfu pays her
respects to Senior Ku Xia.\"

Ku Xia smiled and nodded, then asked, \"What are you doing here?\"

\"I\'m here to practice my fist techniques,\" Yu Juanfu replied.

She may as well have not replied at all.

However, Ku Xia wasn\'t bothered at all, and his response was just as
dry and devoid of substance. \"I can see that you\'ve already reached
the Vajra Body Tier. Keep it up.\"

Both fell silent, but neither found it uncomfortable or awkward in the
slightest.

Ku Xia wasn\'t a calculating individual, and he certainly wasn\'t hoping
to win Zhou Shenzhi\'s affection by looking after Yu Juanfu. Instead, he
was simply truly very fond of this exceptionally talented young woman.

Yu Juanfu was jokingly referred to as the junior who had claimed all of
Zhou Shenzhi\'s affection, and it was proclaimed that this was why Zhou
Shenzhi had no affection left for anyone else.

Yu Juanfu and Huai Qian\'s marriage agreement had been made when they
were both still children. The patriarch of the Huai Clan wasn\'t fond of
the bullheaded and foul-tempered Huai Qian, so he wasn\'t actually
unhappy at all that Yu Juanfu had run away to get out of the arranged
marriage.

Not only was the Yu Clan not criticized for not keeping her on a tighter
leash, but many of the seniors of the Huai Clan also consoled their good
friends in the Yu Clan by telling them that it was a good thing for
young people to see more of the world, and that there was no hurry to go
through with the arranged marriage.

Huai Qian was a cultivator, and even though Yu Juanfu was a pure martial
artist, given her aptitude, she was sure to live a long life, barring
any mishaps, so they could afford to take things slowly.

The two of them returned to where Ku Xia was teaching his lesson, and Ku
Xia gestured for Yu Juanfu to take a seat on one of the vacant cushions.
Yu Juanfu was happy to oblige, and she removed her bag from her back and
resumed her meal of flatbread and water.

Lin Junbi opened his eyes and flashed her a smile; she had clearly
noticed him but pretended not to have seen anything.

\*\*\*

Qi Jinglong was slowly walking along with his disciple on the street
outside the Ning Manor.

\"I hear that Chen Ping\'an is a real big shot these days,\" Bai Shou
said in a hushed voice. \"People around these parts call him Second
Shopkeeper, and his wife is also really well-known on the Sword Qi Great
Wall. Sword Immortal Li once told me in private that she can\'t bear to
see Ning Yao because whenever she does, she feels frustrated and
inferior.\"

Qi Jinglong didn\'t say anything.

They knocked on the door, which was opened by Nalan Yexing.

Qi Jinglong introduced himself, and a peculiar look appeared on Nalan
Yexing\'s face, but he then smiled and led the two of them to the Dragon
Slaying Cliff.

Chen Ping\'an had been cultivating diligently just now, but he had
already left the pergola and made his way down from the Dragon Slaying
Platform to welcome Qi Jinglong and Bai Shou.

Bai Shou was finally able to heave a sigh of relief after seeing Chen
Ping\'an. Otherwise, every day on the Sword Qi Great Wall felt like
torture. However, his joy was fleeting, and it was quickly dashed by the
thought that Chen Ping\'an was a certain someone\'s master. With that in
mind, Bai Shou immediately hung his head in dejection.

Nalan Yexing had already departed.

Chen Ping\'an led the two of them into the pergola, then smiled and
asked, \"You didn\'t get enough recognition on the Northern Complete
Reed Continent after your three battles, so you had to come to the Sword
Qi Great Wall to show off, is that it?\"

\"I had nothing better to do, so I came to see our sect leader and Sword
Immortal Li, and I thought I may as well pay you a visit too,\" Qi
Jinglong explained.

Chen Ping\'an tucked his hands up their opposite sleeves as he leaned
against the railing, and only then did he notice that Bai Shou seemed a
little despondent.

In the pergola, Bai Shou sat down next to Chen Ping\'an.

Qi Jinglong wasn\'t bothered by this. He knew that his disciple was a
little closer to Chen Ping\'an.

\"We paid a visit to Downtrodden Mountain prior to coming here,\" Qi
Jinglong revealed with a smile. \"After hearing that your first disciple
has only been training fist techniques for a year, Bai Shou offered to
fight her with only one hand while also restricting his cultivation base
to the Lower Five Tiers.\"

Chen Ping\'an could already guess the outcome of the battle.

\"That disciple of yours was still scared, so she asked him if he could
use only a single leg as well,\" Qi Jinglong continued.

\"And he agreed?\" Chen Ping\'an asked as he turned to Bai Shou with an
amused expression.

\"He did,\" Qi Jinglong confirmed with a nod. \"And he was really
pleased with himself, too. He told Pei Qian that he would stand still on
the spot and allow her to attack as she pleased.\"

\"You don\'t even need to tell me the outcome.\" Chen Ping\'an chuckled
with a shake of his head.

He then pulled out a flagon of Bamboo Sea Small World wine that he had
recently freeloaded off someone at the wine shop and declared, \"Let\'s
drink to Sword Immortal Bai Shou\'s resounding victory!\"

Qi Jinglong waved a hand to refuse the wine, while Bai Shou spat through
gritted teeth, \"I am absolutely certain that she definitely hasn\'t
been training martial arts for just a year or two! Be honest with me,
Chen Ping\'an! How many years has she been training in martial arts?
Ten?!\"

Despite Qi Jinglong\'s refusal, Chen Ping\'an still tossed him the
flagon of wine, then pulled out another one for himself. He had gotten
these flagons of wine for free anyway, so he could afford to be
generous. He removed the clay seal, then took a sip to discover that
this flagon of wine seemed to taste particularly good.

He sat with his legs crossed, resting one hand on the railing as he
asked, \"Was that disciple of mine wounded by your sword qi? Even if she
was, it\'s fine. In a sparring match, she deserves to be taught a lesson
if she\'s inferior to her opponent.\"

Bai Shou was glowering at Chen Ping\'an with such intense fury that his
eyes looked as if they were about to pop out of their sockets, and his
hands clenched up into tight fists before he slammed them down onto the
bench with a heavy sigh.

Qi Jinglong set the flagon of wine down beside himself, then smiled as
he recounted, \"Even though Bai Shou was the one who was sent flying,
that disciple of yours seemed even more dumbstruck than him! For some
reason, she was also really sheepish, and she crouched down beside him
with a concerned expression, as if she were worried that he was going to
die.

"She then ran away to meet up with her two friends, and they began
discussing how they were going to get themselves out of trouble. I only
listened in briefly on their conversation, and I overheard Pei Qian
saying that she couldn\'t use the excuse that someone tripped again. She
said that you didn\'t really believe her the last time that she used
that excuse, so she had to make up a more convincing story this time.\"

Bai Shou felt utterly humiliated as he leaned back against the railing
with his hands over his face.

\"I promised Pei Qian not to tell you about this, so you\'re not allowed
to punish or reprimand her over this,\" Qi Jinglong warned. \"Otherwise,
I\'ll never be able to set foot on Downtrodden Mountain again.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and nodded in response.

He wasn\'t planning to say anything to her about this anyway.

\"I don\'t care what happens; I\'m never going to Downtrodden Mountain
again,\" Bai Shou grumbled. \"If Pei Qian has the guts to come to the
Great Emblem Sword Sect, then I\'ll face her again there! As long as I
don\'t get complacent next time and use even half of my cultivation
base---\"

\"Alright, I\'ll tell Pei Qian that your next sparring match together
will be on Graceful Peak,\" Chen Ping\'an interjected with a nod and a
smile before Bai Shou had a chance to finish.

All of Bai Shou\'s bravado immediately disappeared, and a pitiable look
appeared on his face as he complained, \"Why do you have to show me up
like that? Just let me talk some smack while Pei Qian isn\'t around!\"

That kick from Pei Qian had been a truly vicious blow.

Not only was Bai Shou knocked to the ground with blood flowing out of
all of his orifices, but even after he forced his eyes open, he felt
completely drunk. In his eyes, it was as if there were several Pei Qians
crouched down before him, swaying back and forth in his field of view.

What was even more infuriating was what she said to him. At the time, he
had been absolutely livid. His lips were trembling, and his limbs were
spasming uncontrollably.

Pei Qian seemed to have noticed that his eyes were a bit out of focus,
so she called out to him in a \"kind-hearted\" fashion and said, \"Here!
Here! I\'m over here! Please be alright; I didn\'t do it on purpose. You
were bragging so much just now, so I didn\'t expect you to be so weak.
It\'s a good thing I was worried I would be harmed by your sword qi, so
I held back and used only about 70% to 80% of my strength. Otherwise,
how am I going to explain this to my master? Get up! Quit playing dead!
If it makes you happy, I can let you get a free hit on me as well, and
we\'ll call it even\...\"

Bai Shou didn\'t hear what she said next because he fell unconscious.

\"What a coincidence!\" Chen Ping\'an exclaimed with a smile. \"Before
you two came, I just so happened to send a letter to Downtrodden
Mountain, telling Pei Qian that she could come to the Sword Qi Great
Wall right away if she wanted.\"

Bai Shou immediately turned to Qi Jinglong and asked, \"When are we
going back to our sect, Master? With both of us away from Graceful Peak,
the thatched cottage is completely exposed to the elements, and just the
thought of that hurts me deeply.\"

This was the first time that Bai Shou had referred to Qi Jinglong as his
master outside of the Great Emblem Sword Sect\'s ancestral hall, and he
did so in an extremely sincere fashion.

Qi Jinglong thought about it for a moment, then replied, \"We have to at
least wait until Pei Qian gets here.\"

All of the color was instantly drained from Bai Shou\'s face.

\"By the way, I heard that there\'s an exceptional martial arts prodigy
from the Middle Earth Divine Continent called Yu Juanfu who wants to
challenge you,\" Qi Jinglong continued.

\"Not interested,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a smile.

\"Don\'t be fooled by the name; it\'s a chick,\" Bai Shou said in a
feeble voice.

Chen Ping\'an was rather taken aback to hear this.

\"She is indeed a woman,\" Qi Jinglong confirmed with a nod. \"She\'s
about the same age as you, and she\'s also a Vajra Body Tier martial
artist with an extremely solid foundation.\"

Bai Shou\'s eyes instantly lit up at the sight of the peculiar look that
had appeared on Chen Ping\'an\'s face, and he mused, \"I don\'t know if
she\'s good-looking or not, but you can always take a few extra glances
at her when you\'re fighting. In a fight between martial artists,
there\'s sure to be some physical contact, so\...\"

Bai Shou\'s voice trailed off into a suggestive silence, but all of a
sudden, he felt an unprecedented sense of peril that chilled him to the
bone, as if he had been plunged headfirst into a glacial pit. He turned
around in a stiff manner to see a woman slowly making her way into the
pergola.

She didn\'t say anything, and there wasn\'t even any displeasure on her
face, nor was she specifically targeting Bai Shou, but he felt as if a
tremendous weight were pressing down upon him, and he could sense that
this woman seemed to have the Great Dao of the entire Sword Qi Great
Wall on her side.

He felt like if she were to display even the slightest bit of
displeasure, then the entire Sword Qi Great Wall would become hostile to
him.

With that in mind, an anxious look appeared on his face as he turned his
gaze back to Chen Ping\'an and said, \"Make sure you don\'t try any
funny business! Rules must be followed in sparring matches between
martial artists, and it\'s not an opportunity for you to get all
touchy-feely! Of course, I\'d say the best thing to do is to turn down
her challenge altogether. There\'s no need to fight her at all.\"

Chen Ping\'an pressed a hand down onto Bai Shou\'s head as he smiled and
warned, \"I\'m going to twist your head off if you keep talking.\"

[]{#chapter-76.xhtml}

# Chapter 598: (1): One-Punch Knockdown

Sword of Coming

\"Greetings, Ms. Ning. I am Liu Jinglong of the Great Emblem Sword
Sect.\" Qi Jinglong introduced himself with a smile as he rose to his
feet.

\"It\'s a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Liu,\" Ning Yao replied with a smile
of her own.

Bai Shou slapped Chen Ping\'an\'s hand away from his head, and Chen
Ping\'an tucked his hands up their opposite sleeves.

However, before he did so, he had already secretly extended a finger and
pushed the flagon of wine sitting on the bench to Bai Shou\'s side. With
one flagon of wine beside Qi Jinglong and the other beside Bai Shou, it
would appear as if he were the only non-drinker of the trio.

Ning Yao sat down beside Chen Ping\'an, while Bai Shou went to sit
beside Qi Jinglong, taking the flagon of wine with him as he went.

\"I visited the Northern Complete Reed Continent in the past, but I
didn\'t go to the Great Emblem Sword Sect,\" Ning Yao said. \"Instead, I
spent most of my time on the Northern Complete Reed Continent traveling
through the mortal world.\"

\"You can come visit the Northern Complete Reed Continent again with
Chen Ping\'an if you get the chance,\" Qi Jinglong said. \"There\'s some
fine scenery to be seen on Graceful Peak.\"

\"It\'ll be difficult for me to arrange a trip anytime soon,\" Ning Yao
said with a shake of her head.

\"That\'s true,\" Qi Jinglong agreed with a nod.

Ning Yao was silent for a moment, then turned her gaze to Bai Shou, who
unconsciously sat up a little straighter. \"You\'re Mr. Liu\'s only
disciple, so why not work hard on honing your swordsmanship?\"

Even though her words were framed as a question, there was no sense of
inquisition in her voice at all.

Bai Shou was like a child in a school having his homework checked by his
teacher, and he replied in a timid voice, \"I\'ll be sure to work hard,
Big Sister Ning!\"

\"For swordsmen, cultivation is a matter of looking into your own
heart,\" Ning Yao preached. \"If you look solely at your sword, then you
will lose your way and stray further and further away from the Great Dao
of heaven and earth.\"

Bai Shou didn\'t dare to do anything but nod in response.

Qi Jinglong didn\'t feel it was appropriate for Ning Yao to preach to
his disciple.

Perhaps it would be rather arrogant for anyone else of Ning Yao\'s
cultivation base to be preaching to Bai Shou, but on the Sword Qi Great
Wall, Ning Yao was no less qualified than any sword immortal to be
instructing others in swordsmanship. Furthermore, Ning Yao wasn\'t
preaching in order to establish a position of superiority for herself.

Instead, she was only willing to impart this valuable advice because she
was in the presence of a friend of Chen Ping\'an\'s, and a disciple of
Chen Ping\'an\'s friend, both of whom were swordsmen who would stand to
benefit from her advice.

\"I\'m going back into seclusion,\" Ning Yao declared as she stood up to
depart.

\"Please do,\" Qi Jinglong said as he also rose to his feet. \"We\'ve
already taken up too much of your time.\"

\"We still have some precious wine at home. If you want it, just talk to
Grandpa Nalan,\" Ning Yao said to Chen Ping\'an.

\"I don\'t drink, Ms. Ning,\" Qi Jinglong hurriedly said.

\"There\'s no need to be shy, Mr. Liu,\" Ning Yao said with a smile.
\"Even if there isn\'t enough wine in our Ning Manor, our Sword Qi Great
Wall has an abundance of both swordsmen and wine.\"

\"That\'s right,\" Chen Ping\'an agreed with a nod as he secretly gave
Ning Yao a thumbs-up.

He had written down whether Qi Jinglong liked to drink wine or not in
his travel journal, so Ning Yao was naturally already aware.

As soon as Ning Yao left, Bai Shou immediately collapsed onto the
railing in relief, then turned to Chen Ping\'an with a resentful
expression and asked, \"Are you not afraid of her, Chen Ping\'an? I was
so scared I felt like I was about to die! I wasn\'t even that nervous
when I met our sect leader!\"

\"What\'s there to be scared of?\" Chen Ping\'an asked. \"I\'m a man;
why should I be scared of my wife?\"

Qi Jinglong suddenly turned to the spot where the walkway was connected
to the Dragon Slaying Cliff, and Chen Ping\'an immediately turned in the
same direction with an anxious expression. However, Ning Yao was nowhere
to be seen.

Realizing that he had been tricked, Chen Ping\'an scoffed, \"I\'m not
sure if your swordsmanship has improved any since you reached the Upper
Five Tiers, but you\'ve certainly picked up some sly little tricks!\"

\"Be honest with me,\" Qi Jinglong said with a smile. \"How many people
on the Sword Qi Great Wall right now think of me as a complete drunkard?
Think carefully about your answer before you tell me.\"

\"I\'ve only been on the Sword Qi Great Wall for a short time, and I\'ve
been really busy every day,\" Chen Ping\'an replied. \"I have to
practice my fist techniques every day, and I also have to make frequent
trips to the top of the city walls to learn swordsmanship from my senior
brother. If I\'m not careful, I could easily end up bedridden for half a
month, and I also have to dedicate twenty hours every day to Qi
refinement.

"That\'s how I was able to make a breakthrough, but even then, I\'m
still only a fifth tier cultivator. There are so many sword immortals on
the streets of the Sword Qi Great Wall; do you not think that a mere
fifth tier cultivator like me would be embarrassed to frequently go out
in public? How many people do you think I could\'ve possibly acquainted
myself with during this past year that I\'ve been here?\"

\"Sounds like you\'re trying to make a lot of justifications for
yourself,\" Qi Jinglong remarked.

Chen Ping\'an had no response to that. He had indeed overdone it a
little.

\"I\'ve heard a great deal about the Ning Clan\'s Dragon Slaying
Platform and Minute Small World,\" Qi Jinglong said as he stood up with
a smile. \"We\'ve already seen the Dragon Slaying Platform, so let\'s go
to the training ground next.\"

\"We\'ve seen the Dragon Slaying Platform? Where?\" Bai Shou asked with
a puzzled expression.

\"Why even have eyes if you\'re not going to use them?\" Chen Ping\'an
chuckled.

\"I\'ll let you off the hook this one time out of respect for Big Sister
Ning!\" Bai Shou snapped.

\"Look down,\" Chen Ping\'an said as he tapped his foot on the ground
below.

Bai Shou was instantly astonished.

\"You mean to tell me this entire hill is made out of Dragon Slaying
Platform?!\"

Chen Ping\'an had already left the Dragon Slaying Cliff with Qi Jinglong
to go to the Minute Small World.

Bai Shou didn\'t go with them. He was much more interested in the Dragon
Slaying Platform than whatever Minute Small World. Back in the Armory,
he had heard that there was an extremely massive piece of Dragon Slaying
Platform here, but he had been limited by his imagination, and he had
thought that it would only have been the size of a table at the very
most.

Never had he imagined that it would be the size of a house! He got down
onto his hands and knees with his backside raised up high, then gently
rubbed the ground with his hand. After that, he gently knocked on the
ground with his knuckles, but they made no sound.

In the end, he mused to himself, \"Holy crap! Big Sister Ning\'s clan is
rich!\"

Walking alongside Chen Ping\'an in the Minute Small World, Qi Jinglong
said, \"I heard quite a few stories about you while I was at the Armory.
Not only is your title of Second Shopkeeper renowned across the entire
Sword Qi Great Wall, but I also heard about it even in the Spring Banner
Inn.\"

\"The bad news always seems to spread much further than the good.\" Chen
Ping\'an sighed in a resigned manner.

\"Can we speak here?\" Qi Jinglong asked.

\"Go ahead. You don\'t have to worry about prying ears here,\" Chen
Ping\'an replied.

There was Nalan Yexing keeping an eye on things, not to mention that the
two of them were in the Minute Small World. Even if a sword immortal
intended to eavesdrop on them, they would have to be wary of having to
face the wrath of three formidable parties.

Even after suffering a drop in cultivation base, Nalan Yexing was still
an Unpolished Jade Tier sword immortal. Furthermore, Qi Jinglong was an
Unpolished Jade Tier sword immortal himself, and he also had the backing
of Sect Leader Han Huaizi, Sword Immortal Li Cai, and the entire
Northern Complete Reed Continent at large. As for Chen Ping\'an, he only
had a single backer in the form of Zuo You, but that was already more
than enough.

After being assured that this was a secure place to speak, Qi Jinglong
said, \"You did all three of those things very well. The principles that
can be learned free of charge and picked up from the ground are often
ignored, and even if they *are* picked up, they\'re generally taken for
granted.\"

\"Continue,\" Chen Ping\'an encouraged with a serious expression.
\"You\'re an outsider as far as the Sword Qi Great Wall is concerned, so
it\'ll be good for me to hear your perspective.\"

\"For the wine shop that you opened, the keys are the couplets and the
accompanying horizontal banner, as well as the safety tablets on the
walls,\" Qi Jinglong said. \"Even for those who visit the shop solely to
drink, they\'ll still occasionally catch glimpses of the names and
sentiments written on those tablets.

"At the silk shop, it goes from the Seal Manual of the Hundred Sword
Immortals to the Seal Manual of the Two Hundred Sword Immortals, then to
the folding fan. As a storyteller sitting at the corner of the street,
you freeload some sunflower seeds and snacks from the children.\"

After speaking on those three things, Qi Jinglong began to provide his
insights, continuing, \"Swordsmen are the wealthiest Qi refiners under
the heavens, but also the neediest. In order to try to fill the
bottomless financial pit of nurturing their bonded flying swords,
countless swordsmen sell everything in their possession and live as if
they\'re broke. Even on the occasions when they have some spare money to
spend, there\'s not much on the Sword Qi Great Wall that they can spend
it on.

"For men, it comes down to drinking and gambling, while for women,
they\'ll perhaps go shopping and buy some things that catch their eye.
However, this type of spending was often not something that a woman felt
worthy of telling others about. The cheap Bamboo Sea Small World wine,
or Azure Divine Mountain wine, can generally only draw in customers once
or twice, but may not be enough to keep them coming back, so you won\'t
have as many regular customers as the established restaurants and wine
shops.

"However, regardless of one\'s reason for doing so, as long as they hang
up a safety tablet on the wall, they\'ll feel some type of sentimental
attachment to your wine shop. On the surface, such an attachment seems
so minor that it\'s entirely inconsequential, but that\'s not the case.
These safety tablets are inscribed using sword qi, and the sword
immortals who make those inscriptions do not do so lightly. The
inscriptions on those tablets are not just errant remarks that don\'t
mean anything.

"Instead, for some sword immortals and swordsmen, they serve as their
final words, something that they\'ve left behind for their peers to
remember them by should they suffer untimely demises on the southern
battlefields. In my eyes, the wine shop is made up of more than just
shoddy chairs and tables, subpar wine, and free yangchun noodles and
pickled vegetables. Instead, whenever I go there, I would feel as if I
were surrounded by the sword intent of all of the swordsmen and sword
immortals who have visited the shop.

"I would browse through the safety tablets with reverence and leave one
of my own in the hopes that those who come after me will see my safety
tablet and learn that I was once here. Of course, as long as business is
decent in the wine shop, you\'ll be able to hear many stories about the
Sword Qi Great Wall there as the shop\'s second shopkeeper, thereby
allowing you to gain an understanding of the complex circumstances of
the Sword Qi Great Wall far quicker than you would\'ve otherwise been
able to.\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded as he added, \"In addition to that, I also wanted
to help Ning Yao\'s friend, who is now my friend. Her name is Die Zhang,
and I wanted to help her attract more business. That was actually my
earliest original intention, and everything else only gradually came to
me over time. It was a very natural process. The ideas came to me one
after another without any real planning on my part, and it was as if it
was all meant to be.\"

\"Given your honesty, you will surely have a very clear and pure sword
heart when you become a swordsman in the future, enough to become a
guest elder at our Great Emblem Sword Sect,\" Qi Jinglong said with a
smile.

\"Did you not try to persuade Sect Leader Han?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

\"I did, and all I received for my efforts was a dressing down,\" Qi
Jinglong replied with a wry smile. \"I didn\'t actually want to go, but
Disciplinary Elder Huang Tong made a request of me to do so, and I
couldn\'t just turn down a senior\'s request.\"

Qi Jinglong had forgotten his flagon of wine on the bench, so Chen
Ping\'an had picked it up for him, and it was now coming in useful.

He offered the flagon of wine to Qi Jinglong and said, \"There\'s a
saying here that a sword immortal who doesn\'t drink will drop back down
to the Nascent Tier, so you need to start drinking right away! Perhaps
it\'ll even allow you to make a breakthrough to the Immortal Tier. You
can then challenge Sect Leader Han to a sparring match, but tell him to
restrict his cultivation base because you\'re much younger than him.
That way, you\'ll be able to beat him back to the Northern Complete Reed
Continent! Isn\'t that a great idea?\"

Qi Jinglong accepted the flagon of wine, but didn\'t drink from it, and
he had no intention of entertaining Chen Ping\'an. Instead, he continued
to speak on the previous subject.

\"Seals were originally ornaments placed on the desks of scholars, and
they align themselves best with a scholar\'s teachings and what they
stand for. In the Majestic World, it\'s extremely rare for a scholar to
entrust their seal and its inscription to others. Hence, even though you
cast out those two hundred seals, the Seal Manual of the Hundred Sword
Immortals and the Seal Manual of the Two Hundred Sword Immortals, to be
sold seemingly without any discretion, it\'s actually a very thoughtful
gesture.

"However, without the wine shop serving as a hub of information,
allowing you to examine the thoughts and life paths of so many sword
immortals and earth immortal swordsmen, there\'s no way you would\'ve
been able to achieve any of this. Right now, people are eagerly awaiting
the next seals to be released, and they\'ll be immediately snapped up on
release, even if the inscriptions that they bear aren\'t necessarily a
good fit for the buyer.

"That\'s because everyone knows that the seals sold in the silk shop are
quite cheap to begin with, and if one were to purchase ten seals, then
they could easily resell them for a profit. Hence, when you made the
first Seal Manual of the Two Hundred Sword Immortals, you were actually
concerned that this was only going to be a small deal on the Sword Qi
Great Wall, and that as soon as you released the third batch of seals,
you would flood the market to create an excessive supply, perhaps even
negatively impacting the value of the previous seals that you\'ve
already released.

"This is why you decided to change tack, and instead of pledging
yourself to engraving the next one hundred seals, you switched to
selling folding fans instead, and you\'ve been a lot more casual and
arbitrary with the text that you\'ve decided to inscribe upon these
fans. In doing so, you\'ve created something similar to slightly
inferior forgeries. Not only do folding fans appeal to female buyers,
but they\'ll also serve as a point of comparison for those who\'ve
previously purchased seals, convincing them that the seals they\'ve
purchased were worthy investments.\"

\"What you\'ve said is all correct, but there\'s one thing that I have
to add,\" Chen Ping\'an said. \"Another reason why I decided to switch
to making folding fans was to hide my intentions. Otherwise, if a sword
immortal sees through my intentions, they\'ll think I\'m too calculating
and develop a negative image of me. If I\'ve already gone to such great
lengths to cover my tracks, yet someone still manages to see through my
intentions, then it won\'t really matter at that point.

"There\'s no need to pursue absolute perfection in any one thing, and I
should give some sword immortals the chance to realize what I\'ve been
up to. The reason why I don\'t mind is that for all of the seals and
fans that I\'m selling, my original intention was never to sell them to
that select group of the most wise and introspective sword immortals.

"Of course, if someone is able to see the truth, yet does not reveal it,
and is even willing to accept a seal that catches their eyes despite
this, then they will have my utmost respect. If I get the chance, I
would apologize to them in person for involving them in my scheme.\"

\"Your thought process is correct, and you\'ve clearly thought things
through very thoroughly,\" Qi Jinglong remarked with a nod.

\"As expected of someone who has visited my Downtrodden Mountain!\" Chen
Ping\'an praised as he gave Qi Jinglong a firm pat on the shoulder.
\"That visit certainly didn\'t go to waste! That little runt, Bai Shou,
is far too inept in comparison, and I can tell that he barely learned
anything! The way that he tried to backtrack earlier was far too stiff
and unnatural. He was trying to get me out of trouble with Ning Yao, but
all he did was dig me into an even deeper hole!\"

In a rare display, Qi Jinglong took a sip of wine unprompted, then cast
his gaze in the direction of the wine shop. Not only were there
swordsmen and wine in that direction, but there was also Yanchi Alley
and Spirit Rhino Alley, among other shoddy alleys, as well as many
children who knew nothing of the Majestic World, but had grown sick of
seeing sword immortals.

Qi Jinglong wiped his lips with the back of his hand, then said,
\"Without at least several dozen years, perhaps over a century of
effort, what you\'re doing now is largely pointless.\"

Chen Ping\'an was silent for a long while, then replied, \"I feel bad if
I don\'t do anything; it\'s as simple as that. That is the extent of my
reasoning behind what I\'m doing, and not much thought has gone into it
at all.\"

Qi Jinglong raised his flagon of wine, seemingly intending to share a
drink with Chen Ping\'an, but the latter scoffed, \"Who do you think I
am, some kind of actual deity? I had to pull out all my tricks just to
get these two flagons of wine! I gave one to you, and Bai Shou took the
other one, so I don\'t have any left!\"

Qi Jinglong lowered the wine flagon and didn\'t drink from it.

[]{#chapter-77.xhtml}

# Chapter 598: (2): One-Punch Knockdown

Sword of Coming

\"You mentioned earlier that you sent a letter encouraging Pei Qian to
come to the Sword Qi Great Wall; what about Chen Nuanshu and Zhou
Mili?\" Qi Jinglong asked. \"If you\'re not permitting them to come as
well, did you explain why in your letter? Given Pei Qian\'s devotion to
you, I\'m sure you can anticipate that she\'ll treat your letter like an
imperial edict, and she\'ll be sure to show it off to her two friends as
well.\"

\"Of course I did,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a smile. \"This is no
laughing matter.\"

\"Good,\" Qi Jinglong approved with a nod.

Chen Ping\'an led Qi Jinglong out of the Minute Small World, then said,
\"Come with me. I wanna show you something.\"

At this point, Bai Shou had already made his way down from the Dragon
Slaying Cliff and had walked quite a few laps around the hill. He felt
it would be a great idea to find someone to draw a pair of portraits for
him, one of him at the foot of the mountain and the other of him seated
in the pergola.

Once he returned to the Great Emblem Sword Sect, he would show the
portraits to everyone on Graceful Peak, and they would surely be
astonished. It seemed that if he truly wanted to build a reputation for
himself, then he couldn\'t rely on Liu Jinglong. Instead, it was much
better to turn to Chen Ping\'an.

Bai Shou spotted Chen Ping\'an and Qi Jinglong as they emerged from the
training ground, so he decided to follow them as they made their way to
Chen Ping\'an\'s residence.

Upon seeing the pitiable little residence, a sense of sorrow instantly
welled up in Bai Shou\'s heart, and he lamented, \"My heart goes out to
you, Brother Ping\'an.\"

Chen Ping\'an raised a leg, and Bai Shou immediately fled the scene.

He felt a little embarrassed by his own cowardly display, so he casually
strolled his way into the residence, then sat down on a chair that was
already placed under the eaves and pretended like he owned the place.

He knew that he had to cherish what little time he had left, given that
Pei Qian was very likely going to show up any day now.

He could tell that Chen Ping\'an and Qi Jinglong were discussing
important matters rather than fooling around, so he knew that it was
best for him to stay away.

Chen Ping\'an led Qi Jinglong into the room with the two tables. On one
table were some folding fan frames that were not yet fully polished, as
well as many blank, uninscribed fan leaves.

There were also quite a few blank seals and some sheets of paper covered
in neat, small text, containing drafts of the contents to be inscribed
on the seals and fans.

On the neighboring table was a map of all of the dragon kilns in the
Dragon Spring Prefecture.

At the moment, there were many places in the Dragon Spring Prefecture
that were still shrouded in mystery, such as the mountain of porcelain,
the immortal tomb, and the entrances of the dragon kilns. Those areas
were concealed by cloud and mist, and even the passengers of immortal
ships that traveled over the prefecture were unable to see those
landmarks in their full glory.

Qi Jinglong gently set his wine flagon down onto the table, and as he
examined the map, he discovered that the placement of the dragon kilns
was far from random. Instead, they formed a long, curved line, and there
was a small circle on the map some distance away from the line.

Qi Jinglong pointed at the circle and asked, \"Is this the Iron Lock
Well?\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded in response.

Qi Jinglong stared at the map for a moment, then suddenly declared,
\"This is a Jewel-Bearing Dragon Ascension Diagram.\"

\"You really do have an incredible eye,\" Chen Ping\'an praised.

\"I\'m decently well versed in formations and talismans, so I\'m
naturally going to be a little more perceptive than you when it comes to
things like this,\" Qi Jinglong replied in an indifferent manner.

\"You\'re speaking in the most nonchalant tone while talking about how
extraordinary you are. This is a whole new level of showing off.\" Chen
Ping\'an chuckled.

Qi Jinglong gently stroked his fingers over the map with a serious
expression, and his eyes narrowed slightly as he said, \"Even just by
looking at this map, I can feel intense resentment and killing intent.
It seems like a true dragon must\'ve really wreaked havoc in the area in
its dying moments.\"

Chen Ping\'an tucked his hands up their opposite sleeves, then leaned
forward to rest his chin on the table.

Qi Jinglong examined the names of the dragon kilns one by one, and he
had one hand clasped behind his back, while his other hand gently traced
over the dragon kilns on the map.

\"As I suspected, all of these kiln entrances were constructed on the
remains of the true dragon corresponding to the important acupoints on
its spinal column,\" he remarked. \"As a result, the pieces of bonded
porcelain fired in each dragon kiln naturally possess different innate
abilities. The dragon is said to have had nine children, every single
one of which is different from all of the others. During my visit to the
small town, I went to that arched bridge, as well as the swordsmithing
shop that Sage Ruan Qiong opened on the bank of the Dragon Whisker
River.

"Those seven wells are rather unremarkable in appearance, but not only
do they bear some Buddhist karma, but they are also distantly connected
to the remains of the true dragon, and they primarily serve a
subjugation purpose. Originally, they were high up in the heavens, but
after the Jewel Small World fell and became part of the Great Li Empire,
the wells became lodged in the earth instead.

"The western mountains chosen by the Dragon Spring Sword Sect serve as
formation eyes that draw fortune into the seven wells, creating a
massive formation that funnels an immense amount of mountain and water
fortune into Divine Elegance Mountain, where the sect\'s ancestral hall
is situated. The placement of many of these dragon kilns actually goes
against conventional wisdom, yet somehow, all of the prior setup has
allowed it to work, and it really is an extraordinary feat.

"For example, if we go by the principles championed by the Naturalists
of the Majestic World, this Prosperous Scholar Kiln should be moved down
by half an inch on the map, or the neighboring Thriving Martial Kiln
should be moved an inch to the right. Only then will they be in balance
and complement one another.

"However, those seemingly minor changes would\'ve been significant
compromises. It\'s a real shame that I didn\'t take a closer look at the
placement of the wells during my visit to the Dragon Spring Prefecture.
I should\'ve taken to the sky to examine the entire area from above.\"

Chen Ping\'an understood every single word that came out of Qi
Jinglong\'s mouth, but when strung together, he had no idea what the
latter was talking about. However, he remained silent, merely nodding
along with a smile, refusing to contribute or ask any questions.

All of a sudden, Qi Jinglong turned to him and asked, \"What are your
eight characters? Without that information, this puzzle is too difficult
for me to solve. It\'s too broad and too deep. Only by using you as an
incision point will I have any chance of making any inroads.\"

Chen Ping\'an set a handful of sunflower seeds down onto the table,
which he had also gotten for free, then shook his head.

\"You\'re already trying to figure things out, so why not let me help
you?\" Qi Jinglong asked with a tightly furrowed brow. \"If I were still
a Nascent Tier swordsman, then I would understand, but now that I\'ve
reached the Upper Five Tiers, the chances of any mishaps occurring are
significantly reduced.\"

\"I\'m just not gonna tell you,\" Chen Ping\'an grinned as he ate some
sunflower seeds. \"What\'re you gonna do about it? Does that piss you
off?\"

Qi Jinglong was largely unbothered as he sat down in a chair and
continued to closely examine the incredibly complex ascending dragon
diagram. Occasionally, he would make a hand seal while simultaneously
flipping through the pages of the two books on the table.

All the while, Chen Ping\'an continued to eat sunflower seeds just for
something to do.

\"Do you know of Ms. Lu from Water Scripture Mountain?\" Qi Jinglong
suddenly asked.

\"Of course, I\'ve heard of Celestial Maiden Lu from Water Scripture
Mountain, but she definitely doesn\'t know of me, so why do you ask?\"
Chen Ping\'an replied with a puzzled expression. \"Oh? Don\'t tell
me\... Did she come to Stalactite Mountain with you? That\'s a very
impressive amount of sincerity that she\'s putting on display! If you
ask me, it\'s about time that you settled down. You\'re really getting
up there in age, so it\'s about time that you found a Dao partner. On
the Sword Qi Great Wall, even the drunkards and gambling addicts look
down on single men.\"

\"She didn\'t come with me; we just so happened to meet on Stalactite
Mountain,\" Qi Jinglong explained. \"After that, we came to the Sword Qi
Great Wall together.\"

Chen Ping\'an rolled his eyes in exasperation, then said, \"Think about
what you just said before you speak to me again.\"

A look of realization appeared on Qi Jinglong\'s face, and he asked,
\"What should I do then?\"

\"There\'s no need to do anything,\" Chen Ping\'an replied in a
nonchalant manner. \"Just act natural. If she wants to see you, then go
and meet her. There\'s no need to put on a cold and inhospitable facade
to deter her. It\'s not like she owes you any money; she simply has
feelings for you, and that\'s no reason to treat her badly. If you
don\'t want any misunderstandings, you can simply not actively request
to meet her.

"However, when you part ways, regardless of which one of you leaves the
Sword Qi Great Wall first, you should go to meet her and bid her
farewell. You don\'t have anyone that you like at the moment anyway, so
you can be more carefree and at ease. If, instead, you go out of your
way to act really out of character around her, that\'s only going to
make it more likely for her to misunderstand.\"

Qi Jinglong was enlightened.

Chen Ping\'an made his way to the neighboring table and began carefully
considering what he was going to write on the blank fan leaf.

After some contemplation, he wrote: \"For a lovestruck young maiden, a
dashing young prince is akin to a refreshing breeze in the summer
heat.\"

It was a rather effeminate piece of prose, and there was certainly
nothing sophisticated or profound about it. These fans were going to be
sold in the silk shop, so he had to cater to his target demographic. He
could put a great deal of thought into these inscriptions and make them
very deep and thought-provoking, but that would hardly be appealing at
all to the women visiting the silk shop, and the fans could end up
having no takers.

Qi Jinglong looked down at the inscription on the fan with a speechless
expression.

He really wanted to take back most of the praise that he had given to
Chen Ping\'an earlier. He had been a traveling salesman throughout the
entire course of his journey across the Northern Complete Reed
Continent, and even now, he was still clearly constantly thinking about
how to make money!

\"Even while working hard in your mental cultivation, you still haven\'t
forgotten your roots as a traveling salesman,\" Qi Jinglong remarked
with a smile. \"You really are always looking to profit wherever you
go.\"

\"Quit trying to mock me,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a nonchalant grin.
\"Let\'s make a bet. I bet you that Celestial Maiden Lu is going to gift
you one of the seals or fans inscribed by me. What do you say?\"

\"I gotta go,\" Qi Jinglong said as he rose to his feet, refusing to
entertain Chen Ping\'an\'s proposal. \"I have to go to the top of the
city walls to instruct the disciples of our Great Emblem Sword Sect in
swordsmanship.\"

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t try to keep him. As they stepped out of the room
together, they discovered that Bai Shou was still sitting on the chair
outside, and he raised the wine flagon in his hand upon catching sight
of Chen Ping\'an.

\"If you\'re still around when Pei Qian gets here, I\'ll make sure to
tell her to go easy on you,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a smile.

\"You don\'t have to do that.\" Bai Shou scoffed. \"It\'s not like I
actually can\'t beat her in a fight. I just can\'t bring myself to go
all-out against her because she\'s a girl, she\'s really young, and she
only recently started training martial arts. Even if I beat her,
there\'s no glory to be had, and that\'s why I don\'t want to fight her
again.\"

\"I\'m going to give you one chance to reconsider, then tell me what you
really want to say,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a sneer.

Bai Shou immediately stood up and made his way to Chen Ping\'an\'s side,
then offered up the flagon of wine with both hands as he implored,
\"Please convince Pei Qian not to challenge me to any further battles.
It\'s only going to harm our relationship.\"

Chen Ping\'an took the flagon from Bai Shou, then slapped him on the
head and reprimanded, \"Regardless of whether you\'re in the Armory or
elsewhere in the city, make sure you talk less and cultivate more. That
mouth of yours is going to get you into trouble around these parts if
you\'re not careful.\"

\"Put a little more respect on my name, Chen Ping\'an!\" Bai Shou
snapped in an enraged voice. \"Who are you to talk down to me like
you\'re my senior?!\"

\"How about this? I\'ll accept you as a sworn brother of mine if you
dare to refer to me as your brother in front of Pei Qian once she gets
here?\" Chen Ping\'an proposed with a smile.

Bai Shou weighed up his options for a moment, then decided, \"We can
continue to be brothers after Pei Qian is gone.\"

Chen Ping\'an sneered. \"What a little coward you are.\"

Bai Shou made a sword seal with his hands and looked up into the heavens
as he declared, \"A courageous and graceful man should not fight with a
little girl.\"

An amused grin appeared on Chen Ping\'an\'s face as he patted him on the
head.

He felt like it was a good thing for Qi Jinglong to have a disciple like
him. Otherwise, it would not be a good thing if they were both so silent
and serious all the time.

Chen Ping\'an escorted Qi Jinglong to the entrance of the Ning Manor,
and Bai Shou quickly made his way down the steps.

He then turned back to Chen Ping\'an with a look of schadenfreude and
teased, \"Your challenger is coming soon! Make sure to keep your hands
to yourself!\"

\"You\'re not going to reprimand him?\" Chen Ping\'an asked as he turned
to Qi Jinglong with an exasperated expression.

Qi Jinglong turned to Bai Shou and said, \"There are some truths that
you don\'t have to articulate.\"

He then turned and extended a bow to Nalan Yexing as a gesture of
farewell, and Bai Shou quickly followed suit.

The two of them left the city and set off back to the Armory.

Chen Ping\'an stood beside Nalan Yexing, and the latter smiled and said,
\"Before going into seclusion, Young Mistress Ning asked me to pass a
message on to you. Her message is: \'Don\'t lose.\'\"

Chen Ping\'an was very relieved.

\"In that case, I know how much power I\'ll have to use.\"

He had a good grasp of his and Yu Juanfu\'s respective levels back when
they were both at the pinnacle of the sixth tier. Prior to his training
under Li Er, he had been an inferior martial artist to Yu Juanfu, but by
the time he overcame his Vajra Body Tier bottleneck, he had already
surpassed Yu Juanfu.

Setting aside Cao Ci, whom Chen Ping\'an had been chasing after this
entire time, he didn\'t want to lose to any other martial artist of the
same cultivation base, nor could he afford to allow himself to lose.

As for Cao Ci, Chen Ping\'an would gladly lose three more, even thirty
more consecutive sparring matches to him. As long as Cao Ci was still
willing to fight him, Chen Ping\'an would be up to the challenge, and no
number of defeats would harm his confidence in the slightest.

*What I\'m aspiring toward are Mr. Qi\'s teachings, Cui Cheng\'s fist
intent, and the ultimate freedom that the strong get to enjoy as
described by A\'Liang. Hence, I have no rivals aside from myself. Chen
Ping\'an is Chen Ping\'an\'s only adversary.*

With that in mind, Chen Ping\'an was brimming with confidence and fist
intent, and Nalan Yexing turned to him with a surprised expression,
seemingly taken aback by the sudden shift in his disposition.

Fully fit and raring to go, Chen Ping\'an immediately\... relegated
himself to a sickbed for half a month.

Upon arriving in the city, Yu Juanfu immediately issued an open
challenge to Chen Ping\'an for three sparring matches. However, she
quickly found out that Chen Ping\'an hadn\'t set foot outside the Ning
Manor even once over the past half-month, proclaiming to everyone that
he was sick. She was astonished to hear this. How could there exist such
a shameless pure martial artist under the heavens?

Had Cao Ci misspoken or made a misjudgment? Cao Ci had once told her
that among all of the martial artists under the heavens around their
age, he was in a league of his own, with Chen Ping\'an close behind,
while everyone else, including Yu Juanfu, was far behind them.

Whenever Cao Ci spoke on such matters, he was always incredibly serious.
He never gave anyone a word of undue praise, nor would he underestimate
anyone\'s abilities.

His assessment of Chen Ping\'an was as follows. \"Chen Ping\'an is a man
of immense mental fortitude, and the path that he walks is one that is
extremely solid and consistent, so if you lose to him once, then
there\'s a very good chance that you\'ll continue to lose to him in
every single one of your subsequent battles. The same may apply even to
me, which is why I\'m never going to give him the opportunity to catch
up to me.\"

All of a sudden, Yu Juanfu rose to her feet with an indignant
expression.

*How is a coward like Chen Ping\'an worthy of such high praise from Cao
Ci?! He\'s been openly challenged by a martial artist of the same
cultivation base, yet he\'s hiding in the Ning Manor like a turtle in
its shell! Is it because he\'s wary of the power of the Yu Clan behind
me? But how is a pure martial artist supposed to make any progress if
they\'re scared of every little thing?*

After her meal of flatbread and water, she put her water bottle into her
bag, then handed it off to Sword Immortal Ku Xia for safekeeping. From
there, she traveled northward, then leaped onto the city wall before
stepping over the edge and began running vertically down the wall toward
the earth.

When she was still several hundred feet above the ground, she stomped
heavily down onto the city wall, sending herself shooting forward like
an arrow.

After drifting down onto the ground, she continued rushing toward the
city with singleminded focus
