mountains or far under the rivers, ruled over lands of desolation and
miasma or oversaw treasured lands of fortune, or whether they were
deities or malicious ghosts, all of the powerful beings in the Savage
World had to mobilize at least half of their forces to join the assault
on the Sword Qi Great Wall.

They would naturally be rushing to their death if they failed to breach
the city wall.

At the same time, however, they would have to charge forward without
fear of death if they wanted to successfully take down the city wall. As
long as the demons were willing to engage in this battle of attrition,
then the more measly ants they were willing to sacrifice, the more the
seemingly towering and formidable Sword Qi Great Wall would lose its
opportune time, geographical advantage, and popular support. Once all
three were lost, that would be the moment when Chen Qingdu was
comprehensively killed, with his soul breaking apart for good.

The Sword Qi Great Wall could be viewed as a world of its own, so the
most critical consideration of this battle was how Chen Qingdu could
maintain the natural advantages of the great wall, and how the Savage
World could overcome their disadvantages as the attacking party. In
fact, this could be regarded as the only consideration in the battle.

Indeed, this was what the sword immortals and the measly sacrificial
demons were fighting for as the former unleashed sword strikes and the
latter charged at the city wall.

The Sword Qi Great Wall was destined to fall if the Savage World
mobilized half of its strength to participate in the assault.

Not only would the Sword Qi Great Wall fall, but several continents in
the Majestic World would be engulfed by turmoil as well. For example,
the Southern Whirl Continent, which was located closest to Stalactite
Mountain, the Circling Ascension Continent in the southwest, and the
Parasol Leaf Continent in the southeast.

So, when the old man in gray had finally reappeared after slumbering for
ten thousand years, his first action had been to divide the Savage World
into twenty territories, after which he had instructed the fourteen
pinnacle great demons to mobilize at least half of the forces in at
least one of their territories to attack the Sword Qi Great Wall. If
they failed to even complete such a small task, then there would no
longer be a need for them to keep living.

Moreover, the pinnacle great demons needed to be willing to ascend the
city wall to challenge Chen Qingdu\'s sword skills after the battle
began. If they were unwilling to do so, then they could stay at the
bottom of the ancient well.

Looking at the twenty territories, the overall cultivation bases of the
demon cultivators in some territories were relatively lacking, and in
these cases, the pinnacle great demons could make up for the lacking
quality in increased quantity. In addition to this, there was one other
thing that the pinnacle great demons needed to do, namely, to force all
of the Upper Five Tier demons to travel north to join the battle. Those
who dared to refuse or hide would be punished with death.

Of course, they couldn\'t be too harsh on these powerful beings who had
overcome many hardships and difficulties to reach the Upper Five Tiers,
so those who were willing to join the battle would all receive rewards
and honors in the future, as well as extremely valuable gifts before
setting off for the battlefield.

If these Upper Five Tier demons died on the battlefield before breaching
the Sword Qi Great Wall and reaching the Majestic World, then their
children or direct disciples were guaranteed to receive a territory in
the Savage World and enjoy a life similar to that of monarchs and nobles
in the mortal world. The sizes of these territories would be determined
by the deceased great demons\' cultivation base and military merits, and
no one else in the Savage World would be allowed to attack them within
one thousand years.

After they conquered the Sword Qi Great Wall and marched into the
Majestic World, not only would the demons receive rewards and honors in
the Savage World, but the Upper Five Tier demons would even be allowed
to establish their own sects and forces on the extremely fertile lands
of the Majestic World.

News of this contract signed by the fourteen pinnacle great demons at
Holding Moon Mountain had already spread throughout the entire Savage
World.

If there were enough top-notch cultivators in one of the twenty
territories, yet they lacked Dao robes, armor, and immortal treasures,
then the old man in gray had been extremely clear about how to address
this issue. He had directly told the fourteen pinnacle great demons not
to hide their treasures, and that they needed to arm their subordinates
regardless of whether they were paying out of their own pockets or
borrowing the treasures from someone else.

In any case, they could follow the agreed strategy and use their own
abilities to recoup these costs once they arrived in the Majestic World.
They were guaranteed to receive at least double what they had initially
invested, and if this still wasn\'t enough, then they could ask the old
man in gray and Holding Moon Mountain for further compensation.

The assault on the Sword Qi Great Wall proceeded smoothly, having been
divided into eight separate stages.

The demons of the Savage World had only just started the first of the
eight stages.

Afterward, the sword immortals guarding the Sword Qi Great Wall would be
astonished again and again. For example, the Savage World would also
have pure martial artists at the tenth tier, and there would also be
magnificent scenes of sword cultivators battling against sword
cultivators atop the city wall. In addition, the Savage World would also
have a large army of Militarian cultivators wearing incredibly valuable
armor pellets.

Some time later, a large collection of mountains would also materialize
on the battlefield, these being the towering Five Mountains that had
been taken from a dozen or so empires. Standing on these mountains would
be countless cultivators unleashing a rain of immortal treasures.

All of the demons on the battlefield right now needed to crane their
necks to gaze up at the majestic city wall, but as time went on, the
battlefield they fought on would slowly rise higher and higher.

In the end, the Sword Qi Great Wall would become a legitimate territory
of the Savage World, and with the demons growing stronger and the humans
becoming weaker, the demons would be the ones enjoying an upper hand in
future conflicts with the Majestic World, able to attack or defend as
they pleased.

Bai Ying started to drink wine. He had heard that there was an abundance
of immortal wine in the Majestic World.

Didn\'t those haughty sword immortals atop the city wall like to unleash
the full power of their blades to kill demons? Well then, they could
attack to their heart\'s content and accumulate as much military merit
as they wanted. In any case, they would eventually drown under the
weight of all the potential military merit.

In reality, the Savage World had already started to scheme and plan
immediately after the wager of the thirteen battles.

The Savage World had suffered heavy defeat in the three previous
battles, but it had only launched those assaults for the sake of
conducting realistic military exercises.

The Sword Qi Great Wall was enjoying a generation of outstanding young
prodigies, led by none other than Ning Yao.

However, was the Savage World not enjoying a similar phenomenon?

Li Zhen, who possessed part of Guan Zhao\'s soul, had naturally been one
of them, and the old man in gray hadn\'t felt any pain regarding his
death. Bai Ying felt even less concern and pity.

One had to realize that the Savage World also had a group of young
demons known as the Hundred Sword Immortals, and their rankings weren\'t
based on their current cultivation bases and combat power, but rather,
determined by their aptitude for the Great Dao and their future
cultivation potential. Bei Qie, the only disciple of the big-bearded
man, was only ranked third out of the Hundred Sword Immortals.

During previous battles at the Sword Qi Great Wall, the human sword
immortals would only leave the city wall together when the two sides
were evenly matched or when the Sword Qi Great Wall was facing a
disadvantage. They would split open the battlefield and appear on the
front lines, resolutely blocking the relentless attacks of the demon
tribe.

It would then be the turn of the earth immortal sword cultivators and
the young prodigies, such as Ning Yao, to leave the city wall, and they
would charge onto the battlefield and battle to the death with the
demons. It was up to their own abilities and fortune whether they lived
or died.

Only at that time would the frail Lower Five Tier sword cultivators
appear on the city wall. If the great demons managed to successfully
ascend the city wall, however, countless of these pitiful ants would be
killed, even if some exhausted sword immortals stayed on the city wall
and tried to stop the great demons.

Flying swords continued to shoot forward from the city wall, with
countless streaks of sword light leaving countless rays of lingering
radiance in the sky. At the same time, many sword cultivators continued
to summon their bonded flying swords back to the city wall, after which
they would retreat from the front lines and make their way to the
northern end of the city wall. They would nurture their flying swords
and ingest alchemical pills, also meditating to recover their spiritual
energy. While they did this, another group of sword cultivators would
quickly take over their original positions and continue to defend
against the demons.

This behavior of the Sword Qi Great Wall caused the biggest headache for
the Savage World.

The sword cultivators could firmly guard the city wall and slowly
deplete the demon army\'s numbers.

Upon witnessing such a scene, a spectating great demon from the Savage
World had once sighed and remarked that the attacking army of demons was
like a colossal and bloated being, waiting to be weakened as it sat
before the great wall. Just how tragic and helpless was this? Just how
futile was this?

[]{#chapter-115.xhtml}

# Chapter 617: (2): Who\'s Worthy of Ning Yao

Sword of Coming

A furtive young boy in black appeared atop the Sword Qi Great Wall, and
after ascending the city wall, the young boy appeared extremely fearful
of death as he collected a Dao robe and a sword from the stalls
temporarily set up by the garment market and the sword market. He put on
the Dao robe and tied the standard sword to his waist, after which he
sprinted along the city wall.

As the young boy in black ran, he came across mountains of the Savage
World being blasted apart by sword immortals, causing shattered rocks to
shoot through the air. Other sword immortals slashed down to pulverize
the large rocks, but there were some that still slipped through the
defenses and crashed into the city wall with thunderous booms.

The young boy in black extended his hands to block a gigantic
house-sized rock for several youthful Middle Five Tier sword cultivators
who were unable to dodge in time. However, despite blocking the large
rock, the slender young boy with an unremarkable appearance couldn\'t
help but vomit several mouthfuls of blood. Even so, he quickly wiped his
mouth and shakily sprinted away before the young Middle Five Tier sword
cultivators even had the chance to thank him.

After sprinting for a while, the young boy finally managed to find some
familiar faces.

He saw many people whom he expected to be here, such as Pang Yuanji, who
was at the peak stage of the Golden Core Tier, as well as Gao Youqing,
who wasn\'t with her older brother Gao Yehou and was instead sticking
close to Pang Yuanji.

He also saw some unexpected and not-too-familiar faces, such as Lin
Junbi, Zhu Mei, and Jin Zhenmeng, who had summoned their bonded flying
swords and were standing beside Sword Immortal Ku Xia.

Of the young sword prodigies who had come from the Middle Earth Divine
Continent\'s Shaoyuan Empire, Yan Lü and Jiang Guancheng had already
left the Sword Qi Great Wall and boarded an intercontinental ship at
Stalactite Mountain, apparently making their way to the Southern Whirl
Continent.

The young boy in black wasn\'t surprised about Sword Immortal Ku Xia
staying behind, but he was extremely astonished to see Lin Junbi and the
others not only staying behind, but actually having the courage to
participate in the battle rather than hiding in the city to watch from
afar.

Elsewhere, there were six people gathered together and launching sword
strikes to kill the attacking demons.

Ning Yao, Die Zhang, Chen Sanqiu, Dong Huafu, Yan Zhuo, and Fan Dache.

Die Zhang was carrying the huge sword, Mountain Suppressing, on her
back, and this was quite amusing to those at the Sword Qi Great Wall.
This was because Great Sword Immortal Yue Qing had a bonded flying sword
named Mighty Guardian of the Five Mountains.

This was similar to how the sword of the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent\'s Sword Immortal Wei Jin coincidentally shared the same name
as Qi Shou\'s pseudo-celestial sword, High Radiance.

Fatty Yan was wielding his sword, Purple Lightning, and furiously
cursing the demons for being shameless, accusing them of using
underhanded methods to target him.

Elaborate Makeup, Dong Huafu\'s sword, which had an extremely feminine
name, was resting horizontally across his knees. The descendant of the
Dong Clan, who never needed to spend money to buy things, wasn\'t
cursing the vile beasts from the demon tribe right now, and he was
instead scolding Fatty Yan for unleashing such weak and floppy attacks.
His sword was limply flailing around like Chen Sanqiu when he became
drunk. Dong Huafu always liked to offend several people at once when he
leveled criticisms.

Yan Zhuo replied that he was deliberately making his flying sword move
in this elusive manner. His flying sword wasn\'t moving haphazardly, and
it was actually moving in a very profound way. Not only would the demons
fail to predict the movement of his flying sword, but even he couldn\'t
fathom Purple Lightning\'s next move. This was what made it so effective
and powerful.

Chen Sanqiu was dressed in white, and this was a Dao robe passed down by
the ancestors of Taixiang Street\'s Chen Clan. Cloud Pattern, the sword
of the elegant young master, had lost its original scabbard a long time
ago, and it was once a sword that had belonged to his friend, Little
Ququ. Chen Sanqiu had become the owner of this sword following Little
Ququ\'s death, and before ascending the city wall this time, he had
brought an additional scabbard from the sword market to sheathe Cloud
Pattern.

As for Chen Sanqiu\'s original sword, he had temporarily lent it to Fan
Dache, his friend who was unable to advance to the Golden Core Tier no
matter what.

Controlling their flying swords to travel beyond the city wall and kill
demons was no easy task.

There were also individuals with not just tough physiques but also
impressive combat power among the demon tribe, and there were also many
demons who had mastered underhanded skills to specifically target the
flying swords of sword cultivators. In addition, a large number of
sacrificial demons would carve talismans onto their bodies for the sake
of capturing the flying swords of the sword cultivators, and they would
immediately self-destruct their demon cores without hesitation once they
managed to capture a flying sword, blasting the swords into pieces.

These sacrificial demons most certainly wouldn\'t make their sacrificial
intents known, and they would even take things a step further by
purposely getting injured or deliberately exposing their weak points by
\"accident.\" Upon crashing into the talismanic traps carved on their
bodies, it was entirely possible that the bonded flying swords of the
sword cultivators would be completely destroyed.

This being the case, did the sword cultivators still dare to unleash the
full power of their swords to attack the demons? Would their attacks
still possess the same indomitable sword intent as before?

This was a huge test for the observation skills of the sword
cultivators, and it was also something that would greatly temper their
Dao Hearts.

Ning Yao, who was carrying a sword on her back and a sword by her waist,
took a quick glance at the young boy in black. She felt slightly
exasperated, but she didn\'t say anything to him. He had already made
his way here, so what could she possibly do? Shoo him away from the city
wall? Even if she did, would he listen to her?

And so, Ning Yao turned around and continued to wield her flying swords.

Ning Yao naturally possessed more than just a single bonded flying
sword, but during the three large-scale battles over the course of less
than twenty years, the demon tribe had only ever witnessed one of her
flying swords.

Chen Ping\'an, who had changed his appearance to that of a young boy,
took a few glances at the six friends and noticed a few things.

Fan Dache was too restrained when he launched sword strikes, rendering
him unable to deliver the destructive power expected of a sword
cultivator at the peak stage of the Dragon Gate Tier.

It wasn\'t that Fan Dache lacked the disposition or courage, but rather,
he was stuck in a relatively awkward situation. Killing enemies on the
battlefield was different from sparring with others on the training
ground in the Ning Residence and the Yan Residence.

Fan Dache was too concerned with catching up to the sword strikes of Die
Zhang, Chen Sanqiu, and the others, hoping that he could cooperate
seamlessly with the bonded flying swords of his friends. As time went
on, this became a negative cycle where Die Zhang made mistake after
mistake, eventually needing the help of Chen Sanqiu and the others.

Standing on the city wall and gazing afar, the battlefield in the
distance would have appeared hazy and unclear to even earth immortal
sword cultivators in the beginning. Now, however, even Middle Five Tier
sword cultivators could focus their gaze and see everything clearly.

Chen Ping\'an knew that this was thanks to the three sages belonging to
the Confucian Sect, the Buddhist Sect, and the Daoist Sect. This was an
extremely profound mystical power that helped the Sword Qi Great Wall
gain an innate advantage over its opponents.

Chen Ping\'an arrived next to Fan Dache, who had a stern expression but
couldn\'t conceal the despondence in his eyes. He didn\'t walk onto the
parapet, and he only stuck his head over to look at the battlefield to
the south. He then compressed his voice into a thread, chuckling softly
and saying, \"You\'re not working together with other people to kill an
Upper Five Tier great demon, so just focus on launching your own sword
attacks. You can ignore Dong Huafu, Fatty Yan, and the others.

\"If their flying swords severely wound some demons but are unable to
kill them in time, then you can control your flying sword to stealthily
shoot over and land the killing strike. It would be a waste to ignore
this free military merit. After all, would those great sword immortals
at the Golden Core Tier have the face to fight for military merit with a
minor Dragon Gate Tier sword cultivator like you? They need to show some
loyalty as your friends, no?\"

Die Zhang\'s flying sword surged forward with resolve, with its sword
intent as pure as its owner.

Dong Huafu habitually launched his flying sword to follow Die Zhang\'s,
and both were ruthless fighters who would go all out with little regard
for their own defenses. Thus, Chen Sanqiu and Yan Zhuo would cooperate
with Die Zhang and Dong Huafu to make up for this shortcoming.

In addition to this, they would naturally launch their own attacks to
kill the demons as well. They had already fought three battles together,
so their cooperation was smooth and seamless, so much so that they could
form an atmosphere similar to an isolated small world.

Meanwhile, Ning Yao\'s formless flying sword was responsible for
targeting the more troublesome demons. While sweeping forward and
killing the demons, the flying swords of Die Zhang and the others were
actually gauging the enemies\' strength as well. In this sense, Ning Yao
was guarding the rear and ensuring that her four companions could launch
attacks without worry.

This made Fan Dache appear a little extra. In fact, Fan Dache also
viewed himself as a huge burden on everyone else.

Fan Dache had trained extensively with his friends at the Ning
Residence\'s training ground, and he wasn\'t an inexperienced sword
cultivator who had never descended the city wall to battle to the death
with the demons either.

The only reason he appeared extra was that his friends were far too
outstanding. The opportunities and openings on the battlefield were
fleeting, and potential dangers and surprises would also appear in the
blink of an eye.

Fan Dache couldn\'t keep up with Die Zhang and the others, regardless of
whether it was his thoughts or the speed of his flying sword.

He didn\'t turn around to reply after hearing Chen Ping\'an\'s voice,
nor was he distracted from launching his sword attacks.

This was a sword cultivator at the Sword Qi Great Wall, someone who was
accustomed to battle and death.

Fan Dache didn\'t hesitate or feel embarrassed, and he heeded Chen
Ping\'an\'s advice to launch his sword attacks. He no longer forced
himself to cooperate with each and every one of his companions\' attacks
to kill the demons, and he instead seized the right opportunities to
deliver the fatal blows against those demons that were already teetering
on the brink of death.

Chen Ping\'an had said before that delivering these relatively easy
fatal blows on the battlefield was the same as picking up money on the
streets --- this was a true test of skill. If anyone dared to call Chen
Ping\'an shameless, then Chen Ping\'an would use the best Bamboo Sea
Small World Wine at the Sword Qi Great Wall to spit in their face.

Chen Ping\'an observed the battle for a moment before continuing to say
in a reminder, \"Fan Dache, there\'s a severely wounded demon playing
dead thirty-six meters to the left of your flying sword. Go on, send it
to the afterlife.\"

A vicious sword strike pierced through the head of the demon lying on
the ground.

Chen Ping\'an swept his gaze across the battlefield and continued, \"Fan
Dache, you can temporarily move your flying sword away from the region
controlled by Die Zhang and the others. You don\'t need to deliberately
follow them, and you can send your flying sword slightly further away to
deal an additional blow to all of the demon corpses in the surroundings,
regardless of whether they\'re playing dead or not. It\'s relatively
safe to attack these demons as they have the smallest chance of being
those sacrificial demons that have talismans carved on their bodies.

\"Don\'t get greedy or try to seek perfection --- there\'s always
military merit for you to collect as long as you don\'t damage the
foundation of your flying sword. Just treat the battlefield to the south
like a brand new training ground. If you want to catch up to Chen Sanqiu
and the others, then remember to look more and think more between your
sword strikes. If you do, then there will eventually come a day when you
can successfully predict the paths of their swords, and you\'ll no
longer feel like you\'re lagging behind and holding them back.

\"Stop your sword! That\'s a sacrificial demon! Let Fatty Yan toy around
with it first.

\"Do you see that? This beast clearly has some brains, and it wants to
pick on you, the weakest link in the chain, after failing to have its
way with Chen Sanqiu and the others. You should run away without
hesitation when this happens. It\'s a pity that the acting skills of
this demon are not quite up to scratch. What kind of desperately fleeing
demon has such a resolute gaze and such steady hands?

\"Steady hands often point to a ruthless heart, so you need to be even
more careful against opponents like this. Your current bonded flying
sword isn\'t sturdy enough, nor are you a Golden Core Tier cultivator.
You\'re not a wealthy young master like Chen Sanqiu or Fatty Yan either,
and you haven\'t poured exorbitant amounts of money into your flying
sword.

"That being the case, you should definitely avoid striving for only
speed and accuracy when you launch sword strikes. You\'re not that type
of person, so you shouldn\'t launch that type of sword strike. You need
to accept this.

\"Say, Dache, you shouldn\'t waste such a good name. Can you please
attain profound enlightenment for once? That Golden Core Tier great
demon is clearly on the verge of death already, with its golden core
having been shattered by Die Zhang, and it\'s simply lying there and
waiting for you to put it out of its misery. I told you to avoid
striving for only speed and accuracy, but I didn\'t tell you to strive
for slowness when you should use speed, did I? And now look, Fatty Yan
has snatched away the military merit.

\"Sixty-nine meters to the northeast of your flying sword --- do you see
that demon? It\'s hesitating after having just lost an immortal
treasure, but it can\'t turn around and retreat due to the imposing
might of the great demon military supervisor in the rear. This reaction
can\'t be faked. Dache, what are you standing there in a daze for? Hack
that demon to death! Tsk, and now it\'s been snatched away by Die Zhang.
Say, Dache, do you actually have a secret crush on our shopkeeper?

\"The demon battling against Chen Sanqiu is presumably a Nascent Tier
great demon that\'s concealing its strength. At the very least, it\'s a
Golden Core Tier demon. It has thick skin and flesh, but its immortal
treasure is far too heavy and cumbersome. You can assist Chen Sanqiu,
but remember to keep your flying sword as close to the ground as
possible. If you\'re able to, then find an opportunity to stab it
between the legs. Don\'t try to aim for critical locations such as its
head or heart.

\"This demon is clearly targeting Chen Sanqiu and the others, so this
battle is bound to last a long time. Oh my, Dache, your crotch strike
truly embodied the demeanor of a sword immortal. Alright, hurry up and
run away --- don\'t bite off more than you can chew. The great demon is
looking at you now. Have Dong Huafu block its path.\"

An Upper Five Tier demon that was responsible for patrolling and
supervising the battlefield seemingly noticed something peculiar in one
area of the battlefield.

This demon was an Unpolished Jade Tier sword cultivator, and it directly
unleashed a fearsome arc of sword light at the city wall, which raced
toward the head sticking above the parapet.

However, the sword on Ning Yao\'s back automatically left its scabbard,
striking down the sword light and causing the flying sword of the demon
to create a huge crater at the foot of the city wall, throwing up a
large plume of dust. After failing to strike its target, the demon sword
cultivator dashed away on its flying sword and burrowed into the ground,
moving around randomly before eventually making its way back to the rear
of the demon army.

Ning Yao\'s sword returned to its scabbard, and her expression was calm
and composed as she continued to manipulate her flying sword in the
distance, hunting down and killing the attacking demons.

Of the six friends, only Ning Yao\'s bonded flying sword hadn\'t
returned to the city wall a single time in three days and three nights.

A golden phoenix spread its wings and swooped down from the city wall,
soaring toward the battlefield to the north and killing the demons in
its path.

Sword Immortal Gao Kui\'s bonded flying sword was shockingly as large as
an intercontinental ship as it descended from the sky.

Zhou Cheng\'s bonded flying sword, Seven Radiance, furiously raced along
the ground, leaving a mangled mess of broken limbs and bodies in its
wake.

Seas of clouds materialized high above the battlefield after Ning
Lianyun, the clan leader of the Ning Clan, summoned his bonded flying
sword, and a ferocious downpour of sword qi instantly rained down on the
ground below.

Great demons from the Savage World also channeled their mystical powers,
riding on vast swathes of dark clouds as they rushed toward the city
wall. Some sword cultivators were unable to react in time, and many of
the bonded flying swords that were engulfed by the dark clouds directly
shattered into pieces as if they were being crushed by a millstone. This
resulted in the affected sword cultivators becoming bloody and wounded
on the city wall.

Ning Lianyun naturally wouldn\'t allow the great demon to succeed in
breaching the sword formation with its dark clouds, so he immediately
manipulated one of the several seas of clouds with his mind.

The vast swathe of dark clouds crashed into Ning Lianyun\'s sea of
clouds.

A young sword immortal from the Nalan Clan, who seldom launched any
attacks, extended a hand and made a pushing motion. A white jade
platform, sparkling and crystal-clear, appeared directly above the great
demon\'s head before crashing down.

The great demon didn\'t try to block the attack, instead choosing to
shoot back and flee. The white jade platform crashed into the large army
of demons belonging to the great demon, instantly flattening demons and
creating a sea of blood within a radius of several kilometers.

Not only that, but the great demon was seemingly being targeted by some
strange mystical ability of the sword immortal, with white jade
platforms that possessed boundless sword qi continuing to plummet down
toward him no matter how he fled and changed directions. Countless
demons were brutally crushed as a result.

Eighteen white jade platforms descended one after another, eventually
managing to suppress the great demon that had nowhere left to run. The
great demon was forced to assume its true form to fight back against the
white jade platform bearing down on its head, and it was ultimately
pushed all the way into the ground as the fracturing white jade platform
finally gave way and exploded apart.

Half of the great demon\'s body was bloody and mangled, and it shot a
vicious glare at the sword immortal who had attacked it before once
again assuming its human form, humphing coldly as it chose to
temporarily leave the battlefield to nurture its wounds.

The sword immortal departed from the city wall in the south, making his
way to the north to rest his mind.

Another sword immortal traveled in the opposite direction, filling in
for the sword immortal who had just left. They were responsible for
overseeing an area of the battlefield.

If a great demon dared to make a move, then a sword immortal on the city
wall would definitely send their flying sword over to engage the great
demon.

Moreover, if a great demon that had previously launched an attack
reappeared on the battlefield, then any great sword immortal in the
vicinity would need to step forward and unleash a sword strike at the
demon.

Some daring great demons that didn\'t fear death would stand closer to
the city wall, resulting in them being attacked by Yue Qing, Ning
Lianyun, Han Huaizi, Li Tuimi, or other great sword immortals who were
at the Immortal Tier but weren\'t members of the top ten pinnacle sword
immortals. Regardless of whether it was one great sword immortal who
launched an attack or several great sword immortals who launched attacks
together, they would all lose a certain amount of military merit if
their attacks failed to severely wound these great demons.

These were the ironclad rules and regulations of the Sword Qi Great Wall
personally established by the old great sword immortal.

Apart from this, the armies of demons commanded by the Unpolished Jade
Tier demons could attack as they pleased. They wouldn\'t be especially
targeted by the great sword immortals on the city wall, and the Sword Qi
Great Wall would accept the losses no matter how many sword cultivators
were killed as a result.

Apart from attacking with their full strength to kill demons, the sword
cultivators first needed to learn how to protect themselves in these
battles of life and death.

A dead sword immortal was nothing more than just that --- dead and
useless.

Meanwhile, a living sword cultivator represented countless possibilities
even if they were yet to become an earth immortal.

Otherwise, where would the battle-hardened sword immortals come from?
Did it make sense for the sword cultivators to hide and cower as they
attacked, relying heavily on the careful protection of their sword
immortal seniors?

This was the reason behind Chen Qingdu\'s comment to Ning Yao. In his
mind, no one was above death!

This was a cruel truth that the old great sword immortal had never kept
hidden from any of the younger generations over the past ten thousand
years.

Deadly battles and perilous conflicts were everywhere at the Sword Qi
Great Wall.

On the two ends of the city wall, and high above in the sky, the sages
of the Confucian Sect, the Buddhist Sect, and the Daoist Sect oversaw
their respective regions and engaged in extremely subtle but even more
critical battles.

The elderly sage of the Daoist Sect oversaw the zenith of the sky, and
he waved the snow-white horsetail whisk in his hand again and again,
shooing away the smoke and clouds. He looked like a renowned scholar
sitting alone atop the mountains and fanning away the summer heat, with
his stories passed down through the generations.

The monk sitting on the straw mat silently recited a sutra, causing
countless golden lotuses to bloom on the ground and continuously rise
into the air, forming a long golden river of floating lotus lights.

The Confucian sage sat upright and opened a sagely scripture, with the
golden characters in the book hovering out one after another. The book
became blank after the Confucian sage finished reading it, and he
promptly moved on to the next sagely scripture.

Chen Ping\'an had already left Fan Dache\'s side. When passing Pang
Yuanji, he had summoned Lightning Devourer and Pine Needle and had them
assist with setting up an illusion technique, only providing the
necessary amount of help and not overcommitting. He also appeared beside
Gao Yehou and Situ Weiran and provided them with some minor help.

He didn\'t linger in the areas guarded by sword immortals, but he would
stop briefly when he came across those Middle Five Tier sword
cultivators who were customers of the wine shop. Not only would he
summon the two replica flying swords, but he would even summon First and
Fifteenth to swiftly dispose of some enemies. However, he definitely
wouldn\'t stay at a single location for any extended period of time, nor
would he continue to advance in a predictable manner.

Chen Ping\'an would occasionally make his way back to areas where he had
previously launched sword strikes, then advance several hundred
kilometers in a single breath. He would rescue the bonded flying swords
of the sword cultivators if he were able to, and he would unleash an
attack to kill some demons if the opportunity arose. He definitely
wouldn\'t stretch himself, and he most certainly wouldn\'t act rashly
for the sake of military merit.

Not only that, but his appearance would also shift between that of an
expressionless young boy in black or an emaciated old man.

Right now, Chen Ping\'an was looking at the female face mask in his hand
and weighing up whether or not he should adopt this disguise. At this
moment, a sword immortal responsible for guarding the formation truly
couldn\'t hold back anymore, and they used their mind\'s lake to chuckle
and scold, \"Can a mighty second tier cultivator like you please know
some shame?\"

This sword immortal had an extremely good relationship with Yue Qing and
Mi Hu, and when Zuo You had challenged Yue Qing to a sword duel before,
he had been one of the sword immortals who had left the city to break up
the fight.

Chen Ping\'an raised his middle finger at the sword immortal, after
which he gritted his teeth and resolutely slapped on the face mask. He
leaped onto the parapet, and he surprisingly adopted the lithe and
shapely gait of a woman.

He then secretly summoned his flying swords to help a group of young
sword cultivators. The sword immortal in the distance was dumbfounded,
but he immediately broke into hearty laughter. He was extremely
impressed by this scholar from the Scholarly lineage, whom he had
previously had a poor impression of.

After laughing for a while, the sword immortal composed himself as he
looked at the young man who had blood slowly seeping through his Dao
robe from the garment market. He continued to provide protection for the
many flying swords soaring beyond the city wall.

The sword immortal faced south and carefully observed every single
detail on the battlefield. At the same time, a thought rose in the
depths of his heart. Perhaps only a young man like this could become Zuo
You\'s junior brother and attract a huge gamble from the old great sword
immortal.

Perhaps only a young man like this was worthy of Ning Yao.

[]{#chapter-116.xhtml}

# Chapter 618: (1): Scorching Summer, Long Path Amid Wind and Snow

Sword of Coming

The sun of dawn illuminated the towering city wall.

Die Zhang, Dong Huafu, and Fan Dache chose to retreat.

Meanwhile, Ning Yao, Chen Sanqiu, and Yan Zhuo chose to stay on the
front lines.

Chen Ping\'an returned to their side and changed his face mask to that
of a middle-aged man. He helped Chen Sanqiu and Yan Zhuo observe the
battlefield, and he would occasionally speak up and give them a
reminder.

Compared to his detailed instructions for Fan Dache, his suggestions to
Chen Sanqiu and Yan Zhuo were far more concise. He was simply helping
them pick up some of the finer details they had missed on the
battlefield.

He offered suggestions on how their flying swords should travel and
where they should land, and he also helped them quickly review their
previous actions, striving to become better. Moreover, it wasn\'t the
case that Chen Ping\'an would overlook the abilities of these two Golden
Core Tier sword cultivators simply because they had become good friends
and often drank wine together, and in reality, he had benefited greatly
from carefully observing the battle and watching the sword strikes of
Chen Sanqiu and Yan Zhuo.

Afterward, Chen Ping\'an went to look for Fan Dache.

Fan Dache felt slightly exasperated after seeing Chen Ping\'an, who now
had the appearance of a middle-aged man. Those who became Chen
Ping\'an\'s enemies were truly as unfortunate as could be. There
wouldn\'t be auspicious azure smoke rising from their ancestors\'
graves, but instead ominous black smoke that even the coffins couldn\'t
contain.

Although exasperated, Fan Dache also felt extremely grateful at the same
time. He would have flailed around for much longer if it hadn\'t been
for Chen Ping\'an\'s arrival and help.

Chen Ping\'an squatted down and tossed Fan Dache a pot of Bamboo Sea
Small World Wine, saying with a smile, \"Remember to think about my good
points.\"

\"You\'re using Fan Dache\'s money to buy wine and then turning around
to give it to him to build goodwill. I\'ve learned a valuable lesson,\"
Dong Huafu commented.

Chen Ping\'an pretended that he didn\'t hear this as he slapped a yellow
paper Cleansing Talisman on his body to get rid of the smell of blood.

\"Are you heading somewhere else to pick up money?\" Die Zhang asked
with a smile.

Chen Ping\'an nodded and replied, \"I\'ll just casually walk around.
I\'m afraid of making things worse instead of better and attracting the
attention of some great demon, so I didn\'t really dare to provide too
much help. I plan to discuss this with the sword immortals afterward,
and I\'ll ask them whether or not I can oversee a small section of the
city wall by myself. I\'ll act as bait and wait for a bite.

\"If any of you retreat from the battlefield at that time, you can make
your way over to witness the impressive demeanor of a great cultivator
soaring through the sky on his sword. Oh, and remember to bring some
wine if you come. You\'re not allowed to watch for free.\"

\"Then I\'m not going,\" Dong Huafu said with a shake of his head.

\"Count me out as well,\" Die Zhang said with a smile.

Fan Dache noticed Chen Ping\'an looking over at him, so he could only
muster his courage and say with honesty, \"I don\'t dare to go.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled widely and said, \"Dache, you don\'t have to come,
but you can surely send some wine over, no? In any case, who cares about
seeing you?\"

Die Zhang and Dong Huafu stood up in unison and continued south to the
city wall.

Fan Dache also wanted to follow them, but Chen Ping\'an raised a hand
and gestured for him to slow down.

\"Do you feel a lot of pressure when you fight side-by-side with your
friends?\" Chen Ping\'an asked. \"Does it feel like you\'re holding them
back every time you try to help them?\"

Fan Dache nodded in response.

Chen Ping\'an smiled and continued, \"It\'s not necessarily a bad thing
to think like this, but you have to suppress these thoughts if you want
things to improve. Don\'t forget, Fan Dache, you\'re a sword cultivator
at the peak stage of the Dragon Gate Tier, and you\'re not yet thirty
years old. Do you know that in the Majestic World, even in the Northern
Complete Reed Continent that\'s renowned for having a huge number of
sword cultivators, it\'s incredibly impressive for a young prodigy to
possess the talent to eventually advance to the Golden Core Tier?\"

Chen Ping\'an pointed at himself and said, \"Just because I exist, it
doesn\'t mean that everyone in the Majestic World is like Chen Ping\'an.
In terms of the ability to kill enemies, there are indeed people around
the same age as me in the mountains who can do better than I can. There
should be quite a decent number of them. However, there are many --- a
huge number --- of them who are inferior to me.\"

He paused for a moment before continuing slowly, \"I traveled
extensively through the martial world in my hometown, the Eastern
Treasured Vial Continent. If you were to cultivate there, Fan Dache, you
would be a prodigy whom an entire mortal empire would have extremely
high hopes in. Perhaps you thought I was always joking in the past, and
that I was teasing myself in a self-deprecating manner by referring to
myself as a mighty fifth tier cultivator. However, that\'s not entirely
true.

\"Over at my hometown, even an Abode Tier demon or ghost can be
undisputedly regarded as a powerful great demon or terrifying malicious
ghost. Just think about this. With this context in mind, just how lofty
is a Golden Core Tier innate sword talent who\'s yet to reach thirty
years old in a place like the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent?\"

Fan Dache nodded and replied, \"I never thought about these things in
the past, and I was never too interested in matters pertaining to the
Majestic World. From a young age until now, I\'ve always regarded my
aptitude and talent as okay but still not good enough.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and spread his hands apart, tapping his fingers at
two opposite ends in the air and saying, \"What I\'m saying is this:
It\'s one extreme for you to regard all of your actions as wrong when
you\'re with Ning Yao, Chen Sanqiu, and the others. Similarly, it\'s
another extreme for you to regard yourself as a formidable sword
cultivator who can rival an entire nation over at my hometown. Neither
of these extremes should be adopted.\"

Chen Ping\'an raised a hand and clenched it into a fist, waving it in
the middle between the two imaginary extremes, explaining, \"These
extremes can exist, and it\'s unavoidable that they do. However, a sword
cultivator\'s Dao Heart should land here, indomitable and unwavering.

\"Speaking broadly, external matters are truly nothing more than just
that, external matters that are very difficult for us to fully control.
On the other hand, the heart of a cultivator is always within reach,
able to be tempered and cultivated to a higher level at any moment. The
small world of the human body is nothing more than a very small world,
but the human heart can encompass all matter and can be even loftier and
vaster than heaven and earth.

\"This is especially the case for sword cultivators, whose flying swords
can travel to wherever their thoughts can reach. They enjoy a sense of
freedom that encompasses their bodies, hearts, and lives. I feel like
this notion is very correct. In fact, I\'ll give it to you for free
along with the pot of wine in your hand.\"

Fan Dache\'s eyes were limpid as he took a large swig of wine. He wiped
his mouth and said in a solemn voice, \"Chen Ping\'an, if you spoke
these words to me in the past, I might have understood you, but I might
not have truly accepted your point. However, things are different now,
and I completely understand you.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled faintly and replied, \"It\'s actually all the same.
I only arrived at where I am today after suffering hardships of various
levels, walking and stopping all the time, and thinking about all manner
of things.\"

Fan Dache fell silent for a moment before suddenly asking in curiosity,
\"Which sage or mighty figure uttered the sentence that you gave me
along with this pot of wine? The more I think about it, the more sense
it makes.\"

Chen Ping\'an rubbed his chin and remarked, \"Dache, so be it if your
little brain isn\'t the brightest, but what\'s with your problematic
gaze?\"

Fan Dache smiled and stood up, forcefully tossing the wine pot aside
before making his way toward Chen Sanqiu and the others.

However, Chen Ping\'an unexpectedly reached forward and grabbed the
empty wine pot, after which he stood up and loudly scolded, \"A measly
Dragon Gate Tier sword cultivator dares to act all high and mighty in
front of a powerful second tier cultivator?! Do wine pots not cost
money?!\"

Fan Dache felt slightly guilty, and he couldn\'t help but look back even
as he briskly walked away. What he saw was the second shopkeeper cocking
his head and placing his finger beside his ear, slowly pulling off his
face mask.

\"Chen Ping\'an, I just can\'t forget her no matter what. Am I very
pathetic?\" Fan Dache asked.

Chen Ping\'an placed the face mask made by Zhu Lian in his sleeve, after
which he smiled and replied, \"In terms of a lovestruck person being
obsessed, there\'s nothing better than this.\"

\"This isn\'t what you said when we just met, was it? You gave me a huge
scolding,\" Fan Dache said in puzzlement.

Chen Ping\'an had a listless expression as he grabbed his Sword
Nurturing Gourd and took a swig of wine. He then smiled and replied, \"I
don\'t have the time and effort to explain this to you. You can mull
over this yourself. Also, try to act more like a mighty Dragon Gate Tier
sword immortal. People get heated and into each other\'s faces when
arguing, but sword immortals shouldn\'t bear grudges after fighting.\"

In reality, Chen Ping\'an was no longer worried about Fan Dache feeling
heartbroken due to romantic reasons. Fan Dache seemingly wasn\'t
outstanding compared to the others when it came to cultivation, speech,
and actions, but Chen Ping\'an was extremely confident that his path of
cultivation would be very sustainable and long-lasting. What Chen
Ping\'an was more worried about right now was Fan Dache listening to his
explanations and understanding them, yet discovering that he couldn\'t
achieve what he needed to. Or perhaps not being able to achieve them
well enough. This would lead to another set of problems.

Being oblivious to certain principles was a formless form of
disapproval, while learning about certain principles and accepting them
was a form of approval. However, failing to act on these principles
would be a second disapproval.

Generally speaking, facing a second disapproval would mean a dead end
for that principle --- it would have arrived at the graveyard in the
heart, and not even a corpse would remain. Most terrifying of all, a
whole string of principles and knowledge related to the deceased
principle would also die alongside it, leading to swathes and swathes of
deaths.

However, Fan Dache unexpectedly said, \"If I\'m temporarily unable to
strengthen the resolve of my sword heart as you described, and if I\'m
unable to stop being affected by Chen Sanqiu and the others, then
remember to remind me about it, Chen Ping\'an. If once isn\'t enough,
remind me twice. I don\'t have any great strengths, but I\'m relatively
good at taking feedback on board.\"

\"Easy done,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a smile.

\"Then you should also take a piece of advice from me,\" Fan Dache said.
\"This battle will drag on for a long time, so it won\'t hurt for you to
rest for a few days or half a month. You should nurture your wounds back
to full health before returning to the city wall.

\"Otherwise, if you continue to fight like this, it will be very
difficult for you to recover to your peak when we need to leave the city
wall and venture to the battlefield in the south in the future. You\'re
my guardian sword cultivator, so you should worry about my safety even
if you\'re not worried about your own. Otherwise, do you still want to
drink free wine in the future?\"

\"That\'s a fair comment,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a nod.

After saying this, Chen Ping\'an truly summoned his talismanic boat and
left the city wall.

When Fan Dache arrived at the city wall to the south, Ning Yao smiled at
him and said, \"Thank you.\"

Fan Dache wanted to keep a stern expression, but he couldn\'t stop the
smile from stretching across his face.

\"What a complete idiot,\" Dong Huafu commented.

Chen Sanqiu, whose flying sword was the most carefree and graceful when
it killed enemies, smiled faintly and said, \"Dong Huafu, if you\'re so
capable, why don\'t you have Ning Yao thank you as well?\"

Dong Huafu turned around and asked, \"Big Sister Ning, can you say thank
you to me?\"

Ning Yao kept looking straight ahead as she replied, \"You can piss
off.\"

Dong Huafu nodded in response, accepting Ning Yao\'s praise. He then
turned to Chen Sanqiu and Fan Dache and asked, \"Big Sister Ning is
always straightforward and honest with me. Can the same be said for the
two of you?\"

Chen Sanqiu gave him a big thumbs up.

Fan Dache took a deep breath and summoned his bonded flying sword,
having it swoop down the city wall with a flash of sword light.

Chen Ping\'an had nothing better to do as he steered his talismanic
boat, so he copied his disciples and lay down on the bow of the immortal
ship, using his hands to paddle it along. To his surprise, the boat
actually seemed to travel a bit faster\...?

[]{#chapter-117.xhtml}

# Chapter 618: (2): Scorching Summer, Long Path Amid Wind and Snow

Sword of Coming

During a slight reprieve in the intense battle, a few young sword
cultivators from the outside world retreated from the southern end of
the city wall to the northern end. At the same time, a group of
well-rested, energetic local sword cultivators silently took their
places. As they crossed paths, most of the sword cultivators in the
latter group now had slight smiles on their faces.

Yu Juanfu sat atop the northern city wall and chomped down on her last
piece of flatbread. She was brimming with fist intent, yet she was
unable to unleash punches from the beginning to the end.

For the first time in her life, Yu Juanfu, who was only able to spectate
the battle after ascending the city wall, felt an extremely strong
desire to advance her martial arts cultivation base. The seventh tier,
the Vajra Body Tier, was ultimately a big step away from the eighth
tier, the Far Roaming Tier. Only after advancing to the Far Roaming Tier
could a martial artist soar through the skies like a Qi refiner,
allowing them to unleash punches to their heart\'s content.

Zhu Mei\'s face was as pale as a sheet, and there was a sense of
lingering apprehension in her heart as she silently wiped the sweat from
her forehead.

She had faced several perilous situations after launching attacks with
her bonded flying sword, and she had either been protected by Sword
Immortal Ku Xia or been saved by Jin Zhenmeng. In fact, she had even
been helped once by Lin Junbi, who was still just a Sea Observation Tier
sword cultivator.

If it hadn\'t been for Lin Junbi seeing through the disguise of a
sacrificial demon, purposely enticing the demon to use its trump card
and eventually withdrawing his flying sword at the last split-second,
allowing Jin Zhenmeng to seize the opportunity to kill the demon, Zhu
Mei\'s bonded flying sword would have definitely suffered damage in that
exchange.

At that time, she would have been forced to retreat from the city wall
even if she were fortunate enough to avoid severe damage to her Great
Dao. She would have been forced to obediently nurse her wounds at the
Sun Clan and thereafter have no further participation in this battle
against the demons.

Lin Junbi was describing his observations and learnings in the previous
battles to Jin Zhenmeng.

This was Lin Junbi\'s first time chatting privately with Jin Zhenmeng
about these matters, and he talked about the tradeoffs, blemishes,
downfalls, and the many exquisite areas of the sword strikes used in the
battles.

There was a warm smile on Jin Zhenmeng\'s face, and it was clear that he
had grown friendlier with Lin Junbi thanks to this conversation, despite
not saying very much.

This was also Jin Zhenmeng\'s first time feeling like Lin Junbi --- a
prodigious youth who was seemingly flawless --- had a slightly more
human touch to him.

Lin Junbi retrieved a small and exquisite porcelain bottle crafted by
the construction office of the Shaoyuan Empire, pouring out three
alchemical pills of different colors. He kept the goose-yellow pill for
himself and handed the raven-blue pill and the spring-green pill to Jin
Zhenmeng and Zhu Mei, respectively.

Jin Zhenmeng and Zhu Mei both responded the same way, hesitating for a
moment before choosing to accept the alchemical pills. The three of them
each ingested an alchemical pill.

Lin Junbi focused his attention and calmed his breathing, slowly
digesting the alchemical pill and letting the abundant spiritual energy
rush into his critical acupoints.

However, Lin Junbi also used a bit of his mind to repeatedly analyze the
conclusion of that trial of self-reflection.

His Dao Heart would become fuller and more complete with each completed
analysis.

The young boy in white, who had introduced himself as Cui Dongshan, had
asked Lin Junbi a question when picking up the Go stones and returning
them to their containers back then. He had asked Lin Junbi whether he
dared to stay at the Sword Qi Great Wall to kill demons.

Lin Junbi had replied yes, but continued that the risks far outweighed
the benefits, so it seemingly wasn\'t worth staying behind to kill
demons.

At that time, the conversation had flowed as such.

\"This isn\'t a suggestion; it\'s a command. You\'re too stupid, so I
have no option but to say a bit more, lest my good intentions be mangled
and misconstrued as ill intentions by you. This should be a great
opportunity for you, so I don\'t want it to become a reason for you to
blame and criticize me in the future. Not only that, but you\'ll even
feel aggrieved when I beat you to death at that time.\"

Cui Dongshan pinched a Go stone with two fingers, waving it around and
continuing, \"Firstly, it\'s not important at all how many great demons
you kill if you choose to stay. Of course, it would be better if you
managed to kill a few more demons and win the approval of one or two
sword immortals.\"

Cui Dongshan casually tossed the Go stone into its container, after
which he picked up another Go stone and said, \"Secondly, Ku Xia will
accompany you and the others, so you won\'t die as long as you act
within your limits. Ku Xia is even more stupid than you, but he\'s
ultimately one of the rare few good people in the mountains. So, the
more you act like a good person, and the more resolutely you unleash
sword strikes to kill a greater number of demons, the more Ku Xia will
recognize and approve of you.

\"Ku Xia has already resolved to fight to the death, so perhaps he might
one day be willing to change the method of his death, dying for the sake
of Lin Junbi instead of dying for the sake of himself. He might die for
the sake of the Shaoyuan Empire\'s future pillar.

\"You need to be careful when that time arrives, and you can\'t allow
Sword Immortal Ku Xia to truly die here for your sake. You need to
relentlessly pursue the avenues of Zhu Mei and Jin Zhenmeng, especially
the former, to have Ku Xia abandon his thoughts of dying a courageous
death and instead convince him to escort the three of you from the Sword
Qi Great Wall.

\"Remember, even if Sword Immortal Ku Xia insists on returning to the
Sword Qi Great Wall by himself, he should at least accompany the three
of you to the Southern Whirl Continent first. Only then can he turn
around and make his way back. As for how to achieve this goal and what
the significance of doing this is, I\'m not going to tell you, and you
can use your young but rusty brain to figure it out yourself.\"

Cui Dongshan tossed the second Go stone into the container and
continued, \"Thirdly, you need to strike a good balance when you
interact with Zhu Mei and Jin Zhenmeng after leaving Stalactite Mountain
and traveling back home. You shouldn\'t gild the lily, and you need to
avoid trying to win their hearts. In fact, why don\'t I teach you a
strategy?

\"This Lin Junbi, who interacts with them, can remain cold and aloof as
always, appearing like a completely different person from when he was
killing demons on the city wall before. Otherwise, all your previous
efforts will go to waste. Zhu Mei and Jin Zhenmeng aren\'t the same as
Yan Lü and Jiang Guancheng, with the latter being pragmatic and the
former being ideological. They\'re complete opposites, so consider this
carefully and make of it what you will.

\"Fourthly, you should shut up after you return to the Middle Earth
Divine Continent\'s Shaoyuan Empire, where the scholarly culture is
flourishing. You shouldn\'t mention a single word about your experience.
If you can\'t control your mouth, then piss off to seclusion and turn
away all guests. Of course, you should naturally have a secret meeting
with your master before you shut your mouth, and you can feel free to
tell him the truth. Apart from your interactions with me, there\'s no
need to conceal anything from your master, no matter how big or small.
Don\'t treat your master like a fool.

\"The imperial preceptor will understand your ambitions, and not only
will he not feel disgusted, but he\'ll even feel pleased about you being
a like-minded person. He\'ll naturally protect you in secret, and he\'ll
do for you, his prized disciple, what masters should do for their
disciples. He won\'t resort to crude methods such as personally stepping
forward to boost your fame and reputation; in fact, he might even do the
opposite to a certain degree.

\"In any case, Yan Lü, who\'s even more stupid than you, has already
become your Go piece, and he\'ll say and do what\'s expected of him
after he returns home. However, the imperial preceptor will suppress the
flow of information within the Shaoyuan Empire, preventing people from
lavishing praise on you for your feats at the Sword Qi Great Wall.

\"Afterward, you can wait for the Confucian schools and academies to
speak for you. In the meantime, the more silent you remain and the more
muted the Shaoyuan Empire is, the more praise will find its way over
from all directions. You can\'t block them or keep them out even if you
want to.

\"Not only will people in the Shaoyuan Empire know about Lin Junbi, but
all of the rulers, officials, cultivators, and martial artists in the
surrounding kingdoms and vassal states will know about Lin Junbi as
well. Everyone will hear about his journey to the Sword Qi Great Wall,
and how he dared to stand firm and draw his sword against the demons,
leaving them dead below the city wall.\"

Cui Dongshan held a Go stone in his fingers and asked with a smile,
\"What was the finest detail included in this fourth point? Think
carefully before you answer, and don\'t disappoint me.\"

\"Having my master think that my interactions with other people and
matters are still relatively naive,\" Lin Junbi replied. \"At the same
time, this will allow Master to do some things that his disciple can\'t
do no matter what, and Master won\'t feel any discomfort while doing
these things.\"

Cui Dongshan tossed the Go stone into its container and said,
\"Fortunately, you aren\'t stupid beyond saving. Just you wait. When the
battle at the Sword Qi Great Wall becomes more intense and deadly in the
future, and when the Majestic World receives a whack and becomes
stupefied but also slightly more alert, your actions at the Sword Qi
Great Wall will only become more and more impressive.\"

Cui Dongshan picked up another Go stone and said with a snicker, \"Even
the sages, noble scholars, and virtuous scholars belonging to different
Confucian lineages from your master will regard you with newfound
respect. The imperial preceptor will increasingly view you as a closing
disciple who has the Great Dao within reach, but the Confucian schools
and academies might not continue to regard you as the disciple of an
empire\'s imperial preceptor. You can experience and ponder the
interesting nature of this by yourself. It will feel like drinking fine
wine.\"

Cui Dongshan waved the Go stone between his fingers and continued,
\"However, remember not to get carried away, or else all of today\'s
praises might become tomorrow\'s criticisms. Moreover, those giving
praises and leveling criticisms are often the same group of people. This
is another interesting point, and after you understand it, it\'s another
intoxicating pot of fine wine.\"

Cui Dongshan once again tossed away the Go stone between his fingers,
causing it to loudly crash into its Go container with a crisp crack. He
then shook his sleeves and said, \"You can use Yan Lü more in the
future, but Zhu Mei is different, and you must receive her recognition
and approval first. Especially when it comes to the latter, you\'ll
receive an unexpected surprise if you manage to forge a good
relationship with her.\"

\"Is it the clan that Zhu Mei belongs to?\" Lin Junbi asked in a quiet
voice.

Cui Dongshan shook his head and replied, \"Not that significant. Your
brain is truly mush, so how are you going to play Go? You\'re only
looking one or two steps ahead, but you still want to win?\"

\"Please enlighten me, Mr. Cui,\" Lin Junbi said in a sincere voice.

\"If Zhu Mei says something, then it\'s essentially the same as Yu
Juanfu seeing it with her own eyes,\" Cui Dongshan said. \"The two of
them have an extremely close and pure relationship, and they\'re almost
always together. What matters won\'t they discuss with each other? Yu
Juanfu approves of Zhu Mei\'s character, so if Zhu Mei approves of you,
she\'ll naturally put in a few legitimately good words for you. And
because of Zhu Mei\'s purity and honesty, Yu Juanfu will naturally
believe her words.

\"You showed a pathetic display of plotting and scheming at the Sword Qi
Great Wall, but not only will that not become a blemish on the Shaoyuan
Empire\'s Lin Junbi in Yu Juanfu\'s eyes, but it might even elevate her
opinion of you. Do you understand what I\'m getting at?\"

\"I\'m afraid of not thinking deeply enough and misunderstanding, so
please explain in more detail, Mr. Cui,\" Lin Junbi replied in a quiet
voice.

Cui Dongshan smiled and explained, \"People who have no flaws are the
least personable, but if someone disapproves of you at first and then
approves of you later, this type of approval will be even firmer and
more unwavering than any type of approval given from the outset. You
don\'t even understand this?

\"You don\'t know how to play Go, and you don\'t know how to read the
human mind either. I\'m already starting to feel some regret about
choosing to engage in this long-term transaction with you. Why do I feel
like I\'m going to lose money? Lin Junbi, I didn\'t feel any anxiety
during all of those Go games with you, but why am I suddenly filled with
worry after deciding to do business with you? Whatever shall I do?\"

Lin Junbi wanted to say something, but he couldn\'t help but hesitate.

Cui Dongshan narrowed his eyes and said, \"You know how to ask
questions, but not how to think for yourself? Do you know that my
patience is limited, and that I\'ll kill you if I need to? Do you know
why? An incorrect answer will mean death.\"

Beads of sweat formed on Lin Junbi\'s forehead as he replied, \"I can
die of stupidity by myself, but I can\'t affect your judgment and have
you find a stupid person to do business with, Mr. Cui.\"

Cui Dongshan smiled faintly and said, \"Not bad, it looks like you can
still be taught.\"

Cui Dongshan placed his palm on the Go stones inside one of the Go
containers, lightly rubbing them as he casually continued, \"As a pure
martial artist who\'s also from the Middle Earth Divine Continent, Yu
Juanfu won\'t detest a sword cultivator who\'s smart and is also willing
to fight to the death. How do you think the Yu Clan, and perhaps even
Old Bastard Zhou Shenzhi, will regard a young sword cultivator whom Yu
Juanfu doesn\'t detest? Is this a trivial and insignificant matter?

\"Have the old bastards in the Yu Clan and Zhou Shenzhi not seen a lot
of so-called smart people, like the original Lin Junbi, in their lives?
That old bastard in the Yu Clan orchestrated the fall of one empire and
the rise of another with a single hand, so what kind of smart person
hasn\'t he seen before?

\"He\'s accustomed to seeing the ebbs and flows of worldly matters after
living for several thousand years, but what he hasn\'t seen much of are
those energetic young people who are both smart and stupid at the same
time. These young people have complete disregard for heaven and earth,
yet they\'re filled with a sense of naivety, daring to risk their
reputation, riches, and lives for the sake of some particular major
matters.\"

Cui Dongshan lightly raised his hand one inch above the Go container,
gently twisting his wrist as he said with a smile, \"These are the
magnificent and changing sceneries in the depths of people\'s minds.
You\'re simply unable to see it clearly. To possess powerful observation
skills and a keen eye for detail? Cultivators don\'t take advantage of
this and turn a blind eye to all kinds of things, so what nonsensical
Dao Heart are they cultivating?

\"You, Lin Junbi, are a cultivator from the mountains who\'s destined to
make a huge impact in the imperial court, so how will you understand and
discriminate between people if you fail to understand the human heart?
How will you control and make use of people? How can you feel confident
while controlling and making use of people?\"

Lin Junbi was wholeheartedly convinced as he said solemnly, \"I, Lin
Junbi, have learned a lot from Mr. Cui\'s lofty teachings.\"

Cui Dongshan looked up and asked, \"Lofty? You\'re using such a basic
and crude word to describe me?\"

Lin Junbi shook his head and replied, \"Both lofty and radiant, rivaled
by only the sun and the moon! I\'m willing to spend my entire life to
pursue such a state, and this most certainly isn\'t the same notion of
loftiness spoken by the common people.\"

Cui Dongshan laughed loudly and remarked, \"Your flattery skills are a
perfect fit for the mountains where I\'m from. Very well, very well
indeed. If the opportunity arises in the future, I might truly take you
as my disciple, and when that happens, you can visit the ancestral hall
to offer incense and kowtow to the portraits.\"

In reality, there was already speculation in Lin Junbi\'s mind, but it
was so preposterous that he didn\'t dare to believe it.

Cui Dongshan retracted his smile and glanced down at the Go board. He
then ran his hand across the board and swept all of the Go stones into
the container, after which he retrieved a solitary black stone and
placed it on the board. He then retrieved several white stones and
formed a large circle around the black stone.

\"Since I\'m raising you like half a disciple, I\'m going to show some
true skills and use this black stone to represent Yan Lü,\" Cui Dongshan
said. \"You need to convince this black stone that it has a lot of
freedom and is unrestrained amid heaven and earth, with its life filled
with possibilities and hope. In reality, however, all of its thoughts
are controlled by you. His life, death, gains, and losses are all
controlled by your plots and calculations.\"

Lin Junbi felt like this was a simple principle that was fairly easy to
understand.

Cui Dongshan then placed an even larger circle of black stones around
the white stones, asking, \"This represents the minds of Old Bastard
Zhou and Old Man Yu. How should you solve this dilemma?\"

Lin Junbi mulled over this for a long time, raising his arm to wipe the
sweat off his forehead before shaking his head and replying. \"There\'s
no solution. In fact, I shouldn\'t even try to think about solving this
dilemma.\"

Cui Dongshan nodded and said, \"Not bad. You\'re half correct.\"

He picked up a white stone and placed it beyond the circle of black
stones on the Go board, saying, \"The state of the Go board is very
difficult to change in the short-term, and life is ultimately not the
same as a Go game, with each player moving one after another. However,
don\'t forget about the unrestrained nature of the human heart. You can
hide a thought in the distance and carefully observe the larger Go board
of heaven and earth with your eyes wide open. Zhou Shenzhi is nothing in
comparison. This is a process of cultivating the heart.\"

Lin Junbi lowered his head and gazed intently at the Go board, which
wasn\'t a Go guide, and fell deep into thought.

\"Deer call to each other, eating the wild cudweed. I have fine wine, so
strum the zithers and blow the reed-organs. \'Tis a shame, though, that
no fine guests are present.\"\[1\] Cui Dongshan retracted his gaze from
the vast lands and turned it to the sky, saying with a faint smile, \"A
guest in the mountains, a lord amid the clouds; Watching birds fly by, I
down a cup of wine.\"

Sitting atop the city wall, Lin Junbi also gazed up at the sky like the
young boy in white.

The person in the poem was none other than Cui Chan, whose game of Go
had inspired the composition of the *Iridescent Cloud Go Manual*.

In fact, his Go skills were even better now than before.

Cui Dongshan put away the Go board and Go container, and after standing
up, he said one last thing to Lin Junbi, remarking, \"I\'m teaching you
these things to tell you that being calculating and scheming isn\'t
interesting at all. It\'s a dead end with no future.\"

1\. This is a slightly modified line based on a line from the *Classic
of Poetry*, the oldest existing collection of Chinese poetry, comprising
305 works dating from the 11th to 7th centuries BC.

[]{#chapter-118.xhtml}

# Chapter 618: (3): Scorching Summer, Long Path Amid Wind and Snow

Sword of Coming

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t make his way back to the Ning Residence straight
away, and he instead took a detour to the wine shop first.

The wine shop wasn\'t closed, but there weren\'t any customers.

Zhang Jiazhen and Jiang Qu, the two young employees who had helped
around in the wine shop before, had already secretly traveled to
Stalactite Mountain, just like Golden Core Tier Sword Cultivator Cui
Wei. Zhong Qiu, Pei Qian, and Cao Qinglang would travel to the Southern
Whirl Continent, while the two youths would follow Cui Dongshan to the
Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.

Right now, the three people helping around in the wine shop were a young
boy called Qiu Long, a young girl called Liu\'e, and a little child
called Tao Ban. They were all handpicked by Die Zhang and were neighbors
she knew.

Among the three of them, Tao Ban was slightly different from Feng
Kangle, who was the same age as him. Feng Kangle had started to save
money for a betrothal gift from a very young age, and he was genuinely a
child who was unafraid of heaven and earth. He was also able to read
people\'s expressions and act in an opportunistic manner. On the other
hand, Tao Ban was very simple-minded and only had the trait of being
unafraid of heaven and earth.

Upon seeing the kind and friendly second shopkeeper arrive, Qiu Long and
Liu\'e, who were sitting at a table, casually chatting, still responded
in a tense, anxious manner and immediately stood up. It was as if
sitting down represented slacking off. Chen Ping\'an smiled and gestured
with his hand, saying, \"There aren\'t any customers, so there\'s no
need to be so tense.\"

Meanwhile, Tao Ban was lying on a long bench elsewhere with an adrift
expression, dazedly staring at the empty street outside.

Chen Ping\'an sat down at the table and asked with a smile. \"What\'s
wrong? You\'re unhappy because you can\'t beat Feng Kangle for that
young girl?\"

\"Say, Second Shopkeeper, am I the type of innate sword talent that
can\'t be identified by anyone?\" Tao Ban asked in a gloomy voice.

Chen Ping\'an was rendered speechless.

He then smacked the table and replied, \"Same rules as before. Grab me a
pot of wine.\"

Tao Ban was unwilling to stand up, so he shouted, \"Big Sister Liu\'e,
grab a pot of wine for Second Shopkeeper. And don\'t forget to accept
payment.\"

Chen Ping\'an retrieved a snowflake coin and handed it to Liu\'e, also
telling her that he wouldn\'t need any pickled vegetables or yangchun
noodles today. He was only going to drink wine. It wasn\'t long before
the young girl returned with a pot of wine and a white bowl, gently
placing them on the table.

Chen Ping\'an poured himself a bowl of Bamboo Sea Small World Wine and
took a sip.

Tao Ban sat up, then lay down on the wine table, looking slightly bored
as he tapped it with his fingers and said, \"Second Shopkeeper, I don\'t
want to sell wine forever.\"

\"Then what do you want to do?\" Chen Ping\'an asked with a smile.

\"I haven\'t figured it out yet,\" Tao Ban replied.

Chen Ping\'an drank wine and didn\'t say anything else.

Tao Ban kept the conversation going, saying, \"Second Shopkeeper, do you
know that many people speak badly about you behind your back? Quite a
lot of our customers speak up for you. However, a lot of the accusations
are very infuriating to listen to.\"

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and replied, \"Oh, is that so? I didn\'t
know. Care to tell me more?\"

Tao Ban started to explain the situation, revealing everything he had
heard to Chen Ping\'an.

The little boy became slightly angry upon seeing the second shopkeeper
continue to drink without responding to him, and he asked with a huff,
\"You\'re not deaf, Second Shopkeeper, but are you actually listening to
me or not?\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and replied, \"I\'m listening.\"

The easterly wind carries the willow branches up; the easterly wind
pushes the willow branches down.

It was the same easterly wind and the same willow branches, rising and
falling in unison. Why care about this?

However, these principles and comprehensions were too solemn, and there
was no need to tell them to little children.\[1\]

Thus, Chen Ping\'an feigned a sense of delayed anger as he exclaimed,
\"These bastards\... How infuriating!\"

\"Should we do something about it?\" the little boy asked with
eagerness.

Chen Ping\'an paused his bowl of wine in mid-air, shooting a sideways
glance at Tao Ban and replying, \"Are you going to fight for me? Or are
you going to keep a lookout for me?\"

Tao Ban sighed and lay down on the table again, lamenting, \"I feel
exhausted when there are too many customers, but I feel bored when there
are no customers. What in the world is going on?\"

\"I know, right? Just what in the world is going on?\" Chen Ping\'an
repeated in a teasing voice.

Tao Ban shot a glare at him and complained, \"You\'re such a mood
killer. You\'re not telling stories anymore, and you don\'t like to
manage the wine shop either. Who knows what you\'re busying yourself
with all the time?\"

Chen Ping\'an waved a hand and said, \"I\'ve spent money to buy wine, so
I\'ll give the plate of pickled vegetables and the bowl of yangchun
noodles to you.\"

A wide smile spread across Tao Ban\'s face.

Liu\'e, who had her ears pricked up the entire time as she listened to
their conversation, immediately passed the message along to Uncle Feng,
asking him to make a bowl of yangchun noodles for the second shopkeeper.

Chen Ping\'an continued to leisurely drink wine.

As he did so, he randomly recalled the calamity faced by Old Assistant
Minister Liu at the Azure Phoenix Nation\'s Lion Garden.

Scholars cared most about their reputation, so they were most afraid of
acting improperly in old age.

Cui Dongshan had said that the many sinister and interlinking methods
had been cooked up by Liu Qingfeng, the old assistant minister\'s eldest
son, and that Li Baozhen had only acted according to the plans.

Chen Ping\'an turned around and took a glance at the various restaurants
and wine shops on the empty street.

In reality, Chen Ping\'an wasn\'t surprised at all about the people and
the remarks that Tao Ban had mentioned. In fact, it could be said that
he had predicted these things a long time ago. This was just like the
characters he had inscribed on the side of a certain seal: The people in
the world act as expected.

To the current Chen Ping\'an, it was difficult to even become angry.

It was even more difficult for him to become disappointed.

It was definitely those people who secretly detested Chen Sanqiu after
making eyes at him but failing to catch his attention in the wine shop
or on Taixiang Street and Ritual Baton Street. The second shopkeeper was
friends with Chen Sanqiu, so these people naturally started to detest
Chen Ping\'an as well.

There were definitely sword cultivators who looked down on Die Zhang\'s
background but were jealous of her cultivation base and fated
