opportunities, so they ended up resenting the bustling nature of the
wine shop and resenting the extremely famous second shopkeeper.

There were also people who had gone with the flow and bullied Fatty Yan
in the past, but as Yan Zhuo\'s cultivation base advanced higher and
higher, their initial arrogance and disdain could only transform into
displeasure and frustration as they were forced to look up at Yan Zhuo
and his relationship with the Ning Residence and Chen Ping\'an.

Of course, there were definitely those who visited Die Zhang\'s wine
shop and attempted to get closer to the second shopkeeper, yet felt like
they couldn\'t find common interests or topics to talk about from the
beginning to the end. They initially didn\'t think much about this, but
following the rise in Chen Ping\'an\'s fame, they couldn\'t help but
view this as a legitimate loss to their interests.

As time went on, these people gradually stopped visiting the wine shop
to drink, and they even liked to invite their friends to other
restaurants and wine shops, speaking ill of Die Zhang\'s wine shop and
Chen Ping\'an. This satisfied them greatly, and the more people who
agreed with them, the more delicious the wine would taste.

These people, especially those who had once put on a show and squatted
down on the side of the street to drink wine and eat pickled vegetables
with the other sword cultivators, suddenly felt a sense of discomfort in
their hearts. Thus, they became increasingly spirited as they insulted
the wine shop with their like-minded companions.

Even so, that wine shop had become increasingly popular, enjoying
booming business. Despite this, those who drank elsewhere and spoke
badly of Die Zhang\'s wine shop would still find many reasons to console
themselves even if they looked around and saw few other customers in
these other restaurants and wine shops. In fact, they might even
convince themselves that everyone was drunk, and only they were sober.
In this way, the small groups of two or three people would become
increasingly tight-knit and sincere with each other.

The Buddhist scriptures stated that rain would fall evenly on all
matter, yet the plants and trees would each have their differences.\[2\]

This phrase had a similar meaning to the common saying: The same type of
rice raises one hundred types of people.

It was very easy to disapprove of a person.

Regardless of whether it was the Sword Qi Great Wall\'s old great sword
immortal, the Majestic World\'s Confucian sages, or the sages of the
Hundred Schools of Thought, these people could be easily disapproved of
and quashed in one\'s mind as long as other people were willing to split
hairs and look for problems.

People needed to do what everyone else did, or they would appear
detached from the masses. Moreover, they needed to take things one step
further, or else they would appear mediocre, eventually suffering the
consequences for this mediocrity.

In contrast, sincerely accepting and approving of a person was very
difficult.

Chen Ping\'an wasn\'t interested in butting heads with these detractors.
Rather, he would strive to observe the complicated lives of these people
whenever he had the free time and opportunity. He would observe the
complex hearts of these people.

Chen Ping\'an took a large swig of wine, downing the remaining contents
of his bowl. He then poured himself another bowl of wine.

Looking at Tao Ban devouring the pickled vegetables and yangchun
noodles, Chen Ping\'an smiled and said, \"Slow down a bit. No one\'s
going to fight you for the food.\"

Tao Ban completely ignored him.

Chen Ping\'an felt a slight sense of longing for his hometown as he
drank wine.

When he was little, a child had once climbed up a tree in the small town
to retrieve a stuck kite with a broken string, yet this child had been
accused of being a thief.

Another time, the child had seen from a distance someone the same age as
him getting bitten by a snake while playing at the immortal tomb, so the
child had immediately helped to apply medicines to the bite wound of the
victim, using knowledge and recipes that he had secretly learned without
permission from the Yang Family\'s medicine shop.

Afterward, when the children saw the tanned loner from Clay Vase Alley,
who always watched them play from a distance, the child who scolded him
the loudest and threw rocks at him the hardest was coincidentally the
child who had received his help before.

Chen Ping\'an hadn\'t understood this in the past, but after growing up,
he gradually realized that the child would have lost his friends if he
hadn\'t acted like this.

However, this didn\'t stop those children from being filial to their
parents and helpful to their elderly neighbors after growing up.

Of course, there were also those who became scoundrels, and some who
were fortunate enough became the lackeys of wealthy young descendants
from Fortune Street and Peach Leaf Alley. These latter people would
glower at others and act aggressively whenever they found the
opportunity to do so.

Even so, when these people received reward money from their masters,
they would still return home and bring their younger siblings, who were
still impoverished and outside the \"circle,\" to the shops in the small
town to spend lavishly and buy a large amount of New Year goods.
Afterward, they would purchase ingredients for their parents to cook up
a delightful New Year\'s Eve meal, which they would enjoy together as a
family.

They would also make some bamboo dragonflies, swords, and sabers for
their younger siblings.

There were also children whose entire families were full of bad people,
with things not changing even after they grew up. Their lives would be
okay, but not too good, even after they married and had children of
their own.

These families would never fight over the right and wrong of some
particular matter, and it was as if their views and opinions were all
the same. Chen Ping\'an hadn\'t understood this even after becoming an
apprentice in the dragon kilns, and it was only after traveling through
the martial world for a long time and learning many principles from the
books that he had finally made heads or tails of this phenomenon.

The child from Clay Vase Alley had grown up day by day, and he would
also feel different levels of unhappiness and vexation about the bad
experiences from his childhood.

Back then, he could only squat down by himself and play the game of
grass fighting, or he would run over to the immortal tomb and shape
various crude clay statues in front of the severely damaged deity
statues.

He would also pick up sticks and branches and hop through the overgrown
paths by himself, pretending that he was wielding a sword and cutting
down the enemies in his path. He would pant heavily from exertion, but
he would also enjoy himself immensely.

There were times when his teeth hurt, and his cheeks became swollen, and
he could only chew on some herbal medicines made according to some basic
recipes. He wouldn\'t want to talk for several days.

However, he would feel happy and fortunate as long as he wasn\'t sick
and hurting and didn\'t experience any calamities. He would feel happy
even if he could only afford a meal here and there.

There were times when he couldn\'t fall asleep at night, and he would
run to the Dragon Locking Well or the old locust tree by himself. The
lonely child would stand under the sky and gaze up at the dazzling
stars, feeling like he didn\'t have anything at all. At the same time,
it also felt like he already had everything.

Afterward, the snotty little kid from the same alley as him learned to
walk and learned to speak.

The young boy wearing straw sandals also met Liu Xianyang.

Afterward, he became an apprentice in the kilns and felt like there was
more to look forward to in life.

He needed to look after the snotty little kid, and he also needed to
learn from Liu Xianyang.

At the time, Chen Ping\'an had hoped that the three of them could have
enough to eat and wear in the future, and that they could smoothly
overcome all hardships no matter the size and severity.

The snotty little kid had said that he would definitely make a lot of
money in the future, allowing his mom to wear gold and silver whenever
she went out. He would also move houses to Fortune Street.

Moreover, even if he didn\'t visit those bastards who had bullied him
and his mom, they would definitely feel terrified and smack their own
mouths, even going as far as to visit him to apologize with chickens and
ducks in their hands.

Otherwise, Gu Can wouldn\'t forgive them, and he would repay the abuse
several times over. If they had scolded him one hundred times, then he
would scold them several hundred times, and if they had kicked him once,
then he would kick them seven or eight times, leaving them rolling on
the ground and on the brink of death.

Liu Xianyang had said that he wanted to learn all of Old Man Yao\'s
skills and become the most skilled pottery-maker in the dragon kilns,
with his pieces becoming the ones that were placed on the emperor\'s
study desk. Not only that, but the emperor would view these pottery
wares as family heirlooms. When he became an old geezer, Liu Xianyang
would definitely be even more impressive than Old Man Yao, and he would
brutally scold his clumsy juniors and disciples every single day.

Liu Xianyang also hoped that he could casually split apart bricks with a
single punch and easily stride across the widest streams with a single
step. That way, all of the children who attended private schools and all
of those buggers who knew a few scholarly phrases would have to look at
him with renewed respect. They would clamor to write couplets for the
Liu Family.

At that time, the three children with similar backgrounds had believed
that their dreams and ambitions were already very grand.

None of them had imagined that compared to their future experiences and
fated opportunities, their so-called grand ambitions were actually very
ordinary, perhaps even very small.

In the end, however, Gu Can had become the type of person that the three
of them had detested the most.

Liu Xianyang hadn\'t become a chivalrous hero either, and he had instead
become a legitimate scholar.

Chen Ping\'an had wanted to enjoy a peaceful and stable life, yet he
hadn\'t managed to achieve this either.

He had earned a fair bit of money and traveled extensively through the
martial world, and he had also come across many people and matters that
he hadn\'t even dared to think about in the past. He was no longer the
little boy wearing straw sandals and wandering up the mountains with a
large bamboo basket to collect herbs. Rather, he was now carrying an
invisible and intangible basket that was filled to the brim with stories
and life experiences that he wasn\'t willing to discard.

The conclusions of some stories were far from perfect. There were lovers
who didn\'t end up together, kind-hearted people who suffered tragic
fates, friendly partings that became eternal partings, and so on and so
forth. The conclusions of some stories were happy, but still carried
some slight disappointments. Meanwhile, some stories were still yet to
reach their conclusions.

However, Chen Ping\'an always believed in seeking light amid darkness
and maintaining hope amid despair. He felt like this would never be
wrong.

Chen Ping\'an put down his wine bowl and became slightly adrift.

He was thinking of Old Man Yao, who liked to be by himself and hold his
hands inside his opposite sleeves.

Chen Ping\'an remembered the sudden arrival of heavy snow when he had
entered the mountains to search for suitable clay with Old Man Yao for
the first time. The wind had been bone-chilling, and the snow had risen
past his knees, almost freezing the young boy wearing thin clothes and a
pair of straw sandals to death.

The taciturn old man had continued to walk forward by himself, only
slowing down slightly to say a few words in an uncharacteristic display.
\"The mountain paths are freezing in winter, yet you\'re not even
willing to spend a single hard-earned copper coin, all for the sake of
freezing yourself to death?

\"The days are cold, and the path ahead is long, so don\'t you
understand the need to wear a bit more? Can\'t you think for yourself if
your parents aren\'t here to teach you?\"

The snowy mountain path was seemingly endless, and the suffering young
boy was subject to even harsher criticisms. He wasn\'t able to cry even
if he wanted to.

The old man ultimately showed little care for Chen Ping\'an\'s life and
death.

When Chen Ping\'an once again felt that genuine sense of despair
creeping up on him, however, someone caught up to them and not only gave
Chen Ping\'an a large bag of warm clothes and dry rations, but the tall
and sturdy young boy even launched a torrent of abuse at his master,
calling him a heartless bastard.

With Chen Ping\'an\'s mind slightly adrift, someone wrapped an arm
around his neck and pulled him backward.

The assailant didn\'t stop here, tightening their grip on Chen
Ping\'an\'s neck and using their other hand to forcefully rub his head.
They laughed heartily and exclaimed, \"It looks like you\'ve grown quite
tall! But have you asked me for permission yet?!\"

The rims of Chen Ping\'an\'s eyes became red as he murmured, \"Why have
you only just arrived?\"

There was only one person in the world who could point fingers and order
Chen Ping\'an around, and Chen Ping\'an was also willing to listen to
this person. And today, they had finally arrived at the Sword Qi Great
Wall.

This person was none other than Liu Xianyang.

1\. The previous remarks symbolize the impermanent form of the willow
branches, which are pushed around by external factors. This draws
parallels to people\'s fate being shaped by external factors, and the
state of being indifferent to such destiny.

2\. This is a line from *Teachings on the Lotus Sutra*, a foundational
Mahayana text teaching that all living beings possess inherent
Buddhahood and can attain enlightenment.

[]{#chapter-119.xhtml}

# Chapter 619: You Can\'t Manage Without Liu Xianyang

Sword of Coming

Qiu Long and Liu\'e were both stunned by what they saw, because the
Sword Qi Great Wall\'s second shopkeeper had never been bullied like
this before. Rather, it was always the second shopkeeper tricking other
people.

Tao Ban was a very stubborn child, and his biggest wish right now was to
protect the wine shop\'s business and help Big Sister Die Zhang and the
second shopkeeper make money every single day. At this moment, however,
Tao Ban abandoned the opportunity to step forward and speak up for the
second shopkeeper. He silently left the table with his plate and bowl,
and he couldn\'t help but glance back at the tall and sturdy young man
in azure, thinking that this person was truly very powerful.

He wanted to become like this person when he grew up, and he definitely
didn\'t want to become someone like the second shopkeeper. Even though
the second shopkeeper would often talk and laugh loudly with the
customers, and despite making so much money every day and being so
famous at the Sword Qi Great Wall, he would always appear like he did
today when there were few customers at the wine shop. He didn\'t look
very happy, as if something were weighing on his mind.

Liu Xianyang let go of Chen Ping\'an\'s neck and sat down on the small
space the latter had shuffled over and created for him. He then waved a
hand at Tao Ban and said, \"Bring us another pot of fine wine and
another wine bowl. Put this under Chen Ping\'an\'s tab.\"

Tao Ban looked at the second shopkeeper, who nodded lightly in response.
Only after seeing this did Tao Ban retrieve a pot of the cheapest Bamboo
Sea Small World Wine. Even though Tao Ban didn\'t want to become like
the second shopkeeper, the second shopkeeper\'s business tactics were
still the most impressive, regardless of whether it was selling wine,
taking bets, engaging in fist fights, or engaging in sword duels. The
little boy felt like this was something he could learn. Otherwise, how
could he compete with Feng Kangle for that girl in the future?

Chen Ping\'an\'s wine pot wasn\'t empty yet, so he poured Liu Xianyang a
bowl of wine and asked, \"Why have you come here?\"

Liu Xianyang was in no hurry to answer this question, and he took a sip
of wine before shuddering and lamenting, \"Sure enough, I still can\'t
grow accustomed to this so-called immortal wine. I\'m not refined
enough, and I still feel like rice wine is the best.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and said, \"I actually brought some of Dong
Shuijing\'s rice wine over, but I\'ve already finished all of it.\"

Liu Xianyang elbowed Chen Ping\'an\'s shoulder and exclaimed, \"Then why
bother mentioning it?\"

Chen Ping\'an rubbed his shoulder and drank by himself.

Liu Xianyang took a large swig of wine and used the back of his hand to
wipe his mouth. He then raised a thumb and pointed at the street behind
him, saying, \"I\'ve come here together with a few fellow disciples, and
it was only on our way here that we heard about the Sword Qi Great Wall
being at war with the Savage World again. I was half scared to death,
and I was afraid that our teachers would become hotheaded and retrieve
some righteous aura from their belly full of scholarly knowledge to show
off to their students, charging onto the city wall to kill demons.

\"If it were up to me, I would rather hide in the Spring Banner Inn, one
of the four big private residences in Stalactite Mountain. I would
diligently read books and take a few glances at the Ape Havoc Estate,
the Plum Blossom Garden, and the Water Essence Palace, the three other
private residences that are equally as renowned as the Spring Banner
Inn.

\"However, my master and my fellow disciples are filled with
righteousness, and I also care greatly about my face. I can be beaten
half-dead, but my face definitely can\'t be hit, so I\'ve mustered my
courage to come here with them.

\"Of course, I heard about many of your feats while staying at the
Spring Banner Inn, and this is my biggest reason for coming here. I need
to give you a good talking to, and I can\'t allow you to continue like
this.\"

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t say anything, and he simply continued to drink
wine.

The most talkative and rambling person in the world was Liu Xianyang.

Chen Ping\'an had experienced this for many years.

When the three children had hung out together in the small town, Liu
Xianyang and Gu Can would often get into arguments over the smallest of
disagreements. Chen Ping\'an couldn\'t be bothered breaking them apart,
so he would simply sit nearby and listen. In any case, the arguments
between the young boy and the little boy would never get too heated. Liu
Xianyang had seemingly never lost an argument before, and this was
because he never cared about winning or losing the arguments, always
smiling and chuckling as he argued.

There were many times when Gu Can had clearly won the argument already,
having cursed all of Liu Xianyang\'s relatives and ancestors. However,
he would somehow feel even more vexed, and he would chase after Liu
Xianyang to hit him. When he ran out of breath, Gu Can would start to
throw sticks and stones. Liu Xianyang wouldn\'t become angry even if he
were accidentally hit by the stones.

Gu Can had once said that there wasn\'t a single good thing about Liu
Xianyang, and that Liu Xianyang was destined for a life of poverty,
suffering, and loneliness. The only redeeming feature of Liu Xianyang
was that he didn\'t hold grudges and wouldn\'t take advantage of his
strength to beat others up.

The three of them each had their own method of survival in the past,
with neither method being superior to the others. There was no clear
notion of right and wrong either, with Liu Xianyang liking to use false
reasoning, Chen Ping\'an feeling like he didn\'t understand principles
and reasons at all, and Gu Can believing that might was right. In the
mind of the little boy, whoever was stronger, richer, and had more
lackeys would be the embodiment of reason.

Liu Xianyang and Chen Ping\'an were only slightly older than him, and it
was difficult to say whether these poor bastards could even find
themselves wives in the future, so just what kind of principles or
reasons could they be in possession of?

Back then, they would climb trees to steal bird eggs, dive into rivers
to catch fish, transplant rice seedlings and steal water, and grab
sprouts from between the fences of the grain drying fields. The three of
them had generally been happy most of the time.

Seizing the moment when Liu Xianyang was drinking, Chen Ping\'an was
finally able to ask, \"How has studying at the Pure Confucian Chen Clan
been?\"

\"What do you mean by \' how has it been\'?\" Liu Xianyang replied with
a chuckle. \"I\'ve already studied there for more than a decade, and
could it possibly be worse than the small town?\"

He was seemingly unaccustomed to the Bamboo Sea Small World Wine, so he
only took small sips as he continued, \"Which is to say, I don\'t regret
leaving the small town at all. Only when I\'m bored might I think about
our hometown: the fields, the messy living quarters of the dragon kilns,
the chicken and dog shit in the alleys, and so on.

\"I do reminisce about these things, but nothing more than that. I
don\'t feel any strong attachment. If it weren\'t for some old debts
needing to be paid and some people needing to be visited, I wouldn\'t
even feel the need to return to the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
Why would I return? There\'s nothing interesting at all.\"

Liu Xianyang shook his head and repeated, \"There\'s truly nothing
interesting at all.\"

Chen Ping\'an suddenly said a name before falling silent. \"Gu Can.\"

Liu Xianyang snickered and said, \"The snotty little kid always wanted
you to become his dad from a young age, and you truly ended up
pretending to be his dad. Is your head screwed on right? So be it if you
didn\'t kill him, and you asked for this yourself, so just endure it if
your conscience feels uneasy. And if you killed him and felt strong
regret, then I would have told you to endure that as well.

\"What\'s up with you now? Haven\'t you endured challenges and hardships
from childhood all the way until now? What, you\'re more capable now, so
you regard yourself as a noble scholar after reading a few books? And
you view yourself as an immortal in the mountains after learning fist
techniques and embarking on the path of cultivation?\"

Liu Xianyang became increasingly angry as he spoke, and he pushed Chen
Ping\'an\'s head and scolded, \"Gu Can? You aren\'t even willing to call
him the snotty little kid anymore?!\"

He became angrier and angrier, not even drinking the wine in his bowl as
he exclaimed, \"You\'re always worrying about this and worrying about
that, and you love to find trouble where there isn\'t any. If it were
me, would Gu Can\'s rising capabilities and subsequent actions after he
left the small town have anything to do with me? I\'m only familiar with
Clay Vase Alley\'s snotty little kid, so if he became a little devil who
wantonly killed innocent people at Bamboo Scroll Lake, then he can seek
death and receive death.

\"It was the snotty little kid\'s ability to enjoy a better life than
everyone else through his bad deeds, and this was helped by the sinister
environment of Bamboo Scroll Lake. However, is anyone obliged to help
him against perilous danger? After all, did I, Liu Xianyang, kill anyone
or harm anyone?

\"Yet, after reading just a few books, you, Chen Ping\'an, are trying to
hold yourself to the standards of sagely morality? You were a complete
novice who couldn\'t even be regarded as a Confucian disciple at the
time, yet you were already so energetic and confident?

\"That being the case, shouldn\'t all of the Confucian sages and noble
scholars ascend to the heavens? Shouldn\'t I, a legitimate Confucian
disciple, and the old ancestor of the Chen Clan, who carries the sun and
moon on his shoulders, have come to the Sword Qi Great Wall seven or
eight hundred years earlier to kill demons? Otherwise, won\'t we feel
frustrated and vexed to death?

\"I seriously don\'t understand how you\'ve become like this, Chen
Ping\'an. I remember you weren\'t like this when you were little. You
didn\'t want anything to do with outside matters, and you didn\'t like
to speak a single extra word. Who taught you to become like this?

\"The private school\'s Mr. Qi? He\'s already dead, so I can\'t
criticize him. In any case, the dead should be respected. Was it the
Scholarly Sage? Okay, then I\'ll scold him later. And what about Great
Sword Immortal Zuo You? Actually, forget about him. He\'s too close, and
I\'m afraid of getting beaten up.\"

Chen Ping\'an finally opened his mouth and said, \"I\'ve always stayed
the same.\"

Liu Xianyang raised a hand, and Chen Ping\'an instinctively shrank back.

Liu Xianyang rolled his eyes and took a sip of wine, after which he
continued, \"Do you know what has surprised me the most? It\'s not the
fact that you\'re filthy rich now, becoming the richest out of all our
companions from back then, because I knew from the very beginning that
you would definitely become rich, very rich. It\'s also not the fact
that you appear to be doing extremely well but are actually quite
pitiful, because I\'m well aware of how stubborn you are, getting hung
up on all sorts of things.\"

The tall and sturdy young man raised his wine bowl and revealed, \"What
surprised me the most was that you\'ve learned to drink, and you
genuinely enjoy drinking.\"

Liu Xianyang placed the wine bowl back on the table --- he truly didn\'t
enjoy drinking wine. He sighed and continued, \"The snotty little kid
has turned out that way, but what can Chen Ping\'an and Liu Xianyang
actually do about this? Which person doesn\'t have their own life to
live? There are many things we can\'t do or can\'t do well regardless of
how hard we try and how much effort we put in. This has always been the
case, and this will perhaps continue to be the case in the future.
However, didn\'t we manage to overcome the most difficult and pitiful
phases in our lives all the same?\"

He reached over and placed a hand on Chen Ping\'an\'s head, saying,
\"It\'s very good that you helped the snotty little kid do so many
things to make up for his wrongs. You couldn\'t have done any better. I
have indeed studied a few sagely scriptures, so I\'m aware that the
world is lacking people like you, fools who actively take on difficult
problems.\"

Liu Xianyang slowly raised his hand before suddenly smacking the table,
scolding, \"However, it\'s very bad that you still feel so distressed
now. It can\'t be any worse. Just look at me. Liu Xianyang is, first and
foremost, Liu Xianyang, a half-assed scholar. So, I don\'t want you to
become that kind of fool. You might feel like this is selfish, but
there\'s nothing to be afraid of as long as you don\'t harm other
people.\"

\"I understand all the principles and theories,\" Chen Ping\'an said.

Liu Xianyang laughed bitterly and continued, \"But you can\'t act on
them, or you feel like you can\'t adhere to them well enough, am I
correct? So you end up feeling even worse?\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded and replied, \"Regarding Gu Can\'s situation, I
actually passed the mental barrier a long time ago. However, I recall
our childhood whenever I see all those lone and wandering ghosts, so I
can\'t help but empathize and feel their pain.

\"I\'m reminded of Gu Can being kicked, causing the little boy to writhe
in pain on the ground, wounded and on the verge of death. I\'m reminded
of you almost being beaten to death in Clay Vase Alley, and I\'m also
reminded of myself almost starving to death. It was thanks to all my
neighbors that I was able to push through that difficult period.

\"So, when I was at Bamboo Scroll Lake, I wanted to do something more. I
didn\'t harm anyone, and I also did my best to protect myself. I wanted
to do something, and I was able to do a little bit here and there, so
why not seize that opportunity?\"

Liu Xianyang also felt bad, and he said slowly, \"I wouldn\'t have left
our hometown if I had known this earlier. Sure enough, you can\'t manage
without me.\"

People often needed to leave home when they had ambitions.

After overcoming many challenges and difficulties to achieve their
dreams, however, people would very often dream of their hometowns.

But, as Liu Xianyang had revealed just then, he didn\'t feel too many
emotional attachments to his hometown, and there wasn\'t anything he
found difficult to let go of.

He at most felt worried about Chen Ping\'an and the snotty little kid.
Of course, he missed Chen Ping\'an far more than he missed Gu Can.

For Liu Xianyang, managing to live a decent life was actually the best
way to respect the Liu Clan. Ever since he was young, he had never cared
about visiting the graves and offering wine in respect, putting up
spring couplets and door gods, repairing the ancestral residence, or the
like. He had done all of this in a perfunctory manner, and he would
always like to borrow some paper money from Chen Ping\'an whenever they
visited the graves during the first lunar month or the Tomb Sweeping
Festival.

Chen Ping\'an had once grumbled about this, but Liu Xianyang had
promptly rebutted all of his complaints, saying that he was the sole
descendant of the Liu Clan, someone who could continue the bloodline and
expand the family tree for the clan. As such, his old ancestors should
be smiling in delight underground. Would they dare to ask too much of
their pitiful and lonesome descendant?

If they truly cared about their descendant, then they should hurry up
and appear in his dreams, telling him where in the small town the large
jars of silver were hidden. After Liu Xianyang became rich, he would
even go as far as to burn several large cauldrons of paper horses and
paper people for them, to say nothing of a small cauldron of paper
money.

Liu Xianyang had always been quite easy-going in some regards, so much
so that he could make jokes about how he was almost beaten to death back
then. He wouldn\'t care at all even if the snotty little kid used this
matter to target him. On the other hand, the snotty little kid had
always been extremely petty and narrow-minded.

Many people would eventually let go of their grudges, treating them as
inconsequential matters to be forgotten. However, some people would
always keep their eyes wide open and stare intently at their account
books, flipping through them all the time to keep track of their
grudges. They would genuinely feel happy doing this, and they wouldn\'t
feel stressed or uncomfortable in the least. Rather, this would be very
satisfying and fulfilling.

\"If you ask a lot of yourself, then the world will eventually ask a lot
of you as well,\" Liu Xianyang said. \"The more time that passes, the
more people will nitpick the actions of good people when they have
nothing better to do. And the better the world becomes, the more people
will nitpick. This is because they\'ll have more time and energy to do
so if the world is a better place, and the world will also become
increasingly tolerant of these selfish people.

\"However, these people will naturally shut up if the world truly
becomes a bad place. Even enjoying a proper meal will be difficult, with
war and chaos reigning; so will they have the time to care about the
good and bad of other people? They can barely control their own lives
and deaths, after all. Do you understand this concept?\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded in response.

\"If you feel like being morally vigilant, even when alone, is the most
important thing, feeling like you should become a better person, then I
can\'t be bothered trying to persuade you,\" Liu Xianyang continued.
\"I\'ll be happy as long as you don\'t die. So, I only have a single
request for you --- don\'t die.\"

\"There are too many unexpected circumstances, but I\'ll try my best,\"
Chen Ping\'an replied.

Liu Xianyang frowned and said, \"The private school\'s Mr. Qi chose you
to accompany those children on a journey to seek knowledge, the
Scholarly Sage chose you because of this to become his closing disciple,
many people at Downtrodden Mountain have chosen you to become the
mountain master, and Ning Yao has chosen you to become her immortal Dao
partner.

\"Regardless of how grand and how good these reasons are, they aren\'t
reasons for you to die here on this battlefield. To put things bluntly,
none of these people who have chosen you want to see you die at the
Sword Qi Great Wall. Who do you think you are? Can the Sword Qi Great
Wall definitely remain standing just because you, Chen Ping\'an, are
here? Will it definitely fall simply if you\'re not here? That\'s
complete and utter rubbish.

\"And don\'t give me your nonsense about doing every little bit you can
or whatnot, Chen Ping\'an. Do I not understand you well enough? Will you
ever lack reasons if you want to do something? You were already able to
rattle off an entire list of reasons when you hadn\'t studied or read
any books back then, so now that you have, you\'ll definitely be able to
delude yourself even more.

\"Let me ask you one thing. Have you ever thought about leaving this
place alive? Are you doing everything for the sake of leaving the Sword
Qi Great Wall alive?\"

Chen Ping\'an fell silent.

\"I take that as a no. Then are you gambling on luck?\" Liu Xianyang
asked. \"Are you gambling that the Sword Qi Great Wall can be defended,
Ning Yao will survive, Zuo You will survive, and all of your new friends
here will survive as well?

\"Chen Ping\'an, do you feel like things are going swimmingly after you
left home, and it\'s finally about bloody time that your fortune is
turning around for the better? Do you feel like you\'ve gone from being
the most unfortunate person to being the most fortunate person? Then
have you considered this before? The more things you possess right now,
the more you\'ll end up losing if you die? And at that time, you\'ll
have become the most pitiful and unfortunate person again?\"

Chen Ping\'an became angry in an uncharacteristic display, and he
exclaimed in frustration, \"Then what should I do?! What would you do if
you were in my position?!\"

Liu Xianyang was calm and composed as he replied, \"The solution is
simple. I would first tell Ning Yao that the two of us have to stay
alive even if the Sword Qi Great Wall falls. In the meantime, we\'ll do
everything in our power and fight with our full strength. It\'s also
important to ask Ning Yao what she thinks.

\"Does she want to die together with you here, becoming a pair of tragic
lovers, or does she want to go with the flow, where staying alive is
viewed as a fortunate outcome? Or perhaps she wants to work together
with you and leave this place alive, with no regrets and no guilt
weighing on your conscience. Even if you owe the Sword Qi Great Wall
today, you\'ll be willing to make up for this in the future.

\"After understanding Ning Yao\'s thoughts, regardless of what her
answer is right now, you still need to ask your Senior Brother Zuo You
for his opinion. What does he want his junior brother to do? Should you
carry on the Scholarly Sage\'s lineage and keep it alive, or should you
die a heroic death on the battlefield as the closing disciple of the
Scholarly Sage? If it\'s the latter, then perhaps it\'s only a matter of
whether you die first or whether your senior brother dies first.

\"And lastly, you need to consult with the old great sword immortal,
Chen Qingdu. If Chen Ping\'an wants to live, will the old great sword
immortal get in the way to prevent this? If not, then can he provide
some help instead? Life and death are a huge matter, so what does it
matter to lose some face and act more shamelessly?\"

Liu Xianyang pushed his wine bowl to Chen Ping\'an and continued, \"Have
you forgotten already? Back in the small town, which of us among the
three had the right to maintain face? Would other people grant our
wishes even if we begged them? And if begging were useful, would the
three of us have treated the corresponding matters as difficult?

\"The snotty little kid begged others not to hurl insults at his mom,
and if his pleading had succeeded, just how many times would he have
kowtowed back then? If you were able to master the skills of pottery
firing by kneeling on the floor and kowtowing a few times, would you
have done this? If kowtowing and splitting my head in two would have
made me rich and influential, you would have seen me kowtowing until a
large crater appeared in the ground.

\"What, you\'ve become successful now, and the pitiful little boy from
Clay Vase Alley has now become the young master of Downtrodden Mountain
and the second shopkeeper of the Sword Qi Great Wall. Yet, you would
rather keep your face and sacrifice your life instead now? Well then, I
can\'t afford to drink your wine. I\'ve read many books now, but I\'m
still a fairly shameless person. I can\'t compare to your lofty self,
and I\'m truly not worthy of being your friend.\"

Chen Ping\'an appeared slightly adrift as he reached forward and pushed
the bowl of wine back toward Liu Xianyang.

It felt like this was the only thing he could do.

Liu Xianyang grabbed the bowl and casually tossed it to the ground,
causing it to shatter. He chuckled coldly and said, \"Peace and
prosperity, my ass. In any case, I\'m not going to throw my life away
here. Rest assured, I\'ll pay respects at Uncle and Aunty\'s graves when
I return home, and I\'ll tell them that their son and daughter-in-law
were both very good people. However, it\'s a pity that they\'re both
dead. Chen Ping\'an, do you think they\'ll be happy to hear this?\"

Chen Ping\'an instantly deflated like a balloon, with his energy,
spirit, and fist intent all deflating as he murmured, \"I don\'t know.
In all these years, I haven\'t dreamed of my parents a single time. Not
a single time\...\"

Liu Xianyang suddenly smiled, turning around and asking, \"What do you
say, Sister-in-Law?\"

Standing behind Chen Ping\'an was a travel-worn young lady who had just
rushed over. She stood in the small world and remained silent for a long
time, after which she finally replied, \"I\'ll kill those who want Chen
Ping\'an to die. If Chen Ping\'an is seeking death himself, then I\'ll
only beat him half-dead because I like him.\"
