# Chapter 620: (1): We\'re All Scholars

Sword of Coming

After Ning Yao sat down, Liu\'e hurriedly brought over a pot of the best
Azure Divine Mountain Wine, quickly walking away after she put down the
wine and wine bowl. Of course, she didn\'t forget to bring a new wine
bowl over for the relatively hot-tempered young man.

Liu\'e didn\'t dare to hang around for too long, and she didn\'t dare to
ask Liu Xianyang for compensation either. To say nothing of her, even
Tao Ban, who cared most about the business performance of the wine shop,
didn\'t dare say anything to Liu Xianyang.

The three shop attendants hid inside the shop. The second shopkeeper and
the outsider had been speaking in a foreign dialect just then, so none
of them had understood the details of the conversation. However, they
could all tell that the second shopkeeper was in a very strange state
today.

And now, they couldn\'t hear the conversation at all after Ning Yao sat
down at the table.

Ning Yao poured herself a bowl of wine and said directly, \"The old
great sword immortal said before that no one can be guaranteed the right
to stay alive, but he didn\'t say that any specific person definitely
has to die. Even I don\'t feel like I must die here to live up to the
Ning Residence and the Sword Qi Great Wall, so it\'s preposterous to
think that it\'s your duty, Chen Ping\'an.

\"I like the current you, Chen Ping\'an, not some future Great Sword
Immortal Chen Ping\'an. It\'s naturally best if you can become a sword
cultivator, but it doesn\'t matter in the least even if you can\'t. If
you have the ambition, then you can continue to cultivate as a pure
martial artist. Or if you have the desire, then you can continue as a
scholar.\"

\"I understand,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a nod.

However, Liu Xianyang shook his head and lowered his voice, seemingly
speaking to himself as he muttered, \"You don\'t understand at all.\"

Ning Yao frowned and glanced at the great wall, saying, \"The old great
sword immortal didn\'t allow me to say too much before, explaining that
he would keep an eye out for you. He was intentionally letting you think
a bit more, or else you would have wasted this trip to the Sword Qi
Great Wall.

\"Seeking survival among perilous danger and managing to survive thanks
to your own abilities is the best way to temper your Dao Heart and
nurture your sword talent. Things would have been slightly lacking if
you received help from other people, even if it were only very minor
support or guidance.\"

Liu Xianyang continued to shake his head, saying, \"Pathetic. Utterly
pathetic. I knew things would be like this. They all look like they have
no desires or requests, but it\'s none other than these people beside
Little Ping\'an who like to demand the most of him.\"

Ning Yao ignored Liu Xianyang as she continued, \"Don\'t feel like
you\'re alone because of your treatment and experiences, and don\'t feel
burdened because of this. The old great sword immortal has taken care of
many young sword cultivators over the past ten thousand years, some of
whom he spoke with and some of whom he never said a word to, with the
latter group of sword cultivators remaining completely oblivious to his
care.

\"Truth be told, I felt like this was quite pointless in the beginning,
and I didn\'t agree to the old great sword immortal\'s proposal.
However, he persuaded me again, saying that he wanted to take another
look at your heart and character to determine whether you were worthy of
him returning that locust wood sword case.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and said, \"I thought the old great sword immortal
already forgot about this matter, just like he forgot about the marriage
proposal.\"

Liu Xianyang extended a finger and lightly twirled his wine bowl on the
table, muttering, \"His sword skills are so lofty already, so he might
as well be more generous if he\'s going to give things to the younger
generations anyway. At the very least, his actions need to match his
status and his sword skills.\"

Under the table, Chen Ping\'an forcefully stomped on Liu Xianyang\'s
foot.

Liu Xianyang put his index finger and middle finger together in front of
his body, appearing like he was forming a sword seal as he exclaimed,
\"A tortoise under its shell, this doesn\'t hurt, and I won\'t yell!\"

In reality, Ning Yao wasn\'t very fond of talking about these matters.
Many thoughts would simply spin around her mind once before disappearing
into the ether, just like how the unneeded aspects of her sword training
and sword tempering would be rendered non-existent. Meanwhile, the
important aspects would naturally be woven into her subsequent thoughts,
eventually becoming an actionable item that was ultimately reflected
through her sword skills, sword intent, or Sword Dao. It was as simple
as this, and she seldom needed to explicitly voice her thoughts.

But today was different.

Ning Yao thought for a moment before saying, \"There aren\'t many things
for the old great sword immortal to think about right now, so how can he
forget these matters? He once told me that he isn\'t afraid of anything,
besides owing debts.\"

Ning Yao paused for a moment before adding, \"Only by having fewer
matters to think about can one\'s thoughts become broader and loftier.
This is the mental state that sword cultivators should strive to
achieve, striding forward on the path of the Great Dao with their sword
light remaining radiant.

\"However, I\'m worried about how I\'ve always thought about very few
things, while you\'re the complete opposite and always think about a
myriad of things, yet you\'ve managed to barely put a foot wrong. I\'m
worried that this mental state I\'m talking about isn\'t suitable for
you, so I\'ve restrained myself from mentioning it this entire time. Now
that Liu Xianyang has clearly explained things to you, whether they were
fair comments, selfish comments, or well-intentioned comments, I felt
like I could finally ignore the old great sword immortal\'s warning and
mention this matter to you.

\"In any case, my thinking is simple. We need to stay alive regardless
of whether the Sword Qi Great Wall falls or not. Neither of us can die!
In the future, we\'ll only throw more punches and unleash more sword
strikes because we\'re not the type of people to forget things.
Regarding this point, you don\'t need to prove yourself to anyone, not
even to the old great sword immortal or Zuo You. It\'s enough for me to
know. So, what do you feel guilty about? If anyone dares to criticize
you for this in the future, you like to speak reason, but I\'ve never
liked to speak reason, so I\'ll treat it as a direct challenge to me.\"

\"I truly understand this time!\" Chen Ping\'an said with a dazzling
smile.

Liu Xianyang smacked the table and exclaimed, \"Beautifully put,
Sister-in-Law! As expected of Ning Yao, someone who can utter the words:
Striding forward on the path of the Great Dao with their sword light
remaining radiant. Sure enough, this is Ning Yao, whom I immediately
knew would become my sister-in-law upon first glance in the small
town!\"

\"Liu Xianyang, here\'s a toast to you! Coming here late is better than
not coming at all.\"

Ning Yao downed the contents of her wine bowl in a single gulp, after
which she placed the wine pot and wine bowl inside her minimization
treasure. She then stood up and said to Chen Ping\'an, \"You can
accompany Liu Xianyang and continue to drink wine. Only after you
recover from your wounds can you ascend the city wall to kill demons.\"

Liu Xianyang stood up together with Chen Ping\'an, chuckling and saying,
\"I feel much more at ease after hearing Sister-in-Law\'s words. It\'s
my fault for leaving home too early, or else it would have been
difficult to say who\'s referring to you as Sister-in-Law and who\'s
referring to you as Darling.\"

Chen Ping\'an threw an elbow into Liu Xianyang\'s chest.

Ning Yao smiled and asked, \"That young lady from Clay Vase Alley who
likes to say strange things and shoot sideways glances at people --- how
is she doing now?\"

Liu Xianyang grimaced and clutched his chest, putting on a bitter
expression as he said, \"It\'s not good to expose people\'s
shortcomings, just like it isn\'t good to hit people\'s faces. This was
the number one rule in the streets and alleys of the small town.\"

Ning Yao jumped on her sword and flew away, leaving a trail of sword qi
in her wake.

Liu Xianyang clicked his tongue in wonder and remarked, \"The hesitant
and indecisive Chen Ping\'an has found himself such a frank and direct
wife. What a strange matter!\"

Chen Ping\'an retracted his gaze and sat down. He didn\'t drink any
wine, and he put his hands inside his opposite sleeves and asked, \"How
is the learning culture at the Pure Confucian Chen Clan?\"

Chen Ping\'an wasn\'t very familiar with the Pure Confucian Chen Clan,
and apart from the old lunar almanac in the Jewel Small World and the
widely renowned Chen Chun\'an from the Southern Whirl Continent, the
only descendant of the Pure Confucian Chen Clan he had genuinely
interacted with was the young woman called Chen Dui.

Many years ago, Chen Ping\'an and Ning Yao had once entered the
mountains together with Chen Dui, the Dragon Tail Creek Chen Clan\'s
Chen Songfeng, and the Wind Lightning Field\'s Liu Baqiao, searching for
the model tree growing from the grave, something that was of great
significance to scholarly clans.

Chen Ping\'an\'s impression of Chen Dui had been quite neutral.

Liu Xianyang didn\'t like to drink wine, so he asked for a bowl of
yangchun noodles and a plate of pickled vegetables instead, placing a
foot on the chair and mixing the two dishes together before finishing it
in a few bites. He then faltered as he looked at the empty bowl, and he
paused for a moment before turning around and asking, \"Are you going to
charge me for this bowl of yangchun noodles?\"

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and replied, \"Besides the wine, everything
else is free of charge.\"

Liu Xianyang came to a realization and remarked, \"Now that makes more
sense. Otherwise, you would have been hacked to death a long time ago.\"

He recalled Chen Ping\'an\'s question from earlier and said, \"Studying
over there is extremely calm and stable. I received several valuable
gifts upon first arriving, things like book-flipping wind, ink-devouring
fish, and so on. I sent all of these things to the snotty little kid
afterward. There were no roadblocks at the Pure Confucian Chen Clan to
speak of, and I would listen to the teachings and explanations of the
scholars and teachers every single day. We would occasionally travel
afar, and these trips would be very smooth-sailing as well.

\"I often made my way onto a large rock cliff beside the river to enjoy
the scenery, and I had no option but to do this. The Pure Confucian Chen
Clan is renowned as an archway that assembles the characteristics of all
teachings, but there wasn\'t a single place there that resembled our
hometown. Only the rock cliff beside the river was slightly similar to
Azure Cow Ridge, where the three of us often played when we were young.

\"I can\'t complain or act pitiful in front of you even if I want to.
Sure enough, I was still more fortunate compared to you, and I hope this
can continue in the future.\"

Chen Ping\'an breathed a sigh of relief.

Liu Xianyang smiled and continued, \"Even if I do have some minor
grievances, would I need you to stand up for me? If you ask your
conscience, which of us has been looking after the other ever since we
became friends?\"

Chen Ping\'an raised his wine bowl and replied with a smile, \"You were
almost killed by that old bastard from Sun Scorch Mountain back then,
and wasn\'t it me who helped you slightly vent your anger?\"

There was truly no need to care about face when speaking with Liu
Xianyang. When it came to acting shamelessly, Chen Ping\'an felt like he
was at most only halfway to Liu Xianyang\'s level.

Liu Xianyang kept his foot on the bench, using his chopsticks to tap the
table as he feigned profundity and said, \"So you\'re still unaware,
huh? That was carefully planned by me, and if it wasn\'t for my
purposeful suffering, could you, a skinny and tanned bumpkin from Clay
Vase Alley who wasn\'t even half as handsome as me, have had the chance
to meet Ning Yao? Tell me honestly, who was the biggest matchmaker for
the two of you?\"

Chen Ping\'an chuckled coldly in response.

Liu Xianyang appeared slightly upset as he remarked, \"Disregarding the
rice wine from our hometown, I never imagined that my first time
drinking wine would be with someone other than my future wife. I\'m
truly a loyal and faithful brother. In fact, I wonder if my future wife
has even been born yet? If she has, then is she anxiously waiting for me
now?\"

Chen Ping\'an continued to drink wine. It was most likely true that Liu
Xianyang hadn\'t drunk any wine after leaving home.

\"Most of the people at the Pure Confucian Chen Clan are good people,
but it\'s naturally unavoidable for the younger generations to possess
some of the problems typical of younger people.\"

Liu Xianyang smiled and continued, \"I made a few friends there, and one
of them also came to the Sword Qi Great Wall this time. He\'s called
Chen Sho, and he\'s the younger brother of Chen Dui. He\'s a very decent
person, and he\'s already a virtuous Confucian scholar, so he naturally
doesn\'t lack a bookish aura. He\'s also a descendant of the Chen Clan,
so it\'s normal for him to possess the aura of a young master as well.
Of course, he also has the immortal aura of someone from the mountains.

\"These three auras represent three different temperaments, which are
sometimes displayed alone, sometimes displayed in pairs, and rarely
displayed all at once. He\'s impossible to stop when these three
temperaments are all displayed together.\"

\"What\'s your current cultivation base?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

He couldn\'t determine Liu Xianyang\'s cultivation base, and he could
only gauge that the sturdy young man was most likely a Middle Five Tier
Qi refiner.

Liu Xianyang shook his hand and replied, \"Don\'t ask. Otherwise,
you\'ll wrap your hands around your head and cry in embarrassment and
anger.\"

\"If news related to me spread to the Spring Banner Inn, then it
definitely isn\'t about me opening this wine shop or whatnot. Haven\'t
you already heard about my several fights?\" Chen Ping\'an asked in
exasperation.

\"Are you a sword cultivator?\" Liu Xianyang asked.

Chen Ping\'an could only shake his head.

\"What tier Qi refiner are you?\" Liu Xianyang asked.

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t want to say anything.

Liu Xianyang pointed at the ground and remarked, \"Are you not going to
squat down to speak with Lord Liu?\"

\"No matter what, I\'m at least a seventh tier martial artist,\" Chen
Ping\'an snapped.

\"You still have the face to say this after fighting with a girl?\" Liu
Xianyang asked with an astonished expression.

\"Are you a Middle Five Tier sword cultivator?\" Chen Ping\'an asked in
curiosity.

Liu Xianyang raised his hands and adjusted his collar, after which he
shook his sleeves and cleared his throat.

Chen Ping\'an changed the topic and asked, \"Apart from your friend, who
else from the Pure Confucian Chen Clan came this time?\"

\"Why do you care about these things?\" Liu Xianyang replied with a
smile.

Chen Ping\'an also shook his sleeves as he said in a joking manner,
\"I\'m a direct disciple of the Scholarly Sage, while the clan leader of
the Pure Confucian Chen Clan is a direct disciple of the Second Sage.
According to the Daoist orthodoxy of the Majestic World, how should the
seniority between us be viewed?\"

\"What a coincidence,\" Liu Xianyang replied with a chuckle. \"The clan
leader of the Chen Clan has also come to the Sword Qi Great Wall this
time, and I\'m coincidentally acquainted with him, seeing that I
frequently ask him for guidance. As for how the seniority between us
should be viewed, let me ask this senior first.\"

Chen Ping\'an retracted his smile and purposely put on an awkward
expression, lowering his head to drink wine as he compressed his voice
into a thread and secretly said to Liu Xianyang, \"Don\'t rush to return
to the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, and it\'s fine even if you stay
in the Southern Whirl Continent. Just don\'t go to the Eastern Treasured
Vial Continent, and definitely don\'t go to the Parasol Leaf Continent
and the Circling Ascension Continent.

\"Our grudges against Sun Scorch Mountain and Light Breeze City can wait
for a few more years, or until the time you become an Upper Five Tier
sword immortal. Otherwise, how will you breach the mountain-protection
formations of Sun Scorch Mountain? I\'ve thought about this before, and
if we don\'t use some schemes, it will be very difficult for us to
challenge Sun Scorch Mountain even if we both possess the combat power
of Unpolished Jade Tier sword cultivators.

\"The sword formations of Sun Scorch Mountain can\'t be underestimated,
and it now has a powerful Nascent Tier sword cultivator as well, someone
who has kept a low profile and cultivated in seclusion for nine years
already. Judging from the situation, it\'s quite likely that this sword
cultivator will successfully advance and exit seclusion.

\"The tides of fortune turn, and Sun Scorch Mountain is finally able to
breathe easy and have its way following the death of the Wind Lightning
Field\'s Li Tuanjing. If it wasn\'t for this sword cultivator still
being in seclusion, Sun Scorch Mountain would have exacted revenge on
the Wind Lightning Field a long time ago, especially with the temper of
those elders in Sun Scorch Mountain\'s ancestral hall. They definitely
wouldn\'t have allowed Huang He to enter seclusion, nor would they have
allowed Liu Baqiao to successfully advance to the next tier.

\"The Wind Lightning Field is different from Sun Scorch Mountain, with
the latter having a very close relationship with the imperial court of
the Great Li Empire. Regarding these relationships outside the
mountains, Huang He and Liu Baqiao have inherited their late master\'s
habits, never interacting with the imperial courts of mortal nations and
only traveling through the martial world. Because of this, the Wind
Lightning Field is far inferior to Sun Scorch Mountain when it comes to
its relationship with the Great Li Empire\'s Imperial Song Clan.

\"Even though Master Ruan is the chief guest elder of the Great Li
Empire, meaning that the empire will respect him and try to win him over
both in private and in public, hence giving the Dragon Spring Sword Sect
another large piece of land afterward, one has to understand the mindset
of a ruler. Will the young emperor allow the Dragon Spring Sword Sect to
slowly grow larger and eventually become the dominant force in the Great
Li Empire? Will he allow Master Ruan to recruit the large majority of
innate sword talents in the continent?

\"He\'ll at most draw a line at Lake View Academy, creating a scenario
where the Dragon Spring Sword Sect and Sun Scorch Mountain dominate the
south and north, respectively, forcing them to keep each other in check.
So, if there\'s an opportunity for Sun Scorch Mountain to produce an
Upper Five Tier sword cultivator, the Great Li Empire will definitely
assist Sun Scorch Mountain with all its power. Meanwhile, the empire
will continue to constrain the Dragon Spring Sword Sect. This will allow
the Great Li Empire to more easily suppress the fortune of the Luminous
Vermilion Empire.

\"Both of us bear grudges against Sun Scorch Mountain, but we have to
concede that the cultivators of this immortal force are extremely
capable both inside the mountains and outside the mountains.
Disregarding everything else and only focusing on that pitiful woman ---
we\'ll ignore the complicated relationships as well and only look at the
results --- she was ultimately able to trap Li Tuanjing through a
romantic relationship and prevent him from advancing to the Upper Five
Tiers.

\"During this time, the ancestral hall of Sun Scorch Mountain definitely
said many solemn things to the woman. Something as simple as the
woman\'s character being poor or her betraying their deep feelings for
each other definitely wouldn\'t have been enough to damage Li
Tuanjing\'s Sword Heart and Dao Heart. With Li Tuanjing\'s judgment
skills and open-mindedness, he definitely wouldn\'t have become
despondent because of these things.

\"Thus, it\'s extremely likely that Sun Scorch Mountain allowed Li
Tuanjing to discover the truth. It was indeed true that the woman had
deep feelings for Li Tuanjing, yet she ultimately chose to side with her
immortal force despite this. Or perhaps she did some things that Li
Tuanjing couldn\'t accept and get over. And it was due to this that Li
Tuanjing continued to feel furious even hundreds of years after her
death.

\"How can we judge the cultures and environments of different clans and
immortal forces? We can look at the choices the elders make on major
matters, and we can also observe the temperaments of the young
descendants and disciples that these forces have raised and taught.
Lastly, we can look at how those belonging to the lowest rungs of these
forces make trade-offs between different gains and losses. By looking
across the spectrum from those in high positions to those in low
positions, it will be difficult for us to make an incorrect assessment
of these forces.

\"Back then, that woman from Light Breeze City\'s Xu Clan was allied
with Sun Scorch Mountain\'s mountain-moving ape, but they were also
scheming against each other at the same time. But what\'s the situation
now? They\'re still firm allies with each other, aren\'t they? At the
end of the day, they share the same values and outlooks, and on the
surface, those who seek nothing but benefits often have more friends.

\"As long as your sword doesn\'t truly cut to their core and foundation,
the surface-level friends of Sun Scorch Mountain will remain as
surface-level friends. In fact, many cultivators who initially had
slightly poor impressions of Sun Scorch Mountain might end up becoming
its friends, even going as far as to speak up for them.

\"In any case, what were the personalities of that little girl with the
surname Tao and the son of the Light Breeze City Xu Clan\'s clan leader
backer? If you\'re willing to listen, I can recount more than a dozen
matters to you right now. Their actions were influenced by the
atmospheres of their clans, so I wasn\'t surprised in the least.

\"The current Sun Scorch Mountain is different from the Sun Scorch
Mountain that existed during Li Tuanjing\'s lifetime, and this isn\'t
solely due to the fact that there\'s no one suppressing it following the
death of Li Tuanjing. The current environment is one where a single
empire represents an entire continent, so what you and I need to
consider is how we can sever the relationship between the Great Li
Empire and Sun Scorch Mountain, as well as how we can cut Sun Scorch
Mountain off from its many allies.

\"We need to make sense of the potential conflicts over benefits that
exist between the three tiers of cultivators in Sun Scorch Mountain
before we challenge it, and we need to clearly understand the characters
of the elders in its ancestral hall. At the same time, we also need to
understand the trump cards available to Sun Scorch Mountain when it\'s
facing a powerful enemy.

\"By considering all of these things, our sword strikes will feel one
hundred times worse for our opponents compared to if we didn\'t consider
anything at all. Our swords will strike not only their bodies, but also
their hearts. This is a huge difference. Physical wounds only require
cultivators to nurture in seclusion, and it might even allow Sun Scorch
Mountain to unite against a common enemy.

\"If our sword strikes are precise, however, we can wound the hearts of
many people beyond the one or several people we physically hit. At that
time, we can sheathe our blades in satisfaction, having already
unleashed sword strikes to our heart\'s content. Those in Sun Scorch
Mountain will naturally battle mental scars for decades or even one
hundred years, and there will naturally be dozens of cultivators who
continue to unleash sword strikes in our stead, cutting deep into Sun
Scorch Mountain\'s heart each time.\"

Liu Xianyang chuckled as he looked at the young man who had unknowingly
transformed from a mute into a chatterbox, and he suddenly said
something a little strange, remarking, \"As long as you\'re willing to
live and no longer keep the mindset you had when I first met you,
thinking that death is no big matter, then your decision to leave the
Jewel Small World is an extremely correct decision. This is because
you\'re more suited to living in a chaotic world than anyone else. If
your mindset has changed, then I\'ll truly be at ease.\"

Chen Ping\'an appeared slightly anxious as he fumed, \"Were you
listening to me at all?!\"

Liu Xianyang smiled and nodded, saying, \"Yes, I was listening to you.
I\'m not deaf, after all.\"

[]{#chapter-121.xhtml}

# Chapter 620: (2): We\'re All Scholars

Sword of Coming

Chen Ping\'an gloomily took a swig of wine.

\"You\'ve been mulling over these things all these years?\" Liu Xianyang
asked in amusement.

\"I didn\'t slack off with either fist practice or cultivation, and I
would use much of my free time to mull over these matters,\" Chen
Ping\'an replied with a huff.

Liu Xianyang pointed at Chen Ping\'an\'s wine bowl and asked, \"Aren\'t
you thirsty after saying so much?\"

Chen Ping\'an simply put his hands inside his opposite sleeves, no
longer wanting to drink wine.

Liu Xianyang smiled and asked, \"Do you truly understand why Sun Scorch
Mountain and Light Breeze City are behaving like this?\"

\"What do you mean?\" Chen Ping\'an asked with a puzzled expression.

\"Why are they harming others for their own gain? Why aren\'t they
acting in a way to benefit others? Or even if they do act in a way to
temporarily benefit others, why is this nothing more than an exquisitely
disguised way to benefit themselves in the long run?\" Liu Xianyang
elaborated his question and asked.

\"On the other hand, why are some people willing to benefit themselves
but also benefit other people?\" Liu Xianyang continued.

He answered his own question, explaining, \"Because these are two
completely different types of people. One type of person resents the
world, while the other type of person feels a close bond with the world.
The former covets fame and riches, chasing after all types of tangible
benefits in a pragmatic manner. Even though the items of their pursuit
are seemingly unreachable in the eyes of mortal people, the tangible
nature of their ambitions actually renders these ambitions fairly
low-level. However, it\'s precisely because these ambitions are
low-level and consistent with innate human nature that they\'re firm and
unwavering.

"The latter type of person is willing to benefit other people while
striving toward their own goals, but their idealistic visions are
genuinely lofty and relatively intangible. They have a connate sense of
closeness with the world, and they\'re willing to forego tangible items
and benefits for the sake of an internal sense of ease and comfort. Of
course, they also strive to feel a deeper sense of belonging in the
world.

\"However, it\'s because of the lofty and intangible nature of their
ambitions that they\'re very prone to feeling disappointed. Indeed, a
fight between the intangible and tangible will often leave the former
bruised and bloodied. Fundamentally speaking, the former type of person
staunchly believes that the world is far from ideal, so they need to
fight for their own benefits to enjoy a better life. Conversely, the
latter type of person believes that the world can become a better place.

\"So, the answer is actually very simple. The Qi refiners at Sun Scorch
Mountain and Light Breeze City might look like cultivators, but in
reality, what they pursue isn\'t the Great Dao. Rather, they\'re simply
pursuing benefits, tangible benefits that are loftier than those pursued
by rulers, officials, and subordinates. In the minds of these people,
they have a clear monetary value attached to each item, understanding
how many immortal coins each cultivation base, each natural treasure, or
each person can bring them.\"

After explaining this, Liu Xianyang said in conclusion, \"I dare say
that you definitely felt a sense of confusion regarding scholars and
cultivators in the outside world after you left the Jewel Small World.
At the same time, you would have also experienced a period of
self-doubt. And in the end, you felt a certain level of rejection toward
the two major notions of scholars and cultivators.\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded and admitted, \"Yes, that\'s true.\"

He benefited a lot from Liu Xianyang\'s explanation.

This was as expected of a scholar who had studied for many years in the
Pure Confucian Chen Clan.

Liu Xianyang took a sip of wine before putting down his wine bowl and
grumbling, \"No, this won\'t do. I can\'t keep up this pretense
anymore!\"

Chen Ping\'an was perplexed.

Liu Xianyang revealed using his mind\'s lake, \"Someone asked me to
deliver this message to you --- I naturally wouldn\'t have thought about
all these things by myself. That person said your mind would feel more
at ease after hearing this, and you would also feel a little more hope
for the world, having better understood these two types of people.

\"As for who spoke these words, Mr. Chen didn\'t tell me, nor did he ask
me to reveal this to you. Rather, he told me to pretend that this was a
level of understanding gained from my studies. I surmise that the person
who wants to help you and can also ask Mr. Chen to help him deliver a
message is most probably the Scholarly Sage.

\"This old scholar is also an interesting character, and when visiting
the Pure Confucian Chen Clan one time, he secretly met me and purposely
introduced himself as an outsider who had come to admire the ancestral
hall of the Chen Clan. Afterward, he chatted with me atop the rock cliff
beside the river for more than two hours. I call this a chat, but it was
actually him rambling on the entire time.

\"Apart from some trivial small talk, he sat there and complained for
more than one hour, grumbling about how Mr. Chen\'s knowledge wasn\'t
lofty enough and how the teachings of the Second Sage\'s lineage
weren\'t good enough. His spittle flew everywhere, and he was truly as
spirited as could be. He even persuaded me to change lineages and join
the Etiquette Sage\'s lineage instead, and I almost felt the urge to
reply with a punch.\"

Upon saying this, Liu Xianyang raised a fist before using his other hand
to lightly push it down. He smiled and continued, \"I enjoyed a hearty
conversation with the Scholarly Sage, and he chuckled and pushed my hand
down after seeing me raise a fist. He said, and I quote, \'Don\'t be
like this. Let\'s discuss things in a civilized manner. We\'re all
scholars, so why don\'t you give me some face.\'\"

Chen Ping\'an pinched his glabella.

His master could genuinely do something like this.

When the sword cultivators of the Northern Complete Reed Continent had
challenged the Pure White Continent back then, his master had most
likely acted in a similar manner to subdue them.

Fortunately, the disciples belonging to the Scholarly lineage --- Senior
Brother Zuo You, Mr. Qi, and even Imperial Preceptor Cui Chan ---
didn\'t inherit this habit.

Chen Ping\'an was naturally reminded of his own disciple, Cui Dongshan.

Chen Chun\'an had personally accompanied the descendants and disciples
of the Pure Confucian Chen Clan and made his way to the Sword Qi Great
Wall. Chen Ping\'an was convinced that Cui Dongshan had definitely
contributed to this decision in one way or another.

There was no need for Liu Xianyang to say anything extra regarding these
matters.

In fact, Chen Ping\'an was already delighted to reunite with Liu
Xianyang in a foreign land.

Chen Ping\'an raised his wine bowl and proposed, \"A toast?\"

\"I\'m done,\" Liu Xianyang replied with a shake of his head.

He glanced up at the sky and said, \"The others and I are all staying at
Sword Immortal Sun Juyuan\'s residence, and I quickly put down my
luggage before hurriedly going to the Ning Residence to look for you.
However, I was greeted by that kind old grandma, and she told me I would
most likely find you drinking at this wine shop. Ning Yao probably came
over after being informed by that old grandma.\"

Liu Xianyang stood up and said with a chuckle, \"In any case, I\'m
likely going to become a frequent visitor to the Ning Residence in the
future, and I\'ll frequently drag you over here to drink wine. This is
because none of my friends believe me when I tell them that I\'m friends
with you, not even Chen Shi. They claim I\'m boasting and speaking from
my ass. How infuriating! I seriously don\'t understand\... How has being
friends with Chen Ping\'an become such an impressive feat? Shouldn\'t it
be the other way around? Was it not Chen Ping\'an\'s greatest fortune to
become friends with Liu Xianyang?\"

Chen Ping\'an stood up and replied with a smile, \"I can even squat
beside the street to drink and chat with you as long as you help the
wine shop attract customers in the future.\"

One of them was returning to the residence of Sword Immortal Sun, and
one of them was returning to the Ning Residence, but they would travel
the same way for a while, so the two of them left the wine shop
together. Before leaving, Liu Xianyang didn\'t forget to pick up the
broken shards of the wine bowl on the ground, quietly saying,
\"Shattered bowl, lasting peace.\"\[1\]

Liu Xianyang wrapped his arm around Chen Ping\'an\'s neck as they walked
along the empty street, almost putting him in a headlock as he laughed
loudly and said, \"You can open your eyes wide and look clearly the next
time we travel to the foot of Sun Scorch Mountain. At that time, you can
witness just how domineering my sword skills are.\"

Tao Ban and the two other young shop attendants looked over at the two
young men.

The second shopkeeper was being ruthlessly bullied today and was unable
to fight back, but he somehow appeared quite happy despite this...?

------------

At Stalactite Mountain, the Northern Complete Reed Continent\'s Sword
Immortal Shao Yunyan stood inside a garden, where the gourd vine had
surprisingly disappeared already.

This was because Shao Yunyan had handed this paramount treasure to Water
Scripture Mountain\'s Lu Sui when she and the Great Emblem Sword Sect\'s
Liu Jinglong had returned from the Sword Qi Great Wall and come here to
bid farewell. In fact, Shao Yunyan had even asked the young sword
immortal, Liu Jinglong, for assistance. Apart from asking Lu Sui to
deliver the almost-ripe Sword Nurturing Gourds outside Water Scripture
Mountain, informing her of who the corresponding buyers were, Shao
Yunyan also asked Liu Jinglong to help escort the delivery of these
Sword Nurturing Gourds.

Lu Sui naturally refused this request. Even though her master had an
incredibly close relationship with Shao Yunyan despite not being Dao
partners, they were ultimately from different immortal forces, and Lu
Sui was also a junior. As such, she didn\'t dare to make such a critical
decision alone and accept such a paramount treasure. However, Shao
Yunyan was extremely stubborn, and she wouldn\'t take no for an answer.

In the end, Lu Sui could only tremble with unease and agree to this
request. If it weren\'t for the accompaniment of Liu Jinglong, Lu Sui
didn\'t believe she could return to the Northern Complete Reed Continent
alive after agreeing to Shao Yunyan\'s request. This paramount immortal
treasure had far too many ties to divine destiny and fate, things that
were as mystical as could be. Even as one of the top ten young
cultivators in the Northern Complete Reed Continent, Lu Sui didn\'t
believe for a second that she could firmly grasp this fated Dao
opportunity.

Before parting ways, Shao Yunyan had smiled and said to Lu Sui, \"Help
me deliver a message to your master. Tell him that I\'ve missed him a
lot these past few years.\"

Shao Yunyan surprisingly left her residence today, making her way around
the various scenic spots of Stalactite Mountain.

Her direct disciples had already taken the remaining valuable treasures
and belongings of the Spring Banner Inn and secretly left Stalactite
Mountain.

One of her disciples perhaps felt like they were free and could act as
they pleased, so they attempted to join forces with some outsiders to
hunt down Lu Sui and Liu Jinglong.

Shao Yunyan didn\'t try to stop this disciple, instead allowing this
immoral individual to pursue their urge to kill. Was it the case that
fortune and calamity were summoned by the actions of people, or was it
the case that they were predestined by the heavens? None of this
mattered anymore.

Like the Spring Banner Inn, the Plum Blossom Garden was also one of the
four major private residences of Stalactite Mountain.

Bian Jing didn\'t travel to the Southern Whirl Continent with Yan Lü,
Jiang Guancheng, and the other young sword cultivators, and he instead
stayed behind at the Plum Blossom Garden by himself.

There was a woman with plum blossom makeup on her glabella, with her
skin pale and her lips red and supple. She was wearing an exquisitely
woven dress, and her beauty was beyond description.

She was the true owner of the Plum Blossom Garden, but she largely lived
in seclusion and seldom ever appeared in front of others.

Bian Jing referred to her as Lady Tuo Yan, and this was a beautiful name
that was a perfect fit for this beautiful woman.

Even though Bian Jing had no interest in romantic relationships, he
still had to admit that Lady Tuo Yan was a very beautiful sight to
behold.

Including the Bamboo Sea Small World\'s Lady Zhu and the Plum Blossom
Garden\'s Lady Tuo Yan, there were ten renowned women in the Majestic
World who were so stunningly beautiful that even immortals in the
mountains would daydream about them and fall head over heels for them.

There was another peculiar fact about these women, that being that they
were all deities, spirits, or ghosts.

Lady Tuo Yan and Bian Jing sat opposite each other in a waterside
pavilion, with the former playing around with an imitation bamboo sea
that the Plum Blossom Garden had just given her. The piece was
exquisitely crafted using bamboo inlaying techniques, depicting a scene
of many thin and well-spaced bamboo. Moreover, the inlaid bamboo was all
sourced from the Bamboo Sea Small World, meaning that this piece was
worth a fortune.

\"Are you that afraid of death?\" Lady Tuo Yan asked.

Bian Jing nodded and replied, \"I\'m actually doing okay, and I really
want to visit the city wall with Lin Junbi and the others. However, the
other person likes to act mysteriously, and they insist that I conceal
myself and remain hidden, saying that they\'ve performed divinations and
that it\'s very easy for me to lose everything and suffer a miserable
fate if I\'m not careful.\"

He then asked, \"Who was the first to suggest creating that new gate?
And what does the Great Heavenly Lord in Stalactite Mountain think about
this?\"

\"You don\'t need to worry about these things,\" Lady Tuo Yan replied.
\"Even if the entire Stalactite Mountain ceases to exist, the old and
new gates will still remain standing.\"

\"There are actually sword immortals acting as inside assistants and
willing to help us guard the gates?\" Bian Jing asked in puzzlement.

Lady Tuo Yan glanced at the young man and replied, \"Is that very
strange? One side has suffered deaths for ten thousand years, while the
other side has enjoyed peace and prosperity the entire time, even going
as far as to laugh about the dead people on the other side. How would
you feel if you were in their shoes? Perhaps you can endure this for one
or two years, but can you endure this for tens upon hundreds of years?
Can people with good tempers become sword immortals?\"

Bian Jing nodded and said, \"If it were me, I would repay the favor
several times over.\"

The young owner of the Stork Inn had lived here his entire life, just
like all of his ancestors. Right now, he was squatting outside the
entrance of his inn and playing with a passing dog.

The sun was warm and gentle, causing the lazy people to become even
lazier. Today was another boring day of peace and prosperity.

------------

Beyond Stalactite Mountain.

It naturally wasn\'t the case that there was nothing left at the Flood
Dragon Trench apart from some small fry, and in reality, it was still a
forbidden land that was extremely difficult to cross even for earth
immortal cultivators. They could only take a detour and stay well away
from the trench.

Further away, there was the Rain Dragon Sect, where the towering statues
of the rain god and the divine general faced off against each other.
Stalactite Mountain\'s Water Essence Palace was a private residence
owned by this immortal force.

Apart from the formidable Rain Dragon Sect, there were several other
immortal forces of various sizes located on the islands of the vast sea,
each with their own fates and vicissitudes.

Along the route of Osmanthus Island, an intercontinental ship, the
fourth scene in the sea was slowly sailing past the opening between the
feet of the Rain Dragon Sect\'s two towering golden deity statues, which
each measured more than three hundred meters in height.

According to legends, the golden divine general, who was resting his
hands on the hilt of his sword, had previously been a primordial deity
responsible for guarding the southern gate of the Heavenly Court.
Opposite him, the deity statue with a blurry appearance and a
five-colored ribbon was the first formal rain god, the predecessor of
the many that existed in the skies today.

This rain god was said to have controlled all of the True Dragons
responsible for summoning clouds and rain, and after having its Dao
Manifestation reconstructed by the old ancestor of the Rain Dragon Sect,
it almost appeared as if this rain god still controlled a portion of
water fortune in the southern region of the sea.

The Rain Dragon Sect, where two deity statues were eternally facing off
against each other, had an ancient tradition with an extremely long
history. When choosing immortal Dao partners, the female cultivators of
the sect would completely rely on tossing down the embroidered balls
specially crafted by the sect.

Upper Five Tier cultivators could naturally obtain these embroidered
balls if they used force, and earth immortal cultivators most certainly
wouldn\'t be able to resist, not even if they used immortal techniques
to fight for them. However, an Upper Five Tier cultivator getting
involved would be an act of challenging the entire Rain Dragon Sect.

Approximately ten years ago, a young Qi refiner with abundant fortune
had traveled past the two deity statues on Osmanthus Island. A celestial
maiden from the Rain Dragon Sect had coincidentally thrown out an
embroidered ball, and the young cultivator had been in just the right
place to catch it. As if ascending to the heavens, the embroidered ball
and the colorful ribbon attached to it had then dragged him up toward
the Rain Dragon Sect in a graceful manner.

Not only that, but the young man had also enjoyed further cultivation
fortune, surprisingly becoming immortal Dao partners with yet another
celestial maiden. This was a paramount fated opportunity and blessed
romantic destiny, so immense that even the distant Old Dragon City in
the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent had heard about it.

The young man called Fu Ke was indeed a fated individual at the Rain
Dragon Sect. He had initially been a measly no-name cultivator, but
after cultivating the Rain Dragon Sect\'s immortal technique, he had
unexpectedly progressed by leaps and bounds. Not only did he have
beautiful Dao partners, but he even advanced to the Golden Core Tier and
became the fastest-advancing earth immortal in the history of the sect.

Moreover, the young man had toiled outside the mountains for many years,
so after reaching the peak, his manner of interacting with people and
matters was far different from that of the other cultivators in the
sect. This resulted in the Rain Dragon Sect viewing him in even higher
regard.

Today, Fu Ke arrived at the feet of a deity statue and gazed into the
distance, a bright glimmer in his eyes. In just a dozen or so years, he
had transformed from an impoverished young cultivator into an esteemed
cultivator even among other immortals.

Cultivators with whom he had overcome difficulties together had heard of
his feats and come here to visit, and Fu Ke would personally head down
to meet them and arrange accommodation for them with the nearby vassal
forces, since the Rain Dragon Sect didn\'t allow outsiders to enter the
island. Fu Ke would give them a healthy sum of money when they left, but
if they were unwilling to leave, Fu Ke would help them find a job or
position in the nearby immortal forces.

There were senior brothers in the Rain Dragon Sect who wanted to travel
to the Sword Qi Great Wall to train, yet they would all be blocked by
the elders of the sect. Fu Ke would accompany them when they gloomily
drank wine, and he wouldn\'t say much as he simply sat there and drank.

Fu Ke had enjoyed unlimited success and glory these past few years, and
he would occasionally pause and feel like he was dreaming. Thinking back
to his pitiful past and thinking of the fellow passengers on Osmanthus
Island back then, it was ultimately he alone who had risen above the
others and ascended to the peak.

However, there was a small knot in the depths of Fu Ke\'s heart. He had
heard many years ago that following his departure from the
intercontinental ship, another young boy from the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent had unexpectedly used some mystical ability at the Flood
Dragon Trench and actually managed to leave alive, earning fame and
glory as a result.

Not only that, but the person with the surname Chen was shockingly
enjoying even better fortune than him, with news of his many feats
traveling to the Rain Dragon Sect through the Sword Qi Great Wall and
Stalactite Mountain\'s Water Essence Palace. Fu Ke smiled and appeared
composed on the surface, even putting in a few good words for the young
man and the Scholarly lineage. In his heart, however, he thought to
himself that it would be good if Chen Ping\'an died at the Sword Qi
Great Wall.

There were naturally no grudges between Fu Ke and Chen Ping\'an.

If Chen Ping\'an died, the world would still continue on the same
trajectory as always, no?

Fu Ke smiled faintly, with his mood improving greatly. He turned around
and left, continuing to cultivate in earnest. If he advanced even
further and became a Nascent Tier cultivator, he would be one step
closer to becoming the future sect leader of the Rain Dragon Sect. At
that time, perhaps he would even have the opportunity to become Dao
partners with a female sword immortal from the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Little did he know, the path of the Great Dao was an unpredictable one.

When the water grass was lush, countless fish would swim around, and
there might even appear flood dragons.

When the heavenly fortunes changed, the seas would dry, and all the
flood dragons would die under the blazing sun.

1\. In Chinese, the term for shattered (碎碎) is homophonic with the
term for lasting (碎碎), hence people say breakage brings peace
(碎碎平安) when they accidentally break something.
