# Chapter 621: (1): Learning Sword Techniques

Sword of Coming

After returning to the Sword Qi Great Wall, Chen Ping\'an chose a
relatively quiet section of the wall measuring approximately five
hundred meters in length to guard by himself.

Generally speaking, for sword immortals under the Unpolished Jade Tier,
only Nascent Tier sword cultivators would have the right to guard a
section of the great wall by themselves. For example, Qi Shou, who had
recently broken through while cultivating in seclusion.

Among the younger generation of innate sword prodigies at the Sword Qi
Great Wall, Qi Shou also became the first person to advance to the
Nascent Tier.

This was an ironclad rule at the Sword Qi Great Wall, and it was also a
prestigious honor.

Because of this, even Ning Yao needed to cooperate with Chen Sanqiu and
the others when she fought on the great wall. Similarly, Pang Yuanji and
Gao Yehou also needed to cooperate with their companions. Of course, the
sections of the city wall guarded by these prodigious groups were longer
than those guarded by ordinary Nascent Tier sword cultivators. In fact,
they could even rival the lengths of the city wall guarded by many
powerful sword immortals.

Chen Ping\'an was an exception, yet this didn\'t draw any protest or
criticism. The reason was that he hadn\'t technically broken any rules.
He hadn\'t become a sword cultivator yet, and he was only a pure martial
artist who had nurtured a few flying swords.

In addition, Chen Ping\'an was willing to take risks and act as bait,
actively attracting the attention of those hiding great demons. Ning Yao
didn\'t say anything, Zuo You didn\'t say anything, and Old Sword
Immortal Yao Lianyun of the Yao Clan didn\'t say anything, so the other
sword immortals at the Sword Qi Great Wall naturally wouldn\'t say
anything or try to block Chen Ping\'an either.

Chen Ping\'an and Qi Shou coincidentally became neighbors on the great
wall.

Qi Shou continued to wield his sword, and he only used a slight bit of
his attention to glance at Chen Ping\'an. He wasn\'t wearing a random
assortment of face masks today, and he was dressed in an azure Dao robe
under the standard Dao robe from the garment market. There was a
standard sword from the sword market resting horizontally across his
knees, and he had yet to summon the two powerful celestial tools he had
used to kill Li Zhen.

It was only the early stages of battle between the two sides, and the
many bonded flying swords of the sword immortals were like a tidal wave
that rushed at the forefront of the battlefield, obstructing the advance
of the demon army. Beyond this army were some demons that had slipped
through the cracks, and it was these enemies that the earth immortal
sword cultivators needed to kill with their swords.

Afterward, if there were still demons that were fortunate enough to
survive, most likely having managed to charge past the second sword
formation, they would be met with a barrage of flying swords unleashed
by Middle Five Tier sword cultivators.

This was also a form of sword practice at the Sword Qi Great Wall, and
those belonging to the three tiers from the Abode Tier to the Dragon
Gate Tier would gradually familiarize themselves with the battlefield
even though their cultivation base was still relatively low. They would
also develop stronger links with their bonded flying swords, allowing
their attacks to become quicker and more natural.

Qi Shou shifted his gaze and glanced at Chen Ping\'an\'s sword attack.
He had still been cultivating in seclusion during Chen Ping\'an\'s
battle with Li Zhen beyond the city wall, so he hadn\'t witnessed the
exchange and had only heard about it afterward. As proud and haughty as
Qi Shou was, he still had to admit that it was slightly disappointing to
have missed the battle.

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t conceal anything today, unleashing all four flying
swords at once. However, he had seemingly learned a new illusion skill
from some unknown person in a hurry, and looking at the appearances of
his four flying swords, they frequently shifted between different forms
and colors.

Demons at the Nascent Tier and Upper Five Tiers could easily see through
this crude illusion technique after a few glances, but it was more than
enough to trick the large army of demons lowering their heads and
charging forward. They would easily suffer a ruthless pummeling after
being slowed down by the four flying swords.

There was another minor aspect to this, and once the demons charging in
front were killed by his sword, the many demons behind them would
continue to charge forward, but would involuntarily slow down.

Compared to the fully concentrating Chen Ping\'an, Qi Shou appeared much
more relaxed as he attacked the demons and slowed them down. Even
distracting himself by glancing at Chen Ping\'an didn\'t affect his
battlefield in the least.

It could be said that the large army of demons from the Savage World was
suffering heavy casualties, but even so, it was still very far away from
the city wall. Sword cultivators like Qi Shou, who had already taken
part in three large-scale battles, appeared relaxed and composed as they
continued to defend their sections of the wall.

Qi Shou also had three bonded flying swords, with Flying Kite being the
quickest and enjoying an advantage when it came to one-on-one battles.
Heartstring was most suited to drawn-out battles, and it was least
afraid of demons with extremely thick skin and tough physiques.

As for the most mystical Jumping Spider, a Daoist sage had further
remarked, \"Owner of the stars, rain upon the mortal world. Similar to
Great Sword Immortal Yue Qing\'s bonded flying sword, Soaring Cloud
Sparrow, and Yao Lianyun\'s bonded flying sword that could summon
numerous seas of clouds, Depths of the Clouds, Jumping Spider was best
at dealing large-scale damage to the enemies.\"

Thus, Qi Shou was able to easily defend his small section of the city
wall even though he had only just advanced to the Nascent Tier.
Generally speaking, only when the overall defensive line of sword
cultivators began to feel fatigued --- including the sword immortals who
started with abundant spiritual energy and the Middle Five Tier sword
cultivators who had relatively less spiritual energy to begin with ---
would the battle enter dangerous territory. Things would become very
dangerous on the city wall, with some sword cultivators being forced to
retreat and an increasing number of sword cultivators being killed by
the demons.

Regardless of whether it was demons that had embarked on the path of
cultivation and assumed human form or beastly demons that were still yet
to develop the ability to assume human form, those that were unlucky or
dared to change their paths and stray into Qi Shou\'s defensive
jurisdiction would all be brutally killed by Flying Kite.

Qi Shou had always been cruel when killing enemies with Flying Kite, and
he liked to gradually slice off the flesh of the demons until their
bones were completely exposed. He enjoyed making them suffer a greater
pain than death.

He would leave the more troublesome demons to his second flying sword,
Heartstring, and the longer these battles dragged on, the less chance of
victory his enemies would have. This was because Heartstring would have
more time to accumulate energy. This flying sword could travel even more
quickly than Flying Kite, and it could use the small wisps of
circulating spiritual energy on the battlefield to automatically look
for the critical acupoints of its enemies.

Qi Shou glanced at the sea of corpses on the battlefield in the
distance. He had witnessed the same thing when ascending the city wall
and unleashing sword strikes against the demon army for the first time,
and back then, he couldn\'t help but ask, \"Why are these vile beasts
unafraid of death?\"

A sword immortal had smiled and explained, \"It\'s not that they\'re
unafraid of death. However, life is cheap in the Savage World, and the
same is true even if they become cultivators. Only by becoming sword
cultivators can they change their fates and become slightly more
valuable, giving them a greater chance of survival when they attack the
great wall.\"

Qi Shou was yet to summon Jumping Spider. There was no need to do so.

When it came to battles between the Sword Qi Great Wall and the Savage
World, the most critical aspect was never the overwhelming power of some
sword immortal or the astounding true body and mystical power of some
great demon. The most critical aspect was always defined by a single
word: attrition.

Each side would slowly weaken and grind down the other, and it was a
competition to see who would comprehensively grind down the other first.
The Savage World relied on its overwhelming strength in numbers, while
the Sword Qi Great Wall relied on the accumulated spiritual energy of
the sword cultivators.

The Sword Qi Great Wall had suffered heavy losses and almost fallen the
previous time it had enjoyed a prodigious generation of innate sword
talent, with all of the young sword cultivators either dying or
suffering severe wounds. This was because the Savage World had
stubbornly continued to attack and had almost held on until the very
end.

It was also after that brutal lesson that an increasing number of
intercontinental ships traveled to Stalactite Mountain, allowing the
Sword Qi Great Wall\'s Nalan Clan and Yan Clan to enjoy significant
rises as they did more and more business with the Majestic World,
purchasing huge amounts of alchemical pills, talismans, and immortal
treasures. These were goods that sword cultivators had looked down on in
the past, yet would now purchase as an extra layer of security.

With intercontinental ships being able to make huge profits by traveling
to Stalactite Mountain, many new clans and immortal forces enjoyed rapid
rises in the nine continents of the Majestic World, becoming so rich
that they were almost breathing money. Among these forces was the Pure
White Continent\'s Liu Clan, the Circling Ascension Continent\'s
Mountain and Water Cave, the Northern Complete Reed Continent\'s Jade
Forest Sect, the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent\'s Old Dragon City,
the Rain Dragon Sect which acted as an important hub, and so on.

On the other side of Chen Ping\'an was Xie Songhua, a female sword
immortal from the Pure White Continent. She had only arrived at the
Sword Qi Great Wall at the end of winter, and she had kept a low profile
the entire time.

She was staying in the private residence of a deceased sword immortal
between the great wall and the main city, and because she had only just
arrived and had no military merit to her name, she was only staying
there on a temporary basis. Xie Songhua almost never interacted with
other people, and she would seldom show up at places that were bustling
with noise.

After she summoned her bonded flying sword, its aura and strength could
only be regarded as extremely mediocre. The flying sword traveled at a
middling speed, with its sword light and sword intent also very
ordinary. It appeared as if the flying sword were only just powerful
enough to kill its enemies.

Qi Shou couldn\'t help but take a glance at the bamboo sword case on Xie
Songhua\'s back.

She was presumably the person helping to scoop in the larger prey as
Chen Ping\'an fished. It was said that she was only at the Unpolished
Jade Tier, and this caused Qi Shou to feel slightly puzzled. If a demon
took the bait and required Xie Songhua to unleash a sword strike using
her full power, this would most certainly be a large fish. Thus, even if
she were a sword immortal at the peak stage of the Unpolished Jade Tier,
would she truly be able to subdue the great demon and prevent it from
dragging Chen Ping\'an away along with his fishing rod?

Could it be that Xie Songhua was the type of sword cultivator that
pursued extremes, yearning to achieve maximum destructive power with a
single sword strike? Such kinds of strange sword immortals had appeared
at the Sword Qi Great Wall before, but only very rarely. They were best
at fighting to the death, and they liked to determine victory and defeat
in a single exchange. If their opponent managed to survive their attack,
however, then they would very likely lose and be killed. Because of
this, these kinds of sword immortals seldom survived for long at the
Sword Qi Great Wall.

From right to left, there were Qi Shou, Chen Ping\'an, and Xie Songhua,
with each guarding a section of the wall.

There were no substitute sword cultivators standing behind the three of
them.

As they defended the great wall, Fan Dache secretly visited Chen
Ping\'an once, not daring to stay for too long as he put down a pot of
wine before running away.

Chen Ping\'an cracked open the clay seal and took small sips of wine,
keeping his eyes on the movements of the demons on the battlefield the
entire time.

In contrast to Qi Shou\'s incisive and almost cruel attacks, Chen
Ping\'an tried his best to kill his enemies in a single blow, or at
least severely wound their physical bodies with each sword strike. At
worst, he would try to inhibit the movement of the demons.

Chen Ping\'an had fallen three tiers following his battle with Li Zhen,
meaning there was no easy way to recover his relatively impressive store
of spiritual energy. For example, he couldn\'t restore his water palace
to its peak state simply by refining some water elixirs.

If Chen Ping'an ignored the potential costs and continued to channel
spiritual energy, he would essentially be overexerting himself, thereby
worsening the fractures on the water seal that initially could have been
repaired. The colorful water god murals would also peel off quicker, and
the small pond beneath the water seal would start to leak.

Simply put, the water palace could be viewed as a vessel that was
initially able to hold half a liter of water fortune, for example.
Following Chen Ping\'an\'s battle, it was now only able to hold less
than two hundred milliliters of water fortune. If he exhausted too much
sword intent and drew on the very last drops of his spiritual energy to
support his sword strikes, he would inevitably fall into a vicious
cycle. Relying on medicines and elixirs to replenish the spiritual
energy in his water palace would only result in more water fortune being
wasted and dissipated, ultimately wasting the incredibly valuable water
elixirs of Mirage Lake\'s water god palace.

This wasn\'t the most troublesome matter.

Even though Pine Needle and Lightning Devourer were only replica swords
from Hatred Sword Mountain, the sharpness of these flying swords
couldn\'t be faulted after they reached advanced refinement. However,
they lacked the innate mystical ability unique to flying swords, and in
some sense, this was also true for First and Fifteenth. Whether or not
one was a sword cultivator, and whether or not one\'s bonded flying
swords were naturally nurtured, would make a huge difference.

There was no need to say anything more about Qi Shou, as Chen Ping\'an
had personally faced his three bonded flying swords before. As for Gu
Jianlong\'s flying sword, Arsenic, this was a legitimate bonded sword of
extremely high grade, so it would very often kill its targets once it
struck them. Once Arsenic properly pierced into its target\'s body, its
sword intent would seep into the victim\'s acupoints and become very
difficult to remove.

In any case, overcoming troublesome matters was also a form of
cultivation.

Chen Ping\'an carefully controlled the expenditure of spiritual energy
in his four critical acupoints while simultaneously repairing his water
palace, mountain shrine, and wood residence. These critical acupoints
were almost completely depleted of spiritual energy, and, looking at the
water palace, for example, many blemishes became increasingly clear
compared to normal conditions.

Thus, Chen Ping\'an immediately closed the gates of the water palace, no
longer using spiritual energy from this critical acupoint. At the same
time, the green-robed children started to busily carry out repair works.
Meanwhile, there was a manifestation of a yin god guarding the wood
residence, and there was the small golden person patrolling around the
mountain shrine.

The situation at the Sword Qi Great Wall was urgent, so Chen Ping\'an
didn\'t have the luxury of resting and recuperating in the city. That
being the case, he took the next best option of tempering himself
through battle, seizing this opportunity to identify all of the small
blemishes and shortcomings in the foundation of his cultivation. He
didn\'t need to worry too much even if this decision would exhaust a
large number of water elixirs from Mirage Lake\'s water god palace, as
well as a huge number of pills from the Ning Residence\'s storage.

He could earn money by killing demons on the battlefield.

This was especially the case given that there were two written rules at
the Sword Qi Great Wall that greatly benefited Chen Ping\'an. When it
came to killing demons, cultivators at different cultivation bases would
receive different monetary rewards for killing demons at the same
cultivation base. For example, a Middle Five Tier sword cultivator would
receive far more money for killing a Golden Core Tier demon than what a
sword immortal would receive for killing a Golden Core Tier demon.

And right now, Chen Ping\'an was killing demons and earning money as a
second tier Qi refiner.

The military supervisors and the battlefield recorders belonging to the
Hidden Official\'s lineage and the Confucian Sect had no issues with
this.

He had suffered a drop in cultivation base due to his abilities, and he
was also acting as bait thanks to his abilities. Taking this into
account, both the military supervisors and the battlefield recorders
felt like Chen Ping\'an deserved the additional rewards.

Chen Ping\'an was seemingly focused on controlling his four flying
swords to navigate through the battlefield and kill enemies, but in
reality, he was actually focusing some of his attention on the two
battlefields beside him as well. Having reached the Nascent Tier now, Qi
Shou\'s sword strikes were markedly different from before, when he had
battled against Chen Ping\'an on the street.

As for Sword Immortal Xie Songhua\'s sword strikes, they were
comparatively more basic and simple, and she simply relied on the
sharpness of her bonded flying sword --- which Chen Ping\'an didn\'t
know the name of --- to kill her enemies. This actually allowed Chen
Ping\'an to comprehend a few more things.

Chen Ping\'an ultimately wasn\'t a pure sword cultivator, so controlling
two flying swords required a lot of focus and spiritual energy, much
more than if he were a sword cultivator. There were naturally benefits
to having the physique of a Vajra Body Tier martial artist, not least
that he could strengthen his soul and spirit. Even so, this couldn\'t
compare to the sword strikes of legitimate sword cultivators.

On the other side of the battlefield, the tidal wave of demons continued
to surge forward, refusing to give the Sword Qi Great Wall any reprieve
no matter how many demons were killed.

Because of this, Chen Ping\'an needed to frequently drink wine, and not
just any normal wine.

Qi Shou was slightly amused as he looked at this. Things were truly
difficult for the second shopkeeper, who was fighting on the city wall
at his own cost. It would be quite unfortunate if he collapsed from
exhaustion before some big fish took his bait.

However, there was a bright glimmer in the eyes of the increasingly pale
young man, and disregarding Chen Ping\'an\'s slight struggle to maintain
control of his flying swords to kill demons and only focusing on his
tenacity, as well as his clever choices regarding some finer details,
his performance was genuinely quite impressive in the eyes of Qi Shou.
Even though they had almost fought to the death before, Qi Shou
wouldn\'t be so petty as to wish Chen Ping\'an injury after injury on
the city wall, and eventually injury to the foundation of his Great Dao.

Thus, Qi Shou used his mind\'s lake to say in suggestion, \"If you
don\'t mind, you can purposely allow a group of vile beasts to charge
through the four battlefields of your flying swords and allow them to
get closer to the city wall. That way, I can summon Jumping Spider and
kill them in one fell swoop, giving me a nice amount of military merit.
Otherwise, you won\'t be able to keep on top of your battlefields in the
long run.\"

Chen Ping\'an was only a second tier cultivator right now, rendering him
unable to even communicate using his mind\'s lake. He could only use the
martial arts technique of compressing his voice into a thread to reply,
\"I appreciate the sentiment, but I don\'t currently need your help. I
can only catch big fish if I appear more pitiful. At that time, I\'ll
ask you for help even if you don\'t offer.\"

He had wasted one or two water elixirs, and even his four critical
acupoints were more wounded than before, making it increasingly
difficult for him to control his flying swords and attack the demons.
However, he would make a fortune if he were able to successfully reel in
an Upper Five Tier great demon.

This was the way to calculate gains and losses.

Just like Qi Shou had guessed, Sword Immortal Xie Songhua was indeed the
type of sword cultivator that pursued an extreme form of sword intent,
seeking to end all battles in a single sword strike.

Xie Songhua was very pragmatic and straightforward, and after the old
great sword immortal chose her to help Chen Ping\'an net his catch, Xie
Songhua had engaged in an open and honest conversation with the young
man. She didn\'t beat around the bush or try to hide anything, and she
directly told Chen Ping\'an that she had come to the Sword Qi Great Wall
to feed her sword one or two great demons. Once she accomplished this
goal and received both the monetary and reputational benefits, she would
immediately leave the great wall and return to the Pure White Continent.

This actually made Chen Ping\'an feel more at ease.

Qi Shou smiled and asked, \"Aren\'t you going to ask your ally, Sword
Immortal Xie Songhua, to help you?\"

\"If I owe a sword immortal a favor, I won\'t dare not return it,\" Chen
Ping\'an replied. \"Not only that, but how I repay the favor will also
become a very challenging problem. On the other hand, owing you a favor
is easier to manage and return. This battle is also destined to drag on
for a long time, so when all is said and done, it\'s difficult to say
which of us will owe the other more favors.\"

Qi Shou felt like Chen Ping\'an was as annoying as always, and he fell
silent for a moment and wordlessly conceded this point. He then asked in
curiosity, \"What percentage of your current struggle is real?\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and replied, \"You won\'t believe my answer no
matter what, so why are you even asking?\"

Qi Shou feigned exasperation and lamented, \"I\'m bored and have nothing
better to do. As a Nascent Tier sword cultivator, none of these enemies
is my match. It feels quite lonely over here.\"

Chen Ping\'an chuckled and said, \"I\'m able to employ a Nascent Tier
sword cultivator and a sword immortal as my door gods. I feel even more
solitude.\"

Qi Shou raised his middle finger.

Chen Ping\'an seized this spare moment to drink another sip of wine, and
inside the wine pot was Bamboo Sea Small World Wine from his wine shop.

As for the Sword Nurturing Gourd by his waist, there was a water elixir
mixed into the wine inside, so Chen Ping\'an wouldn\'t drink this wine
until things became dangerous. In any case, the pots of wine that Fan
Dache occasionally brought over could help Chen Ping\'an replenish his
spiritual energy, so there was temporarily no need to worry. As for the
several valuable alchemical pills inside Fifteenth, which also doubled
as a pocket treasure, these were more targeted and would mainly be used
for situations where his mountain shrine and wood residence were almost
completely exhausted of spiritual energy.

[]{#chapter-123.xhtml}

# Chapter 621: (2): Learning Sword Techniques

Sword of Coming

There were all kinds of strange and fantastical scenes on the
battlefield.

A sea of clouds suddenly materialized and covered an area of fifty
kilometers in radius over the battlefield, and gazing afar from the city
wall, a speck of light instantly burst into existence and tore apart the
sea of clouds, with another ray of light sinking into the clouds
immediately afterward. These attacks then collided with the earth,
triggering a thunderous rumble.

Some demon cultivators furtively snuck past the first sword formation
established by the sword immortals, and when they suddenly reappeared,
they would all be dressed in silver armor without exception. As they
charged forward, these suits of armor could repel the flying swords of
several earth immortal sword cultivators. Before they were targeted and
killed by powerful sword immortals, they would attempt to create
talismanic formations not above the battlefield, but deep underground
instead.

The mountain-moving demons personally led by Great Demon Zhong Guang
continued to maintain their colossal true forms as they ceaselessly
threw mountains at the great wall, making them appear like catapults
from the battlefields of the mortal world.

There was also a great demon, whose name wasn\'t known, hovering
extremely high up in the sky and holding a crystalline white jade vase
in its hand. The vase was tilted downward, with its opening pointing at
the Sword Qi Great Wall and a river rushing down. The river looked like
a length of white silk cloth descending from the skies, yet it never
reached the ground, instead colliding with the tidal wave of sword qi
unleashed from the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Elsewhere, a great demon hid deep underground and revealed its gigantic
true body measuring several hundred meters in length when it suddenly
emerged from the earth. The great demon looked like a mix of a snake and
a flood dragon, and it attempted to destroy the bonded flying swords of
many Middle Five Tier sword cultivators in a single strike.

However, this great demon was instantly noticed by Great Sword Immortal
Li Tuimi on the city wall and promptly pushed back with a single sword
strike, forcing it to retreat underground with its gigantic body. It
attempted to leave the battlefield, but the flying sword continued to
pursue it, with blinding sword light rushing through the ground and
causing it to tremor. In fact, the sword light was so brilliant that it
was visible even through the thick earth.

There were also the demon cultivators that arrived in the second sword
formation after running around and navigating through the flying swords
of the first formation. These demon cultivators would throw some
gravel-like substances onto the battlefield, instantly summoning
hundreds of large skeletal puppets dressed in suits of armor. These
puppets would use their huge bodies to capture the bonded flying swords
of the sword cultivators, and they would immediately explode after
netting a catch.

Because these puppets were located near the boundary of the first and
second sword formations, their violently exploding bones and armors
would affect both earth immortal sword cultivators and Middle Five Tier
sword cultivators. When it came to the earth immortals, perhaps only the
sharpness of their flying swords would be affected by these explosions.
As for the Middle Five Tier sword immortals, however, many of their
flying swords would be severely damaged, and some would even be
completely destroyed.

Standing on the battlefield, some sword cultivators would completely
forget about the flow of time. On the other end of the extreme, some
sword cultivators would tremble with fear and trepidation, feeling like
each passing second was hours or even days.

The sun set, and the moons rose.

The Sword Qi Great Wall was extremely familiar with the three moons of
the Savage World, and they were seemingly becoming brighter and
brighter. It was as if the moonlight were shifting toward the
battlefield and especially favoring the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Qi Shou glanced at Chen Ping\'an and said in warning, \"Be careful of
failing to catch any big fish and being tired to death instead. If this
continues, you\'ll only have the ability to retract your swords a single
time.\"

Chen Ping\'an definitely wouldn\'t have needed to expend so much mental
energy if he were simply wielding his blade against normal enemies.

Now, however, Chen Ping\'an was on high alert the entire time, guarding
against any potential surprises. He didn\'t know where his enemy was
hiding, nor did he know when some great demon would suddenly make a move
against him. If the great demon were sinister and didn\'t strive to kill
Chen Ping\'an, only striving to destroy his four flying swords, this
would still leave him with severe wounds.

Chen Ping\'an raised his Sword Nurturing Gourd and took a large swig of
wine, replying with a whisper, \"And that\'s why this is a competition
of patience and acting. If our enemies still don\'t dare to take a
bigger risk for a bigger reward and truly end up making me feel
impatient, then I\'ll just retrieve my flying swords and ask someone
else to replace me on this section of the wall. It\'s no big deal, and
I\'ll simply abandon this plan of acting as bait.\"

There were countless damaged souls wandering around the battlefield, and
they were continuously shredded to bits by the permeating sword light.
This was another tragedy ringing through the battlefield.

Corpses piled up into mountains again and again, only for the ferocious
attacks of the sword immortals to pulverize the battlefield and flatten
these mountains of corpses time and time again. The entire earth sank,
and the formation cultivators from the Savage World weren\'t allowed to
freely stabilize the earth to gradually elevate the height of the
battlefield.

The atmosphere of bloodshed and malice from death grew thicker and
thicker, unable to be purified and swept away even though the sword
immortals already had a plan and were channeling unique mystical
abilities with their flying swords.

These flying swords swept through the battlefield and tried their best
to wash away the auras of violence and brutality, but they still
struggled immensely to obstruct the formation of some great trend as the
battle continued to drag on, causing the initially clear view that the
sword cultivators had over the battlefield to gradually become hazier.

This was a fight for favorable conditions on the battlefield.

On the other side, the large army of demons from the Savage World became
increasingly fearless and deranged as it charged forward and pushed
toward the great wall. In fact, more and more demon cultivators were
feeling a purer sense of conviction and sacrifice as they stepped onto
the battlefield.

Indeed, it wasn\'t just sword cultivators from the Sword Qi Great Wall
who could bravely march toward death.

And thus, the Daoist sage overseeing the skies plucked a hair out from
his snow-white horsetail whisk, throwing it to the ground and summoning
a sudden burst of torrential rain over the battlefield, clearing away
the sanguine atmosphere and replacing it with a more refreshing one.

There was a stunningly beautiful great demon sitting atop the clouds,
making her appear much like a noble maiden of the Majestic World. She
was wearing two dazzling jade bracelets on each of her wrists, one black
and one white, and they delicately hovered around her skin without
making much contact. A five-colored ribbon gently hovered around her,
and her billowing black hair was seemingly held together by a golden
hairband that was actually suspended in the air.

She immediately retrieved an ancient scroll from her sleeve, lightly
unfurling it to reveal a painting of undulating mountain ranges. There
were dense collections of large peaks and powerful rivers rushing
through them, and it was as if some immortal mystical power had been
used to trap this scenery inside the scroll. It looked to be much more
than just a simple painting.

Dressed in a rose-colored Dao robe, the beautiful great demon smiled as
she retrieved a seal and exhaled a breath of True Qi onto the inscribed
characters. She then lightly stamped the scroll, causing rays of
iridescent light to shoot tens of thousands of meters into the
surroundings. At the same time, the green mountains and blue rivers in
the scroll gradually started to lose their luster.

The great demon lightly pushed the ancient scroll, causing it to
instantly vanish from the spot, leaving behind only the stamped
vermilion characters.

A majestic painting measuring five hundred kilometers in length and
fifty kilometers in width materialized over the battlefield, and not
only that, but spiritual energy emanated from the painting and attempted
to block the torrential downpour summoned by the Daoist sage.

The heavy rain thundered into the painting of mountains and rivers.

Following the collision, not a single drop of rain was able to reach the
battlefield below.

However, heavy rainfall suffused with spiritual energy immediately fell
in the Savage World, lashing the mountain ranges depicted in the
majestic painting hanging over the battlefield.

The Daoist sage flicked his horsetail whisk and shattered the painting,
allowing the torrential downpour formed by horsetail hair to land on the
battlefield below again. The beautiful great demon stabilized the
painting in response, once again blocking the rain. However, the Daoist
sage used his horsetail whisk to shatter the painting a second time.

This process played out again and again, and when the vermilion stamp in
front of the great demon finally lost its glow and shattered into
pieces, she smiled widely and said, \"I\'ll gratefully accept your
precious gift.\"

When she retrieved the seal again, a streak of sword light blasted
through the air toward her. The bracelets on her wrists and her golden
hairband automatically soared into the sky and collided with the sword
light, leading to a blinding explosion of sparks and flames that rained
down onto the earth below.

The great demon was forced to retreat more than fifty kilometers despite
blocking the sword light, and glancing down at her bracelets, it was
fortunate that there was only some very minor damage. This being the
case, she no longer blocked the torrential rain with her painting
scroll, and she continued to observe the battle from afar.

The person who had unleashed the sword strike from the Sword Qi Great
Wall was Lu Zhi.

The beautiful great demon committed this to memory.

When women developed grudges against other women, they would often
become even more vicious and spiteful than normal.

Chen Ping\'an was eventually forced to retrieve all of his flying swords
at once, unable to have any great demon take his bait. This was
unexpected, but it was also very reasonable at the same time.

There was no need for Xie Songhua and Qi Shou to communicate with each
other as they immediately joined hands to take over Chen Ping\'an\'s
battlefield, half and half. This would allow Chen Ping\'an to rest for a
moment before drawing his blades again.

The large-scale battle had only just begun, and the large majority of
the demon army were measly ants using their lives to push the front
lines forward. There weren\'t many demon cultivators, and it could be
said that the Savage World was exhibiting more patience this time
compared to their three previous assaults on the Sword Qi Great Wall.

The sword formations established by the sword cultivators were
interlinked and strategically placed, and the attacking demon army was
seemingly displaying an indescribable sense of order as well. They were
no longer as crude and chaotic as before. However, there would
occasionally still be some disjunction on the battlefield, almost as if
the mastermind behind the scenes wasn\'t experienced enough when it came
to commanding armies in battles.

Sword cultivators practiced sword techniques, while demons largely
practiced martial arts.

The three moons hung high in the sky.

An unfamiliar old man wearing Confucian robes appeared beside the
Confucian sage, and he was currently gazing up at the glowing moons in
the sky.

He was none other than the Pure Confucian Chen Clan\'s Chen Chun\'an,
the number one individual of the Southern Whirl Continent.

Chen Chun\'an retracted his gaze and said to the traveling disciples and
descendants in the distance, \"Go and help. Remember to abide by the
local customs.\"

The young cultivators scattered along the great wall.

The Confucian sage, who also belonged to the lineage of the Second Sage,
commented, \"There are quite a few scholarly talents among them.\"

\"The Southern Whirl Continent has many more exceptional talents like
this,\" Chen Chun\'an replied.

The Confucian sage smiled and said, \"This isn\'t the Majestic World,
after all, so I won\'t be able to speak with the old great sword
immortal if I don\'t do something.\"

Chen Chun\'an nodded and raised one hand into the air.

One of the moons in the sky of the Savage World surprisingly started to
sway slightly, appearing as if it were about to be dragged over to the
old man\'s side and eventually drawn into his sleeve.

A great demon stood up from their throne and materialized between the
moon and the old man.

After resting for a while, Chen Ping\'an returned to the city wall and
continued to wield his swords. Seeing this, Xie Songhua and Qi Shou
returned the section of the wall to Chen Ping\'an to defend.

A tall and sturdy young man in Confucian robes quietly sat to the side,
not saying anything and not disturbing Chen Ping\'an from launching his
sword strikes. He simply stared at the battlefield for a long time
before finally saying, \"Just pretend you\'re running out of energy and
let all of the demons through. The closer to the city wall they get, the
better.\"

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t hesitate at all, and he immediately commanded the
four flying swords to retreat.

He allowed the demons in his defensive jurisdiction to freely surge
forward.

Liu Xianyang closed his eyes as if he were entering a dream.

Qi Shou turned around and glanced at the unfamiliar young scholar who
was seemingly drifting off to sleep. He then glanced at the raucous
demons surging forward along that section of the wall.

Qi Shou was just about to summon his flying sword, Jumping Spider.

However, it was also at this moment that Liu Xianyang opened his eyes.

Without exception, all of the demons along Chen Ping\'an\'s section of
the wall were killed in an instant.

Even Sword Immortal Xie Songhua couldn\'t help but turn around and
glance at Liu Xianyang.

This was because she hadn\'t detected any ripple of spiritual energy,
nor had she noticed any wisp of sword qi. In fact, there wasn\'t a
single sign of sword intent to be found on the battlefield.

Chen Ping\'an carefully observed the battlefield that had suddenly
fallen deathly silent. There were truly no surviving demons along this
stretch of the battlefield.

Liu Xianyang was seemingly caught by surprise as well, and he rubbed his
chin and murmured, \"Are they truly so fragile?\"

Xie Songhua and Chen Ping\'an\'s minds were stirred slightly at almost
the exact same moment.

\"It\'s coming!\" Qi Shou exclaimed in a quiet voice.

Liu Xianyang, who was only carrying a standard sword from the sword
market, nodded and commanded his sword to automatically leave the
scabbard on his back, after which it drew a long arc through the sky. A
small golden deity of unknown origin materialized in the sky, catching
the standard sword and continuously gathering primordial sword intent
that had a strong affinity with the Great Dao from the surroundings as
it descended toward the ground.

After descending for a while, the small golden deity eventually slashed
down and struck a thin ray of sword light that had burst forth from a
corpse and was ferociously shooting toward Chen Ping\'an. The ray of
sword light, which wasn\'t especially far from the city wall, was
deflected and pushed toward the ground. Following this, the small golden
deity also disappeared with its standard sword.

Rays of sword light shot out from the sword case on Xie Songhua\'s back,
racing into the distance with astounding speed.

In the end, she successfully shattered the bonded flying sword of the
attacking demon sword immortal.

Xie Songhua only managed to retrieve half of her sword light, and she
returned them to their positions in her sword case before standing up
and saying, \"Chen Ping\'an, you\'re on your own in the short-term --- I
need to rest and recuperate for a while. Otherwise, my trip here will be
pointless if I don\'t manage to kill any Upper Five Tier demons.\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded in response.

Liu Xianyang turned around and walked toward Xie Songhua, appearing as
if he were going to take over the battlefield of the female sword
immortal.

Chen Ping\'an wanted to say something, but he couldn\'t help but
hesitate.

Liu Xianyang bent down and smacked Chen Ping\'an\'s head when he walked
past behind him, chuckling and saying, \"Same old rules as always. Just
watch and learn.\"

Ever since meeting each other and becoming friends, it had always been
Liu Xianyang teaching Chen Ping\'an all kinds of things. After leaving
home and only just reuniting after ten years, things were still exactly
the same as before.

[]{#chapter-124.xhtml}

# Chapter 622: Confrontation

Sword of Coming

First, it was a young man in Confucian robes ascending the city wall and
using some mysterious mystical ability to instantly kill a swathe of
demons.

Afterward, it was Xie Songhua unleashing blades from her sword case and
comprehensively destroying the bonded flying sword of a demon sword
immortal, causing the latter to fall to the Nascent Tier. In fact, even
this Nascent Tier cultivation base was unstable and on the verge of
falling. As such, it was difficult to say whether this demon could still
be regarded as a sword cultivator in the future.

Innate sword talents were rare, after all, and it wasn\'t the case that
a sword cultivator with a high cultivation base could casually nurture a
new bonded flying sword after their original one was destroyed. In other
words, this great demon had suffered a huge loss in its exchange with
Xie Songhua, and it could be said that it had lost more than just its
cultivation base in this battle.

Along with this, it had also lost the many benefits that came with being
a sword cultivator. Demons ultimately weren\'t the same as sword
cultivators from the Sword Qi Great Wall, so it would also be
ridiculously difficult for them to cultivate alternative techniques and
return to the Upper Five Tiers.

The attacking demons evidently faltered along the sections of the city
wall guarded by Chen Ping\'an, Liu Xianyang, and Qi Shou.

According to the rules of the Sword Qi Great Wall, Xie Songhua had
achieved all of opportune timing, geographical advantage, and human
harmony when unleashing the full power of her swords. It could be said
that she had performed a remarkable feat.

This was significant military merit, and with the severely wounded demon
being a most valuable sword cultivator from the Savage World, Xie
Songhua had essentially killed half an Immortal Tier demon or the
equivalent of a complete Unpolished Jade Tier demon. Regarding how one
was rewarded, this would depend on one\'s choice between these two
options.

If a sword cultivator chose the former option, they would need to again
kill half an Immortal Tier demon, and only then would they be able to
claim the corresponding military merit. If a sword cultivator chose the
latter option, they would face a small loss, but they could immediately
receive money and treasures from the Lord Hidden Official.

However, it was clear that Xie Songhua was hungry for more and wanted to
unleash more sword strikes.

Qi Shou sighed in grief and lamented, \"The good fortune has all been
eaten up by Sword Immortal Xie. I need to play it safer now.\"

He resolutely summoned his third flying sword, Jumping Spider, and
established a sword formation around himself, lest he be secretly
attacked by some Upper Five Tier demon sword cultivator as well. He then
turned around and asked, \"Are you getting a cut of this handsome
reward?\"

Chen Ping\'an was sitting cross-legged on the city wall, and he placed
his hands on the standard sword resting horizontally across his knees
before shaking his head and replying, \"No, I\'m not.\"

He wasn\'t earning a single copper coin for acting as bait.

Liu Xianyang smiled and asked, \"Are the two of you friends?\"

Chen Ping\'an shook his head again.

Qi Shou chuckled coldly and snickered, \"Friend my ass. More like
enemies. Once we leave the city wall, this second shopkeeper will try
his best to screw me over, and I\'ll also take full advantage of my
cultivation base to suppress him.\"

Liu Xianyang nodded and said, \"Then this place is quite similar to our
hometown. People here are simple and honest.\"

There was a huge number of military supervisors in the large army of the
Savage World, and they would ruthlessly wield their weapons and wreak
havoc and death if the army dared to show any signs of slowing down
their offensive.

Thus, the demons continued to surge forward along the section of the
great wall guarded by the three young men. Not only that, but they
seemingly had increased support to deal with the three people as well,
with a group of demon cultivators that had elementary knowledge of
Talismanic Dao haphazardly throwing out stacks of yellow paper talismans
and attempting to cloud visibility over the battlefield. Plumes of dust
rose into the air, and the surrounding spiritual energy also became
unstable and chaotic.

The demons on the front line were all humongous in size and responsible
for dying first, and it was likely that the demon army wanted to draw
more attacks from Liu Xianyang, which would then allow them to figure
out his techniques.

Qi Shou was unfazed by this, and Flying Kite and Heartstring continued
to rapidly race around the battlefield, releasing sword light that
dismembered many demons measuring more than a dozen meters in height.
These limbless demons crashed to the ground and wailed in agony.

Things would always be like this when Qi Shou wielded his sword against
enemies. Apart from making his enemies suffer cruel deaths, skinning
them alive, severing their tendons, and cutting their flesh until bone
was visible, he would sometimes act like he was right now, purposely
giving them severe wounds without killing them. His victims would be
forced to struggle in vain on the battlefield, unable to do anything but
obediently wait for death.

This was especially the case for those demon cultivators that had
assumed human form. They were targeted more often by Qi Shou\'s flying
swords, with their stomachs also sliced open and their intestines left
hanging out. Some demon cultivators couldn\'t bear to watch on, and they
attempted to rescue these suffering victims, yet they would quickly
become victims themselves.

Chen Ping\'an took a swig of medicinal water elixir wine from his Sword
Nurturing Gourd as he continued to control his flying swords to kill
enemies. First and Fifteenth would attempt to kill their targets in a
single strike, but if the demons possessed overly tough physiques or
managed to survive even after having their critical acupoints
penetrated, then Pine Needle and Lightning Devourer would race over to
deliver an extra one or two killing blows.

There were indeed some sacrificial demon cultivators that attempted to
secretly suppress and capture Chen Ping\'an\'s swords, wanting to
destroy these flying swords as they died. However, Chen Ping\'an was an
expert when it came to scheming and acting, and this was not to mention
First, which was only slightly slower than Fifteenth, possessing
exceptional toughness.

Earlier, a sacrificial demon had remained very well hidden and purposely
suffered many wounds, with its entire body bloody and mangled. Not only
that, but it had even grabbed another demon to use as a shield to block
the attacks of First. However, First simply pierced through the glabella
of the demon in front before directly retreating and disappearing in a
flash.

The sacrificial demon cultivator had timed things perfectly to
self-destruct its demon core, and before falling dead, it had dazedly
stared at the city wall as if feeling slightly confused. Meanwhile,
First had only been hit by the shockwave of spiritual energy resulting
from the self-destruction, having nimbly flown away from the demon
cultivator\'s trap. It was completely unharmed, but this had been quite
taxing on Chen Ping\'an\'s mental energy.

Just like Qi Shou had said, Chen Ping\'an wasn\'t a sword cultivator, so
his spiritual energy and mental energy wouldn\'t be able to sustain his
sword strikes for very long.

Moreover, the battle between the Savage World and the Sword Qi Great
Wall had only just begun.

Even so, Qi Shou was well aware that Chen Ping\'an would be like a fish
in water once the sword cultivators needed to leave the city wall to
fight on the battlefield below.

Liu Xianyang didn\'t launch any visible attacks, and his swords were
still nowhere to be seen. However, from the north to the south, more and
more demons were killed before the section of the wall initially guarded
by Sword Immortal Xie Songhua.

This was completely unreasonable.

Chen Ping\'an couldn\'t help but warn, \"Be careful. You\'ll attract the
attention of the great demons.\"

Liu Xianyang used his mind\'s lake to reply, \"The biggest and only
drawback of my sword technique is its destructive power. It\'s nowhere
near strong enough. There\'s no other problem apart from this.\"

He paused for a moment before continuing, \"Listen carefully and don\'t
forget a single word of what I\'m about to say.\"

Chen Ping\'an was just about to say something upon hearing this.

However, Liu Xianyang didn\'t so much as glance at Chen Ping\'an as he
smiled and said, \"Don\'t give me any nonsense and just listen carefully
when Boss Liu speaks. Will you be able to learn this technique even if I
teach you all of the mantras and tricks?\"

Chen Ping\'an remained silent.

Liu Xianyang continued to use his mind\'s lake to teach the mantra. He
knew that Chen Ping\'an had always had a good memory from a young age,
so he explained the mantra as he recited it, completely unworried that
Chen Ping\'an would remember incorrectly. In fact, Liu Xianyang went
into great detail and complexity with his explanation.

What he expounded was none other than the sword scripture passed down
through his clan.

There had been two family heirlooms passed down in the Liu Clan, and
apart from the sword scripture, there had also been the severely
scratched suit of wart-like armor, one that was bluish-black in color
and had no artistic quality to speak of. The woman from Light Breeze
City\'s Xu Clan had obtained the suit of treasured armor back then,
allowing the Xu Clan to become like a tiger given new wings.

The Nascent Tier cultivator of the Xu Clan became one of the most
powerful and destructive cultivators in the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent, and with the indestructible suit of armor, the Xu Clan was
now viewed as a potential sect-level force for the future, only slightly
behind its ally, Sun Scorch Mountain.

From a long-term perspective, the Xu Clan being able to join hands with
the Great Li Empire\'s Pillar Yuan Clan through marriage --- even if
only through a direct daughter marrying an illegitimate son --- was
still a very positive development that would only have benefits and no
drawbacks. The reason the Yuan Clan had agreed to this unpleasant
marriage during the turbulent times in Light Breeze City was, most
critically, because the clan leader of the Xu Clan had the potential to
advance to the Upper Five Tiers.

Back then, Liu Xianyang\'s plan had been to sell the treasured armor and
keep the sword scripture, and the price to pay for keeping the sword
scripture was losing half his life. Moreover, if it weren\'t for the
rules of the Jewel Small World, the mountain-moving ape from Sun Scorch
Mountain would have gladly taken the remaining half of Liu Xianyang\'s
life as well.

This was also very unreasonable.

In any case, Liu Xianyang had become a scholar now, and he had even
received fortune from misfortune when lying on the sickbed in Ruan
Qiong\'s sword shop. Teetering on the verge of death, he had managed to
learn sword techniques in his dreams. As a scholar, he needed to abide
by rules and principles, but this wouldn\'t interfere with him seeking
revenge.

\"Have you remembered everything?\" Liu Xianyang asked. As he spoke,
wisps of sword intent flowed around him, appearing as if they were
forming a shield and protecting him.

Chen Ping\'an nodded and replied, \"Yes, I have, but I surmise that I
won\'t be able to learn it. The threshold to entry is too high.\"

Liu Xianyang smiled and said, \"Then, as always, just adjust your
mindset and stay positive. You can compare your talent with anyone else,
but just don\'t compare it with Boss Liu. Is learning sword techniques
very difficult? It\'s so-so for me, but it\'s obviously very difficult
for you. However, taking a step back, what was the most significant
craftwork in our hometown? It was pottery firing, wasn\'t it? And we
both managed to learn it.

\"So, your current situation is similar to the period of time when you
were learning pottery firing. Back then, you felt like you would never
be able to master this skill, and you were convinced that you would
never become a proper kiln worker, right? You had a gloomy expression
the entire time, and you were always quiet and sullen. But look at you
now. Would you craft one or two pieces of porcelain wares even if the
emperor begged you to? Would that not depend on your mood?

\"There are naturally many details that need to be mastered when it
comes to this sword technique passed down by my ancestors, and even
though you\'re much slower than me when learning new things, you\'re
ultimately able to learn and master them. So, what are you worried
about? You\'re inferior to me in all aspects, and you need me to teach
you everything. You need to accept this and get used to this.\"

\"I\'m genuinely used to this already,\" Chen Ping\'an replied in a
quiet voice.

Liu Xianyang laughed heartily and remarked, \"That\'s a brilliant habit!
There\'s no need to change it!\"

------------

To the south of Chen Ping\'an and Liu Xianyang\'s defensive line, there
was a huge military tent located behind the main army and surrounded by
layers upon layers of demons. There was a small and unremarkable wooden
sign hanging outside the entrance of the huge tent, and the two lone
characters on it read: Jia Shen.

There were many study desks of various sizes inside the huge military
tent, with mountains of books and scrolls completely covering all of
them. A lot of these were heavily damaged military books, and they were
all copies instead of originals. Even so, they were still viewed as
precious treasures, and the demon cultivators would all treat them with
utmost care as they studied them.

When books were rare, the readers would treat them with much more care
and value, willing to carefully go over every single sentence and
character. They would study the contents instead of simply reading them,
digging deep for the knowledge buried within.

The military tent covered a huge area, and almost one hundred demon
cultivators were gathered here. They didn\'t appear young because they
were lofty cultivators with the ability to change their appearances, but
rather, they were indeed fairly young.

Among them was the young sword cultivator called Bei Qie, who was
sitting cross-legged and leaning back on his sword case.

Beside him was a demon called Yu Si, a sword cultivator the same age as
him and also ranked among the Hundred Sword Immortals of the Savage
World. Yu Si was flipping through a military book right now, and just
like Bei Qie, he also didn\'t have a surname right now.

A young man pushed aside the tent curtains and stepped inside.

Yu Si looked up and asked with a smile, \"How did you do in battle this
time, Tun Tan?\"

\"Not as good as last time. I only managed to destroy three flying
swords,\" Tun Tan replied.

The young man put up three fingers and shook his head as he spoke, after
which he squatted down beside Yu Si and Bei Qie and said in a gloomy
voice, \"It\'s truly very difficult to get near the third sword
formation. There was slightly more commotion on my battlefield, and some
sword immortals immediately rushed over to quell the situation and
protect those Middle Five Tier sword cultivators with unsteady sword
strikes. I was almost cut in half at the waist by a burst of sword qi,
and it was genuinely a very dangerous encounter.\"

A brilliant smile appeared on Tun Tan\'s face as he continued,
\"However, I wasn\'t too far away from the battlefield along Chen
Ping\'an\'s section of the wall. He\'s neighbors with Qi Shou, and Qi
Shou has indeed broken through to the next tier. He\'s also very
impressive, and he managed to control the battlefield with just two
flying swords. Afterward, a scholar appeared on the great wall, and his
immortal techniques were incredibly strange and powerful. Those who were
struck by his techniques would be killed in mysterious and unknown
ways.\"

A young woman sitting behind the study desk glanced at the map and said
slowly, \"The sword immortal you were facing was most likely Situ Jixue,
an Unpolished Jade Tier sword cultivator from the Golden Armor
Continent. His bonded flying sword is called Heavy Cavalry, and the
sword at his waist is called Majestic Pass. His destructive ability
isn\'t outstanding, but he\'s able to maintain an extraordinary level of
offensive and defensive capabilities, so being able to escape death at
his sword is already an impressive feat.

\"I\'ll make things clear, Tun Tan. You can continue to slowly
accumulate military merit, but don\'t go dying on the battlefield. Your
section of the battlefield is commanded by Mu Ji, and you\'re also a
potential candidate for the Hundred Sword Immortals. After working so
hard, Mu Ji is finally looking at the opportunity to have a surname
bestowed upon him, so please don\'t die and strip him of this
opportunity.\"

A bashful young man sitting behind a study desk near the young woman
looked up and said in a quiet voice, \"Don\'t die. Otherwise, I\'ll feel
guilty for a very long time even if I\'m bestowed with a surname.\"

The young man called Tun Tan cracked a grin and replied, \"I
understand.\"

The Hundred Sword Immortals of the Savage World were prodigies of the
Great Dao officially chosen by Holding Moon Mountain, and their
importance was only second to that of Ascension Tier great demons.

These demon sword cultivators, regardless of their current cultivation
base, were all incredibly valuable.

Those at Jia Zi Tent and Holding Moon Mountain would hold accountable
and severely punish those responsible for the death of any demon sword
cultivator.

Right now, there were five demon sword cultivators inside the Jia Shen
Tent.

There was Tun Tan, Bei Qie, Yu Si, the young woman who had revealed Situ
Jixue\'s abilities, and the young man who appeared like a misfit in the
corner.

Mu Ji turned around and glanced at a study desk, habitually speaking in
a soft voice as he said slowly, \"Have we managed to determine the
origin of that Confucian disciple\'s immortal technique and whether or
not he\'s actually a sword cultivator? The losses we\'ve suffered on
this battlefield have already far exceeded our expectations, so we need
to make the necessary adjustments.

\"Our sword immortal already failed to kill Chen Ping\'an before, but if
you and the others conclude that we do indeed need to employ the help of
a sword immortal, and I also agree with your proposal, then I\'ll use a
messenger flying sword to deliver the message and ask a sword immortal
to launch a surprise attack on the Confucian disciple. If this request
is turned down, then I\'ll personally visit the Jia Zi Tent of generals
to discuss the matter with them. You don\'t need to feel any pressure
because of this.\"

A young man shook his head and said, \"We need more deaths to gather
some more clues.\"

Mu Ji nodded in response.

\"The Southern Whirl Continent\'s Chen Chun\'an has personally come to
the Sword Qi Great Wall, so that young scholar definitely belongs to the
lineage of the Second Sage. This is without a doubt,\" the young woman
said. \"In reality, we can reduce the number of soldiers we deploy to
that section of the wall to a suitable degree, since we\'ll definitely
receive a secret messenger flying sword from the great wall very soon.

\"After the Jia Zi Tent verifies the information, they\'ll naturally
redirect the letter to us. If the letter reveals the background and
abilities of this person, then our Jia Shen Tent still has two remaining
chances to employ the help of a sword immortal. We can use both chances
at once and choose to either kill that scholar or kill Chen Ping\'an.
Otherwise, we can take a step back and kill Qi Shou. We\'ll allow the
two sword immortals to choose the most suitable target based on the
actual situation.\"

Mu Ji contemplated this proposal for a brief moment before nodding and
replying, \"This is a solid plan.\"

The bashful young man then pulled a piece of yellow paper from the stack
next to his hand, folding it into a small bird and gently throwing it to
the entrance of the large tent. \"Pass on my command. Slow down the
offensive on the Sixth Jia Shen Front. Apart from not being allowed to
retreat, they\'re allowed to prioritize protecting themselves and
staying alive.\"

The paper bird flew out from the Jia Shen Tent.

Yu Si, the young demon sword cultivator with a strange name, said in
amusement, \"Tun Tan, even though your cultivation base isn\'t high
right now, you have many different abilities and will have the
opportunity to challenge Chen Ping\'an when those sword cultivators
leave the city wall in the future. Compared to idiots like me and Bei
Qie, who only know how to barge forward, you can more easily gain an
advantage over Chen Ping\'an.\"

Tun Tan thought for a moment before nodding and saying, \"I\'ll give it
a go.\"

The Jia Shen Tent was one of sixty military tents in the army of the
Savage World named after the Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches, and
with the exception of the Jia Zi Tent being the main commander\'s tent,
the remaining military tents were each responsible for managing the
soldiers in a specific section of the battlefield.\[1\]

Since the Jia Shen Tent started with the character \"Jia,\" the
importance of this large military tent was already very evident.
According to the military rules, even sword immortal great demons would
be punished by immediate death if they dared to barge into Jia-level
military tents without permission.\[2\]

Things were orderly in the Jia Shen Tent, with each demon performing its
own duties. The overall atmosphere was relatively relaxed.

The young woman, who had a map unfurled on the table in front of her,
looked up and said in a solemn voice, \"For the sake of our growth and
for the sake of conquering and maintaining control over several large
continents of the Majestic World in the future, we\'ve already suffered
an additional ten thousand deaths on the Jia Shen Battlefield for no
good reason. Our merits are carved on the corpses of these soldiers, so
don\'t think for a second that this is amusing or fun.\"

A deathly pale young man sitting in an isolated corner by himself
chuckled coldly and scoffed, \"Soldiers? Can those brainless ants even
be regarded as military assets? It\'s better off that these ants die in
battle. That way, they can save food for the army while also helping us
fight for the world. This is killing two birds with one stone. The
Savage World is unable to sustain so many useless ants to begin with, so
their dying here is for a worthy cause. They\'re finally able to make a
very minor contribution.\"

The young man then glanced at the nearby Bei Qie and Tun Tan and
continued, \"Leave Chen Ping\'an for me to deal with. If anyone dares to
fight me for him, then don\'t complain about my flying sword having no
eyes and accidentally wounding my allies.\"

Quite shockingly, this person was actually Li Zhen, who had transformed
from a child into a young man. He still possessed a portion of
Primordial Prisoner Li Zhen\'s remnant soul, and he had used a secret
technique of Holding Moon Mountain to reconstruct his physical body,
after which he had pieced together a complete soul.

Bei Qie was completely unfazed.

The brilliant smile remained on Tun Tan\'s face as he replied, \"No
complaints from me.\"

Yu Si smiled with squinted eyes and said, \"I wouldn\'t dare to. In any
case, I don\'t have the right to be regarded as Young Master Li Zhen\'s
ally.\"

The arrogant young man suddenly smiled and stared intently at Yu Si,
saying, \"I encourage you not to learn from those people in the Majestic
World and speak in such a provocative manner.\"

Yu Si raised his hands in surrender and said in mock pity, \"I\'ll shut
up then, okay? I\'ll shut up.\"

Mu Ji furrowed his brows and looked up, speaking in a more solemn tone
in a rare display. However, his voice was still softer than that of Li
Zhen, Yu Si, and the others as he said, \"Li Zhen only lost by the
finest of margins, and this is no reason for you to take pleasure in his
misfortune, Yu Si. All of you are sword cultivators who enjoy a loftier
status than everyone else, so you should also have an equally lofty
mental state.\"

Yu Si immediately put on a serious expression and nodded in response.

Mu Ji then turned around and said to Li Zhen, \"A loss is a loss, and
that was due to your lack of abilities, Li Zhen. You being able to
revive afterward is also thanks to your ability as the closing disciple
of Holding Moon Mountain. These things are outside my control, and I
don\'t care about them. I\'m only responsible for the victories and
losses on the Jia Shen Battlefield. I need to carefully consider each
small victory and loss on the battlefield.

\"The battle will be intense and deadly afterward, but you still need to
listen to the commands, Li Zhen. Ignoring military rules and acting of
your own accord will amount to dragging down the entire Jia Shen Tent.
If that\'s the case, then you\'ll need to face the consequences
yourself.

\"However, if the time is right and you\'re still willing to seek Chen
Ping\'an out as your opponent, then that\'s entirely up to you. I won\'t
care even if you fight to the death. The Jia Shen Tent definitely won\'t
stop you. In fact, I\'m willing to offer my own military merit to help
you create the opportunity to face off against Chen Ping\'an and fight
to the death. This is because fighting alongside a Li Zhen who dares to
die again will be a great honor.\"

Mu Ji looked around and asked in a solemn voice, \"Why did Li Zhen
engage in that battle? Why did he face off against Chen Ping\'an below
the Great Wall? Are you people not aware? Did any of you have the right
to be in his position? So, how can this be a reason for you to laugh at
Li Zhen now? Just because he lost the battle and died?

\"Well, the Savage World has never won a battle against the Sword Qi
Great Wall over the past ten thousand years. Not a single battle! All of
those Ascension Tier seniors, and even the entire Holding Moon
Mountain\... Which of these entities isn\'t a joke?! If you\'re so
capable, then laugh at those humans after you enter the Majestic World.
You\'re free to laugh at them as much as you want!\"

Mu Ji took a deep breath, with his expression becoming downcast as he
murmured, \"Saying these things to you people doesn\'t make me feel
happy.\"

Among those inside the Jia Shen Tent, Li Zhen somewhat seemed willing to
listen to Mu Ji. Sure enough, he stopped butting heads with Yu Si and
the others, closing his eyes and continuing to rest his mind. At the
same time, he performed advanced refinement on five bonded items.

\"Handsomely said, Mu Ji,\" the young woman praised in a teasing voice.

The young man smiled shyly, with a slight blush appearing on his cheeks.

Bei Qie, who could almost be regarded as a mute, spoke up in an
uncharacteristic manner, saying, \"The flying sword from the Jia Zi Tent
is about to arrive.\"

Sure enough, a messenger flying sword soon arrived at the Jia Shen Tent.

Mu Ji\'s expression became solemn after he read the secret letter, and
he revealed, \"We only know that the scholar is called Liu Xianyang and
hails from the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. He\'s not a descendant
of the Pure Confucian Chen Clan, so we\'re still in the dark about his
cultivation techniques.\"

The young woman sighed and said, \"Then let\'s act according to the
worst-case scenario. We\'ll sacrifice more soldiers to uncover the
truth.\"

\"Yu Si, make your way to the battlefield and remember to disguise
yourself well,\" Mu Ji suddenly said. \"Face a single sword strike and
then immediately retreat. There\'s no need to hesitate at all. The
destructive power of Chen Ping\'an\'s swords isn\'t especially great,
but his ability to observe and understand the battlefield is incredibly
detailed and thorough. With his personality, I dare say that his trump
card is definitely much more than just that female sword immortal. If
you don\'t die on the battlefield, some other sword immortal will
quickly be responsible for keeping a close eye on you.\"

Yu Si resolutely stood up with a look of eager excitement on his face.
However, he grumbled and complained, \"Wow, karma is biting back so
quickly.\"

Mu Ji turned around to look at Bei Qie.

Yu Si instantly sprinted out of the Jia Shen Tent, not giving Mu Ji the
opportunity to change his mind.

Mu Ji shifted his gaze again, saying to Tun Tan, \"I\'ve done some
calculations, and your accumulated military merit is still far from
being enough to purchase that immortal treasure of Elite Cavalry River.
However, this doesn\'t matter, and I\'m willing to take the lead and
chip in with some military merit. Everyone else who chips in will also
earn annual dividends in the future. Who\'s willing to join me?\"

The young woman shook her head and said, \"I\'m also saving up, so I
can\'t offer anything.\"

\"You can offer something,\" Mu Ji interjected. \"You\'ll make up your
investment before this battle is over. Believe me, this definitely
won\'t delay you from obtaining that treasure.\"

Li Zhen opened his eyes and asked, \"Is there any need to purchase it? I
can directly walk over and ask for it.\"

Mu Ji shook his head and was just about to turn down this offer.

However, Li Zhen had already stood up, and he asked the young woman,
\"Which treasure do you need? Just tell me, and I\'ll retrieve it
together with the other one. I can\'t be bothered making two trips.\"

The young woman didn\'t hesitate, and she directly said the name of that
paramount treasure. She then laughed loudly and raised her cupped fists
high into the air, expressing her thanks.

Li Zhen expressionlessly walked out of the Jia Shen Tent.

He looked up at the Sword Qi Great Wall, where the northern section of
the great wall appeared extremely hazy right now. In stark contrast, the
battlefield was vividly clear from the northern section of the great
wall.

Li Zhen retracted his gaze and faltered for a brief moment. He turned
around, cupping his fists and bowing in respect in a rare display.

Standing beside him was a big-bearded man carrying a sword and a saber.

The man nodded in acknowledgment and said, \"You go ahead and do your
things.\"

Li Zhen flew away on the wind.

Bei Qie walked out of the Jia Shen Tent and greeted his master.

\"I want to see a certain person, so you need to do something for your
master,\" the big-bearded man said. \"Go and kill Chen Ping\'an.\"

Bei Qie nodded silently.

1\. The Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches (天干地支) were used to name
the years, months, and days in ancient China. There are ten Heavenly
Stems and twelve Earthly Branches.

2\. Jia (甲) represents the first of the ten Heavenly Stems.

# Chapter 623: (1): Sword Training

Sword of Coming

The loud echo of a horn reverberated throughout the battlefield,
following which the demon army started to retreat.

After attacking for more than twenty days, the large demon army still
failed to push their front lines to the city wall.

The sword immortals atop the city wall were still spirited and graceful
as always, while the great demons from the Savage World had seldom
participated in the battle. Only a small handful of Ascension Tier and
Immortal Tier great demons had channeled their mystical abilities, and
none of them had truly joined the demon army in its assault. Thus, it
appeared as if the Sword Qi Great Wall had easily repelled the assault
of the Savage World.

Over the past few weeks, the two most outstanding battles acknowledged
by everyone included Zuo You once again charging deep into enemy
territory with nothing but himself and his sword. He almost destroyed
the Geng Wu Tent, which was located closer to the large army of demons,
and this caused two Ascension Tier great demons to step forward and
attack him.

However, Zuo You still refused to retreat, and his majestic sword qi
stretched from the city wall all the way to the distant ground, peering
down at the vast earth like a tangible small world that had materialized
in the sky. With Zuo You as its core, boundless snow-white sword qi
formed a colossal dome that blotted out heaven and earth, ruthlessly
annihilating the bodies and souls of all demons in its path.

Those at the Sword Qi Great Wall couldn\'t see Zuo You at all. They
could only see his sword qi and sword light.

Immortal Tier Sword Immortal Mi Hu, who had secretly broken through
recently, was standing beside his younger brother, Mi Yu, who was still
at the Unpolished Jade Tier. The two brothers both felt mixed emotions.

Mi Hu felt like things would truly be satisfying if Zuo You could
unleash even more sword qi. All of the sword immortals in the world
should be like this. In contrast, there was a bitter expression on Mi
Yu\'s face, and he thought to himself that Zuo You\'s sword qi was
seemingly too abundant.

If it were said that Zuo You\'s magnificent battle against the two
Ascension Tier great demons was taking place on the earth, then the
other battle was truly taking place in the skies.

When Chen Chun\'an stepped forward and made a move, one of the bright
moons in the Savage World was astonishingly dragged from the lofty skies
to the earth.

Almost the entire Savage World descended into a state of utter terror
and panic, worried that the moon, which was growing larger and larger in
their eyes, would truly crash to the earth.

The old man in gray from Holding Moon Mountain still didn\'t step
forward to stop Chen Chun\'an, and he instead looked up and remarked
with a smile, \"Quite an impressive technique, Scholar. \"

This was as expected of Chen Chun\'an, someone regarded as another
towering peak in the lineage of the Second Sage.

Casting one\'s gaze over the eight large continents beyond the Middle
Earth Divine Continent, there was the Southern Whirl Continent\'s Chen
Chun\'an, the Northern Complete Reed Continent\'s Spiritual Master Fire
Dragon, and the Pure White Continent\'s God of Riches. Each had their
own strengths, and even the haughty Qi refiners from the Middle Earth
Divine Continent didn\'t dare to recklessly accuse these individuals of
being lightweights.

The old man in gray allowed the Ascension Tier great demon, who referred
to itself as Lotus Flower Nunnery Master, to unleash its full strength
against Chen Chun\'an.

The Ascension Tier great demon was a Daoist priest who had refined half
of the moon\'s soul, allowing it to enjoy a strong advantage in terms of
conditions and geography. However, it was still unable to block Chen
Chun\'an\'s divine technique of slowly drawing a moon to the earth.

In reality, this sense of slowness was actually an illusion. If there
were truly a primordial deity or an ascended immortal residing on the
moon, they would presumably be able to experience the wind blasting past
their body as the moon rapidly plummeted to the ground.

Outside the battlefield, the demon cultivators with relatively high
cultivation bases --- especially those approaching the Upper Five Tiers
--- could increasingly feel the stifling pressure permeating through the
surroundings. They could clearly see the \"Moon Palace\" on the bright
moon, where many vast but lifeless mountain ranges rose and fell. Upper
Five Tier demon cultivators with better eyesight could even see the
lifeless ruins of the Moon Palace. There were gigantic columns of
decayed wood, primordial corpses that could flatten the mountains, and
hovering garments that were as large as lakes and rivers.

A Militarian sage from the Majestic World had once made a remark that
was more praise than criticism. \"\'Tis a shame the pure Confucian
scholars aren\'t domineering, with their essays unable to reach the
heavenly roads.\"

If the speaker of this remark were able to witness Chen Chun\'an\'s
formidable feat at the Sword Qi Great Wall, they would most likely
refrain from making such a preposterous statement.

Meanwhile, of the nine large continents in the Majestic World, the Sword
Qi Great Wall wasn\'t actually the most familiar with the Middle Earth
Divine Continent. Rather, it was most familiar with the Southern Whirl
Continent, which was located closest to Stalactite Mountain. This meant
it was extremely familiar with Pure Confucian Chen Chun\'an.

Of course, this was also in large part thanks to A\'Liang\'s heavy
promotion, especially his remark that Chen Chun\'an was a relatively
unique and mighty figure among scholars. A\'Liang described Chen
Chun\'an as an old scholar wielding hammers, possessing both scholarly
talent and martial prowess. Indeed, he was very impressive, being able
