to write good essays and also being able to fight.

However, the bright moon ultimately didn\'t land on the earth. The Lotus
Flower Nunnery Master unleashed its full power and fought a stalemate
with Chen Chun\'an for one entire hour. As a result, this particular
moon appeared extremely large and bright on that night.

These two battles were the most genuine fights between paramount
immortals.

These battles also provided a significant boost to the morale of the
Sword Qi Great Wall, inspiring the sword cultivators to attack quicker
and more viciously. This caused the waterfall of sword qi, which was
formed by the convergence of tens of thousands of bonded flying swords,
to become increasingly ferocious and formidable.

However, despite the sword qi being overwhelming, most of the demons
that charged forward to their deaths were only ordinary pawns. Only a
small number of demon cultivators truly advanced with the large army.

As a result, the large majority of sword cultivators at the Sword Qi
Great Wall only managed to earn piddling amounts of military merit.

Thinking back to Sword Immortal Xie Songhua from the Pure White
Continent, she had kept a low profile the entire time, yet she had
suddenly launched a devastating strike and astonished the entire
battlefield. She was one of the few people who had obtained significant
military merit.

After the large demon army stopped its assault, it didn\'t abandon the
corpses of its soldiers on the battlefield as it had typically done in
the past. It didn\'t leave these corpses under the scorching sun and
allow certain sword cultivators from the Sword Qi Great Wall to
\"collect money.\"

The demon tribe started to show respect toward those that had fallen in
battle, doing its best to collect the corpses along with the belongings
of the deceased. The demons carefully sorted through and stored
everything, preparing to return the corpses and belongings to the
relevant next of kin.

The Sword Qi Great Wall naturally wouldn\'t allow the demon tribe to
swagger around and clean up the battlefield so easily.

Most importantly, there was a profound reason for the demon tribe\'s
temporary retreat.

A great demon was holding a golden pot in his palm, one that was
decorated with a mouse offering treasures. After activating this
treasure, all of the ownerless spirit tools and immortal treasures that
were brimming with spiritual energy on the battlefield automatically
rose from the ground and rapidly flew toward the golden pot.

Elsewhere, there was a great demon holding a Jewel-Chasing Dragon Jade
Tablet crafted from ink-black jade, and after tightening its grip, the
jade tablet released a brilliant light as well as countless black flood
dragons, each as long as a finger.

Like sinister flood dragons breaking free from suppression, these black
flood dragons instantly transformed into enormous beasts after
slithering far away from the jade tablet. They slammed their claws into
the ground, easily sending plumes of dust more than fifty meters into
the air as they attempted to brutally kill the sword cultivators who had
jumped down from the city wall.

Great Demon Zhong Guang, who had previously commanded a large-scale
assault on the Sword Qi Great Wall, summoned a bonded item. This was a
bowl of water, and he lightly exhaled over it, creating a ripple on the
surface of the water. A profoundly deep whirlpool suddenly materialized,
appearing as blindingly brilliant as the galaxies in the night sky.

The wandering souls of the demons on the battlefield transformed into
numerous tornadoes that swept toward the south, attempting to fuse into
the bowl of water.

After collecting these souls, Great Demon Zhong Guang could either
return them to the Savage World beyond this battlefield or he could keep
them inside the paramount treasure, lest they be formlessly refined by
the sword qi and sword intent of this place.

Profoundly concentrated and pure spiritual energy appeared to always
have low affinity with people, but in reality, it would display a
mystical and strong affinity toward those cultivators who enjoyed both
favorable timing and geographical advantage.

The many primordial sword intents lingering over the Sword Qi Great Wall
were the best example.

However, those severed limbs, broken bodies, and rivers of blood would
seep into the earth, greatly transforming the aura and fortune of the
battlefield.

The sword immortals needed to deal with this, and even though they would
most certainly fail to purify the entire battlefield, they still needed
to cleanse as much of it as they could.

Otherwise, the so-called favorable timing that originally belonged to
the Sword Qi Great Wall would gradually lean toward the Savage World
instead.

Besides the old great sword immortal and the great wall beneath their
feet, this favorable timing was one of the biggest shields of the sword
cultivators.

And with this in mind, one of the strangest scenes appeared on the
battlefield. The two sides had clearly paused the battle already, yet
more and more great demons and sword immortals started to channel their
abilities. These powerful beings used all kinds of techniques and
treasures to manipulate and gather the many immortal treasures and
damaged spirit tools on the battlefield. However, a significant portion
of these treasures was smashed into pieces as they were relentlessly
fought over.

In any case, despite the huge commotion caused by the sword immortals
and great demons, things were actually quite muted compared to the
intense clash between the two armies before.

There was a short period of rest following the pause in battle, and
according to the historical rules, sword cultivators would be allowed to
rest and recuperate for anywhere from two to ten days.

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t leave the city wall straight away, and he
continued to sit there cross-legged and observe the long-range abilities
of the sword immortals and great demons.

Liu Xianyang walked over and sat down beside Chen Ping\'an. He needed to
meet up with his friends and fellow disciples soon, and the most
important aspect of his trip to the Sword Qi Great Wall was still to
study and learn.

Regardless of what the other Confucian disciples from the Second Sage\'s
lineage thought, Liu Xianyang didn\'t actually care very much about
killing demons. In fact, he might not have been willing to participate
in the battle if it hadn\'t been for Chen Ping\'an sitting here. This
was also a clear reflection of how Liu Xianyang had always been more
relaxed and carefree than Chen Ping\'an.

As for when they would leave the Sword Qi Great Wall, no one was clear
about this. This was completely up to the sage of the Chen Clan. Liu
Xianyang scratched his head and gazed at the suddenly rising and
suddenly waning bursts of ferocious sword light in the distance, saying,
\"Count my military merit under your name.\"

Chen Ping\'an nodded in response, smiling as he offered his Sword
Nurturing Gourd to the sturdy young man.

Liu Xianyang shook his head and said, \"I\'m good. Even if I want to
drink wine to let loose, I would at least need a beautiful young lady to
accompany me, no?\"

He had heard about Chen Ping\'an composing the *Seal Manual of the Two
Hundred Sword Immortals* at the Sword Qi Great Wall, so Liu Xianyang
also planned to ask Chen Ping\'an for a pair of seals. One would be
relatively straightforward, and he would inscribe the characters: Great
Sword Immortal Liu. The other would be more sincere and down-to-earth,
and he would inscribe the characters: Liu Xianyang Preserves His
Integrity As Purely As Jade.

Chen Ping\'an lowered his voice and asked, \"That demon cultivator was
actually unscathed after being struck by your sword?\"

Liu Xianyang smiled and replied, \"He was also a sword cultivator, and
he had a defensive treasure as well. He\'s not so easy to kill.\"

Things were very lively on Qi Shou\'s side of the great wall.

Many people made their way over, and this was because Qi Shou had broken
through and exited seclusion just before the commencement of the battle.
He had successfully advanced to the Nascent Tier, after which he had
guarded a section of the great wall by himself. This was indeed worthy
of praise and celebration.

Qi Shou clearly lived up to his reputation as the leader of his small
group, and he was also a descendant of the Qi Clan to begin with, so it
wasn\'t long before a group of more than a dozen good friends gathered
around him.

Chen Ping\'an was familiar with some of them, for example, Dragon Gate
Tier Sword Cultivator Ren Yi, who had manned the first trial back then.

There was also Golden Core Tier Sword Cultivator Pu Yu, who had been
responsible for conducting the second trial. He was dressed in white and
was an especially handsome and elegant young master.

There were also several female sword cultivators around the same age as
Qi Shou, and coming here to congratulate him was only half their goal.
The other half of their goal was to look at his two neighbors. Unlike
the noble ladies in the Majestic World, the young women here were far
bolder and more straightforward, and right now, these female sword
cultivators didn\'t conceal their judgmental gazes as they looked Chen
Ping\'an and Liu Xianyang up and down. Their so-called whispers were
also far from quiet.

During the rotation of personnel atop the Sword Qi Great Wall before,
some sword cultivators had seized the brief moment of reprieve to chat
with their friends and acquaintances. They would occasionally discuss
the situations on the other sections of the wall, and among these topics
would be the second shopkeeper and the scholar from the Southern Whirl
Continent. There was quite a lot they could chat about.

As for which sword cultivator had died and whose bonded flying sword had
been destroyed in battle?

They would surprisingly just nod in acknowledgment and say nothing else.

Chen Ping\'an swirled his Sword Nurturing Gourd around and said in a
teasing voice, \"And would you look? Aren\'t there beautiful young
ladies now? Care for some wine?\"

Liu Xianyang jumped down the city wall and muttered, \"I\'m off.\"

After Liu Xianyang walked far away, one of the young female sword
cultivators smiled and asked, \"What\'s the name of your friend, Second
Shopkeeper? Does he currently have Dao partners or mistresses?\"

\"Why didn\'t you ask him directly just then?\" Chen Ping\'an replied
with a chuckle.

The female sword cultivator also chuckled and said, \"Because I\'m shy.
Obviously.\"

Chen Ping\'an felt slightly exasperated. They had been looking at Liu
Xianyang as if he were naked just then, displaying no sign of timidness
at all.

This female sword cultivator was called Situ Longqiu, and she was a
mistress\' daughter from Taixiang Street\'s Situ Clan. She was at the
peak stage of the Sea Observation Tier, and she was good friends with
Dong Bude. Her cultivation base was middling among those at the same age
at the Sword Qi Great Wall, but she was outgoing and cheerful in a way
that was very much like those in the martial world.

Through Situ Longqiu\'s added exaggeration and flair, interesting
stories at the Sword Qi Great Wall would often become even more
interesting. In fact, many rumors and gossip originated from her and
Dong Bude chasing the wind and clutching at shadows, and this would
cause real news to feel extremely fake, but fake news to feel even more
legitimate than real news.

When Dong Bude had visited the Ning Residence and asked Chen Ping\'an to
help her inscribe three seals, one of them had been for none other than
Situ Longqiu.

The second shopkeeper was an upstanding person who didn\'t discriminate
between old and young; Situ Longqiu always swore that she was telling
the truth, Gu Jianlong would often step forward to speak fairly and
candidly, Dong Huafu spent money like it was nothing, and Wang Xinshui
was always confident before a fight but not so much afterward\... They
were now the five newest unique personalities of the Sword Qi Great
Wall.

The five previous unique personalities included A\'Liang\'s impressive
gambling skills making him a public enemy, the Lord Hidden Official
having the best temper and never hitting people, the old deaf guy
telling people to speak like proper humans, Lu Zhi being breathtakingly
beautiful, and Mi Yu failing to be recognized for his sincerity and this
having nothing to do with his sword skills or cultivation base.

Right now, the encounter between Chen Ping\'an and Situ Longqiu could
probably be regarded as an encounter between mighty figures.

Situ Longqiu suddenly smiled and asked, \"Is Goose Lake Mountain very
famous in the Majestic World?\"

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and replied, \"It\'s a little-known
mountain in the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. The scenery there is
top-notch, but it hasn\'t made a name for itself yet. However, I have a
good friend who likes to write travel journals while traveling around
the martial world, and he has told me about the stunning scenery of this
place, one of which was a large waterfall named Longqiu. This is why I
have a fairly deep impression of Goose Lake Mountain.\"\[1\]

\"And here I was thinking that it was one of the Five Mountains and
widely renowned throughout the world,\" Situ Longqiu said in
disappointment.

She then smiled widely and said, \"So be it. This is already very
good.\"

The reason for Situ Longqiu\'s question was the strange contents
inscribed on the side of the seal that Dong Bude had given her: Resting
at Goose Lake Mountain\'s Longqiu Waterfall, I dream of blazing stars in
my slumber. Overjoyed, I\'m unable to sleep, so I jump barefoot into the
long grass.

Situ Longqiu had asked many knowledgeable friends in her clan --- people
with impressive libraries of books --- about this after receiving the
seal, yet none of them had managed to offer a good explanation about
Goose Lake Mountain\'s Longqiu Waterfall.

Chen Ping\'an recalled something, and he said with a smile, \"In fact, I
do have one piece of good news for you. It\'s extremely likely that
Goose Lake Mountain will become a vassal of the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent\'s New Eastern Mountain in the future, promoting it to the
level of a \'crown prince\' mountain. This should greatly improve its
renown.\"

Situ Longqiu faltered for a moment before asking, \"Crown prince
mountain? What nonsense is this?\"

She then laughed loudly and continued, \"In any case, this sounds like a
good thing.\"

She turned around and walked back to Qi Shou\'s side, after which they
jumped on their swords and returned to the main city in the north
together.

1\. The waterfall here is referred to as Longqiu (龙湫), which is the
same as Situ Longqiu\'s name. The Longqiu waterfall is a real waterfall
that exists at Goose Lake Mountain (雁荡山), a coastal mountain range in
southeastern Zhejiang province in eastern China.

[]{#chapter-126.xhtml}

# Chapter 623: (2): Sword Training

Sword of Coming

Guo Zhujiu had sprinted over just then, and she had already been
squatting beside her master for a long while. After Situ Longqiu left,
the young girl whispered to her master, \"Rest assured, Master, your
secret is safe with me. I won\'t say anything to the Master\'s wife.
Master\'s wife is lofty, but I\'m still on your side.\"

Chen Ping\'an smiled and commented in a soft voice, \"Regardless of
whether it\'s you or Big Sister Situ, both of you can be regarded as
celestial maidens in my hometown.\"

\"Celestial maidens?\" Guo Zhujiu asked in curiosity. \"Do they still
fart? If they do, are their farts fragrant? Do they keep these farts
contained inside their dresses on purpose? Otherwise, they can\'t be
regarded as celestial maidens, can they? After all, I wouldn\'t be able
to accept something like this if I were a man who looked up to celestial
maidens. So, if I were a celestial maiden, I would hide under my
blankets to fart in secret. I would then lift a corner of my blanket and
use it as a fan. That way, I most likely won\'t end up smelling my own
fart.\"

Chen Ping\'an was already accustomed to Guo Zhujiu\'s wild and peculiar
manner of thinking, so he simply took another sip of water elixir wine
from his Sword Nurturing Gourd, further easing the dire situation in his
pitiful water palace that was almost sucked dry of spiritual energy. He
then smacked the young girl\'s head, standing up and saying, \"Let\'s go
and look for Master\'s wife.\"

The master and disciple made their way to Ning Yao\'s section of the
great wall.

Guo Zhujiu skipped and hopped, but it was a shame that she wasn\'t
wearing the small bamboo bookcase on her back right now. \"How many
great demons did you kill, Master?\" she asked in a casual voice.

\"It\'s already a good result that your master managed to stay alive,\"
Chen Ping\'an replied with a chuckle.

Guo Zhujiu\'s mind was as nimble as could be, and she didn\'t hesitate
for a second before nodding and remarking, \"Master, you are being
benevolent and temporarily sparing their worthless lives.\"

\"How are things going on your father\'s side?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

Guo Zhujiu cracked a grin and replied, \"I saw him on my way here, and
he allowed me to look for you and return home later.\"

This was a simple response, and her comment of seeing her father \"on
the way here\" was worthy of deeper consideration. This eased the
gloominess in Chen Ping\'an\'s mind, which had gradually accumulated
while he experienced the first large-scale battle in his life. The
gloominess was replaced with warmth, and it was as if the clouds had
parted to reveal the bright moon.

Chen Ping\'an had been responsible for defending a section of the great
wall closer to the middle, which was relatively far away from where Ning
Yao and the others were.

Guo Zhujiu wasn\'t afraid of traveling long distances, and even taking
one extra step would be good as she explored everywhere with her master.
As she walked around, she might even overtake her senior sister, who
wasn\'t very tall.

They continued to walk along the city wall, passing Sword Immortal Wu
Chengpei, who was at the peak stage of the Unpolished Jade Tier, on the
way. He had yet to unleash a single sword strike, and he had used the
entire battlefield as a whetstone to temper and train his sword.

There were all kinds of strange and peculiar bonded flying swords at the
Sword Qi Great Wall, with some able to transform into the godly bodies
of primordial deities, some able to create talismanic formations, some
able to summon the five lightnings around themselves and unleash the
Five Lightning Righteous Technique, and so on.

There was even a pair of earth immortal Dao partners, and one of their
flying swords could transform into a flood dragon, while the other\'s
flying sword was named Painting Eyes. The strength of these flying
swords would increase considerably when they were unleashed together,
and their attacks were no inferior to those of sword immortals. There
were countless more examples, and there were truly all kinds of bizarre
and fantastical bonded flying swords at the Sword Qi Great Wall.\[1\]

It was no wonder that the Sword Qi Great Wall didn\'t need any
additional Qi refiners to help.

Pang Yuanji didn\'t leave the city wall either, and following beside him
was a young woman who admired him. She was none other than Gao Youqing,
Gao Yehou\'s younger sister.

Pang Yuanji smiled and nodded in acknowledgment when he saw Chen
Ping\'an and Guo Zhujiu.

Chen Ping\'an also smiled and nodded in response, after which he asked,
\"How many great demons did you kill, Brother Pang?\"

\"The same as you,\" Pang Yuanji replied with a smile.

\"You\'re a lofty earth immortal, so why are you comparing yourself to a
measly second tier cultivator? This is cheapening yourself,\" Chen
Ping\'an said.

Guo Zhujiu ran over to Gao Youqing and stood on her tippy-toes, patting
the latter\'s head with a kind expression as she nodded and lectured,
\"Youqing, a married daughter is like spilled water that can\'t be
recovered, so since you\'re yet to get married, you need to make sure to
restrain yourself. Remember to restrain yourself, okay?\"

Gao Youqing swatted away Guo Zhujiu\'s unwelcome hand, shooting a glare
at the young girl and scolding, \"Don\'t utter such nonsense, Lü Duan.\"

The young girl looked at the elegant Pang Yuanji in white through the
corners of her eyes.

Chen Ping\'an and Guo Zhujiu continued to walk along the Great Wall, and
Chen Ping\'an gestured for Guo Zhujiu to remain silent when he saw an
excitedly talking young man on the parapet.

However, Gu Jianlong immediately felt like something was amiss after
Chen Ping\'an took a few steps, and it wasn\'t long before he discovered
the warmly smiling second shopkeeper. Without saying so much as an
additional word, Gu Jianlong beckoned to his friends and jumped on his
flying sword, hurriedly rushing back to the main city.

Two unfamiliar faces appeared at Ning Yao\'s section of the great wall.

One was Virtuous Scholar Chen Shi from the Pure Confucian Chen Clan, and
the other was Noble Scholar Qin Zhengxiu from the Southern Whirl
Continent\'s Mountain Foot Academy.

The two of them didn\'t kill demons like Liu Xianyang, and the reason
for this was very simple. They weren\'t sword cultivators, and the demon
army was unable to advance close to the city wall, so they were unable
to provide any help. Moreover, sword cultivators were very particular
about having highly compatible and seamless cooperation when they
launched sword attacks, so Chen Shi and Qin Zhengxiu might have very
easily been more trouble than help if they had attempted to launch any
attacks of their own, despite some of their mystical abilities being
overwhelmingly powerful.

Because of this, the two good friends were legitimately sightseeing as
they walked along the entire carriageway of the great wall. When
returning the same way, they seized this pause in battle to greet Chen
Sanqiu and the others.

The Confucian noble scholar who had taken the sword, Righteous Aura,
from the Sword Qi Great Wall back then was good friends with Qin
Zhengxiu, and the two of them had also become noble scholars at the same
time.

It was this noble scholar who had asked Qin Zhengxiu to help him deliver
a message and greeting to the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Qin Zhengxiu was currently chatting with Die Zhang.

Die Zhang was revealing some insider information about large-scale
battles, saying that the Sword Qi Great Wall didn\'t need to explicitly
strive to kill as many demons as possible early on in the battle. In
fact, the sword cultivators might even consolidate the battle lines
depending on the situation, choosing to slowly kill their enemies.

When things became urgent and the demon army reached the foot of the
great wall, giving them a very good chance to build a wall of corpses
and reach the parapet, then a large number of sword immortals would
leave the city wall to stabilize the front lines. They would sever the
battlefield into two, allowing the earth immortal sword cultivators to
jump down the city wall with their respective units to kill the
attacking demons. Middle Five Tier sword cultivators with insufficient
combat power could stay back to guard the city wall.

Chen Sanqiu and Yan Zhuo were squatting to the side and chuckling in
secret as they watched on. They copied the second shopkeeper and held
their hands inside their opposite sleeves, making them appear like
farmers squatting in the fields and staring at their crops.

It was very rare to see Die Zhang speaking to others in such a soft and
gentle manner.

Ning Yao was resting her mind with her eyes shut.

When Qin Zhengxiu had introduced himself and explained his relationship
with the other Confucian noble scholar, Ning Yao had spoken a few
sentences in an uncharacteristic display. Only afterward had she walked
away to nurture her sword intent by herself.

Dong Huafu and Fan Dache were discussing what they should drink and eat
after they returned to the city. Dong Huafu praised Fan Dache for a
decent performance this time, and he suggested that they should buy a
pot of Azure Divine Mountain Wine to celebrate.

\"There was most likely a renegade sword cultivator before, and they
paid the price of sacrificing a bonded flying sword to secretly deliver
a message to the demon tribe,\" Chen Shi suddenly said.

This was an extremely unpleasant way to put things.

Indeed, this was probably the reason why Chen Shi would inexplicably
make enemies wherever he went as soon as he left home.

However, Ning Yao and the others were completely unfazed.

\"Rain needs to fall, women need to marry, and shops need to make money
--- no one can stop these things.\"

Dong Huafu turned around and said, \"They at least sacrificed a bonded
flying sword for the sake of staying alive. In the future, I wonder
whether scholars like you from the Southern Whirl Continent will dare to
genuinely sacrifice half their lives to stay alive. I\'ve heard that
scholars who aren\'t cultivators might possess profound knowledge, but
they\'re quite lacking when it comes to tolerating pain. How does that
saying go again? There\'s no knife in the kitchen, there\'s no well in
the backyard; hanging oneself is too unsightly, and the beams are too
hard and too cold?\"

Qin Zhengxiu furrowed his brows.

Meanwhile, Chen Shi laughed and said, \"There is indeed such a saying.
This can\'t be helped. There are far too many scholars in the Majestic
World, the good, the bad, and everything in between.\"

Dong Huafu stole a few glances at the young scholar before nodding and
saying, \"You\'re a fairly easygoing one. You should treat me to some
wine later.\"

Chen Shi found this quite interesting, and he smiled and asked,
\"Shouldn\'t you be the one treating me to some wine?\"

Dong Huafu smiled and called out, \"Hey, Dache.\"

\"Even the second shopkeeper is unable to make Dong Huafu pay for
anything,\" Fan Dache immediately revealed in exasperation.

Qin Zhengxiu turned around and looked over. There were two visitors, one
being a deathly pale young man wearing a standard Dao robe from the
garment market and carrying a standard sword from the sword market. He
looked very much like a sickly and frail person with insufficient combat
power, but because he was accompanied by Liu Xianyang, Qin Zhengxiu knew
that he was Chen Ping\'an from Dragon Spring Prefecture, which was
located in the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent\'s Great Li Empire.

Qin Zhengxiu also knew that Chen Ping\'an was a direct disciple of the
Scholarly Sage, making him the junior brother of Great Sword Immortal
Zuo You. Watching Liu Xianyang unleash sword strikes beside Chen
Ping\'an before had truly been an eye-opener for this noble scholar. Liu
Xianyang had kept his abilities very well concealed in the past, and
even Chen Shi, who had an extremely good relationship with Liu Xianyang,
was only finding out for the first time that Liu Xianyang was actually a
sword cultivator.

Chen Ping\'an smiled and bowed in respect, saying in greeting, \"My
respects to Noble Scholar and Virtuous Scholar.\"

Qin Zhengxiu and Chen Shi also bowed in response, returning the gesture.

\"When disciples of the Second Sage and the Scholarly Sage meet, they
should at least argue with each other even if they don\'t fight,\" Dong
Huafu mumbled quietly.

Ning Yao stood up and said, \"It\'s time to head back.\"

Chen Ping\'an summoned his talismanic boat and stepped onboard.

Meanwhile, Qin Zhengxiu and Chen Shi politely turned down Chen
Ping\'an\'s invitation, saying that they wanted to wander around the
Sword Qi Great Wall for a while longer.

The talismanic boat sailed north.

Chen Ping\'an and Guo Zhujiu were sitting on one side and rowing very
hard.

Chen Sanqiu and Yan Zhuo were sitting on the opposite side and rowing
equally as hard.

Dong Huafu shook his head and remarked, \"This is far too
embarrassing.\"

Fan Dache wholeheartedly agreed with this.

Qin Zhengxiu observed this from the city wall.

With the exception of Chen Ping\'an, all of the passengers on the
immortal ship were actually sword cultivators. Despite this, none of
them flew back to the city on their flying sword.

Chen Shi smiled and said, \"Liu Xianyang always boasts to me about Chen
Ping\'an from his hometown, saying that apart from being a bit quiet and
reserved, he\'s incredibly smart and very quick at learning new things.
It\'s almost like he has no flaws at all. In the beginning, Liu Xianyang
even patted his chest and confidently promised me that Chen Ping\'an
would definitely become the most skillful pottery maker one day.
Afterward, however, Liu Xianyang never mentioned anything about pottery
firing at the dragon kilns again.\"

\"Even Liu Xianyang most likely didn\'t imagine that Chen Ping\'an would
become the closing disciple of the Scholarly Sage,\" Qin Zhengxiu said.

Chen Shi glanced at the talismanic boat in the distance and commented,
\"Chen Ping\'an probably didn\'t imagine that Liu Xianyang would become
a sword cultivator either.\"

He then sighed with emotion and remarked, \"My older sister once said
that the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent\'s Jewel Small World was a
treasured land with extraordinary people.\"

1\. This refers to the idiom (画龙点睛) about bringing a painted dragon
to life by painting its eyes last.

[]{#chapter-127.xhtml}

# Chapter 623: (3): Sword Training

Sword of Coming

Inside the Jia Shen Tent, Sword Cultivator Yu Si stepped inside, and
apart from Li Zhen, the gazes of everyone else immediately focused on
him.

\"How did it go?\" Mu Ji asked.

Yu Si smiled and replied, \"Not bad. I can confirm he\'s a sword
cultivator and not some Confucian disciple cultivating righteous aura or
whatnot. However, his sword techniques are extremely profound and
mystical.\"

After saying this, Yu Si raised his arm, which radiated a faint aura of
blood. \"Do you see this? My Dao robe isn\'t damaged at all.\"

Yu Si then rolled up his sleeves, and his arm that was initially wrapped
in several sheets of golden paper had already become bloody and mangled.
He chuckled in anger and revealed, \"I was fortunate to have some
defensive treasures. Otherwise, I would have been severely wounded by
this person\'s elusive sword intent if I weren\'t directly killed.\"

\"How did Liu Xianyang launch his sword attacks?\" Mu Ji asked.

Yu Si shook his head and replied, \"I apologize, but I genuinely don\'t
know how he launched his sword strikes. It was silent and undetectable,
and it struck me out of nowhere\... If I had to make a comparison, it
would be like getting goosebumps after being glanced at by some
senior.\"

Mu Ji furrowed his brows and asked, \"Is it because Liu Xianyang\'s
sword qi is too quick? So quick that it can pierce through the river of
time without even causing the slightest of ripples? For example, Qi Shou
has broken through recently, and his flying sword called Heartstring
possesses a bonded mystical ability wherein it\'s able to greatly
minimize the natural obstruction that the river of time has on flying
swords, allowing it to become incredibly quick. Or perhaps Liu
Xianyang\'s bonded flying sword is even more peculiar than this?\"

\"Great Sword Immortal Han Huaizi from the Northern Complete Reed
Continent and Liu Jinglong, the newest sword immortal of the Great
Emblem Sword Sect, also possess exceptionally strange and mystical
flying swords,\" the young woman said. \"Even though we don\'t know the
names of these flying swords, we know that they\'re widely regarded as
being close to Dao.\"

Yu Si smiled and shook his head vigorously. He shook his wounded arm,
and he felt slightly pained about the destruction of his golden
talismans. \"His cultivation base likely isn\'t very high, and he\'s
certainly not an Upper Five Tier sword immortal. It\'s simply that his
sword technique is far too strange.\"

A messenger flying sword arrived at the Jia Shen Tent.

A smile spread across Mu Ji\'s face after he read the secret letter. In
fact, a slight smile appeared on the faces of everyone inside the Jia
Shen Tent.

Mu Ji stood up and walked around the study desk, holding his index
finger and middle finger together to draw a circle. A hovering scroll
measuring approximately three meters long appeared inside the large
military tent.

\"The Gui Wei Tent has already delivered intelligence reports to all of
the other military tents,\" Mu Ji said in a solemn voice. \"This is an
illustration of the Sword Qi Great Wall\'s defensive distribution, and
the letter records and marks out the rough responsibilities of each
Upper Five Tier sword immortal, as well as some relatively permanent
postings.

\"In addition to this, there are also detailed records specifically
relating to the Nascent Tier sword cultivators who are able to guard a
section of the great wall by themselves, as well as relating to those
Golden Core Tier sword cultivators who possess remarkable destructive
power. There are also some individual notes related to those young and
prodigious Dragon Gate Tier and Sea Observation Tier sword cultivators,
such as Ning Yao and her companions.\"

Mu Ji started to list out the names of the most important sword
immortals and sword cultivators, as well as what sections of the great
wall they were defending and what their specific responsibilities were.
Each time he said a name, the young woman would write it down on the
hovering scroll in extremely small characters. Fortunately, those in the
Jia Shen Tent were all demon cultivators with extremely good eyesight.
Even if their cultivation bases weren\'t very high, they would be able
to focus their gazes and clearly see the characters on the scroll,
regardless of how tiny the characters were.

The names on the scroll were separated into three colors: gold,
vermilion, and black. These colors corresponded respectively to Upper
Five Tier sword immortals, Nascent Tier sword immortals, and all Middle
Five Tier sword cultivators, including those at the Golden Core Tier.

\"The names here represent the most important sword immortals and sword
cultivators. This is true even for those seemingly unremarkable names
written in black. In fact, the lower their cultivation base, the more we
need to find an opportunity to kill them,\" Mu Ji stressed.

\"Then I\'ll use the gold ink to circle those special names?\" the young
woman suggested.

Mu Ji nodded and said, \"Go ahead. For example, there\'s Sword Immortal
Guo Jia\'s daughter, Guo Zhujiu. There\'s also Gao Yehou\'s younger
sister, Gao Youqing.\"

The top ten paramount cultivators of the Sword Qi Great Wall were all
listed on the hovering scroll. In addition to them, there were also the
many great sword immortals such as Great Sword Immortal Yue Qing, Clan
Leader Yao Lianyun, the Northern Complete Reed Continent\'s Han Huaizi,
and Guest Elder Li Tuimi of the Yan Clan.

It wasn\'t that the great demons of the Savage World hadn\'t considered
these fine details in the past when launching assaults on the Sword Qi
Great Wall. Rather, it was the case that their plans could never keep up
with the changes.

This time, the Savage World had sixty military tents, including the Jia
Shen Tent, which represented close to five thousand demon cultivators.
There were military tents like the Jia Shen Tent that were only
responsible for their own sections of the battlefield, but more of the
military tents needed to provide assistance and work together to achieve
some greater goal.

The Jia Shen Tent was relatively special, given that it had a very large
number of innate sword talents who had the potential to become sword
immortals in the future. Because of this, there was no need for the Jia
Shen Tent to divide its attention and focus on other matters. Inside the
tent were Li Zhen from Holding Moon Mountain, Bei Qie, Tun Tan, Yu Si,
and the young female sword cultivator, Liu Bai. There were only one
hundred innate sword talents in the Savage World, and just the Jia Shen
Tent alone was already housing five of them. It clearly couldn\'t house
any more than this.

The other military tents had additional tasks and responsibilities. For
example, the Gui Wei Tent needed to keep an eye on the movements of the
most powerful sword cultivators at the Sword Qi Great Wall. At the same
time, they needed to record the sword strikes of each sword immortal on
the great wall, as well as why these sword immortals had launched
attacks, whom they had targeted with these attacks, how much power they
had put into these attacks, what the destructive power of these attacks
was like, and whether or not they had broken through to the next tier.

Most importantly, and most difficult of all, they needed to determine
whether these sword immortals were purposely concealing their strength.
If the answer was positive, they needed to pay extra attention to these
sword immortals to see whether they remained so \"polite\" when they
launched attacks in the future.

If this were confirmed, it would verify the sword immortals\' sincerity,
and in turn, the demon tribe would reduce the number of soldiers
deployed to the relevant battlefields by the relevant military tents.
They would slightly reduce the ferocity of the attacks, but definitely
not to a degree that would be easily noticeable.

Otherwise, if the two opposing sides reached a tacit agreement, but this
was discovered by the Sword Qi Great Wall, then Chen Qingdu\'s temper
was such that the offending sword immortals would definitely suffer
terrible fates. Once Chen Qingdu executed a sword immortal to make an
example, who else would dare to secretly assist the Savage World?

Elsewhere, the Xin Mao Tent was responsible for the specific deployments
of all Upper Five Tier cultivators in the demon tribe\'s army, assigning
these cultivators to the various military tents and their corresponding
battlefields.

The Geng Yin Tent was responsible for supply and replenishment, and the
Yi Wei Tent was responsible for the replenishment and reinforcement of
troops, directing them to the correct locations behind the battlefield
to set up camps and provide reinforcements as required. At the same
time, the Yi Wei Tent would also identify the most suitable battle
fronts to advance along.

As for why most of the Savage World\'s paramount great demons were
missing apart from a select few, this was partially because there was
temporarily no need for these powerful beings to help out on the
battlefield, and partially because they were actually very busy as well.

Mobilizing half of the Savage World\'s power to attack the Sword Qi
Great Wall was something that the demon tribe had never done before in
its history. Moreover, there were many unruly territorial forces behind
the battlefield, and not all of them were willing to obediently listen
to the commands of the paramount great demons.

Some extremely powerful great demons failed to observe and understand
the situation, so the only option was to forcefully subdue them. There
were also many demons that acted obediently on the surface, but actually
concealed their strength in secret. Most troublesome of all were the
clashes and internal conflicts that took place between fellow demons.

There was even a group of sword immortals that didn\'t act like
upstanding and righteous sword immortals, and they were completely
unwilling to properly launch their sword strikes on the battlefield.
Instead, they transformed themselves into sinister assassins, especially
targeting the generals who were leading armies to the battlefield in the
north, inhibiting the many demon armies marching to the Sword Qi Great
Wall.

Things would become nightmarishly difficult when sword immortals were
hellbent on leaving immediately after assassinating their targets.
Defeating a sword immortal and killing a sword immortal were two
completely different concepts --- the gulf between them was like the
gulf between heaven and earth.

Why did the Jia Shen Tent still want to kill Chen Ping\'an even though
they were keenly aware that he was acting as bait? This was because Chen
Ping\'an hadn\'t just defeated Li Zhen, but he had actually managed to
kill Li Zhen. He would become a huge thorn if he were allowed to live
and mature, so it was worth the Jia Shen Tent taking a gamble and
deploying an Upper Five Tier sword cultivator.

However, their intelligence had been lacking at the time, and they had
failed to accurately assess the sword techniques and destructive ability
of Sword Immortal Xie Songhua from the Pure White Continent. As a
result, the Jia Shen Tent had failed to kill Chen Ping\'an, and they had
even paid a huge price for their attempt. Mu Ji resolutely took
responsibility for this failure, even if doing so might cost him the
opportunity to receive a bestowed surname from Holding Moon Mountain and
record his name in the genealogical records. Mu Ji didn\'t regret his
decisions at all.

Death was inevitable in war. This was no game, and the number of deaths
would only continue to climb until it reached eye-watering figures.
However, things would be cast in a positive light if victory were
achieved, and everything could be rectified and made up for in a casual
manner. If defeat were handed down, in contrast, then it would be
difficult to say who the owner of the Savage World would be in the
future.

The Savage World was larger than the Majestic World by approximately two
Northern Complete Reed Continents. Contrary to its large size, however,
the Savage World could somewhat be viewed as an empty and desolate shell
compared to the wealthy and flourishing Majestic World. The lands of the
Savage World were barren and unable to produce many crops and materials.

Even though the Savage World indeed possessed some unique advantages,
these were far inferior compared to those possessed by its neighbor.
These differences were ginormous, but they were a result of comparing
one large world to another large world.

In any case, the demon tribe was extremely quick at reproducing and
expanding. In addition, cultivators from the demon tribe were almost
free from the constraints of virtue and morality.

Of course, there were also some humongous empires that ruled over vast
stretches of land, with some of this land so fertile that many other
forces coveted it. There were also many treasured lands with abundant
spiritual energy, and it was said that some of these treasured lands
were no inferior to the blessed lands in the Majestic World and the
Heavenly World.

Yu Si took a swig of low-quality wine before wiping his mouth and saying
with a smile, \"I also stole a few glances at Chen Ping\'an when I was
on the battlefield, and just like Tun Tan said, he\'s a very sly person.
He\'s a very difficult opponent to come up against.\"

\"He\'s suffered a fall in his cultivation base, and he isn\'t an innate
sword talent either, so it\'s naturally a big stretch for him to launch
many attacks right now,\" Li Zhen said. \"It was largely thanks to Liu
Xianyang and Qi Shou\'s help that he could defend his stretch of the
great wall. Even so, he\'s most skilled at analyzing the destructive
power of his own flying swords, his enemies\' combat power, and the
finer details on the battlefield. He\'s also exceptionally skilled at
fighting battles of attrition.\"

\"We need to have an overwhelming advantage if we want to target this
person,\" Liu Bai said.

\"Then how about we try to surround him as a group?\" Mu Ji suggested.
\"Li Zhen will be our main offensive, Yu Si will bring up the rear and
keep things under control, and Tun Tan will be responsible for
identifying weak points and launching opportune attacks. As for whether
or not this will work, we won\'t know unless we try.\"

\"Let me take Li Zhen\'s place,\" Bei Qie suddenly said.

Li Zhen\'s expression became dark.

\"This is an instruction from my master,\" Bei Qie added.

Only after hearing this did Li Zhen\'s expression improve.

Casting one\'s gaze over the paramount great demons of the Savage World,
even renowned and domineering rulers such as Skeletal Great Demon Bai
Ying and the owner of Elite Cavalry River would face large amounts of
criticism.

Bei Qie\'s master was one of the few mighty figures who were easier to
see in person, and this was because he traveled around the world all
year long, belonging to no sect and having no permanent residence.
However, he faced very few criticisms, and at most, demons would accuse
him of refusing to fight for the Savage World even though he possessed
such paramount power.

The demons said that if he had been willing to participate in the wager
of thirteen battles back then, there would have been no need for the two
large-scale assaults on the Sword Qi Great Wall afterward.

However, Bei Qie\'s master had bluntly refused to participate.

Two great demons had perished after breaking their vows, and some
disciples of their sects had descended into insanity, shockingly seeking
Bei Qie\'s master out to exact revenge.

Bei Qie\'s master didn\'t even draw his blade, and it was said that he
had casually killed the leading Unpolished Jade Tier demon with a single
punch. Indeed, he had easily hammered the foolish demon to death with
just a single punch.

Bei Qie had still been a young and bastard sword cultivator back then,
and he had used his sword to kill the remaining demon cultivators one
after another. Only a few measly ants were spared and allowed to flee
back to their sects, delivering news of their overwhelming defeats.
Afterward, they had rushed back over with some other cultivators to
apologize to Bei Qie\'s master. In the end, two Unpolished Jade Tier
demons had served as subordinates to Bei Qie and his master for many
years, often helping Bei Qie to train and spar.

The principles in the Savage World had always been very direct and
simple: Might was right.

If the Savage World had its own official history books, then each and
every page would most definitely be exuding strong auras of violence and
bloodshed.

Many forces had worked hard to be on the verge of forming powerful
nations and empires, yet a large number of them had been wantonly
crushed and annihilated by powerful and eccentric great demons. Many
capitals that reflected the blood, sweat, and tears of several
generations of rulers were transformed into ruins overnight, with the
palaces and streets transforming into seas of blood.

For example, the six trusted generals of Skeletal Great Demon Bai Ying
all liked to reduce entire nations into mass graves, turning their
populations into skeletal puppets. Afterward, they would raise these
puppets and pit them against each other, watching their numbers dwindle
until some usable talents were nurtured.

Only sword cultivators, regardless of their cultivation base, were
fortunate enough to be spared from these mysterious calamities.

This was a rule established by Holding Moon Mountain.

Sword cultivators in the Savage World were similar to scholarly talents
in the Majestic World, and one could even argue that the former were
more protected and pampered than the latter.

This was actually very strange, since the common enemy of the Savage
World was those sword cultivators from the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Regardless of how the Savage World attacked the great wall, and no
matter how many times they suffered bruising defeats, they were still
willing to feel a sense of sincere respect toward the sword immortals
and sword cultivators of the Sword Qi Great Wall.

This didn\'t stop them from being ruthless on the battlefield.

After leaving the battlefield, demon cultivators who had personally been
involved in the brutal battles might feel unbridled resentment at the
mention of sword immortals from the Sword Qi Great Wall, but they would
never slander or abuse these enemy sword immortals.

[]{#chapter-128.xhtml}

# Chapter 623: (4): Sword Training

Sword of Coming

Ning Yao returned to the Ning Residence by herself, saying that she was
entering seclusion to refine her sword.

The others drank wine at Die Zhang\'s wine shop, and Fan Dache had
already accepted his fate and borrowed money to treat his companions.

They drank very quickly, and it wasn\'t long before Chen Sanqiu and the
others returned home. Guo Zhujiu dashed along the eaves and scaled the
tall walls, rushing home to reunite with her small bamboo bookcase. They
had been apart for a long time, and the young girl missed the bamboo
bookcase dearly.

In the end, the only people left at the wine shop were the shopkeeper,
the second shopkeeper, and numerous alcoholics who had run here to
satiate their craving. Die Zhang was busy serving customers, while Chen
Ping\'an was squatting next to the street and drinking.

Yu Juanfu and Zhu Mei surprisingly visited the wine shop to drink as
well.

Yu Juanfu held a pot of wine and walked toward Chen Ping\'an, and the
sword cultivators who were chatting nonsense with the second shopkeeper
immediately grinned and gave up their spots. They were each more
understanding than the other.

Yu Juanfu sat on the steps nearby, and Zhu Mei remained standing not far
away. The young woman was ultimately unable to emulate Big Sister
Zaixi\'s boldness.\[1\]

\"Chen Ping\'an, is your fist technique not widespread in the Eastern
Treasured Vial Continent?\" Yu Juanfu asked.

Chen Ping\'an shook his head and replied, \"Very few people learn it. In
fact, I can count the number of people on my fingers. In this sense, it
can be regarded as a minor fist technique. Judging from the loftiness of
its fist intent, however, it can be regarded as a major fist
technique.\"

Yu Juanfu nodded in understanding and said, \"Chen Ping\'an, strive to
advance to the Far Roaming Tier sooner rather than later. Disregarding
the talks about being prodigies or whatnot, it\'s not a bad thing for
you and Cao Ci to be walking in front of me on the path of martial arts.
At the very least, this is what I think. Don\'t be like those
cultivators in the mountains, who insist on walking lone paths.\"

Chen Ping\'an raised his wine bowl and replied with a smile, \"Let\'s
work hard together.\"

Yu Juanfu left with Zhu Mei after drinking her pot of wine.

Chen Ping\'an said goodbye to Tao Ban before returning to the Ning
Residence. After arriving at the entrance, he suddenly told Grandma Bai,
who was waiting for him there, that he needed to return to the city
wall.

He stepped aboard his talismanic boat and left the main city, flying
over the many private residences of the sword immortals.

After arriving at the city wall, Chen Ping\'an looked for Senior Brother
Zuo You first.

He voiced his thoughts, to which Zuo You smiled and said, \"It\'s very
good that you\'re able to think like this --- it saves me some trouble.
How much can you do with your current cultivation base? The overall
situation will roll on along its original path, completely unmoved by
your small fixes here and there.

\"Your intentions are good, but that\'s about all. Your actions are
largely futile. Before this, however, I have a question I want to ask
you. Disregarding cultivation base and status and only focusing on a
single possibility, will you choose to die here if doing so can save the
Sword Qi Great Wall?\"

Chen Ping\'an remained silent.

Zuo You paused for a moment before continuing, \"This is just an
impossible situation, so it\'s fine as long as you have an answer in
your heart. If you don\'t challenge yourself, how can you possibly
challenge heaven and earth? Don\'t feel like overthinking things or
thinking about too many things is necessarily bad.

\"The Confucian Sect talks about all things having fundamentals and
incidentals, just like all events have beginnings and conclusions, and
one will be close to the Great Dao once they understand the sequence of
such matters. Similarly, the Buddhist Sect talks about concepts of
progression, gradual comprehension, instant enlightenment, and
meditative insight, while the Daoist Sect also talks about the notion of
slow accumulation. In other words, you can take things slowly.\"\[2\]

Chen Ping\'an looked down at the battlefield in the south and replied in
a soft voice, \"I definitely won\'t forget your teachings, Senior
Brother.\"

Zuo You recalled a matter and said, \"You can\'t slack off in your
scholarly studies. Let me ask you two more small questions. Why do the
Buddhist Sect and the Daoist Sect have such different views on
constructing statues of deities? And looking at the Four Great
Bodhisattvas --- Wisdom, Compassion, Action, and Aspiration --- what\'s
the better or best way to rank them according to Master\'s theory of
sequential order?

\"Should wisdom come first, after which compassion is born, then a noble
aspiration is formed and acted upon? Or should compassion exist first,
which gives rise to noble aspiration, after which action is eventually
born from wisdom? Have a good think about these two questions.\"

\"Alright,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a nod.

He then smiled bitterly and said, \"These aren\'t small questions as you
say, Senior Brother.\"

\"They are indeed small questions for me, and they can\'t even be
regarded as questions for Master,\" Zuo You replied.

Chen Ping\'an bade farewell and took his leave. Something tugged at his
mind, so he didn\'t visit the thatched cottage to look for the old great
sword immortal.

Rather, there was one additional thing for Chen Ping\'an to do.

Zuo You frowned and said in a disgruntled voice, \"Can\'t you be more
direct? Is it necessary to torment my junior brother like this?\"

If it weren\'t for the old great sword immortal possessing lofty sword
skills, Zuo You would have asked him who he thought he was.

Chen Qingdu arrived beside Zuo You, with his hands clasped behind his
back as he smiled widely and remarked, \"Having lofty sword skills is
good. I feel refreshed and energetic every single day.\"

Chen Qingdu\'s gaze was resting on a small world extremely far away from
the city wall.

There was a proper private school inside this small world, and a man in
Confucian robes was currently imparting knowledge to a classroom of
young boys and young girls.

He first talked about the establishment of poetry, using the lines \"The
sun sets behind the mountains\" and \"Spring grass sprouts by the pond\"
as examples. He explained that these lines appeared direct and shallow
at first glance, but in reality, they captured the essence of the
scenery and didn\'t allow future generations to surpass them.\[3\]

This Confucian scholar was going by the pseudonym of Zhou Mi, and behind
him was a pair of screens decorated with gold mountains and blue waters.
On the table in front of him were many books and scholarly curios, which
naturally included a nine-piece set that contained within it the four
treasures of the study, paperweights, and inkstick rests.

The more flashy but insubstantial the spirit tools were --- perhaps they
would only be treated as miscellaneous trinkets by ordinary immortal
forces and wealthy mortal clans in the Majestic World --- the more they
would be viewed as precious treasures by demon cultivators in the Savage
World.

This Zhou Mi was none other than the great demon with the second-highest
throne in the abyssal ancient well. He was second only to the old man in
gray, and his throne was, in fact, even higher than that of Liu Cha, the
big-bearded man carrying a saber and a sword.

He was widely renowned as the Savage World\'s \"Sea of Knowledge,\" the
Holding Moon Mountain of the scholarly world.

Zhou Mi had perused a myriad of books and was deeply knowledgeable in
all matters, including the Three Teachings, the Hundred Schools of
Thought, poems and prose, arithmetic, painting, geology, music, and so
on.

He had given himself the title of Old Bookworm, and he was also known as
Omnipotent Old Fox.

Among his disciples were Shou Chen, Cai Ying, Tong Xuan, Tong Yin, Yu
Zao, and the Jia Shen Tent\'s Liu Bai, all of whom were part of the one
hundred innate sword talents.

Apart from them, his earlier generation of disciples had already become
successful cultivators of the Militarian Sect, the Commercialist Sect,
and the Foretellers.

When it came to the surnames of Zhou Mi\'s disciples, they could only
receive this after they breached and defeated the Sword Qi Great Wall.

In reality, the person responsible for keeping the genealogical records
was none other than Zhou Mi.

It was said that Skeletal Great Demon Bai Ying had once asked in
curiosity, \"Mr. Zhou, do you want to become the leader of scholars in
our world?\"

Zhou Mi had smiled and replied, \"This isn\'t enough.\"

Today, Zhou Mi talked about the need to be innocent as a person, how one
should develop a good grasp of society and its people when interacting
with them, and other such miscellaneous knowledge. His lecture went on
for more than one hour.

Moreover, he would often ask his students for their answers before
providing his own answer. If someone were able to offer an outstanding
answer, then Zhou Mi would directly give them a scholarly curio. Just
then, he had given one of his students a seal that he had personally
inscribed with the characters: Endless Streams and Mountains.

When Zhou Mi had just started teaching, he had once told his first
generation of disciples that scholars in the Majestic World no longer
held principles and reason in high regard --- these things were
ubiquitous and nothing special. There were naturally reasons for this,
and the positives and negatives and rights and wrongs were incredibly
complicated.

However, scholars in the Savage World were far from reaching this lofty
level, and they were far from a state where everyone possessed
principles and reasons. This was because their foundation was too poor,
so they needed to harbor a feeling of respect when they first set foot
on the path of scholarly pursuit. Zhou Mi\'s students only had one piece
of homework: They needed to transcribe classics belonging to the Three
Teachings and the Hundred Schools of Thought every single day.

Today\'s final topic in class pertained to the relationship between
humans and time. This touched upon a fundamental tenet. Even though
demons could assume human form after gaining sentience and intelligence,
Zhou Mi held the staunch belief that only those who studied scholarly
texts could be regarded as proper humans.

There was a warm smile on Zhou Mi\'s face as he explained his thoughts
in detail.

Before ten years old, time was like a small stream that slowly trickled
forward, so slow that it was as if one would never grow up and be able
to see the scenery in the distant lands.

After twenty years old, one wouldn\'t care about the flow of time,
unperturbed about whether it was quick or slow. Even taking a single
glance would be a waste of time.

After thirty years old, the flow of time would start to surge forward,
catching people completely off guard as they were forcefully yanked
forward.

After forty years old, time would appear like a thundering river
imminently about to enter the sea.

After sixty years old, time would suddenly transform again, becoming a
tranquil lake so still that not a single ripple existed.

Before death, time would turn into a waterfall that sank into the deep
pool below.

Some students listened carefully and understood, while some students
were distracted and lacked care.

Zhou Mi didn\'t categorize his students because of this, and he smiled
faintly and continued, \"The purer a knowledge or teaching is, the more
it appears to have no real meaning on the surface. In my view, however,
true power and influence in the world don\'t come from those who occupy
high positions, nor do they come from those with bigger fists. Rather,
it comes from those who can genuinely affect the minds of many people.

\"It\'s very good if you can comprehend and accept this, but it doesn\'t
matter if you can\'t. As long as you possess an outstanding skill and
don\'t lock down your own heart, you\'ll always have the chance to
ascend higher and higher with the passing of time. The scenery of the
Great Dao is stunning, and it\'s yours to pluck after you arrive at the
Majestic World.\"

After saying this, Zhou Mi turned to the pair of screens decorated with
mountains and waters behind him. In reality, he was actually looking
toward someplace on the Sword Qi Great Wall. He smiled faintly and said,
\"Claim not the sky is too lofty and lacks eyes and ears, say not the
earth is too thick and lacks a heart and mind.\"

\"You\'re still a long way off being able to establish your own
teaching,\" Chen Qingdu said with a smile.

------------

At night, an expressionless man left the Sword Qi Great Wall and entered
Stalactite Mountain through the new gate, making his way to the Sword
Reverence Pagoda.

The person accompanying him was Yan Zhuo\'s father, Yan Ming, the clan
leader of the Yan Clan who had done business with the intercontinental
ships of the Majestic World for countless years. He was using an
illusion technique.

The Sword Reverence Pagoda was already closed for the day, so only two
people walked inside. The expressionless man started to take down the
portraits of the sword immortals, one after another.

\"Help me inscribe a seal, Chen Ping\'an,\" Clan Leader Yan Ming said.
\"I\'ll ask Yan Zhuo to bring a blank seal to the Ning Residence
afterward, and I\'ll also offer one grain rain coin for the inscription.
You don\'t need to think about the contents, and I want the inscription
to read: Climbing the city wall is like visiting a grave.\"

Chen Ping\'an had just put away another portrait, and he thought about
this for a moment before asking, \"Can I add a few more characters?\"

\"Elaborate,\" Yan Ming said with a smile.

\"Launching a sword strike is like offering wine in respect,\" Chen
Ping\'an replied.

Yan Ming fell silent for a moment before nodding and saying, \"I won\'t
make you inscribe those extra characters for nothing. I\'ll offer you
two grain rain coins instead.\"

\"There\'s no need to pay me, Uncle Yan,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a
shake of his head.

\"It\'s too little? So you would rather receive nothing at all?\" Yan
Ming asked.

Chen Ping\'an was rendered speechless.

Yan Ming gestured for Chen Ping\'an to continue collecting the
portraits. Walking beside the young man, his expression was indifferent
as he said, \"To have a scholar who can throw punches and launch sword
strikes at the Sword Qi Great Wall, and who\'s willing to speak with a
good conscience\... I would feel like paying you for every single
character if I weren\'t a businessman.\"

Chen Ping\'an carefully put the portraits away.

Why had the old great sword immortal asked him to do this? Why did he
need to retrieve all of the sword immortal portraits from the Sword
Reverence Pagoda? Chen Ping\'an was unable to make any sense of this.
So, he simply did as he was told.

The two of them left the Sword Reverence Pagoda together, and while
walking down the stairs, Chen Ping\'an suddenly asked, \"Uncle Yan, can
I sit here for a short while?\"

Yan Ming nodded and said, \"I\'ll wait for you at the main entrance.
Don\'t stay here for too long.\"

He then walked away.

It was late at night, and only a single moon hung in the sky of the
Majestic World.

Chen Ping\'an was in a daze as he sat alone on the steps.

If he liked someone, he would look after her forever. He would
completely hand himself over to her.

If he left first, then what he saw last would be her. If she left first,
then what she saw last would be him.

Could he find a friend who didn\'t complain about the best wine being
expensive, but would also be satisfied with the lowest quality wine?

Could some of the deceased continue to survive in his mind, motivating
him to do better whenever he thought of their speech and actions?

Growing up wasn\'t a slow and meandering process, nor was it
encapsulated by walking from one place to another. Rather, growing up
would often happen in the blink of an eye.

Wherever his mind wandered, wherever his flying sword resided, his body
and mind would always be free.

However, how could he become a sword cultivator?

For some unknown reason, not a single wisp or tendril of remnant
primordial sword intent at the Sword Qi Great Wall was willing to give
its favor to Chen Ping\'an.

Chen Ping\'an exhaled and stood up, deciding that he would make a
compromise this one time even if he were unable to find a highly
suitable bonded item. He would gather all bonded items of the Five
Elements, which should allow him to return to the Willow Tendon Tier,
the third tier of Qi refinement.

However, doing this would be like prematurely accelerating his growth on
the path of cultivation. Afterward, this cultivation tier would indeed
become a Cultivator Trapping Tier.

Chen Ping\'an secretly returned to the Sword Qi Great Wall with Yan
Ming.

According to the instructions he had previously received from the old
great sword immortal, Chen Ping\'an retrieved all the portraits from his
minimization treasure and handed them to Yan Ming, then returned to the
Ning Residence.

Over at the city wall, Chen Qingdu accepted Chen Ping\'an\'s
minimization treasure. However, not only did he not open the
minimization treasure and retrieve the portraits, but he even cast a
restriction technique onto the minimization treasure before tossing it
back to Yan Ming and saying, \"Return it to that young lad, and tell him
that a small issue has occurred, rendering the minimization treasure
temporarily unopenable. Tell him we can address this problem later.\"

Yan Ming mustered his courage and left the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Chen Qingdu and Zuo You stood beside each other and gazed into the
distance.

\"Is your junior brother an idiot?\" Chen Qingdu suddenly asked.
\"Didn\'t he obtain the final item of the Five Elements a long time ago?
Why isn\'t he refining it?\"

\"That was something manipulated by Spiritual Master Fire Dragon, and it
also pertains to the fundamental True Qi of pure martial artists,\" Zuo
You replied. \"Chen Ping\'an is completely unable to separate that item
out with his current cultivation base, and one small mistake will cost
him everything. Stop making these cynical comments, Chen Qingdu. Will
you only be satisfied if he falls three tiers in Qi refinement and one
additional tier in martial arts for the sake of the Sword Qi Great
Wall?\"

\"And what about you, his Senior Brother? Are you just freeloading and
refusing to help?\" Chen Qingdu said with a chuckle.

This comment was like a knife to the heart because Zuo You was genuinely
unable to help right now.

His sword skills were too lofty, and his sword qi was too abundant,
making it very easy for his Great Dao to conflict with that of the item
hidden by Spiritual Master Fire Dragon. If that were to happen, Chen
Ping\'an\'s entire body would transform into a deadly battlefield.

To be very blunt, this was the Sword Qi Great Wall, so if even Chen
Qingdu didn\'t do something, then it would definitely be impossible for
anyone else.

In any case, did anyone dare to ask Chen Qingdu to do something?

Zuo You dared to, but he knew that things would be futile if Chen Qingdu
were unwilling.

Chen Qingdu remained silent for a moment before asking, \"Can Chen
Ping\'an tolerate pain?\"

Zuo You nodded and replied, \"Yes, he can.\"

Chen Qingdu smiled and asked, \"A price needs to be paid if you want me
to isolate that fire seed and refine it into his fifth bonded item. Chen
Ping\'an needs to walk a path similar to that of becoming a true spirit
or deity, where his body will be subject to grueling tests that will
leave him frail and emaciated. Rest assured, it\'s only similar, and
it\'s not actually the same. Otherwise, to say nothing of you, even the
old scholar will fight me to the death.\"

Zuo You started to hesitate in an uncharacteristic display.

This was a huge dilemma.

Chen Qingdu clicked his tongue in wonder and remarked, \"So much for you
being the senior brother. You\'re not even as bold and direct as your
junior brother. If Chen Ping\'an were here, he would have already nodded
and agreed to my suggestion.\"

Zuo You immediately stood up and said, \"I\'ll set up a protection
formation. I\'ll leave the city wall for a while, and I\'ll make up for
any missed sword strikes later.\"

Chen Qingdu placed a hand on Zuo You\'s shoulder and said, \"Protection
formation my ass. Stay here and do your job. There\'s no doubt about
being able to successfully refine the bonded item, and will there be any
point in having a protection formation for the path that follows? Your
ability to kill enemies is quite good, but it\'s a shame that you\'re
truly no good at teaching sword techniques to save others.\"

Zuo You was infuriated upon hearing this.

He had put up with the old great sword immortal not twice in a day,
three times a day, or even five times a day. Rather, the old great sword
immortal was relentlessly disrespecting his master and ruthlessly
picking on his junior brother. Was the old great sword immortal taking
him for a temperless clay Bodhisattva?

Chen Qingdu increased the pressure on Zuo You\'s shoulder and said with
a faint smile, \"Zuo You, it looks like you still don\'t have faith in
your junior brother.\"

\"How confident are you?\" Zuo You asked with a frown.

Chen Qingdu raised a single finger and replied, \"One with two zeroes.
Is this not enough?\"

Zuo You was slightly skeptical.

Chen Qingdu smiled and continued, \"Your sword skills are so lofty, so
would I dare to lie to you?\"

Zuo You directly drew his sword.

The entire Sword Qi Great Wall instantly noticed some anomaly.

Chen Qingdu shifted positions slightly and used his hand to grab the
blade, allowing Zuo You\'s sword to slash across his palm.

A huge amount of sparks immediately sprayed across the city wall.

------------

The intense battle between the Savage World and the Sword Qi Great Wall
resumed, but Liu Xianyang didn\'t appear on the city wall this time.
Instead, he was accompanying Chen Chun\'an.

Chen Ping\'an was once again neighbors with Qi Shou.

Qi Shou found something a little strange: Chen Ping\'an appeared
slightly different from normal today.

He was still wearing a standard Dao robe from the garment market, with a
bamboo jade folding fan slid into his waistband. Chen Ping\'an turned
around and said to Qi Shou with a smile, \"It\'s only been a few days,
but Brother Qi\'s elegant demeanor is even stronger than before.\"

Qi Shou instantly came to a realization. Upon further thought, however,
he started to feel unsure again. Heavens knew whether this was another
illusion technique.

\"Stay further away from me,\" he snapped.

Chen Ping\'an flicked open the folding fan and lightly rocked it back
and forth, creating a cool breeze as he casually summoned his four
flying swords. He then shook his head and said with a sigh, \"Brother
Qi, oh, Brother Qi, who gave you the courage and confidence to look down
on a powerful third tier cultivator as a measly Nascent Tier
cultivator?\"

Qi Shou completely ignored this. However, he was especially vicious as
he killed enemies today.

He had initially wanted to ask why Zuo You had suddenly unleashed a
sword strike before, but he didn\'t want to say a single word to Chen
Ping\'an right now.

On a section of the city wall near the thatched cottage, Zuo You used
his mind\'s lake to ask the old great sword immortal, \"Will he be able
to continue the momentum and nurture a flying sword after successfully
refining that bonded item and enduring the immense pain? What grade will
the flying sword be?\"

There was a blank look on Chen Qingdu\'s face as he replied, \"Did I
ever say that? Do such good deals exist in the world, where bonded
flying swords are handed out for free?\"

Zuo You turned around and looked at the old man standing at the entrance
of the thatched cottage.

Chen Qingdu retracted his smile and said, \"I once borrowed a locust
wood sword case, so I need to return the favor. I\'ll have Chen Ping\'an
become a sword case first, or more accurately, become a sword scabbard.
As for whether he can nurture a powerful bonded flying sword that\'s
blessed by heavenly fortune, and regarding what grade the flying sword
is, that\'s completely up to his own abilities.\"

Zuo You took a deep breath and soared away from the city wall, once
again flying alone on his flying sword into the enemy army to look for
an Ascension Tier great demon.

Inside the secret room of the Ning Residence.

Only the yin soul of Chen Ping\'an --- who was now a third tier Qi
refiner and a seventh tier pure martial artist --- had left his body to
patrol the Sword Qi Great Wall. Meanwhile, his true body and his yang
soul were still at the Ning Residence.

This was because the old great sword immortal said that the yin soul had
accumulated far too many thoughts, which were also far too
miscellaneous. As such, his sword couldn\'t become pure no matter how it
was washed. Even if it were washed until it was bright and pure, it
would no longer be Chen Ping\'an\'s sword.

Chen Ping\'an focused his attention and calmed his breathing, thinking
again and again about a sentence from a book: Mind dashing to the far
extremes, heart soaring to great heights, contemplating in silence, with
thoughts connecting one thousand years.

When his mind became silent, approaching a state of slumber, only a pair
of thoughts remained in the depths of his heart, slowly swimming around
his mind\'s lake. The two thoughts didn\'t fight, instead maintaining a
harmonious relationship with each other.

The body and mind of a sword cultivator would always be free.

He was pursuing the greatest destructive power, power even loftier than
the heavens!

Chen Ping\'an suddenly opened his eyes and said in a solemn voice,
\"Please launch a sword strike, Old Great Sword Immortal.\"

Sword light erupted inside the secret room.

Chen Ping\'an\'s skin and flesh instantly split apart, with even his
Vajra Body Tier physique appearing like papier-mache as he became bloody
and mangled in the blink of an eye. His limbs and bones, his internal
organs, and even his eyes were then comprehensively melted by the sword
light, instantly transforming him into nothing but bones.

In the end, not even a skeleton was left.

In the vast and boundless night, a dazed young man appeared dejected as
he stumbled along a path with no light. He was simply stumbling forward
on instinct.

As he walked, he eventually arrived near a hunchbacked little boy
wearing straw sandals. The latter was carrying a large basket and
walking slowly.

The little boy stopped and looked up at the young man, appearing very
sad and seemingly not understanding why he was still suffering so much
after growing up.

And thus, the heartbroken little boy lost the motivation to continue
forward. He squatted down on the ground, leaning against the large
basket that could never be filled to the brim, as he started to sob.

The young man shakily squatted down and dazedly looked at his younger
self.

The two of them looked at each other.

The young man said two words to the little boy, \"I\'m sorry.\"

The little boy then wiped away his tears and offered a hand.

The young man held the little boy\'s hand and stood up, with the two of
them advancing together.

The young man was still dazed, and he simply relied on his instinct and
inherent thoughts to describe all of the beautiful things the little boy
would experience in the future, seemingly forgetting about all the
challenges and hardships he had also faced along the way. It was as if
he couldn\'t remember those bad people and matters, as well as the
complexity of the world.

A smile gradually appeared on the little boy\'s face, and his expression
became one of slight eagerness as he looked up at his older self.

In the end, the little boy stopped and tightly gripped the straps of his
basket. His smile was dazzling, and he pointed toward the path in front
of them for his older self.

The young man looked over, and a faint and flickering light appeared on
the path that had initially been pitch black.

All of a sudden, a brilliant radiance illuminated heaven and earth.

1\. Shi Zaixi is a pseudonym for Yu Juanfu.

2\. This is a line from *The Great Learning* (大学), one of the \"Four
Books\" in Confucianism, attributed to one of Confucius\' disciples,
Zengzi.

3\. These are lines from the poems *Climbing White Stork Tower* and
*Climbing the Lakeside Pavilion*, respectively.
