# Chapter 630: (2): Assassinating the Hidden Official

Sword of Coming

Mi Yu withdrew his bonded flying sword, but didn\'t return his longsword
to its scabbard.

He knew that he was completely and utterly screwed.

Unless his brother could somehow save him, he was almost definitely
going to be thrown into the same prison as the old deaf guy.

Lu Zhi hurriedly raced onto the scene atop her flying sword, looking
absolutely livid.

\"You useless piece of shit!\" she spat through gritted teeth, while Mi
Yu remained standing still on the spot in a daze.

Lu Zhi immediately made a hand seal to try and gather the remnants of
Chen Ping\'an\'s soul, hoping against hope that she could somehow save
him, but it was all completely futile.

Lie Ji had sacrificed himself without any hesitation, and in doing so,
he had ensured Chen Ping\'an\'s demise beyond a shadow of a doubt.

Lu Zhi turned her gaze to the thatched cottage in the distance, then
consulted the old great sword immortal through her mind\'s lake.

\"Have Chou Miao select three swordsmen to enter the Hidden Official\'s
branch alongside him,\" Chen Qingdu said.

\"That\'s it?!\" Lu Zhi snapped.

\"You\'re asking *me* what to do after you\'ve failed in your duties?\"
Chen Qingdu countered.

\"What was I supposed to do, follow Chen Ping\'an around everywhere he
goes?\" Lu Zhi hissed. \"What about the other swordsmen of the Hidden
Official\'s branch then? Who\'s going to protect them? And what should I
do with Mi Yu? Kill him?!\"

\"We\'ll make a decision on Mi Yu later; just leave him be for now,\"
Chen Qingdu said.

Lu Zhi could only suppress the killing intent raging in her heart as she
returned to the section of the carriageway where the Hidden Official\'s
branch was gathered with Mi Yu.

After returning to the Hidden Official\'s branch, she displayed a rare
moment of hesitation, then broke the bad news.

\"The Hidden Official has been killed by traitor Lie Ji, who also died
during the attack. Mi Yu is going to be temporarily detained on
suspicion of malfeasance. Chou Miao will be joining the Hidden
Official\'s branch along with three others. All of you are to leave this
place right away and move to the summer palace.\"

Guo Zhujiu immediately burst into laughter. \"You have a great sense of
humor, Sword Immortal Lu!\"

Lin Junbi and the others were also exchanging disbelieving glances with
one another.

\"That\'s all I have to say,\" Lu Zhi sighed. \"Make sure to look after
yourselves.\"

With that, she departed without another word.

\"Alright, now that Lu Zhi\'s gone, you can tell us the truth, Sword
Immortal Mi,\" Guo Zhujiu said with a wide grin. \"It was kind of funny
when Lu Zhi said it, but I\'m going to get angry if you repeat the same
joke\...\"

Even though she was grinning from ear to ear, tears were already
swimming in her eyes. Her face puckered up as she spoke, and in the end,
she trailed off into a heartbroken silence.

Lin Junbi heaved a forlorn sigh.

The mantle of the Hidden Official really was heavy.

Unpolished Jade Tier Sword Immortal Lie Ji was ranked very far back in
Secondary Book A, only separated from Mi Yu by a few pages, but that was
exactly why he had been able to catch Chen Ping\'an and Mi Yu completely
off guard.

As for why he had done what he did, only the heavens knew the answer to
that question.

Dong Bude\'s complexion had turned quite pale, and she was clearly
struggling to come to terms with this outcome.

Gu Jianlong and Wang Xinshui\'s fists were tightly clenched, and they
refused to believe that Chen Ping\'an was truly gone.

All of the other swordsmen had also fallen into a dejected silence.

Before long, a sword immortal with a youthful appearance arrived on the
scene. He was an Unpolished Jade Tier sword immortal who was only just
over a hundred years of age, and he was said to be the Unpolished Jade
Tier sword immortal with the most solid cultivation foundation that the
Sword Qi Great Wall had seen in three thousand years.

It was Chou Miao, the boy who had ventured deep into the Savage World
with A\'Liang once upon a time.

He was accompanied by a female Nascent Tier swordsman by the name of Luo
Zhenyi. She was of a similar age to Chou Miao, and she had many single
sword immortal admirers on the Sword Qi Great Wall for her stunning
beauty.

In addition, there was also a young Golden Core Tier swordsman named Xu
Ning, who possessed two bonded flying swords, White Silk and Mountain
Scenery.

Then there was the young Dragon Gate Tier swordsman, Chang Taiqing.

\"Mi Yu can stay with me. Everyone else, move to the summer palace,\"
Chou Miao instructed. \"Zhenyi, Xu Ning, Taiqing, I\'ll get the three of
you to help everyone out.\"

A wry smile appeared on Mi Yu\'s face.

Clearly, Chou Miao was instructing him to stay by his side so that he
wouldn\'t be able to do anything.

The original swordsmen of the Hidden Official\'s branch began silently
packing up their things, and while they didn\'t harbor any animosity
toward the new additions to the group, they didn\'t exactly welcome them
with open arms, either.

Before they knew it, they had grown accustomed to Chen Ping\'an\'s
presence.

Guo Zhujiu remained seated behind her desk in a daze as she murmured,
\"I\'m not going anywhere. I\'m staying here to wait for Master.\"

\"Alright, just come to the summer palace when you feel like it then,\"
Chou Miao said.

From there, Chou Miao and everyone else departed from the top of the
city walls, making their way to the summer palace, while only Guo Zhujiu
remained behind.

As everyone arrived on the plaza outside the summer palace, they were
greeted by a rather unexpected sight, one that immediately explained to
Chou Miao why he hadn\'t been appointed the new Hidden Official.

In Chou Miao\'s eyes, it didn\'t really matter whether he became a
swordsman of the Hidden Official\'s branch or remained outside the city
to do battle. Both were forms of cultivation in themselves.

Luo Zhenyi\'s trio was certainly very surprised, while Mi Yu was so
relieved that he almost burst into tears.

Lin Junbi also heaved a sigh of relief.

Compared with Chou Miao, whom he didn\'t know anything about, Lin Junbi
still much preferred working with Chen Ping\'an, who had somehow
miraculously risen from the grave.

Sure enough, Chen Ping\'an was standing at the entrance of the summer
palace, watching everyone with a smile on his face.

His complexion was deathly pale, but his eyes were exceptionally bright.

\"Come take a walk with me,\" Chen Ping\'an said as he beckoned to Mi
Yu.

He then turned to Chou Miao and said, \"When I\'m not around, I want the
four of you to listen to Lin Junbi\'s opinions and advice.\"

\"No problem,\" Chou Miao replied with a nod.

Chen Ping\'an led Mi Yu down a walkway on a stroll elsewhere, while
everyone else entered the main hall of the summer palace.

Upon their arrival, they discovered that all of the secret documents
previously stored in the winter palace had already been transferred
here. They were stacked up against the three walls of the main hall in
an orderly fashion, and many of them had slips of paper attached to
them, making them easier to identify and browse through.

Judging from the neat, compact script handwriting on those slips of
paper, it was clear that this was Chen Ping\'an\'s handiwork.

Chen Ping\'an didn\'t say anything, and Mi Yu also remained silent.

Chen Ping\'an removed his Sword Nurturing Gourd from his waist, then
also pulled out a flagon of Bamboo Sea Small World wine that he offered
to Mi Yu.

\"I\'ll pass. I\'m too spooked to drink after what just happened,\" Mi
Yu sighed with a wry smile.

\"Countless types of people drink wine, but the wine itself is always
faultless,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a smile. \"Go ahead and drink, and
if you have any questions, go ahead and ask.\"

\"What happened?\" Mi Yu asked. \"If you\'re here, then who did Lie Ji
kill just now?\"

\"It was a Substitution Talisman of a very high caliber adhered to a
puppet that truly possessed the physique of a Vajra Body Tier martial
artist,\" Chen Ping\'an explained. \"On top of that, the old great sword
immortal also cast some illusions to make it more convincing. However,
just that alone definitely wouldn\'t have been enough to fool you, which
means that it also wouldn\'t have been able to fool Lie Ji, so I also
planted a part of my soul into the puppet.

"Every single step and every single breath that the puppet took was
meticulously controlled by me from this summer palace, and while I
sustained some pretty substantial injuries from the puppet\'s
destruction, it was certainly worthwhile, considering we managed to weed
out a traitor and a sword immortal, at that.

"I was actually initially intending for someone else to take the bait.
As for who that person is, you\'ve been with me this entire time, so
I\'m sure you had some ideas, but I presume you\'ve most likely already
forgotten.\"

\"When you were provoking Yang Zhi and Huang Luan earlier, was that also
in preparation for this?\" Mi Yu asked.

\"The swordsmen on our side are able to send messages to the Savage
World in secret, so the reverse is definitely also true,\" Chen Ping\'an
said with a smile. \"As for why Lie Ji turned traitor, that\'s something
that we\'ll never know. Perhaps he resented the Majestic World, perhaps
he resented the old great sword immortal, perhaps he resented the Sword
Qi Great Wall, or perhaps it was some combination of those things. In
any case, I\'m sure he had his reasons.

"Otherwise, he wouldn\'t have carried out the assassination with so much
resolve and finality. However, I\'m not really interested in finding out
his reasons. He\'s already dead anyway. It\'s a good thing that we
managed to weed him out so early. Otherwise, if he had turned traitor at
a more damning moment, then he could\'ve easily taken down one or two
sword immortals with him.\"

\"Is this the sole reason why I was dragged into the Hidden Official\'s
branch?!\" Mi Yu asked as he stopped in his tracks, looking both furious
and resigned.

Chen Ping\'an made no attempt to deny it, smiling and nodding as he
replied, \"Not only that, but Lu Zhi was also called upon for the same
purpose. If we didn\'t put on a sufficiently convincing act, then we
wouldn\'t have been able to fool the potential traitors among us. All of
the sword immortals who decide to betray the Sword Qi Great Wall
immediately become very cunning and devious.

"With Lu Zhi protecting everyone in the Hidden Official\'s branch, only
an Immortal Tier sword immortal who manages to somehow get close to me
would have any realistic chance at killing me under her watch. Anyone
else who tries would only be throwing their lives away for nothing. When
I\'m away from Lu Zhi, it creates a sense of urgency, like this is a
brief window of opportunity that they must capitalize on before it slips
away.

"Hence, Lu Zhi is really just there for show. At the same time, I
couldn't make it too obvious. For example, I couldn't just leave Lu Zhi
without your accompaniment. If I did that, it would be abundantly clear
that there\'s something suspicious going on.

"I am already not carrying Sword Immortal and not wearing Golden Sweet
Wine; if I went wandering around without your protection on top of that,
then all of the potential traitors on the Sword Qi Great Wall would be
too suspicious to make a move.\"

Mi Yu took a long swig of wine and didn\'t say anything.

\"Now that everyone thinks the Hidden Official is dead, there\'s
undoubtedly going to be a drop in morale,\" Chen Ping\'an continued.
\"Our sword formations are going to be negatively impacted as a result,
and that\'s simply an unavoidable outcome. However, at the same time,
this also makes it easier for us to throw out more bait and set more
traps, and I actually value that more than simply weeding out a
traitorous sword immortal.\"

Mi Yu could only stare at Chen Ping\'an in a stunned silence.

\"I\'ve been thinking a lot ever since I became Hidden Official, but
most of the things I\'ve thought of have been completely useless and
impractical,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a smile.

\"If you were to hold a grudge against someone on the Sword Qi Great
Wall, I bet they would end up dead before they even knew how or why they
were being killed, isn\'t that right?\" Mi Yu sighed.

Chen Ping\'an considered the question for a moment, then nodded and
replied, \"I should be able to pull that off, but I\'ve never considered
such a thing because it\'s simply not worth it. The purity and sanctity
of one\'s Dao Heart is a very precious thing, and it\'s not worth
tarnishing something so important just to settle something as trivial as
a personal grudge.\"

\"Is that really what you think?\" Mi Yu asked as a sharp look appeared
in his eyes. \"What about everything that the Qi Clan did to the Ning
Clan? Do you not resent them at all for what they did? Do you truly have
no selfish desires? Now that you\'ve become Hidden Official and read
through all of the secret documents, I\'m sure you know all of the
filthy secrets that have never seen the light of day. Is all of that
really something that you can just stomach and be fine with?\"

\"Why don\'t you take a guess, Brother Mi?\" Chen Ping\'an replied with
a smile.

However, Mi Yu continued to stare at him intently, waiting for an answer
to his question.

\"I don\'t know what to tell you.\" Chen Ping\'an shrugged. \"I\'m just
not the type of person to hold grudges.\"

All of a sudden, Mi Yu seemed even more dispirited than Chen Ping\'an,
despite the fact that it was the latter who had just suffered spiritual
damage instead of the other way around.

\"Guo Zhujiu is still on the carriageway,\" Mi Yu sighed. \"When should
we notify her to come here?\"

\"Let\'s wait for a bit longer,\" Chen Ping\'an replied.

\"You\'re constantly calculating and trying to manipulate everyone!\" Mi
Yu exclaimed with an exasperated shake of his head. \"Guo Zhujiu is just
a little girl, and she\'s your disciple! Even if you have her best
interests in mind, do you not feel guilty at all for doing this? Don\'t
you ever get tired of being so calculating all the time?\"

\"You think it\'s enough just to have a clear conscience?\" Chen
Ping\'an countered. \"Do you think Lie Ji had a completely clear
conscience? Why would a sword immortal like him just throw away his life
like that? How much resentment did he harbor to make him go to such
extremes?\"

Mi Yu had no response for this.

The two of them returned to the main hall of the summer palace, and Mi
Yu sat down at the spot reserved for him.

However, instead of doing the same, Chen Ping\'an sat down on the steps
outside.

\"In the near future, no one is allowed to set foot outside of the
summer palace,\" Chen Ping\'an said. \"None of you are permitted to see
anyone in private, and if caught doing so, you will be executed on
charges of treason. Messages can only be sent out via flying sword. The
contents of all flying sword messages that are sent out by Chou Miao and
the other new additions to our group must be known to Lin Junbi and the
original twelve swordsmen of the Hidden Official\'s branch, and vice
versa. Furthermore, those contents must be recorded on paper by Sword
Immortal Mi Yu.\"

\"If you don\'t trust us, then why bring us into the Hidden Official\'s
branch?\" Xu Ning asked.

\"Before you speak to me, you must first refer to me as Lord Hidden
Official,\" Chen Ping\'an said.

Xu Ning did as he was told, respectfully referring to Chen Ping\'an as
Lord Hidden Official before repeating his question.

Only then did Chen Ping\'an reply with a smile, \"How can you expect me
to trust any of you when I don\'t even trust myself?\"

Xu Ning fell silent, while Luo Zhenyi and Chang Taiqing both turned to
Chen Ping\'an with angry expressions.

Xuan Can and Cao Gun held Chen Ping\'an in very high regard in their
hearts, and they glowered directly at the three swordsmen with hostile
expressions, making no effort to hide their allegiances.

\"Focus on your duties, do as you\'re told, and speak as little as
possible,\" Chou Miao said. \"The four of us have been chosen to join
the Hidden Official\'s branch, so we are obligated to follow the Hidden
Official\'s instructions.\"

Chen Ping\'an turned to him with a smile and said, \"If I die, Sword
Immortal Chou Miao and Junbi are the best candidates to take my place as
Hidden Official.\"

Lin Junbi pretended not to have heard him, as did Chou Miao.

In the darkness of the night, a messenger flying sword was sent to the
top of the city walls. Shortly thereafter, a heartbroken little girl
flew slowly to the summer palace atop her flying sword, weeping
inconsolably the entire way.

However, after arriving at the summer palace and seeing her resurrected
master, a jubilant smile immediately broke through her tears.

She was so ecstatic that she began jumping up and down on the spot in
front of Chen Ping\'an, her arms and eyebrows raised in celebration as
she proudly declared, \"I was the only one out of everyone who was
convinced that you weren\'t dead, Master! I just wasn\'t expecting you
to have already come here. This is why you\'re the master, and I\'m the
disciple; I clearly still have much to learn!\"

\"I already told you that as long as I\'m around, none of you have to
think about matters related to life and death, and that promise still
stands,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a smile as he pulled a little bamboo
bookcase out of his minimization treasure. \"This is for you. If you
don\'t think it\'s too much of a burden, you can carry it on your back,
but you\'re not allowed to show it off to anyone.\"

Guo Zhujiu immediately put the little bamboo bookcase on her back and
exclaimed, \"This little bamboo bookcase must\'ve grown legs and come
running to you, Master! The little bamboo bookcase that my senior sister
gave me must\'ve turned into a spirit and come to you. Next time, you
can make an ordinary bookcase that hasn\'t grown legs and give it to my
senior sister, and I\'ll keep this one.\"

\"You can work that out with Pei Qian yourself the next time you see
her.\" Chen Ping\'an chuckled with a shake of his head. \"Rest assured,
I won\'t play favorites.\"

He then patted Guo Zhujiu on the head and urged, \"Get to work now. We
can\'t afford to slack off in our duties.\"

Guo Zhujiu skipped her way up the steps, then jumped up into the air and
turned around so that her back was facing everyone. She stood like that
for a moment, then turned back around and entered the main hall.

Instead of following her inside, Chen Ping\'an continued to stroll
through the summer palace, and everywhere he went, he was inside his own
small world.

He pulled out an azure talisman, then began speaking into it. \"I
wouldn\'t make you deliver the bamboo bookcase to me for nothing, old
great sword immortal. If there are any sword immortals who try to snoop
around the summer palace while we\'re here, then kill them. Those who
are willing to take such risks are far too impatient, and they have no
further value to our Sword Qi Great Wall. If there really are any sword
immortals who come here to throw their lives away, then mark the
contributions of killing them under Sword Immortal Mi Yu\'s name.\"

Even though Chen Ping\'an was speaking inside his own small world, Chen
Qingdu was able to hear him as clear as day.

He didn\'t agree to or refuse Chen Ping\'an\'s request, but his
intentions were already conveyed through his silence. He had chosen Chen
Ping\'an to be the new Hidden Official, and he would allow Chen Ping\'an
to do as he pleased.

\"Let me ask you this one more time: have you really made up your
mind?\" the old great sword immortal asked, changing the subject. \"Will
you really not regret it if it turns out to be you? You\'re not going to
explain things to Ning Yao in advance?\"

\"How is my senior brother doing?\" Chen Ping\'an asked, also choosing
to change the subject.

Chen Qingdu told him that Zuo You was doing fine.

Chen Ping\'an tucked the azure talisman up his sleeve, then pulled out a
new talisman before chanting an incantation, and in the blink of an eye,
he had already arrived in the winter palace.

Chen Ping\'an walked alone in the otherwise deserted winter palace.

The interiors of both palaces were very simple and unadorned, and there
were almost no extra pieces of decor at all.

Chen Ping\'an wanted to familiarize himself with the environment here.

Prior to leaving the winter palace to return to the summer palace, he
murmured to himself, \"I\'ve made up my mind. I\'ll do it.\"

[]{#chapter-143.xhtml}

# Chapter 631: (1): The Light Breeze and the Shimmering Moonlight

Sword of Coming

In the past, there was only one gate on Stalactite Mountain that led to
the Sword Qi Great Wall. Since then, a new, larger gate had been opened,
and as a result, the old gate sat relatively abandoned compared with its
heyday.

The little Daoist priest was still sitting and reading as he usually
did. This time, he was doing some light reading in the form of a book
written by a disillusioned scholar. He casually grabbed a handful of
moonlight, then kept it beside himself and the book, using its radiance
to illuminate the pages.

Last time, he had been thrown for a complete loop by Cui Dongshan, who
had managed to convince him that a completely innocent and vanilla
romance story was a raunchy tale of scandalous taboos.

He was so disgusted by that experience that he had struggled to mentally
recover for quite a few days, unable to work up any interest in any book
during that time. Thus, he had no choice but to abandon that hobby, one
of very few that he had, and he could only sit in a daze, staring off
into space all day.

However, after refraining from reading for about a month, he was feeling
incredibly bored, and after picking up the hobby again, he completely
indulged himself by fetching a large stack of books and reading through
them day and night in a near-obsessive fashion.

Even though he was an immortal with an eidetic memory, he read very
slowly and meticulously, often rereading certain parts that caught his
interest.

The other gatekeeper, the sword-hugging middle-aged man, snuck over to
the little Daoist priest. However, it then occurred to him that this
counted as malfeasance, so he rushed back to his post and set his
longsword down on top of the pillar, then returned to the little Daoist
priest\'s side with a flagon of wine to read the same book that he was
reading.

The sword-hugging man reeked of alcohol, and the little Daoist priest
turned away slightly in disdain, but the sword-hugging man quickly
followed, leaving the little Daoist priest to heave a resigned sigh. He
knew the kinds of lengths that a bored swordsman would be willing to go
to in order to assuage their boredom, so he could only let his neighbor
be.

The man pointed at a certain passage of the book and began offering his
commentary. The little Daoist priest was already accustomed to his
constant droning, so he ignored the man and flipped the page.

The man didn\'t mind, continuing to offer his insights on the previous
passage even though the page had already been turned.

After reading through the entire book, the man sighed in a disappointed
manner. \"That was way too boring! There weren\'t any raunchy scenes at
all!\"

The little Daoist priest set down the book in his hand and picked up
another one, this one a riveting wuxia story that instantly had the man
hooked.

At a particularly exciting part of the story, he began taking swigs of
wine while staring intently at the pages, latching onto every word as he
mused, \"As expected of the protagonist chosen by the heavens! The
cultivation arts that he can master in just a single night are too
complex for other martial arts prodigies to master even in an entire
lifetime! Man, I really envy him. It\'s a real shame that the mantra for
the cultivation art isn\'t fully laid out in the story. Otherwise, I
could give it a try as well\...\"

\"You see that? It\'s exactly as I predicted! The unkempt,
deranged-looking old men in these stories always turn out to actually be
unfathomable masters! I knew he would take a liking to the protagonist!
The old geezer sacrificed sixty years\' worth of cultivation base to
open up his conception and governor vessels and completely cleanse his
body of all impurities. Once he returns to the martial arts world,
he\'ll be completely invincible!\"

\"I wouldn\'t say he\'s invincible just yet,\" the little Daoist priest
disagreed, seeing as they were only halfway through the book. \"Even
though he\'s just received sixty years' worth of internal energy, he\'s
only been cultivating for twenty years himself, so that only amounts to
eighty years\' worth of internal energy in total.

"It\'s already been mentioned that the scourge who\'s wreaking havoc in
the martial arts world has over a hundred years of internal energy under
his belt, so the protagonist is still no match for him for now.\"

The man stroked his chin and nodded in agreement as he mused, \"He\'s
still missing a good weapon, but that\'s probably not going to come
anytime soon, given that we\'re only halfway through the story.\"

\"There\'s no hurry,\" the little Daoist priest said as he flipped over
the page. \"If everything comes to him too quickly and easily, the
payoff won\'t be as satisfying.\"

The author of this book was only using his writing talents to pay the
bills, and he would most likely never imagine that his work would be
read by a pair of unfathomable immortals even mightier than those in his
story.

One of them was a sword immortal of the Sword Qi Great Wall, someone who
had taken part in the thirteen battles against the demon tribe. He had
befriended countless heroic figures and even had a female sword immortal
for a soul mate.

However, even someone of his lofty status paled in comparison with the
little Daoist priest, who had left the Heavenly World to come to the
Sword Qi Great Wall to hone his Dao Heart.

The sword-hugging man was a prisoner among prisoners, forced to remain
here as gatekeeper year after year.

All of a sudden, the little Daoist priest closed the book, and the
sword-hugging man was immediately up in arms. \"What\'re you doing?\"

\"This is a nice book, so I\'m going to pace myself and not read it all
at once,\" the little Daoist priest explained.

The sword-hugging man groaned in dismay as he lay down on his back, then
casually asked, \"What kind of place is the Heavenly World?\"

\"It\'s a place with many customs and rules, quite similar to the
Majestic World,\" the little Daoist priest replied just as casually.

\"Has the Daoist second disciple still not found the five hundred Daoist
enforcers?\" the man asked.

The little Daoist priest didn\'t feel like this was a secret that had to
be closely guarded, so he replied, \"He\'s probably still quite a long
way off. It\'s not an easy task.\"

\"It sounds like everyone\'s really busy,\" the man mused as he rested
the back of his head down onto his folded hands as a makeshift pillow.

\"You and I are the only ones who *aren\'t* busy,\" the little Daoist
priest remarked with a smile.

There was a popular saying on the Sword Qi Great Wall that had been left
behind by A\'Liang, proclaiming that those who didn\'t cultivate through
the night would never attain the Great Dao. As for how one was to
cultivate through the night, working hard on Qi refinement and sword
refinement was the worst way to go about it. The slightly better way to
do it was to drink.

Even if one drank until their coffers were empty, and they no longer had
money for wine, they could collect moonlight in their cup free of
charge, so their cup would never run empty. As for the best way to
cultivate through the night, all of the men on the Sword Qi Great Wall
knew how, but they would merely respond with a sly grin when asked.

\"I disagree,\" the man said as he looked up at the bright moon in the
night sky. \"We\'re working day and night here, are we not?\"

The little Daoist priest turned to the man with a puzzled expression,
then asked, \"You do know you can easily find yourself something to do,
right? Given how dire the situation is on the Sword Qi Great Wall, if
you insist on returning to battle, I\'m sure Chen Qingdu isn\'t going to
stop you.\"

\"I\'m tired,\" the man replied, then closed his eyes to rest.

\"With that mentality, I doubt you\'re ever going to make any further
progress in your cultivation,\" the little Daoist priest chuckled.

\"If that\'s the case, then so be it,\" Zhang Lu casually replied.

The little Daoist priest reached out to scatter the handful of moonlight
that he had been using as a lamp, then looked up into the sky and mused,
\"Only those in a state of serenity can see the world for what it truly
is.\"

\"Did your master teach you that?\"

\"No, I read it from some random book.\"

\"I\'ve been thinking about something, Jiang Yunsheng. There are many
stories told of heroic figures who rise up to fight in the face of
injustice, throwing caution to the wind and disregarding even their own
survival. Do you think that\'s a good thing?\"

\"I don\'t know, and I can\'t be bothered to think about it.\"

\"All unions are eventually going to end in separation. I\'m going to
miss you when you\'re gone. If I get the chance, I\'ll go visit you in
your hometown.\"

\"Why\'re you getting all sappy on me all of a sudden? How do you not
feel embarrassed as a grown man saying something like that to another
grown man?\"

\"You\'re a grown man? But you look like a child. Surely you can\'t be
that old.\"

\"Are you asking for a beating, Zhang Lu?!\"

The man turned over and promptly fell asleep.

On any of the Majestic World\'s nine continents, there was no way that a
sword immortal of this caliber would\'ve been reduced to such a pitiful
position.

The little Daoist priest continued reading, feeling a little sorry for
Sword Immortal Shao Yunyan.

\*\*\*

Doing business and earning money was an all-day affair that didn\'t stop
for day or night.

All immortal coins were said to be formed by the purest spiritual energy
under the heavens, but was there actually even a single clean immortal
coin under the heavens? That was difficult to say.

A giant ship unloaded its cargo in exchange for a bunch of resources
from the Sword Qi Great Wall\'s alchemical pill market, then promptly
departed from Stalactite Mountain.

This particular intercontinental ship belonged to the Mountain and Water
Cave, a prominent sect of the Circling Ascension Continent, and it had a
rather unimpressive name of Clay Pot.

It was said that the founding father of the Mountain and Water Cave came
from very humble beginnings, but after climbing up the social ladder, he
spent his entire life distancing himself from those humble beginnings,
basking in luxury and excess. It was only in the naming of the
intercontinental ship that had earned him so much of his wealth that he
displayed his original roots.

A Nascent Tier administrator was standing on the ship\'s top-floor
observation deck, doing some mental calculations. According to his
calculations, they would be able to make at least seventy grain rain
coins from this trip to Stalactite Mountain.

At the moment, several of the most powerful mortal empires of the
Circling Ascension Continent were at war with one another, and if they
could take full advantage of the chaos and find the right buyers, then
that sum could even be doubled.

Things weren\'t peaceful in the cultivation world, either. Out of the
priceless treasures that were born from the will of the world, as many
as three of them were pseudo-celestial tools, and countless cultivators
had been fighting over them.

At this point, many earth immortals had already perished in the
bloodbath, and there were even quite a few immortals of the Upper Five
Tiers who were gradually beginning to rise to the surface. If it
weren\'t for their fear of repercussions from the Confucian academy,
they would\'ve already gotten personally involved, rather than settling
for pulling strings behind the scenes.

For powerful business sects like the Mountain and Water Cave, all of the
conflicts taking place in the mortal world and the cultivation world
were fantastic news.

The Jade Forest Sect\'s immense wealth came from the fact that the
Northern Complete Reed Continent was rife with swordsmen. As a result,
the rate of sect turnover in the cultivation world was extremely high,
and all of that unrest presented opportunities for money to be made.

As for the Liu Clan of the Pure White Continent, they were a rather
unique case. They could do deals with anyone, and many of the
transactions that they dealt with went beyond the scope of money.
Instead, they often paid money and received compensation in the form of
things that money couldn\'t buy.

What was most remarkable of all about the Liu Clan was that one of its
primary business doctrines was to ensure that everyone they were doing
business with could make money, and what was even more remarkable was
that they had truly managed to accomplish this. Over time, this had
become one of the clan\'s foundational rules, one that was passed down
from generation to generation.

The old Nascent Tier cultivator had reaped some fine spoils on this trip
to Stalactite Mountain. With the approval of the patriarch of the
Mountain and Water Cave, he had met up with quite a few fellow
businessmen from the Circling Ascension Continent and Golden Armor
Continent in one of the finest rooms in the Ganoderma Inn to discuss a
collaborative money-making endeavor.

In total, they would have eight intercontinental ships at their
disposal, and if they could work together as a united front, then the
Yan Clan and the Nalan Clan of the Sword Qi Great Wall wouldn\'t have
the option of getting better prices elsewhere.

They agreed to meet up at an intermediary ferry station that wasn\'t far
away from Stalactite Mountain, where they would distribute all their
goods among one another, with each ship solely focusing on selling just
a few types of goods. From there, they would make their way to
Stalactite Mountain to barter with the Sword Qi Great Wall.

That was only the first order of business, and it was met with almost no
objections. Everything had gone so smoothly because the Mountain and
Water Cave insisted on making it work, and they promised that if
everyone earned money from this arrangement, then it would be confirmed
as a feasible option going forward, and they would continue to
collaborate in this fashion in the future.

However, if anyone made any losses from this arrangement, then the
Mountain and Water Cave would cover their losses.

The second order of business pertained to the huge amount of supplies
that the Sword Qi Great Wall required to support its war efforts against
the Savage World. In light of this increased demand, the Mountain and
Water Cave proposed that everyone pool together their resources to
construct a few new intercontinental ships. They also paid for the
patriarchs of the other sects to help establish one or two new smoother
trade routes and kill off all of the roadblocks on the route.

On top of that, those patriarchs were to preside over the ships to
ensure that the journeys went smoothly. In the past, there wasn\'t
enough money on offer, but things were different now. Even if the
patriarchs themselves weren\'t swayed by the compensation being offered,
all of them had sects, direct disciples, and relatives, and with some
convincing from the respective sect leaders, they all agreed to play a
part.

The third thing was a little troublesome. Both Yan Ming and Nalan
Caihuan had gone to the top of the city walls, and they had temporarily
left their juniors to attend to their clans\' affairs. Those juniors
were nowhere near as shrewd and capable as Yan Ming and Nalan Caihuan,
but they were a huge pain to deal with because they refused to negotiate
at all on price, and they stuck to the rules without any room for
compromise.

If an agreement couldn\'t be reached, then they would simply bide their
time and wait. Everyone knew that the Sword Qi Great Wall couldn\'t
afford to wait for long, and that they would inevitably be the first to
fold, but each additional day that the intercontinental ships stayed on
Stalactite Mountain was very costly, so the Mountain and Water Cave and
the other intercontinental ships were all eager to break the stalemate.

There had been past instances in which the intercontinental ships had
gone a little overboard with their bartering during times of war on the
Sword Qi Great Wall, and as a result, they had been told by the Nalan
Clan to either lower their prices or piss off.

The pressure had been mounting with each passing day, and right as the
administrators on the intercontinental ships were planning to make a
compromise, things suddenly took an unexpected turn. A relatively
unknown young man on the Circling Ascension Continent\'s
intercontinental ship was somehow able to convince the administrators on
all of the ships to maintain a unified front, even if it meant risking
going back empty-handed.

All of the intercontinental ships left Stalactite Mountain overnight to
dock at the Rain Dragon Sect\'s subsidiary islands, and they told the
Sword Qi Great Wall that they were simply going to give up on this
money-making opportunity.

The young man was ultimately able to help all of the intercontinental
ships make huge profits, and as it turned out, he was none other than
the founding father of the Mountain and Water Cave.

At the time, he had only been a Sea Observation Tier cultivator, yet
even back then, he was able to convince all of the sly old foxes on the
intercontinental ships to go along with his plan. No more than thirty
years after that, he had founded his own sect and had his own
intercontinental ships.

[]{#chapter-144.xhtml}

# Chapter 631: (2): The Light Breeze and the Shimmering Moonlight

Sword of Coming

After the event, the Nalan Clan had tried to target the two
intercontinental ships from the Mountain and Water Cave in retaliation,
but the Mountain and Water Cave was able to easily deal with those
attempts at retaliation. Over time, the Nalan Clan had no choice but to
swallow the bitter pill and continue doing business as usual.

Then came the rise of the Yan Clan, and the clan leader, Yan Ming, was
easier to work with, certainly not as bullheaded and unyielding as the
Nalan Clan when it came to doing business. Many swordsmen had fiery
tempers, yet compared with them, Yan Ming was more like a true
businessman.

He performed his duties with diligence, doing his best to secure the
best deals for the Sword Qi Great Wall while also trying to provide
money-making opportunities for all of the intercontinental ships as
well. Clearly, he was a big believer in facilitating a mutually
beneficial relationship.

After Nalan Caihuan took over the Nalan Clan\'s business affairs, she
had also developed a decent relationship with the people on the
intercontinental ships. As for Yan Ming and Nalan Caihuan, the two of
them didn\'t really see eye to eye, but they weren\'t constantly at each
other\'s throats, either.

For the most part, they tried to stay out of each other\'s way, but in
private, there would occasionally be some conflicts of interest between
the two.

A direct disciple of the Nascent Tier administrator arrived on the
observation deck, seemingly to report something, but he appeared rather
hesitant.

\"If you have something to say, then go ahead and say it,\" the old
Nascent Tier cultivator prompted with a smile.

\"Master, in the past, we\'ve always allowed the Sword Qi Great Wall to
purchase goods from us on credit, and they would always repay us in both
principle and interest once their battles against the Savage World are
over, and the amount of interest they have to pay depends on how long
payment has been delayed by, so why is it that this time, our patriarch
wants us to join forces with everyone else to refuse the Sword Qi Great
Wall the option of buying on credit?\" the young man asked.

\"The Sword Qi Great Wall is currently keeping a very tight lid on
things. No one is permitted to approach the city walls, even a regular
visitor like me,\" the old man said. \"In the past, I\'ve always been
able to find a place to stay in a sword immortal\'s residence for a few
days, but this time, I wasn\'t even granted entry into the city. In the
end, I had to discuss business with the people from those two clans in a
residence between the city and the Mirage Market.

"However, the more secretive they are, the more telling it actually is.
Clearly, the Savage World is launching a very fierce assault right now,
and it\'s going to be an almighty struggle to keep them at bay. How much
wealth do you think the Yan Clan and the Nalan Clan possess?\"

\"It must be a lot,\" the young man replied. \"Both Yan Ming and Nalan
Caihuan are very shrewd and capable when it comes to doing business, so
I\'m sure they\'ve accumulated a great deal of wealth for both their own
clans and for the Sword Qi Great Wall.\"

The old man nodded with a smile and said, \"The more wealth they
possess, the more we stand to gain. Not only do we have to take
everything from the Yan Clan and the Nalan Clan, but we also have to do
the same to the alchemical pill market as well.

"As for the rule against purchases on credit that we\'re going to
impose, that\'s something that we\'re naturally going to be taken
seriously, but at the same time, it can be something that\'s also not
taken seriously. If Yan Ming and Nalan Caihuan want us to not take the
rule seriously, then they\'ll have to show us some sincerity.\"

\"Is it really a good idea to be pushing them like this? I heard that
all sword immortals have rather foul tempers,\" the young man said in an
uneasy voice.

\"So what?\" the old man sneered. \"The patriarch of the Nalan Clan,
Nalan Shaowei, is one of the ten most powerful sword immortals of the
Sword Qi Great Wall. On our Circling Ascension Continent, no one would
dare to even breathe in his direction! His temper is extremely foul, but
what can he do to us?

"Sure, he can kill all of us with ease, but would he dare to do that? At
the end of the day, money is the most powerful thing under the heavens,
superior to even the hardest of fists and the sharpest of swords.\"

What the young man truly wanted to ask was why they couldn\'t just earn
a little less? Instead, why did they have to try and extort the Sword Qi
Great Wall for everything they had every single time?

The old man seemed to have read his thoughts, and he chuckled. \"Your
cultivation aptitude is decent, but your incompetence when it comes to
doing business is astounding! If you can earn more money, then why
settle for less? How is someone who is always willing to settle for less
ever going to make any big money? With that kind of mindset, you\'re
never going to become someone like our patriarch.

"For now, just mind your business and focus on yourself. Only when you
become a more important figure in the Mountain and Water Cave than me
will you have the right to talk about earning less money, but I\'m
absolutely certain that if you really can reach such heights someday,
then you\'ll be even more eager to earn money than me. When you look
back on your current mindset, you\'re going to find yourself completely
laughable!\"

\*\*\*

On this day, the youngest Golden Core Tier earth immortal in the history
of the Rain Dragon Sect, Fu Ke, left the ancestral mountain on the
island where the Rain Dragon Sect was situated and traveled to a
subsidiary island to meet a friend.

The Rain Dragon Sect didn\'t have an intercontinental ship because it
didn\'t need one. The sect had over twenty subsidiary islands, all of
which had docks, and in total, there were tens of thousands of people,
consisting of disciples and servants of the sects under the Rain Dragon
Sect.

The vast majority of the intercontinental ships from the Northern
Complete Reed Continent, as well as some from the Southern Whirl
Continent, had to stop here mid-journey.

Fu Ke was traveling alone on a talismanic boat, and his destination was
Green Jade Island, an island home to some extremely precious immortal
trees that had a jade-like material, which many of the intercontinental
ships that docked at the island purchased at high prices.

The intercontinental ships had all made massive profits on Stalactite
Mountain, so they could afford to make these purchases, and they would
be able to sell the material for additional profits once they returned
home anyway.

Green Jade Island was situated to the northeast of the Rain Dragon Sect,
so in the past, the inhabitants of the island would often be able to see
the old rainbringer dragons traversing back and forth between the Flood
Dragon Trench and the Southern Whirl Continent. If they were lucky, they
would even spot some exhausted dragons plunging into the sea.

Due to its close proximity to the Flood Dragon Trench, the Rain Dragon
Sect had always treated these rainbringer dragons with kindness and
benevolence. If they encountered any exhausted flood dragons that
floated up to the surface of the sea, unable to return to their lairs,
then they would even send powerful cultivators to help manipulate the
current to carry the flood dragons to the Flood Dragon Trench.

However, this had become a very rare occurrence in recent years because
an extremely mighty sword immortal with a terrible temper had laid waste
to the majority of the Flood Dragon Trench, seemingly just to enhance
his own reputation.

He was collectively denounced by the old people on Green Jade Island as
a sword immortal who possessed immense power, but none of the morality
and sense of responsibility to match. Fu Ke actually knew enough about
this incident to speak out against the criticisms aimed at the sword
immortal, but he saw no reason to do so.

Fu Ke\'s talismanic boat didn\'t land directly outside his friend\'s
private residence. Instead, he followed the rules and docked his
talismanic boat on the shore at the entrance of the island, then
proceeded from there on foot.

Along the way, he extended greetings to some of the people that he
encountered, and everyone who was able to speak to him, even if it was
just to exchange some meaningless small talk, felt extremely honored.

Fu Ke\'s friend was a cultivator of the Lower Five Tiers by the name of
Yu Fujing, and he was a complete nobody on the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent. The two of them had been friends for a very long time, and
originally, they had come from similar backgrounds with similar
cultivation bases.

However, their paths in life completely diverged when Fu Ke, a man who
was completely down on his luck at the time, decided to go and see
Stalactite Mountain just to tick it off his bucket list. Ultimately, he
didn\'t reach his destination, but he encountered a massive fated
opportunity along the way in the Rain Dragon Sect. It had truly been a
life-changing turn of events, and he was certainly no longer down on his
luck.

News of Fu Ke\'s meteoric rise quickly spread to the Eastern Treasured
Vial Continent thanks to word of mouth from the passengers traveling
aboard the Osmanthus Island intercontinental ship, and Fu Ke instantly
became an admired figure among vagrant cultivators and someone to be
envied even by official immortals.

After hearing the news, Yu Fujing decided to come and try his luck.
Initially, he was only hoping that Fu Ke would spare him some money for
old time\'s sake. If he could get even just a few lesser heat coins out
of Fu Ke, then he would\'ve been completely satisfied. However, to his
surprise, Fu Ke had proven himself to be a truly good friend, inviting
Yu Fujing to meet him in the Rain Dragon Sect.

At the time, Yu Fujing had been so timid and tentative that he didn\'t
even dare to set foot on the island. Instead, he merely stated his name
and declared that he was an acquaintance of Fu Ke\'s, too ashamed to
even claim to be Fu Ke\'s friend.

Fu Ke immediately left the Rain Dragon Sect to meet his good friend, but
the rules of the sect prevented him from bringing Yu Fujing onto the
island, so he arranged for Yu Fujing to stay on the nearby Green Jade
Island. He told Yu Fujing that he could stay on the island for as long
as he liked, and that he didn\'t have to be in a hurry to return to the
Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.

After Fu Ke\'s departure, Yu Fujing felt very grateful, but also a
little disappointed, because Fu Ke hadn\'t told him anything. To his
surprise, just a day later, the disciplinary elder of the Green Jade
Island\'s ancestral hall paid him a personal visit, asking him if he
would be willing to become an internal sect disciple of Green Jade
Island. An internal sect disciple of the island was inferior in status
to a direct disciple of the ancestral hall, but Yu Fujing was still so
grateful for the offer that he almost burst into tears.

Even though Green Jade Island was only a subsidiary island to the Rain
Dragon Sect, it had a Nascent Tier earth immortal at the helm! Back home
on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, Yu Fujing wouldn\'t even have
dared to imagine that he would someday become an internal sect disciple
of an immortal power with a Nascent Tier patriarch.

The disciplinary elder was a Golden Core Tier earth immortal, and never
in Yu Fujing\'s wildest dreams would he have imagined that a vagrant
Lower Five Tiers cultivator like himself would be spoken to so amicably
by a Golden Core Tier earth immortal.

After that, Yu Fujing began cultivating on Green Jade Island as an
official immortal. He was given far superior cultivation arts compared
with what he had been using in the past, but his cultivation aptitude
was very mediocre, so progress came very slowly.

Even the Abode Tier, which was regarded as an easily reachable target
for the vast majority of cultivators on Green Jade Island, was likely a
mark that he would never be able to reach. However, that didn\'t seem to
matter, and the cultivators of the ancestral hall still treated him with
a great deal of respect.

On this occasion, Fu Ke had arrived on Green Jade Island to visit Yu
Fujing, and after hearing the news, Yu Fujing immediately charged out of
his room.

It wasn\'t like there was much point in cultivation for him. Unless he
was blessed with additional fated opportunities, or someone was willing
to invest huge sums of immortal coins into his cultivation, he was never
going to be able to make anything out of himself anyway.

Upon reaching the entrance, Yu Fujing suddenly stopped in his tracks,
and only after stalling for quite some time did he finally open the
door. After a brief wait, he spotted Fu Ke, who was bidding farewell to
the Nascent Tier patriarch of Green Jade Island.

Yu Fujing hurriedly sped up in his footsteps, hoping to be able to get a
word in with the Nascent Tier immortal, and the latter really did stop
in his tracks.

Yu Fujing strode forward and laid a firm hand down onto Fu Ke\'s
shoulder, jokingly denouncing him as a disloyal friend who shunned his
brothers in preference for his wives. Fu Ke merely smiled and took the
jab in silence.

Yu Fujing turned to extend a respectful salute toward the old Nascent
Tier patriarch, and the latter gave him some smiling words of
encouragement, telling him to work hard in his cultivation and that he
had a bright future ahead.

It was the type of generic stuff that seniors said to the juniors just
for something to say, but Yu Fujing still made sure to listen with an
earnest expression. Following the old Nascent Tier immortal\'s
departure, Yu Fujing dragged Fu Ke into his private residence. It
wasn\'t very large, but it was still a private residence, nevertheless.

There was a very strict hierarchy system on Green Jade Island, and aside
from the brightest young prodigies of the ancestral hall, Yu Fujing was
the only Lower Five Tiers cultivator on the island to have a private
residence.

Fu Ke pulled out three flagons of immortal wine brewed by the Rain
Dragon Sect from his minimization treasure, and the two friends had one
flagon of wine each. As for the remaining flagon, Fu Ke told Yu Fujing
that his master was an avid drinker, so he could give that flagon of
wine to his master as a gift.

\"I take back what I said earlier; you\'re a great friend!\" Yu Fujing
chuckled as he gave Fu Ke a thumbs-up.

\"I have plenty of wine for you to drink, but make sure you don\'t get
drunk,\" Fu Ke said with a smile. \"This stuff may taste innocuous, but
it really hits you when you least expect it. If you like this wine,
I\'ll have people deliver it to you on Green Jade Island even if I
don\'t come here myself.\"

\"You\'re a real big shot now, aren\'t you?\" Yu Fujing jibed. \"Now
that you\'ve become an earth immortal, you don\'t even want to come and
see me anymore, is that it?\"

\"What kind of nonsense are you spouting now?\" Fu Ke sighed in an
exasperated manner. \"I\'ve encountered a minor bottleneck, so I need to
go into seclusion for a while. Otherwise, I would definitely come to see
you myself.\"

Yu Fujing took a sip of wine, and he rested one foot on a chair as he
cast his gaze out the window and sighed. \"Never did I imagine that I
would be sitting here with you, drinking this expensive immortal wine.\"

\"Fate is always a fickle and unpredictable mistress,\" Fu Ke said with
a smile.

Yu Fujing was drinking quite quickly, despite Fu Ke\'s attempts to get
him to slow down.

Initially, Yu Fujing harbored nothing but gratitude toward Fu Ke, but as
Fu Ke ascended higher and higher, molding a perfect image around
himself, Yu Fujing gradually began to develop some nefarious ideas.

Fu Ke had abandoned his past wife, pretending that she never existed,
and now, he had it all. He had two stunningly beautiful new wives, and
he had become a direct disciple of the Rain Dragon Sect\'s ancestral
hall. In the wake of his meteoric rise, it seemed that he had forgotten
all about his past life.

Of course, Yu Fujing wasn\'t threatening Fu Ke, and he certainly
wouldn\'t dare to do so, given that Fu Ke was both his friend and an
earth immortal.

Thus, as they were drinking together, Yu Fujing brought up this matter
in passing while reminiscing about past events, making it seem like he
had merely inadvertently brought up the subject as part of his
reminiscence.

Fu Ke set his flagon down onto the table.

Yu Fujing immediately slapped himself across the face. \"I really need
to keep a lid on this loose mouth of mine! I didn\'t mean anything by
that, Fu Ke; I promise I won\'t tell anyone about your past.\"

Fu Ke merely smiled in response, and mere moments later, Yu Fujing was
dead.

[]{#chapter-145.xhtml}

# Chapter 631: (3): The Light Breeze and the Shimmering Moonlight

Sword of Coming

Fu Ke picked up his flagon of wine, then continued drinking alone as he
cast his gaze out the door and murmured to himself, \"You came to me to
see if you could change your fate, and I reciprocated. I left the Rain
Dragon Sect to meet you, and I gave you an opportunity of a lifetime. If
you had remained grateful instead of taking everything that I gave you
for granted, perhaps I would\'ve even made you my right-hand man.

"Your cultivation base and aptitude aren\'t anything special, but
you\'ve always been a smart man. Unfortunately, you\'ve decided to
squander this opportunity, so you can\'t blame me for silencing you.
You\'re only a cultivator of the Lower Five Tiers, and you\'ve never
witnessed the scenery on the mountain summit, yet I have.

"It\'s a beautiful place, but you must also constantly tread with
caution because a fall from the mountain summit will shatter you into a
million pieces. I can tell that you were initially grateful to me, but
you\'ve since shown yourself to be an envious and insatiable wolf that I
can never satisfy.

"If I keep you by my side, I\'m eventually going to regret it, so I may
as well put an end to things here and now. You know, there was another
reason why I decided to keep you by my side. Every time I saw you, it
served as a warning of sorts to me. Seeing you reminded me of how low
and wretched I once was, and it served as a warning for me to never grow
complacent or take anything for granted.

"You really think it\'s a big deal if you die? I can simply leave this
place without doing anything or offering any explanation, and the
entirety of Green Jade Island will pretend like you never existed. Well,
I suppose that\'s not true. Even though you\'re dead, they\'ll still be
grateful to you for establishing a connection between Green Jade Island
and me.

"You could\'ve easily lived a cozy life here, with the entire island
treating you like an esteemed guest. That\'s what a smart person
would\'ve done. In the end, you were too short-sighted, and it\'s led to
your demise.\"

Fu Ke rose to his feet, then turned to take a glance at the lifeless Yu
Fujing as he concluded, \"I told you not to get drunk or you may say
something that you\'ll regret, but you didn\'t listen.\"

With that, he really did simply depart from Green Jade Island without
any explanation, returning to the Rain Dragon Sect on his talismanic
boat.

As he lay on the talismanic boat with his eyes closed, he began to think
about his future. For now, his priority was to reach the Nascent Tier,
and from there, he would ascend to the Upper Five Tiers and become
leader of the Rain Dragon Sect.

He would then lay claim to the Water Essence Palace on Stalactite
Mountain, following which he would return to the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent to visit all of the celestial maidens that he had once
regarded as goddesses who were completely out of his reach.

He would take a few of them as his maidservants, such as Su Jia of Sun
Scorch Mountain\... Actually, no, she had already fallen from grace,
reduced from a phoenix soaring in the heavens to an earthbound chicken
with its wings clipped and its legs broken. She could be the most
beautiful woman in the world, but it still wouldn\'t change the fact
that she was damaged goods that weren\'t worth touching.

Fu Ke raised a hand up high, then gently clenched it into a fist as he
smiled and murmured to himself, \"I wonder if I\'ll have the chance to
claim a few of the female sword immortals on the Sword Qi Great Wall for
myself. I hear that Luo Jian and Situ Weiran are both quite young and
beautiful, and they\'re also top-tier prodigies to boot. Maybe I\'ll
have a chance to swoop in and take them once the Sword Qi Great Wall
falls.\"

Even if the Sword Qi Great Wall were to fall, the Confucian sages would
be the ones to clean up the mess, so Fu Ke and the Rain Dragon Sect had
nothing to worry about, and there was no guarantee that the Sword Qi
Great Wall would fall anyway.

Fu Ke couldn\'t help but find the swordsmen of the Sword Qi Great Wall
rather amusing. The Qi refiners of the Majestic World were all scared of
death, yet the swordsmen of the Sword Qi Great Wall seemed to all
embrace death and be terrified of living.

*It\'s a real shame that those imbeciles of the Savage World are so
useless,* he thought to himself.

\*\*\*

Reed Flower Island was a neighbor of the Rain Dragon Sect, yet it
hadn\'t become a subsidiary island to the sect, and that hinted at the
notion that there was something special about the island.

Over the past thousand years, that sword immortal was the only one who
had managed to come out on top against the Rain Dragon Sect. Aside from
him, all other cultivators who passed through the area, including even
the earth immortals and Upper Five Tiers immortals, had all been forced
to submit to the Rain Dragon Sect in one way or another.

The Rain Dragon Sect was situated very far away from the three nearest
continents, so its authority was almost completely unchallenged, and
under many circumstances, the rules of the Rain Dragon Sect had to be
obeyed over even the rules of the Confucian academies.

The reason why Reed Flower Island hadn\'t been forced into submission by
the Rain Dragon Sect even after all this time actually had nothing to do
with the native cultivators on the island. Instead, it had everything to
do with a set of ancient ruins on the island, which had been given the
name of the Creation Cave by some people who had nothing better to do.

It was said that there was an unfathomable Daoist cultivator of unknown
origins in the cave who claimed the entirety of its fortune and didn\'t
allow anyone else to encroach upon his territory. However, even the most
senior cultivators on Reed Flower Island were unable to definitively
corroborate or refute this story, as it was all in the far-too-distant
past.

None of the foreign cultivators who dared to venture into the Creation
Cave had returned, and over time, it simply became ubiquitously
acknowledged as an off-limits area. After all, no matter how precious
fated opportunities were, they would hardly do you any good if you were
dead.

The fact that even the Rain Dragon Sect hadn\'t conquered these ruins
was already very telling, and all of the cultivators of Reed Flower
Island knew that it was in their best interests to leave the place well
alone.

The only relatively close neighbor to Reed Flower Island was the Rain
Dragon Sect\'s southwesternmost subsidiary island, and it was actually
only a distant neighbor to the Rain Dragon Sect.

There were many cultivators on Reed Flower Island, but the island
wasn\'t very wealthy, and the blame for that fell squarely upon the
reclusive Parasol Leaf Continent. The continent was so averse to
interacting with other continents that it wasn\'t willing to construct
even a single intercontinental ship.

While it was true that the route from the Parasol Leaf Continent to
Stalactite Mountain was more perilous than the other routes, such as the
one from Old Dragon City, that was really not a valid excuse. If the
Parasol Leaf Sect and the Jade Tablet Sect were determined to make it
happen, then they could easily establish a trade route between the
Parasol Leaf Continent and Stalactite Mountain.

Unfortunately, even though the Parasol Leaf Continent wasn\'t lacking in
powerful sects, they were also renowned across the entire Majestic World
for their self-sufficiency. For example, the Jade Tablet Sect owned the
Cloud Cave Blessed Land, so the profits to be made from intercontinental
trade really didn\'t appeal to them at all.

In the words of Jiang Shangzhen, \"I can make money even from sneezing
and farting; I don\'t have the spare time to go all the way to
Stalactite Mountain to make money! You can mock me for my meager
cultivation base, but I won\'t allow anyone to insult my money-making
abilities! If anyone dares to do that, then I\'ll crush them under the
weight of my wealth!\"

If the Parasol Leaf Continent had some intercontinental ships, then Reed
Flower Island would be the prime location to house an intermediary ferry
station.

Reed Flower Island was very cut off from the outside world, and they
primarily made money by sending pearl divers out to sea.

Hence, the cultivators on the island really liked to gossip about things
that happened outside of their island. After all, hardly anything
interesting ever happened on the island, and unlike the Rain Dragon
Sect, Reed Flower Island had never produced any noteworthy prodigies.

On this day, a conflict broke out between two groups of young
individuals, all of whom had very mediocre aptitude for cultivation.

They were debating whether a certain prodigious swordsman of the Rain
Dragon Sect would be able to compare with the most exceptional prodigies
of the Sword Qi Great Wall. This so-called prodigy had become a Golden
Core Tier swordsman before turning a hundred.

One camp said there was no comparison between the two, while the other
disagreed.

As their bickering continued, the conversation began to shift, and
before they knew it, they had begun discussing the Sword Qi Great Wall.

Some of them said that the Sword Qi Great Wall was home to countless
heroic figures and had the most sword immortals in any given place. It
was said that one would be able to see sword immortals everywhere they
went, even if they were only taking a stroll out on the street.

They proclaimed that the Sword Qi Great Wall was a sacred place, and
that a cultivator would have wasted their life if they didn\'t go to
visit the Sword Qi Great Wall and drink there at least once.

Ever since the beginning of time, the most effective trick in an
argument had always been to disagree with every assertion that the
opposition made. Thus, the opposing camp immediately began to denounce
all of the swordsmen on the Sword Qi Great Wall as complete idiots.

Their argument was that if the Sword Qi Great Wall wasn\'t full of
fools, then why was it that every single intercontinental ship that went
to Stalactite Mountain was able to profit from them?

There was even a boy who declared that once he was grown up, he would
also go to Stalactite Mountain to make money, and he would do such a
good job of it that the coffers of all of the sword immortals on the
Sword Qi Great Wall would be completely empty by the time he was done.

An old cultivator who just so happened to be passing by scoffed at them
for talking about things that they knew nothing about, and he sternly
ordered them to return to their cultivation.

However, they didn\'t follow his orders. Instead, they insisted on
hearing his opinion on the matter, and whichever camp that he sided with
would be deemed the winner of the argument.

The old man was a renowned storyteller on Reed Flower Island, and he was
very easygoing and approachable, so he got along with everyone.
Sometimes, when he was in a good mood, he would give out wine to others,
even to children who were clearly far too young to be drinking.

The old man was a Golden Core Tier earth immortal, and a chair was
reserved for him in the ancestral hall. He owned a huge, sprawling
private residence on the island, and he had also jointly opened a shop
with a friend on the street at the foot of the Milu Cliff on Stalactite
Mountain.

On top of that, he was very well traveled, having been to many places,
including the Southern Whirl Continent, Old Dragon City on the Eastern
Treasured Vial Continent, and Skeleton Shoal on the Northern Complete
Reed Continent.

He was respected as a very experienced and knowledgeable senior figure
on the island, so whenever the young cultivators had arguments similar
to this one, they were always eager to hear his opinion.

Whenever the old earth immortal got drunk, he would begin telling all
sorts of interesting stories on a wide variety of topics, such as the
local customs and traditions in different places in the Majestic World,
and his stories never failed to inspire a sense of amazement and
wanderlust among the children of Reed Flower Island.

The stories the old man liked to tell most were about Jiang Shangzhen.
He always liked to claim that he had once shared a drink with Jiang
Shangzhen at the same table, but no one believed him.

On this day, the two groups of young individuals refused to let him
leave until he weighed in on their argument, so he could only placate
them by speaking favorably of both the prodigious swordsman of the Rain
Dragon Sect and the prodigies of the Sword Qi Great Wall. Only then was
he finally able to leave.

The old man made his way down the mountain along a wide mountain path
that was lined with thriving, ancient trees. With nothing better to do,
he began to habitually count the steps until he made his way to the
shore of Reed Flower Island.

Looking out at the boundless waves, he felt in a very good mood. The
shop at the foot of the Milu Cliff had been doing quite well over the
past couple of years, earning him many lesser heat coins.

Most importantly, this money felt clean to the old man, and it didn\'t
weigh on his conscience at all. Occasionally, he would feel so grateful
to the Sword Qi Great Wall in the dead of night that he would be struck
by the urge to send them some money, but whenever this absurd thought
surfaced in his mind, he would begin chuckling to himself in
self-deprecation.

*Who do you think you are, Song Sui? Does the Sword Qi Great Wall need
your charity? Do you even know any of the sword immortals there?*

The old man scratched his head, feeling a little forlorn. He had never
been able to make anything out of himself, and he wished that he had
actually drunk at the same table as Jiang Shangzhen as before. If that
were the case, then at the very least, he wouldn\'t feel guilty when he
told that story to the children on the island.

The old man cast his gaze back up the mountain, and he hoped that the
peace would continue to last, and that there would only be minor frets
here and there, but never any major concerns.

A short while later, he made his way back up the mountain, counting the
steps once again as he walked up them in a slow and unhurried fashion.

As he did so, he reminisced about a young boy and a young girl, the
latter with a pair of rosy cheeks. The boy wasn\'t handsome, nor was the
girl all that pretty, but they liked each other. As cultivators, such a
short walk was naturally nowhere near a taxing endeavor, but the girl
frequently stopped to rest, and the boy would sit with her on the steps,
looking out at the moon above the sea together.

The old man stopped in his tracks, then turned to look out at the moon
above the sea, and in doing so, he felt like he could see the girl in
his memories.

All of a sudden, he pressed a hand to his own forehead to steady
himself, and he cast his gaze up the steps with wide eyes. Just now, he
had felt something rather strange for a fleeting moment, but as he
inspected his surroundings, he didn\'t see anything amiss.

The old man was very careful and observant, and even though he hadn\'t
actually shared a drink with Jiang Shangzhen, it was true that he had
traveled across multiple continents and encountered many strange people
and events.

Hence, he knew better than to brush off that strange feeling just now as
a mere figment of his imagination. Thus, he immediately flew onto the
top of an ancient pine tree, but still, he didn\'t see anything amiss,
and the mountain-protection formation was completely undisturbed.

In the end, the old man cast his gaze toward the lone peak that had been
marked as a restricted area on Reed Flower Island. That lone peak was
home to the mysterious Creation Cave.

\"If the old immortal in there really does come out of seclusion, then
that should be a good thing,\" the old man murmured to himself in a
self-deprecating fashion.

The sea was even more vast than the nine continents, and throughout
history, countless immortals had flown out to sea to pick out an
auspicious location, where they would go into seclusion to attempt a
breakthrough. They either succeeded or perished, and everyone else was
none the wiser.

\*\*\*

The Jade Tablet Sect was situated in the southern part of the Parasol
Leaf Continent. The region was filled with mountains covered in lush
greenery, and there was an abundance of spiritual energy, making it a
cultivation paradise.

There was a seemingly endless line of brilliant prodigies coming out of
the Jade Tablet Sect, so it never had to worry about not having enough
young talent to replace its more established cultivators. The only
concern was how they should distribute their cultivation resources among
their many exceptional prodigies to ensure that there was no undue
favoritism on display.

At the very top of the pecking order was naturally none other than the
leader of the sect, Xun Yuan, and below him was the slightly younger
Jiang Shangzhen, followed by the number one prodigy among the younger
generation, Wei Ying.

The other prodigies of the same generation as Jiang Shangzhen and Wei
Ying would be much more renowned in just about any other sect, but
instead, they were all relatively unknown in the Jade Tablet Sect as
they were completely outshone by those two.
