# Chapter 631: (4): The Light Breeze and the Shimmering Moonlight

Sword of Coming

There was a mountain called the Nine Battle Peak that was laden with
palaces and pavilions, and while it wasn\'t a small world, it certainly
seemed like one.

The mountain was constantly taking in spiritual energy from all of the
mountains outside of the Jade Tablet Sect\'s ancestral mountain, as well
as all of the sect\'s rivers, lakes, and creeks. The mountain was very
special because all of the sect leaders throughout the history of the
Jade Tablet Sect had once cultivated on its summit.

The same applied to the current sect leader, Xun Yuan, and it was only
after he became sect leader that he moved out of the mountain.

It was said that back when Jiang Shangzhen reached the Golden Core Tier,
he had thought that the Nine Battle Peak was his for the taking, only
for the rug to be pulled out from under his feet.

He had been so enraged by his unexpected failure to move into the Nine
Battle Peak that he had left the Parasol Leaf Continent to go and wreak
havoc on the Northern Complete Reed Continent, completely ruining the
Jade Tablet Sect\'s reputation on the Northern Complete Reed Continent
in the process.

After Xun Yuan moved out of the Nine Battle Peak and before Wei Ying
moved in, it had remained unoccupied because everyone knew that the next
person to reach the Golden Core Tier on the mountain would undoubtedly
become the next sect leader.

Wei Ying was still an infant when he was taken to the Jade Tablet Sect,
and at nineteen years of age, he moved into the Nine Battle Peak, an
outcome that came as a surprise to no one.

Ever since he moved into the Nine Battle Peak, Wei Ying always liked to
cast his gaze toward the Divine Script Peak, never making any effort to
conceal his gaze. In his eyes, that was his next home. As long as he
cultivated in peace and didn\'t do anything unnecessary during this
time, the Divine Script Peak was eventually going to be his, so there
was no need for him to hide his ambitions.

On this day, Wei Ying was standing in the walkway on the top floor of a
building, casting his gaze toward a certain spot on the Divine Script
Peak, but on this occasion, he was joined by a tall and slender young
man. Unlike his father, the young man had a rather unremarkable
appearance. His eyebrows were very sparse, and the only piece of
resemblance that he bore to his father was his extremely long and narrow
eyes.

The man was Jiang Heng, but his name was listed as Jiang Beihai in the
Jade Tablet Sect ancestral hall and the Jiang Clan\'s genealogical
records. However, those who were familiar with him still habitually
referred to him as Jiang Heng.

Among the younger generation of the Jade Tablet Sect, it was considered
an important point of difference whether they could refer to Jiang
Beihai as Jiang Heng, because regardless of whether it was Jiang Heng or
Jiang Beihai, the fact of the matter was that he was Jiang Shangzhen\'s
only son.

At the moment, Wei Ying was the heir-apparent to Xun Yuan, so Jiang Heng
was definitely inferior to him in status, but he was still most likely
going to be the next owner of the Cloud Cave Blessed Land. However, in
recent years, there had been some rumors proclaiming that Jiang
Shangzhen had had another son in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land under his
alternate identity of Zhou Fei, and that had been a constant sore spot
for Jiang Heng over the past few years.

Still, he had no choice but to suppress his dissatisfaction, and he
certainly didn\'t dare to reveal his intention of sending someone into
the Lotus Flower Blessed Land to kill off this younger brother of his.
The reason for this was very simple: the one that Jiang Heng feared the
most was none other than his own father, Jiang Shangzhen. Everyone on
the Parasol Leaf Continent was aware of how terrifying Jiang Shangzhen
was, and Jiang Heng feared him even more than the average person did.

Jiang Heng\'s mother was the daughter of an old ancestor of an extremely
lofty status in the Jade Tablet Sect, and she knew that Jiang Shangzhen
had never truly loved her. However, whenever she spoke of Jiang
Shangzhen to Jiang Heng back when he was still a child, a genuinely
happy expression would still appear on her face, and she would tell him
that she was very content just to be able to stay by Jiang Shangzhen\'s
side.

On the day that she passed, Jiang Shangzhen had sat beside her sickbed
with a gentle expression, holding onto her hand in silence. Even on the
verge of death, Jiang Heng\'s mother clutched tightly onto Jiang
Shangzhen\'s hand, and she smiled as she said something that made Jiang
Heng\'s heart sink.

\"I went to see that woman in secret once. She was already an old woman
at that point, and I could tell that she wouldn\'t have been all that
pretty even back when she was young. I know you decided to name Jiang
Heng what you did for her sake, and I granted you your wish, yet you
never even thanked me. In all of the years that we\'ve been together,
that\'s the only thing that I\'m mad at you about.\"

Jiang Shangzhen reached out his other hand to gently pat the back of her
hand, and he chuckled, \"Did you know that while you were observing her
in secret, I was also observing *you* in secret? At the time, you looked
so adorably triumphant, like you had just scored some major victory.\"

The woman nodded in response, then departed from the world with a smile
still lingering on her lips.

Jiang Heng was sitting on a chair by the side of the bed, sobbing in an
inconsolable fashion.

\"How long are you going to keep crying for?\" Jiang Shangzhen asked as
he turned to Jiang Heng with a smile.

The child immediately sat up straight and suppressed his sobs in a
fearful manner.

At the time, Jiang Shangzhen told him something that he didn\'t
understand, but still committed firmly to memory. \"If you can\'t be
yourself, then learn to deceive yourself. It\'s not going to be easy
being my son.\"

However, setting aside his deep-seated fear of his father, Jiang Heng
actually lived a very good life in the Jade Tablet Sect. In fact, aside
from a tiny handful of people in the sect, one of whom was Wei Ying, he
led a better life than everyone else.

At this moment, Jiang Heng was following Wei Ying\'s gaze, looking out
at the Divine Script Peak as he smiled and asked, \"You still can\'t
forget Sui Youbian?\"

\"Yes, but also no,\" Wei Ying replied with a shake of his head. \"It\'s
true that I still can\'t forget her, but not because I\'m in love with
her or anything like that. What bothers me the most about her is that
she would rather die than come to visit my Nine Battle Peak.\"

Wei Ying leaned against the railing, then turned his gaze to Jiang Heng
and chuckled, \"When it comes to knowing a woman\'s heart, Uncle
Jiang\'s expertise remains unmatched.\"

Jiang Heng rested his elbows down onto the railing, not wanting to
discuss this subject.

His name was a joke among many of the old ancestors of the Jade Tablet
Sect, and many of them were no match for his father in both battle and
mind games, so they enjoyed taking out their anger toward Jiang
Shangzhen by picking on Jiang Heng. All of them could tell that Jiang
Shangzhen didn\'t have any high hopes for Jiang Heng anyway, so they
could pick on him without any qualms.

\"Looking at the state of the Divine Script Peak, I\'m sure our sect
leader will be able to reach the Ascension Tier,\" Jiang Heng said,
changing the subject.

\"Indeed,\" Wei Ying agreed with a smile and a nod. \"It looks like I
have a long wait ahead if I want to inherit the position of sect leader.
Thankfully, the Jade Tablet Sect can only have a single sect leader, but
the Parasol Leaf Continent can accommodate two to three Ascension Tier
cultivators. I wonder who\'s going to become the third one.

"If you ask me, Huang Ting of Peace and Tranquility Mountain and the
child who left the Planchette Writing Sect to go to the Confucian
academy are the likeliest candidates.\"

Jiang Heng genuinely admired Wei Ying for the latter\'s willingness and
courage to speak about anything that he wanted. He hadn\'t gained this
courage after moving into the Nine Battle Peak. Instead, he had been
like this ever since he first embarked on the path of cultivation.

Jiang Shangzhen had always been very fond of Wei Ying. He often lamented
that his true son wasn\'t like his son, but thankfully, he had Wei Ying,
who was more like a son to him than his actual son, living on the Nine
Battle Peak.

At the moment, things were going very well for the Jade Tablet Sect, and
not just on the Parasol Leaf Continent, either.

Not only was Sect Leader Xun Yuan about to reach the Ascension Tier, the
Jade Tablet Sect\'s lower sect, the True Realm Sect, had also already
completely established itself in Bamboo Scroll Lake.

On top of that, the Parasol Leaf Sect, Peace and Tranquility Mountain,
and the Planchette Writing Sect had all recently been dealt heavy blows,
and there were many people proclaiming that if the Jade Tablet Sect
wanted to expand northward, then no one would be able to oppose them,
even if the aforementioned three sects were to join forces.

The Jade Tablet Sect had always been number two on the Parasol Leaf
Continent for thousands of years, yet all of a sudden, it had risen to
the top without really doing anything. Looking into the future, it
seemed like the Jade Tablet Sect\'s position would remain unchallenged
for at least the next few thousand years, even if it were to continue to
do nothing.

Surely, Sect Leader Xun Yuan was laughing himself awake at night.

Of course, the dramatic fall from grace of the Parasol Leaf Sect had
played a pivotal role in the Jade Tablet Sect\'s rise to the top.

First, their Ascension Tier ancestor, Du Mao, inexplicably perished, and
not only that, but he had even taken down a small world with him. To
make matters even worse, even the colored glaze golden body fragments
that he left behind didn\'t all fall to the Parasol Leaf Sect.

On top of that, Zuo You had brought the entire sect to its knees,
scarring the Dao Hearts of virtually every single cultivator in the sect
to different degrees in the process. The Parasol Leaf Sect had fallen so
far that Jiang Shangzhen even dared to hold a banquet high up in the
clouds right on the border of the Parasol Leaf Sect\'s territory.

In the past, when Du Mao was still alive, Jiang Shangzhen would\'ve had
to flee for his life if he didn\'t want to be cut down on the spot.

Immediately following this unfortunate sequence of events came the
defection of that Upper Five Tiers ancestor, who went to the Jade Tablet
Sect with one of the Parasol Leaf Sect\'s most prized treasures.

That same Upper Five Tiers ancestor ultimately accompanied Jiang
Shangzhen to the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent to establish a lower
sect for the Jade Tablet Sect, but nothing had been heard of him in
recent years. Apparently, he had gone into seclusion.

\"On the subject of Huang Ting, I think it\'s quite a shame that her
fortune is solely restricted to a single continent,\" Wei Ying suddenly
said. \"If the swordsmen of the Parasol Leaf Continent weren\'t so
reclusive, and more of them were willing to travel to the Sword Qi Great
Wall, then even if the Parasol Leaf Continent ultimately still can\'t
become the Northern Complete Reed Continent, it should\'ve at least
accumulated enough fortune to give rise to one or two Immortal Tier
sword immortals long ago.

"If I were in charge of the Parasol Leaf Continent, I would immediately
send all of the swordsmen to Stalactite Mountain, and each time they
returned, they would bring back some fortune with them. Over time, the
Parasol Leaf Continent\'s Sword Dao fortune would be bolstered year
after year.

"Of course, these traveling swordsmen would have to be kept in the dark.
Otherwise, they\'d all go to the Parasol Leaf Continent with impure
intentions, and it wouldn\'t work as well. If Sui Youbian had remained
in the Jade Tablet Sect, I would\'ve been willing to help her compete
against Huang Ting in the Sword Dao.\"

Jiang Heng didn\'t know if this was something that Wei Ying had thought
of himself, or if he were merely parroting something that Xun Yuan had
told him. In any case, he wasn\'t going to ask.

As for how Sui Youbian had come to the Jade Tablet Sect and why Wei Ying
thought so highly of her, Jiang Heng didn\'t care to know.

\"I\'m just a useless guy who lives only for the sake of it,\" Jiang
Heng said with a lazy smile as he cast his gaze into the distance.
\"I\'ll leave it to you to think about all of this big picture stuff.\"

As Jiang Heng stared off into the distance, his thoughts began to drift
back to his past journey to Stalactite Mountain, to Lady Gui on the
Osmanthus Island, to the sword above the clouds in Old Dragon City, to
the Plum Blossom Garden on Stalactite Mountain\...

Jiang Heng had embarked on that journey with full confidence and
resolve, determined to own the Parasol Leaf Continent\'s first
intercontinental ship and open up a new money-making avenue for the
Jiang Clan. It wasn\'t going to generate much income, but at the very
least, it was something, and perhaps it would finally make his father
think highly of him for once.

However, everything had gone against him on that journey, and it
ultimately ended in failure. To further compound his woes, a disgusting
rumor began to spread not long after he returned to the Jade Tablet
Sect, proclaiming that he had somehow ended up with a younger brother.

After leaving the Nine Battle Peak, Jiang Heng returned to his own
residence, which was still the same old residence where his mother had
once lived.

He sat on the doorstep, looking into the empty room, and his voice began
to choke up as he said, \"Father was lying to you, Mother. At the time,
he was still in the Cloud Cave Blessed Land, so how could he have gone
to see you? Do you know he was lying? Of course you do. You were always
so smart and introspective; there\'s no way you didn\'t know. This is
how you always were your entire life.

"Everything you did was for the sake of that heartless bastard. Wait for
me, Mother. Someday, I\'m going to make him personally apologize to you;
I swear it! From that day forth, I will no longer be Jiang Heng. My name
will be Jiang Beihai\...\"

All of a sudden, an extremely familiar voice rang out nearby, one that
sent chills running down Jiang Heng\'s spine. \"Now, now, that\'s no way
to be talking about your father, is it?\"

Jiang Heng\'s entire body stiffened up as he turned around to face the
smiling man behind him.

\"I finally come home for once, and I immediately overhear my own son
plotting my downfall,\" Jiang Shangzhen sighed. \"It\'s a good thing I
couldn\'t care less about you. Otherwise, I would surely be so enraged
and disheartened that my Dao Heart would be instantly broken, causing me
to plummet down several tiers in cultivation base.\"

Jiang Heng rose unsteadily to his feet with an ashen complexion.

Jiang Shangzhen observed Jiang Heng for a moment, then smiled and nodded
as he said, \"You\'re a little dumb, but I suppose that can\'t be
helped, considering you do take after your mother, but that\'s not
entirely a bad thing. They say that fools are often fortunate because
they\'re always quick to forget their sorrows. I\'ll let you off the
hook just this once.

"As your father, I haven\'t really ever been around, so it\'s not really
my place to reprimand you. However, you must remember that even if I
haven\'t been the best father, you still have to be a good son, and
while you\'re at it, be kind to your siblings as well. Don\'t cause more
trouble for me than you need to.\"

Jiang Heng\'s mind was in a complete daze, and he could only nod in
response in a wooden manner.

Jiang Shangzhen turned to depart as he sighed, \"How did I give birth to
an ugly runt like you? You\'re such a massive eyesore to look at! Don\'t
you feel ashamed being so hideous with such good-looking parents? From
now on, whenever you\'re in my presence, only speak to me with your head
lowered.\"

Only after Jiang Shangzhen was gone did Jiang Heng dare to wipe the
sweat and tears from his face, feeling as if he had just brushed
shoulders with death.

If someone were to overhear the scathing remarks Jiang Shangzhen had
aimed at his son, perhaps they would\'ve been sympathetic towards Jiang
Heng, but in reality, compared with some of the things that Jiang
Shangzhen had said to him in the past, this wasn\'t even all that bad.

After leaving the residence, Jiang Shangzhen went straight to the Divine
Script Peak ancestral hall to welcome Xun Yuan as the latter emerged
from seclusion, following a successful breakthrough to the Ascension
Tier.

Wei Ying possessed both the cultivation base and the status required to
have a seat in the ancestral hall, and one that was ranked quite highly,
at that, but due to the special nature of the Nine Battle Peak, he
didn\'t have a seat in the ancestral hall.

This was a rule that had existed in the sect for a very long time, and
there was no room for negotiation.

Jiang Shangzhen was in a rather foul mood after overhearing Jiang Heng
earlier, but his mood was instantly lifted as soon as he entered the
ancestral hall.

[]{#chapter-147.xhtml}

# Chapter 631: (5): The Light Breeze and the Shimmering Moonlight

Sword of Coming

If, for some reason, an immortal were to set off from Reed Flower Island
by sea and make a beeline for the Parasol Leaf Continent, then they
would arrive ashore somewhere near the Planchette Writing Sect.

The Planchette Writing Sect\'s ancestral mountain was called Hanging
Garment Mountain, and it was enshrouded in a sea of clouds all year
round.

In the past, it was once ranked alongside Peace and Tranquility Mountain
in the central region of the Parasol Leaf Sect, and the two were
situated one in the west and one in the east, creating a balance with
the Parasol Leaf Sect in the north and the Jade Tablet Sect in the
south.

Even though the Planchette Writing Sect was a Daoist sect, it didn\'t
fall under the three branches of the White Jade Capital in the Heavenly
World. In that regard, it was similar to Mount Longhu on the Middle
Earth Divine Continent and the Mystery Capital Temple of the Heavenly
World.

Prior to the major crisis that befell the Parasol Leaf Sect, the
Planchette Writing Sect had been slightly superior to Peace and
Tranquility Mountain in terms of reputation. The two had been at odds
with each other for a very long time, and out of the two great demons
that had wreaked havoc on the continent, one had dealt a heavy blow to
the Planchette Writing Sect, while the other had done the same to Peace
and Tranquility Mountain.

In light of their shared misfortune, the two sects had set aside their
past differences and become allies. Cultivators from both sects had been
fighting alongside one another for many years, and the relationship
between the two was much improved.

One night, a young man and a young woman made their way to the
Planchette Writing Sect, which had already sealed itself off from the
outside world for many years.

Prior to this, the Planchette Writing Sect had moved Sky Calling Street,
which had been situated halfway up the mountain, to the foot of the
mountain. Since then, the bustling street had become a constant source
of sorrow for Sect Leader Ji Hai, as whenever he laid eyes upon it, he
was reminded of his Dao partner, who had personally created this street.

On Sky Calling Street, the young man wearing a Confucian robe purchased
some small trinkets, refusing to buy anything that was priced in excess
of ten snowflake coins.

He was accompanied by an extremely beautiful woman carrying a sword on
her back, but no one dared to make a pass at her for a very simple
reason: the sword on her back indicated that she had come from Peace and
Tranquility Mountain, and there was only a single Daoist nun on Peace
and Tranquility Mountain who was this stunningly beautiful.

Indeed, it was none other than the Nascent Tier sword immortal, Huang
Ting.

Back in the day, even He Xiaoliang of the Divine Edict Sect, now the
leader of the Northern Complete Reed Continent\'s Refreshing Sect, had
been ranked second below Huang Ting in terms of fortune.

The young man by Huang Ting\'s side was Zhong Kui, the former Confucian
noble scholar, and the one who served as Chen Ping\'an\'s inspiration to
become an accountant.

\"Even though I\'m no longer a Confucian disciple, I\'m ultimately still
not a direct disciple of the Planchette Writing Sect, and I can\'t just
expect Sect Leader Ji to teach me that secret technique just on the
basis of my teacher,\" Zhong Kui said with a smile. \"I\'m a very close
friend of Chen Ping\'an\'s, and you\'re on good terms with Chen Ping\'an
as well, so that makes us friends too. Seeing as that\'s the case, I
think you\'re obligated to put in a good word for me.\"

Huang Ting had only recently returned from her journey to the Northern
Complete Reed Continent, where she was unable to overcome her Nascent
Tier bottleneck. After returning to Peace and Tranquility Mountain, she
proclaimed that she was going into seclusion, but the reality was that
she simply couldn\'t be bothered to see anyone.

On the way back, while passing through the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent, she had visited the Great Li Empire, intending to check on
Pei Qian to see how her sword and saber techniques were coming along.
However, Pei Qian wasn\'t on Downtrodden Mountain at the time.

Instead, she was greeted by a pair of rather sleazy individuals who were
very hospitable to her. The older one of the two tried to swindle her
into becoming a guest elder on the mountain, while the other one was
practically drooling as he ogled her like a starving man staring at a
delectable meal.

Huang Ting was not in the mood to be joking around with Zhong Kui. She
had only accompanied him on this trip because the mountain master had
practically forced her to do so.

Thus, she replied with a serious expression, \"I have a letter from our
mountain master that should be able to help you out, but I\'m not going
to do anything for you beyond that. If Ji Hai refuses, then there\'s
nothing I can do except wish you luck.\"

A concerned look appeared on Zhong Kui\'s face upon hearing this.

Huang Ting couldn\'t help but feel a little exasperated. This was a very
important matter, so he should\'ve taken it seriously earlier. Why was
it that he was only taking it seriously now that he was on Hanging
Garment Mountain? Back on Sky Calling Street at the foot of the
mountain, Zhong Kui had shown himself to be extremely shameless when
bartering with the street vendors.

Huang Ting was very well-traveled herself, but even she had to concede
her inferiority to Zhong Kui in this regard. However, even though Huang
Ting had no interest in going out of her way to help Zhong Kui, she
actually had quite a positive impression of him.

During the battle on Peace and Tranquility Mountain, Zhong Kui was the
one who had predicted the enemy\'s next move and saved the mountain from
certain catastrophe. Huang Ting already felt very guilty for her failure
to defend Peace and Tranquility Mountain, and if Zhong Kui hadn\'t
limited the damage, then her guilt would\'ve been even further
compounded.

On the way here, Zhong Kui had made many stops. He stopped at the banks
of rivers and lakes to chat extensively with the water ghosts inside,
and he made casual conversation with the ghosts roaming through
graveyards. Huang Ting allowed him to do as he pleased. If he was in no
hurry, then as an outsider, she was naturally in no hurry, either.

As the two of them scaled the mountain, Ji Hai was still yet to make an
appearance, and that was not a good sign.

The two of them weren\'t exactly exceptionally important figures on the
Parasol Leaf Continent, but Ji Hai had always been known to be quite
hospitable and approachable for someone of his status. Even if Huang
Ting were only visiting the Planchette Writing Sect herself, Ji Hai
would\'ve either gone to the entrance of the mountain to greet her, or
at the very latest, he should\'ve certainly already appeared at this
point at the top of the steps leading up to the mountain summit.

However, Zhong Kui remained unbothered, and he was still making casual
conversation with Huang Ting. \"I heard that you once fought Liu
Jinglong on Temper Mountain on the Northern Complete Reed Continent.
Since then, he\'s become a sword immortal, and I\'ve heard that his
three opening battles as sword immortal were very spectacular.\"

\"It\'s no real surprise that he became a sword immortal,\" Huang Ting
replied with a nod. \"My Nascent Tier bottleneck is larger and steeper
than his, so I\'ve fallen behind him a little, but for cultivators like
us, a delay of a few years is nothing to be concerned about. Compared
with Lin Su and Xu Xuan, who are ranked above him, I think he\'s
actually going to rise to greater heights than both of them. Of course,
that\'s just my personal opinion.\"

\"Did anyone fall in love with you at first sight on your journey to the
Northern Complete Reed Continent?\" Zhong Kui asked with an intrigued
expression.

\"There were quite a few, in fact,\" Huang Ting replied, seeing no
reason to hide this information. \"There was a cultivator from the Flax
Robe Sect. He was a really good guy, and I was considering introducing
my junior sister to him.\"

\"Is there anything more devastating for a man to hear than for the
woman of their heart to call them a \'good guy\'?!\" Zhong Kui wailed,
feeling utterly distraught for the Flax Robe Sect cultivator that he had
never even met. \"Please don\'t say anything like that ever again,
Celestial Maiden Huang! Surely he would\'ve rather you ignored him than
hear something so soul-crushing!\"

Huang Ting couldn\'t be bothered to respond.

Zhong Kui cast his gaze out toward the sea in the west and murmured to
himself, \"I really want to go and see the Sword Qi Great Wall, but my
teacher won\'t let me.\"

Huang Ting took a glance at him, and he continued with a wry smile,
\"I\'m not a swordsman like you; I can\'t just do as I please. We
scholars always have to follow a bunch of rules.\"

\"You\'ve lost your noble scholar title, and you\'re not even a
Confucian disciple anymore, yet you still cling stubbornly to your
status as a scholar,\" Huang Ting remarked with an amused smile.

The one good thing about Zhong Kui was that he could take a joke, and he
wasn\'t ever bothered, even if someone poured salt over his wounds.

\"If a scholar can still maintain a steady heart even after their
interests are harmed, then that scholar can be said to have achieved a
decent level of mental cultivation,\" Zhong Kui said. \"I have gone even
beyond that level, and Chen Ping\'an was drawn to me precisely for my
righteous aura. In fact, he admired me so much that he begged me to
agree to become sworn brothers with him, but I refused because he\'s too
uneducated and can\'t even write any good poems.\"

\"I don\'t see it,\" Huang Ting said flatly, and Zhong Kui turned his
gaze up toward the mountain summit with a slightly forlorn look on his
face.

He was thinking about Jiu Niang\'s inn. Now that he was gone, who was
going to be writing all of the spring couplets in his absence?

All of a sudden, Zhong Kui turned to Huang Ting and said, \"Now that I
think about it, Peace and Tranquility Mountain has everything *but*
peace and tranquility. Shouldn\'t your mountain be partially to blame
for all of the unrest on the continent, given its terribly ironic
name?\"

\"Are you looking for a beating?\" Huang Ting asked with a smile.

\"If you can beat me back to life from the dead, then go right ahead.\"
Zhong Kui grinned.

\"Do you not resent your fate at all?\" Huang Ting asked as the smile
faded from her face.

\"No,\" Zhong Kui replied with a shake of his head. \"What\'s meant to
be mine will always end up becoming mine, and what\'s destined to be out
of my grasp will always remain out of my grasp. The same applies to life
and death.\"

\*\*\*

Ever since the rise of Du Mao, the Parasol Leaf Sect had never been in
such a terrible position.

Their sect leader had used certain unorthodox techniques to overcome his
bottleneck and become an Immortal Tier sword immortal, but at the cost
of never being able to make any further progress in his cultivation.
That, in addition to the fact that the sect\'s mountain-protection
formation was still standing, certainly made things a little easier.
Otherwise, the next few years were going to be even more difficult to
endure for the Parasol Leaf Sect.

The sect\'s disciplinary elder had defected with one of the sect\'s most
prized treasures, dealing an additional heavy blow to morale, which was
already at an all-time low.

The Parasol Leaf Sect wasn\'t lacking in talent. On the contrary, it had
many exceptional prodigies, but the majority of them were yet to grow to
their full potential.

Over the past several thousand years, the Parasol Leaf Sect had always
been very overbearing and domineering in everything that they did, and
all of the other immortal powers were already accustomed to this. In
fact, they would even actively help the Parasol Leaf Sect in order to
curry favor. However, now that the Parasol Leaf Sect had fallen from
grace, all of the transgressions that they had gotten away with in the
past were coming back to bite them.

Not only was the Parasol Leaf Sect receiving criticism from all
directions, but some of the sects who were a bit further away and
possessed a decent amount of power had also begun actively working
against the Parasol Leaf Sect. At this point, many of the sect\'s
lower-end guest elders had already defected to other sects under the
promise of brighter futures and heightened status.

Hence, even though the leader of the Parasol Leaf Sect had reached the
Immortal Tier, he still felt constantly exhausted by everything that he
had to deal with.

Even the mountain and water deities that had previously been completely
obedient to the Parasol Leaf Sect had secretly forged an alliance with
one another, and they had worked up the courage to begin bartering with
the Parasol Leaf Sect.

In the past, many mortal empires would offer up their brightest
cultivation prodigies to the Parasol Leaf Sect, but many of them had
since begun taking those prodigies to the Planchette Writing Sect or
Peace and Tranquility Mountain, even if those two sects were further
away.

Parasol Leaf Sect had committed many transgressions in the past, but
they had also done many good things to benefit the entire continent, so
it was certainly not fair to say that they solely exploited everyone
around them without any reciprocation.

Unfortunately, in this social climate, none of the cultivators on the
Parasol Leaf Continent were willing to bring up any of the Parasol Leaf
Sect\'s past good deeds.

A purple-robed man was standing on the bank of a river within the
territory of the Parasol Leaf Sect. This was a place where Sword
Immortal Zuo You had previously lingered briefly.

In the beginning, the man harbored nothing but intense fury and
resentment toward Zuo You, but as time passed, he began to realize that
the Parasol Leaf Sect had already been accumulating bad karma for far
too long, leading up to its catastrophic fall from grace.

In the past, the Parasol Leaf Sect was far too reliant on Du Mao\'s
power to maintain their status, and Du Mao was far too domineering and
conceited for his own good.

Emboldened by the power of Du Mao and the Parasol Leaf Sect as a whole,
the disciples of the sect constantly went around doing whatever they
pleased. If they encountered any conflict outside the sect, then they
would simply kill the opposition, regardless of who was at fault. If
they couldn\'t do that, then they would bring up the Parasol Leaf Sect
as an intimidation tactic to force those who had wronged them to submit
to their will.

If that still didn\'t work, then they would return to the sect and
implore their masters and seniors to stand up for them. Ultimately, the
outcome was always the same, and the disciples of the Parasol Leaf Sect
always got their way.

As aforementioned, the Parasol Leaf Continent had done many good things
over the past several thousand years, but the bad heavily outweighed the
good, and the sect\'s selfish nature had been perfectly reflected by Du
Mao in his final moments.

In order to survive, Du Mao had destroyed a small world, putting himself
above the interests of the entire sect. Not only were all of the sect\'s
disciples and guest elders completely disheartened by this incredibly
selfish final act, but even the sect leader was also sorely
disappointed. Having said that, if he had been in the same position as
Du Mao, then he was certain that he would\'ve made the same choice.

A timid-looking young woman arrived by the man\'s side, and he turned to
her with a smile and asked, \"Is his sword heart recovering well?\"

The man was referring to the bright prodigy of the sect who had the
makings of a sword immortal and had been personally given a longsword by
Du Mao, but all it had taken were a few scathing remarks from Zuo You to
almost completely shatter his sword heart.

\"My senior brother\'s sword heart is recovering very well, Sect
Leader,\" the young woman happily reported. \"Once he fully mends his
sword heart, he should be able to immediately make a breakthrough.\"

The man was utterly exhausted, and he had sacrificed any chance of
further progression in his cultivation for the greater good of the sect,
but whenever he gazed upon the faces of these young men and women who
were going to serve as future pillars of the Parasol Leaf Sect, he felt
a little less disheartened and a little more hopeful for a brighter
future.

\"I know things have been really hard on all of you for the past few
years,\" the man sighed. \"Many of the responsibilities that should\'ve
been shouldered by your seniors have fallen upon your shoulders
instead.\"

The young woman had been collectively appraised by the ancestral hall as
someone who was too timid for her own good. During times of peace and
prosperity for the sect, she had always been lacking in resolve, and her
personality had been as soft and mellow as her voice. However, these
difficult times seemed to have awakened the grit and gumption within
her, and while many others had become disheartened and defeated, her
resolve and Dao Heart had been strengthened instead.

The young woman shook her head vigorously as she mustered up her
courage, then raised her voice and replied loudly, \"I don\'t feel like
things have been hard on me at all, Sect Leader! Both my cultivation and
mental cultivation have become much improved over the past few years, so
you don\'t need to worry about me at all!\"

The purple-robed sword immortal was very pleased. The timid young woman
who had previously been too afraid to even make eye contact with others
now possessed the courage to speak loudly even in the face of the sect
leader.

Prior to his departure, he said, \"There is hope for our Parasol Leaf
Sect, yet. I believe in all of you, and all of you must also believe in
yourselves.\"

With that, he flew away atop his flying sword, leaving the young woman
on her own.

Only after he was long gone did she sit down on the riverbank, where she
began staring off blankly into the distance.

She couldn\'t help but wonder if that unreasonable sword immortal was
still just as unreasonable in the face of the Savage World on the Sword
Qi Great Wall.

# Chapter 631: (6): The Light Breeze and the Shimmering Moonlight

Sword of Coming

Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, Old Dragon City, feudal lord\'s manor.

On this day, Song Jixin, or rather, Feudal Lord Song Mu of the Great Li
Empire, was feeling quite flustered, and he had gone to lie down on a
bench in the walkway for some peace and quiet.

All manner of people from all walks of life were desperately trying to
make their way into the feudal lord\'s manor, and Song Jixin felt like
there were too few people around him that he could trust and be tasked
with shouldering some of his burden.

As long as they possessed sufficient smarts and cultivation base to be
of use, Song Jixin didn\'t care at all about their background, but they
had to be hand-selected by him.

Otherwise, Song Jixin was constantly having to personally deal with
parties like the Fu Clan, the Cloud Forest Jiang Clan, and even the
likes of Sun Scorch Mountain and Light Breeze City, and it was all very
bothersome.

The problem was that he couldn\'t just ignore many of the people who had
the right to enter the manor.

In the past, he hadn\'t felt like it was a difficult task to deal with
different types of people, and it still didn\'t feel too difficult now,
but it was still an exhausting endeavor, nevertheless.

Even though he had already been a feudal lord of the Great Li Empire for
quite a few years, he didn\'t feel like a feudal lord who supposedly
presided over half of the entire continent.

Even cultivators of the Nascent Tier and the Upper Five Tiers had to
treat him as an equal, and even the most powerful generals of the Great
Li Empire and important figures from the clans of the pillar generals
had to speak and behave in a respectful manner in his presence.

This was still something that he hadn\'t gotten used to, and it felt
like a dream.

However, what actually bothered him the most was something that seemed
extremely trivial. Zhi Gui had been his maidservant for just about as
long as he could remember, and she had been constantly by his side
through his hardest days, yet she seemed to have been growing more and
more distant of late.

In Song Jixin\'s eyes, she was becoming more and more difficult to read.

In reality, nothing about Zhi Gui\'s words or behavior indicated that
anything was amiss, but Song Jixin could sense that something was
strange about her and the Fu Clan of Old Dragon City.

He didn\'t want to ask her about it; he wanted her to voluntarily tell
him about it herself.

Thus, he refused to ask, and she refused to tell.

Song Jixin closed his eyes as he lay on the bench, intending to take a
nap, only to abruptly sit up with an alert expression.

A white-robed man had appeared beside him, sitting on the same bench.

It was none other than the tenth tier martial artist, Song Changjing.

\"This is already enough to make you feel tired?\" Song Changjing asked
with an indifferent expression.

Song Jixin nodded as he replied, \"I can\'t say that I\'m carrying out
my duties particularly well, but you can rest assured that at the very
least, I haven\'t made any major mistakes. If you have criticisms for
me, I would listen in earnest and do my best to correct my mistakes.\"

\"If scolding you is actually going to do anything, then I would scold
you to death right now!\" Song Changjing sneered.

Song Jixin was instantly struck by a sense of asphyxiation, as if a
massive weight were suddenly pressing down upon him.

\"Ma Kuxuan of True Martial Mountain is going to come and work here in
the future,\" Song Changjing said.

Song Jixin\'s expression instantly darkened at the thought of the little
bastard from Apricot Blossom Alley who always liked to play dumb. There
were very few people that Song Jixin resented as intensely as he did Ma
Kuxuan.

Song Changjing stood up to leave, but before he did so, he took a glance
at Song Jixin and said, \"I can promise to do one thing for you. For
example, when you want to kill Ma Kuxuan, you can tell me, but you can
only ask for one thing from me, and there are many requests that I
can\'t fulfill. For example, you can\'t ask me to kill His Majesty so
that you can claim the throne. As for whether you want to waste this
opportunity on Ma Kuxuan, that\'s up to you.\"

Song Jixin rose to his feet and nodded in response.

At the moment, the seaside Dragon Scaling Platform outside Old Dragon
City was a strictly off-limits area under personal orders from Feudal
Lord Song Mu himself. Thus, very few people were able to set foot on the
platform, and among Qi refiners, only those at the Nascent Tier and
above were entitled to such a privilege.

However, the most frequent visitor of the Dragon Scaling Platform was a
maidservant from the feudal lord\'s manor.

She was only a maidservant, but one would never guess that from her
stunning appearance. Apparently, she was only a mortal woman, yet she
was even more flawlessly beautiful and captivating than even
accomplished female cultivators.

On this day, she was once again standing at the highest point on the
Dragon Scaling Platform on her own, inspecting her surroundings.

The Golden Core Tier guest elder of the Fu Clan who had previously been
cultivating in a thatched cottage near the Dragon Scaling Platform had
already moved elsewhere.

Right now, if even she couldn\'t sense anything, then it was certain
that there was no one observing Old Dragon City through the use of
immortal observation techniques.

Her eyes were glowing with golden radiance, and she was wearing the Fu
Clan\'s dragon robe, which had refined the entire sea of clouds.

At this point, she was no longer someone that anyone on the Eastern
Treasured Vial Continent could kill on a whim. Instead, *she* was now
the one who could kill whoever she pleased on the continent, with the
exception of a small handful of people.

However, in her eyes, this paltry cultivation base was still completely
pointless.

Even Fan Junmao, who had become the Southern Mountain God, was enough to
make her feel restricted, and in the future, Fan Junmao\'s rate of
cultivation progression was going to be just as fast as hers.

Zhi Gui looked down at a horned four-legged snake that was lying
obediently by her foot.

She raised her foot, then stomped heavily down upon it. The poor little
thing didn\'t dare to run away, and it could only thrash frantically at
the ground with its tail to beg for mercy, causing the entire Dragon
Scaling Platform to tremble violently.

\"You think you can survive just by shaking your tail and begging for
mercy?\" she snapped. \"You\'re even more pathetic than that idiot who
has to hide even when he\'s crying to himself!\"

She stomped down with even greater force, causing the four-legged snake
to sink into the ground.

After withdrawing her foot, she turned to look into the south in a daze
at the blurry sky.

The one who could keep her in check was dead, and he had suffered a
truly pitiful demise.

There was one other person also capable of keeping her in check, but he
was completely in the dark.

\*\*\*

That night, on the Fan Clan\'s Osmanthus Island intercontinental ship,
Lady Gui and her disciple, Jin Su, were sitting together in a peaceful
courtyard.

\"Why\'re you eating moon cakes when it\'s not even the Mid-Autumn
Festival, Mistress?\" Jin Su asked with a smile.

\"I just feel like it,\" Lady Gui replied in a gentle voice after
carefully chewing on and swallowing a mouthful of moon cake.

Only in the presence of her mistress did Jin Su behave like a little
girl, and she extended her legs and interlaced her fingers before
performing an exaggerated stretch. After that, she looked up at the
night sky. The ancestral osmanthus tree on the island was extremely
tall, so much so that it was as if the moon were nestled in its
branches.

Lady Gui took a small bite of moon cake, then jibed, \"So I take it that
you still like Sun Jiashu and not Fan Er?\"

\"Did you have to bring that up now, Mistress?\" Jin Su complained as
her cheeks became slightly flushed with embarrassment.

\"Alright, alright, I\'ll admit that was untimely of me.\" Lady Gui
chuckled.

Jin Su continued to stare up at the moon hanging from the branches of
the ancestral osmanthus tree, and she said, \"I heard that there are
moons in every world, and that the Savage World even has three. Then,
there are also all of the small worlds and blessed lands as well, so
which moon is the real one, or are they all real? Is everyone able to
look up at night and see a moon no matter where they are?\"

\"Perhaps the real moon is the one in your heart,\" Lady Gui replied
with a smile.

\"If only things could always be like this,\" Jin Su suddenly sighed,
seemingly completely unprompted.

\"The moon goes through a constant cycle where it\'s rarely ever full,
but that\'s only the moon that people see; the moon in people\'s hearts
isn\'t like that,\" Lady Gui said with a smile. \"Having said that,
there\'s never been a definitive answer on which one is better.\"

Lady Gui joined her disciple in looking up at the moon. She had grown
accustomed to looking down at the human world from the moon, but looking
up at the moon from the human world was actually not bad as well.

\*\*\*

The project to reestablish the Azure Phoenix Nation\'s grain
transportation system was finally complete, and all of the officials and
departments involved were very pleased with their work.

Initially, this was a project that no one had high hopes for. Not only
was it difficult to carry out, but it was also very easy to offend
people in the process. On top of that, there was a very high likelihood
that something would go wrong, and if that did turn out to be the case,
then it could very easily become a blemish on the political resumes of
everyone involved.

Hence, in the very beginning, the project had only been overseen by two
palace ministers from the Ministry of Works and the Ministry of Revenue,
both of whom had been sent from the capital. They were joined by the
governor of a provincial city that the transportation channel ran
through, and those three were the most prominent figures responsible for
the project.

Below them was Liu Qingfeng, who had been \"promoted\" from county
magistrate to assistant grain transportation overseer.

However, what came as a surprise to everyone was that the project went
extremely smoothly, and the officials in charge climbed higher and
higher up the ranks. The assistant ministers of the Ministry of Works
and the Ministry of Revenue were fighting over one another for the
opportunity to leave the capital and take part in the project, despite
the purportedly terrible working conditions there.

Half a year later, the chief minister of the Ministry of Works traveled
there himself, and he remained on the site until the project\'s
completion, having apparently worked tirelessly alongside all of the
manual laborers in the process. Upon his return to the capital, all he
brought back with him was an umbrella that was signed with countless
names as a collective token of gratitude for his work.

The emperor was very pleased, and many officials were promoted, while
others who were already in very high positions in the officialdom were
given some other rewards.

Even though Liu Qingfeng was one of the progenitors of the project, he
had been content to keep a low profile this entire time, and he didn\'t
actually benefit much from the important role that he played in the
project\'s completion.

The two palace ministers and the governor who had worked alongside him
felt a little disgruntled on his behalf, but having been with him for so
long, they could see that he wanted no part of the spotlight, so they
didn\'t raise any complaints in their official reports.

Since then, the three of them had all received promotions, yet to this
day, they still didn\'t really understand why Liu Qingfeng had chosen to
keep himself so far out of the spotlight.

Liu Qingfeng had been exiled from his clan, and he was an official whose
reputation had been dragged through the mud, so he should\'ve been
desperate to claim any merits that he could in order to redeem himself.
Anyone else in his position could\'ve been excused for trying to
manufacture fake merits that didn\'t exist, yet here he was, denying a
significant merit that was rightfully his.

In the wake of the project, he resembled a thin, dark farmer from all
the manual labor and sun exposure, and that wasn\'t even to mention the
fact that he was solely responsible for ironing out all the details and
planning for the project. However, in the end, he was the only one who
hadn\'t been promoted for his efforts, having merely become an assistant
prefectural overseer, which was the same rank as his past position of
assistant grain transportation overseer.

On this day, Liu Qingfeng was on his way to a remote prefectural city in
the Azure Phoenix Nation, where he was set to work in his new position.
He was traveling in a horse-drawn carriage driven by Wang Yifu.

Scholarly Attendant Liu Suo was sitting beside Wang Yifu, while Liu
Qingfeng was inside the carriage, reading a book. Reading while
traveling in a bumpy carriage was very damaging for one\'s eyesight, yet
whenever Liu Suo reminded Liu Qingfeng of this fact, the latter would
reassure him that he would stop reading soon, but never did. Over time,
Liu Suo simply gave up in his attempts to persuade Liu Qingfeng to stop
reading.

Over the course of the journey, Liu Qingfeng didn\'t read any sagely
scriptures. Instead, he was browsing through maps of all of the Azure
Phoenix Nation\'s official roads. He was even going through the local
county chronicles to pick out all records related to those roads, and
regardless of the size of the roads and whether they had already been
abandoned, he would still make sure to circle those records and make
transcriptions of them.

Liu Suo didn\'t feel like he would ever be able to figure out what his
master was thinking. He was on very good terms with Wang Yifu. The
latter had already become a county lieutenant, yet he was still willing
to toil away in the grain transportation channel project with Liu
Qingfeng, and it was clear that he was a very loyal friend. Thus, Liu
Suo liked to refer to him as County Lieutenant Wang, and Wang Yifu
didn\'t object to the title.

Liu Suo had been Liu Qingfeng\'s scholarly attendant all along, and in
the beginning, they left the Lion Garden to travel together before
making their way to the capital for the imperial examinations. Only
after that did they go to the county office.

He was still just a boy, yet he was no longer as young as he had been at
the outset of their journey. The boy was very happy about this, but in
the future, he would likely look back on this with sorrow.

At the moment, his main source of sorrow was that his master was still
quite a young man, nowhere near forty years of age, yet his sideburns
were already turning silver. What saddened him even more was that his
master didn\'t look anything like the sophisticated scholar that he had
once been.

At around dusk, the horse-drawn carriage arrived at a relay station.
After submitting the passports and official documents, the three of them
spent the night at the relay station. In the eyes of the relay
station\'s petty officials, Liu Qingfeng didn\'t look like an official
at all. Instead, the carriage driver looked much more like an official
to them.

Liu Qingfeng\'s official rank wasn\'t particularly lofty, but nor was it
anything to be scoffed at, so the petty officials decided to arrange two
rooms for the three of them to stay in, both of which were standard
rooms that weren\'t good or bad.

After dinner, Liu Qingfeng began reading under the light of a lamp,
pulling out a writing brush and some ink as he did so.

\"You really should give cultivation a try, Mr. Liu, even if it\'s just
to save your eyes from the strain of reading,\" Wang Yifu suggested with
a smile. \"You don\'t have to save this paltry amount of immortal coins
for the Great Li Empire. In any case, the imperial court of the Great Li
Empire will be making much more than this going forward.\"

\"I\'ll pass,\" Liu Qingfeng replied as he shook his head and set down
his book. \"I am aware of the limitations of my cultivation aptitude.\"

This was the second time that Wang Yifu had brought up this matter
today, and he had been met with refusal from Liu Qingfeng on both
occasions, so he decided not to bring it up again.

In a rare display of restraint, Liu Qingfeng was able to resist the urge
to read after opening a book. Instead, he closed the book, then
suggested, \"Wanna have a drink together?\"

Wang Yifu was very much surprised by this proposal, and he chuckled,
\"You are a hundred times the scholar and politician that I am, but when
it comes to drinking, it\'s the other way around.\"

\"We haven\'t even begun drinking yet, and you\'re already insulting
me,\" Liu Qingfeng said with a wry smile and a shake of his head.

Wang Yifu was once one of the staunchest pillars of the northernmost Lu
Empire on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.

In the very beginning, the Great Li Empire was merely a subsidiary
nation of the Lu Empire.

Liu Suo fetched two bowls and some wine, and it was just some ordinary
wine that was very affordable, but didn\'t taste half-bad.

Liu Suo poured some wine for the two men, but the two of them remained
still, and a puzzled look appeared on his face as he asked, \"Aren\'t
you two going to drink? Do you want me to fetch some dishes to help the
wine go down? I don\'t think I\'ll be able to get any at this hour, but
I can try.\"

\"County Lieutenant Wang and I don\'t even dare to drink if you\'re not
at the table,\" Liu Qingfeng said with a smile.

Liu Suo burst into laughter and sat down at the table.

He always found his master\'s jokes very amusing, but they were very few
and far between.

Liu Suo didn\'t have much capacity for wine. He didn\'t enjoy drinking,
and he also didn\'t dare to drink too much. He had to keep an eye on his
master, and if Wang Yifu insisted on getting Liu Qingfeng to drink
beyond his limits, then Liu Suo would have to step in.

Thankfully, Liu Qingfeng drank very slowly, and Wang Yifu never
encouraged him to drink, much to Liu Suo\'s relief. In fact, he was so
relieved that he ended up drinking a bit too much himself.

Wang Yifu set down his bowl, then said, \"I\'ve actually always been
very curious about how you see the cultivation world, Mr. Liu.\"

Liu Qingfeng took a sip of wine, then said, \"There\'s not much point in
discussing that. The boundary between the cultivation world and the
mortal world isn\'t actually as clear-cut as we think it is. The only
fundamental difference is that those in the mortal world have shorter
lifespans, while those in the cultivation world live longer.\"

\"What about all of the unfathomable powers that immortals wield? Isn\'t
that a much clearer point of difference than the lengths of their
lifespans?\" Wang Yifu asked.

Liu Qingfeng shook his head with a smile as he replied, \"I am but a
defenseless scholar, and even the average mortal soldier can kill me
with ease, so what difference does it make to me?\"

\"So in your eyes, the power that cultivators wield is not really of any
consequence,\" Wang Yifu remarked.

\"Those who are wealthy, especially those who possess immense wealth,
are just like accomplished cultivators in that both have received
tremendous blessings from the world,\" Liu Qingfeng said. \"They have
enough money to not have to worry about material needs for several
lifetimes, so they should be thinking about opening their coffers and
giving back to the world that has blessed them so.

"I\'m not saying everyone should be selfless and learn from moral sages.
Instead, what I\'m saying is that by giving back, you stand to earn more
in the future. At the end of the day, you\'re not giving back out of a
sense of selflessness, but instead, for more future gain. Indulging and
tolerating those who break the rules is a massive disservice to those
who follow the rules.\"

Liu Qingfeng turned to the half-drunk Liu Suo as he spoke, then smiled
and asked, \"How can we be sure that the rules that we establish are
definitely good and correct?\"

\"That\'s something for you to think about, Master,\" Liu Suo replied
with a grin. \"I don\'t want to think about it, and I won\'t be able to
think of an answer even if I try. However, I suggest you think less
about stuff like this as well. Otherwise, I\'m going to feel tired for
you.\"

\"Just keep drinking and don\'t think about anything then,\" Liu
Qingfeng sighed with an exasperated wave of his hand.

Wang Yifu raised his bowl and proposed a toast to Liu Qingfeng.

Liu Qingfeng also raised his bowl and said, \"I\'ll try to keep up, but
I fear I\'m nearing my limits.\"

Before long, Liu Suo had already fallen asleep with his head resting on
the table.

The casual conversation between Wang Yifu and Liu Qingfeng continued,
and it was very rare that he got to speak to Liu Qingfeng for so long.

Liu Qingfeng remained very calm and composed when speaking about feats
that were very significant in Wang Yifu\'s eyes, but when speaking about
a minor thing that Wang Yifu had never even thought about, Liu Qingfeng
threw his head back and downed a large mouthful of wine, seemingly to
drown his sorrows.

\"The loss of a regional dialect anywhere in the Eastern Treasured Vial
Continent is a heartbreaking thing. There are many extremely fragmented
scholarly lineages out there, but as long as their books still exist,
there\'s a chance for them to be saved. However, if a dialect is gone,
then it\'s completely gone along with the many local customs and
traditions attached to it.\"

Liu Qingfeng\'s voice trailed off into silence as he stared blankly at
the window.

The window was closed, so he couldn\'t see the moon outside, and he
didn\'t know if it was brighter than the day before or was going to be
dimmer than the moon of the next day.
