# Chapter 631: (7): The Light Breeze and the Shimmering Moonlight

Sword of Coming

Xu Yuanxia returned to his hometown and opened a martial arts academy.
However, he had a secret hobby of writing books. One time, a servant who
was cleaning his room happened upon his work, and his secret hobby was
exposed, becoming the butt of many jokes.

Xu Yuanxia was no longer a young man, and his appearance was rather
unsightly, but there were still many women who were willing to marry
him.

After all, he was clearly not strapped for money, and even more
importantly, he seemed to have connections everywhere, including with
the local gangs and factions, the county magistrate, the officials of
the prefectural office, and he seemed to be able to get in a word or two
with everyone.

A single man with bulging coffers would never remain single for long
unless they preferred it that way.

A bunch of immortals had arrived in the mountains around the city, and
they had claimed a peaceful, scenic mountain for themselves. Before
long, the mountain was completely enshrouded in cloud and mist.

Many of the local residents quickly swarmed to the mountain and gathered
at its foot, begging for immortal fated opportunities or for the
immortals to help them overcome certain hardships in life, but all of
them were ignored.

While one of the immortals on the mountain was passing through the area,
he spotted a cultivation prodigy. It was a young girl who had once been
considered completely unremarkable in the prefectural city.

She vehemently refused to go with the immortal to cultivate on the
mountain, wanting only to marry her childhood sweetheart and live a
peaceful life together. The young man that she liked just so happened to
have been an external disciple of Xu Yuanxia\'s at his martial arts
academy.

At the young man\'s request, Xu Yuanxia made his way up the mountain,
and using a combination of principles and the saber strapped to his
waist, he was able to convince the Qi refiners not to take the girl by
force. The cultivators weren\'t particularly advanced in cultivation
base, and they were quite reasonable as well, quickly agreeing to his
request.

However, shortly thereafter, the girl\'s parents stormed into Xu
Yuanxia\'s martial arts academy and kicked up a massive fuss,
proclaiming that he had ruined their daughter\'s future. In particular,
there was an old woman who was so racked with grief that she fell
unconscious, and she almost passed away on the spot.

Ultimately, the girl also changed her mind and agreed to go and
cultivate on the mountain, perhaps convinced by her mother, or perhaps
simply of her own accord.

As a result, Xu Yuanxia had offended both the immortals on the mountain
and the girl\'s family with nothing to show for it. However, he had seen
and experienced far too much during his travels, and this didn\'t really
bother him.

Prior to parting ways, the young couple had vowed to remain loyal to one
another, and they envisioned a bright future together.

One of them would continue to learn martial arts from Xu Yuanxia before
establishing his own faction, while the other would become a cultivator,
and the two of them could even help each other out in the future.

However, it only took a year before her visits became less frequent, and
after another year, she didn\'t bother to come back at all. Even when
the man went to find her, she refused to see him.

The young man didn\'t drink at all in the past, but he began to drown
his sorrows.

Xu Yuanxia was very sympathetic to his situation, but there was nothing
that he could do.

As it turned out, the girl really had the makings of a cultivator, and
one time, she was spotted flying through the air over the prefectural
city with her seniors and martial brothers and sisters.

It was close to dusk at the time, and as soon as the young man saw her
flying overhead, tears immediately began to stream down his face.

There was nothing that Xu Yuanxia could say to make him feel better.

That night, Xu Yuanxia lay on the roof of his house, drinking wine, and
he began to miss his two young friends, Zhang Shanfeng, who was both
smart and stupid at the same time, and Chen Ping\'an, who always seemed
to have a million things on his mind.

He wondered how many flagons of wine he would have to drink when the
three of them were next reunited.

At the moment, the world was a very strange place, and Xu Yuanxia could
only hope that his two friends were safe and well.

As his thoughts began to stray, he decided that if he were to shave his
beard, then he would be the most handsome one of the three.

\*\*\*

Inside an alley in Cloud Pagoda City of Bamboo Scroll Lake, a young man
and a snot-nosed boy who lived across from each other were squatting
together in a yard, roasting a cob of corn.

The young man split the cob of corn into two and handed the boy one
half.

The boy was furious, refusing to accept the corn as he complained, \"Why
do I get the smaller half?! You\'re older than me, and I\'m still
growing, so why can\'t you give me the bigger half? Do you want to marry
my sister or not?!\"

\"I\'ve never had the smaller half of corn in my life; always the bigger
half, and I\'m not about to make an exception for you,\" Gu Can said
with a smile.

The boy could see that Gu Can didn\'t appear to have been kidding
around, and he was getting free corn from Gu Can anyway, so he decided
to relent, munching on his corn as he asked, \"How come you still eat
roasted corn so much when you\'re so rich?\"

\"Why not?\" Gu Can countered. \"I\'ve gotten so hungry in the past that
I\'ve even eaten dirt before.\"

\"What a load of nonsense!\" the boy scoffed with a roll of his eyes.
\"No girl is ever going to like you if you keep lying like that!\"

The boy was completely oblivious to the fact that the young man eating
corn with him was once considered a ubiquitous nightmare for just about
everyone in Bamboo Scroll Lake. There was a time when he faded out of
the spotlight, but it didn\'t take long before he once again became an
important figure in Bamboo Scroll Lake, and his current way of life was
much more sustainable. Instead of killing everyone that he didn\'t like
the look of as he had in the past, he had learned to coexist with
others, and he did so very well.

In the wake of that meeting with Gu Can before Liu Zhimao went into
seclusion, the latter had already become completely convinced that Gu
Can was fit to become his own direct disciple, and he had even left the
all-important River Severing Sutra to him.

On top of that, Tian Hujun also saw Gu Can as the only one who could
possibly save her.

The young general of the Great Li Empire who had been previously
stationed in Cloud Pagoda City, Guan Yiran, was already gone, and the
new general sent by the Great Li Empire to fill his place was clearly a
friend of his. Gu Can knew that this was a friend, but also not a
friend, but it wasn\'t actually important anyway.

The new emperor of the Stone Brush Nation, Han Jingling, the youngest
assistant minister of the Ministry of Rites in the Stone Brush Nation,
Huang He, and many \"old friends\" of Gu Can\'s had come to see him in
secret at one point or another.

Most importantly, Gu Can had once received a visit from an unexpected
guest. He was immediately able to identify the visitor, even though they
had cast an illusion on themselves.

Gu Can didn\'t bother to play dumb, immediately extending a respectful
bow as he greeted, \"Gu Can pays his respects to Sect Leader Jiang.\"

Jiang Shangzhen had been in quite a good mood at the time, and not only
did he make his way inside, he even shared a drink with Gu Can. He made
the room into an isolated small world, then said some shocking things to
Gu Can, seemingly treating him as a trusted confidant.

Jiang Shangzhen complained that he was living in constant distress,
having to deal with someone snoring loudly at his bedside.

He also denounced the old leader of the Jade Tablet Sect for his
terrible site selection. He could\'ve chosen any other place, yet he
insisted on choosing this godforsaken place, seemingly intentionally to
prevent Jiang Shangzhen from being able to sleep soundly at night.

Gu Can merely listened and held his cup in both hands, refusing to speak
or drink.

The intentions behind Gu Can\'s actions, or lack thereof, were very
simple. Essentially, he was conceding that while he was in Bamboo Scroll
Lake, he would do everything that Jiang Shangzhen saw fit for him to do.
As for what he thought and what he wanted to do, none of that was
important.

With Gu Can completely unresponsive, Jiang Shangzhen only had a few cups
of wine before departing.

Aside from certain things that Jiang Shangzhen told him, Gu Can never
kept any secrets from Zeng Ye and Ma Duyi. However, in the beginning,
the two of them were still very concerned, worried that he would revert
back to the Gu Can of old, the Gu Can from Cyan Gorge Island, as opposed
to the Gu Can who had embarked on that long journey with Chen Ping\'an.

Thankfully, Gu Can quickly laid their concerns to rest. Even though he
was very busy attending to all types of social engagements, he still
made sure to dedicate at least six months of each year to traveling the
world near Bamboo Scroll Lake with Zeng Ye and Ma Duyi.

During their travels, they encountered many unexpected conflicts, and
there was one occasion when they encountered a horrific tragedy.

On that occasion, Gu Can didn\'t try to smooth things over or simply
ignore everything as he had done in the past. Instead, he
single-handedly slew the twelve Qi refiners who were the perpetrators at
the heart of the incident, killing each one of them with just a single
attack. Among them was a Dragon Gate Tier cultivator that Zeng Ye and Ma
Duyi had been quite wary of, but he was no match for Gu Can, even though
the latter didn\'t even count as a swordsman.

Even Zeng Ye and Ma Duyi were very satisfied with that outcome. Those
cultivators deserved everything that had come to them.

After making short work of the group of cultivators, Gu Can held his
sword in one hand before making a fist with his other hand. He gently
struck his sword-wielding hand with his fist, shaking off the blood on
the blade, and by the time he turned around to face Zeng Ye and Ma Duyi,
the sword was already sheathed.

\"Let\'s go,\" Gu Can said with a smile. \"They were born from heaven
and earth, and now, heaven and earth get to reclaim their bodies, so we
can just leave them here.\"

At this point, Gu Can had already accumulated a great deal of wealth for
himself. In addition to Cyan Gorge Island, which Liu Zhimao had secured
for him, quite a few other islands were also recorded under his name, so
he very rarely visited this residence in the small alley. However, each
time he returned from his travels, he would always make sure to come and
spend a night here.

There was enough corn for both of them, and even though the boy was only
able to get the smaller half each time, he was still able to eat until
his stomach was round and full.

All the while, there had been something on Gu Can\'s mind, namely the
two pawns that he had painstakingly planted on Sun Scorch Mountain and
in the Light Breeze City Xu Clan. Even though he didn\'t know when they
would come in useful, there was no hurry, so he would just have to take
things one step at a time.

The boy burped loudly, then plopped down onto the ground, turning his
gaze to Gu Can as he asked, \"Who else aside from me would be so kind as
to always let you have the bigger half of corn?\"

Gu Can took a glance at the boy, and the latter suddenly felt a little
afraid.

Gu Can smiled as he pointed at the boy\'s face and said, \"Wipe the snot
from your face.\"

The boy immediately sucked the snot back up his nostrils, not even
bothering to wipe with his sleeve or the back of his hand.

After some thought, Gu Can said, \"It\'s probably going to be very
difficult for that person and me to return to the way things once were,
but that\'s fine. As long as I don\'t make any big mistakes, he\'ll
continue to think of me. Many good friends eventually grow apart. Right
now, my relationship with him is neither close nor distant, and that\'s
actually quite comforting to me.\"

He turned to the fearful boy sitting on the ground as he smiled and
asked, \"What do you think?\"

For some reason, the current Gu Can felt completely unfamiliar to the
boy, so he was instinctively treading with caution as he said in a quiet
voice, \"Whatever you say, I guess. I\'m too young to know anything.\"

\"You\'re not as smart as me, but you\'re plenty smart as well,\" Gu Can
said with a smile.

The boy immediately regained his courage, rolling his eyes as he
scoffed. \"You think I\'m smart? Tell that to my teachers!\"

All of a sudden, Gu Can stood up and instructed, \"Go and stay in my
room for a bit. Make sure you don\'t go through my stuff.\"

The boy didn\'t know what was happening, but he still obediently did as
he was told. However, after entering Gu Can\'s room, he got up onto the
tips of his toes to look over the windowsill, worried that something
would happen to Gu Can.

\"It\'s fine if you don\'t want to come in; I\'ll come out to meet
you,\" Gu Can said as he turned to the entrance of the courtyard with a
smile.

A timid-looking scholar appeared at the entrance of the courtyard, then
said in a slightly feeble voice, \"My name is Liu Chicheng, and I come
from the White Mountain Nation, the one that\'s really close to Lake
View Academy. I\'ve been traveling through Bamboo Scroll Lake, and I
don\'t know how I ended up here, but I assure you this is all a
misunderstanding! I\'m not a thief; I\'m a legitimate scholar! I
swear!\"

Gu Can\'s eyes narrowed slightly, and he cupped his fist in a salute as
he said, \"If you don\'t need me to come out, then please come in
yourself, Senior.\"

The scholar stepped into the courtyard, and as he did so, his
disposition completely changed.

\"What an impressive young man you are,\" Liu Chicheng mused.

\"I\'d gladly take this praise from you as long as what you\'re about to
say next isn\'t \'impressive young men like you need to be nipped in the
bud and killed early,\'\" Gu Can said with a smile.

Liu Chicheng burst into laughter upon hearing this.

\"A brilliant young man you are, indeed! I came here to retrieve the
River Severing Sutra as I was worried that it may have fallen into the
hands of someone unfit to inherit it, but I can now see that this is a
match made in heaven! You look quite young, but your cultivation base is
nothing to sneeze at. What\'s your name, kid?\"

A thought occurred to Gu Can, and a peculiar look appeared on his face
as he asked, \"Are you trying to find another disciple, Senior?\"

A slightly awkward look appeared on Liu Chicheng\'s face at this
question, and he sighed, \"Well, this is a little awkward.\"

\"I implore you to be civilized, Senior,\" Gu Can said, and all of a
sudden, the respectful look faded from his face as he concluded,
\"Otherwise, your joy may turn to sorrow soon.\"

\"I don\'t doubt that,\" Liu Chicheng mused with a smile. \"You
shouldn\'t stay in a little pond like this one. Instead, you should go
to White Emperor City on the Middle Earth Divine Continent.\"

\*\*\*

The Great Li Empire was on the up and up.

Recently, a light shower had rained down on the territory of the Great
Li Empire\'s former Central Mountain.

At this point, all of the gods of the Great Li Empire\'s former Five
Mountains had been demoted to normal mountain gods. Furthermore, three
mountains were about to be selected as subsidiary mountains to the new
Northern Mountain, Cloud Drape Mountain, and that was a very
heart-wrenching turn of events for certain mountain gods.

Previously, there had been no such precedent on the entire Eastern
Treasured Vial Continent, but similar things had happened in the past on
the Middle Earth Divine Continent. However, the outcome had never been
very good. Not only was this an endeavor that required significant
investments of money and resources, but it was also very likely that
something would go wrong in the process.

The reason for this was very simple. The subsidiary mountains were often
extremely far away from the Five Mountains, as opposed to being close
neighbors. The existing mountain gods were already inferior in status to
the gods of the Five Mountains, and once their mountains became
subsidiaries to the Five Mountains, there would be even more rules and
restrictions imposed upon them.

The gods of the Five Mountains would be able to travel to any of their
five subsidiary mountains extremely quickly and assess the merits and
transgressions of the mountain god, whereas in the past, according to
the rules established by the Confucian sages, only the Ministry of Rites
had the authority to do this.

Not only that, but the gods of the Five Mountains could take mountain
and water fortune from their subsidiary mountains as they pleased. Of
course, they could also do the opposite and reciprocate their subsidiary
mountains, but no matter how convincing the promises that they made
sounded, could they really be trusted?

A woman in green was making her way down a mountain path while holding
an oil-paper umbrella. She was going to reason with someone, and if that
didn\'t work, then she would eat something. After all, the entire
territory of the former Central Mountain now belonged to the Dragon
Spring Sword Sect.

On her northbound journey, she picked up a little girl along the way and
brought her along with her.

The little girl was a spirit, and she asked with a wide smile, \"Do you
know the alternate name that we have for umbrellas, Big Sister Xiuxiu?\"

\"No,\" Ruan Xiu replied in a distracted manner.

\"We call them flower canopies. Isn\'t that a really nice name?\"

\"Yep.\"

\"Why do you not seem to have any energy, Big Sister Xiuxiu?\"

\"I finished all my pastries, so I\'m hungry.\"

\"That explains it. Have you heard that if you eat bayberries without
spitting out the core and watermelon without spitting out the seeds,
they\'ll keep you full for longer?\"

\"Well, aren\'t you a smart little girl?\" Ruan Xiu chuckled as she
patted the little girl on the head.

The little girl raised her foot to look down at her mud-caked shoe and
sighed. \"What a pain.\"

\"It really is,\" Ruan Xiu replied with a nod.

The little girl distanced herself from Ruan Xiu a lot, then began
stomping through the mud with a series of loud squelches as she asked,
\"Do you have someone you like, Big Sister Xiuxiu?\"

\"I do,\" Ruan Xiu replied with a smile.

The little girl turned to look at her from the side for a long while,
then asked, \"Why isn\'t he with you, Big Sister Xiuxiu?\"

Ruan Xiu thought about it for a moment, then replied, \"He *is* with me.
He\'s always in my heart.\"

The little girl pressed a finger against her cheek and made a funny face
as she scoffed. \"Don\'t you feel embarrassed saying that as a girl?\"

\"Should I?\" Ruan Xiu asked, once again looking distracted and
absentminded.

\*\*\*

On this day, the girl who wore red all year round didn\'t stay in
Mountain Cliff Academy. Instead, she went to an ordinary mandarin garden
on the outskirts of the Great Sui Nation\'s capital.

It was a pity that it still wasn\'t winter yet. Otherwise, the mandarins
hanging on the trees would resemble little girls dressed in red.

Li Baoping had only come here on a whim after recalling that she had
once passed by this place, and now that she had seen it, she was
satisfied, so she began to return the same way she had come from.

On the way back, she ran into two people whom she was ecstatic to see.

They were Pei Qian and Cui Dongshan.

Pei Qian immediately launched herself at Li Baoping, who patted her on
the head and remarked, \"Looks like you\'ve grown a little taller yet
again. Make sure you don\'t grow too fast. Otherwise, you\'re going to
turn from a short pear into a thin reed.\"

The elation on Pei Qian\'s face instantly turned to concern.

Li Baoping pinched Pei Qian\'s cheeks as she chuckled. \"I was just
kidding. You\'ve grown in stature, but you\'re still not all that
bright.\"

Pei Qian had so many things that she wanted to say to Li Baoping, but
the latter gestured for her to wait, then turned to Cui Dongshan and
asked, \"Is my junior uncle doing well?\"

\"He is,\" Cui Dongshan replied with a smile and a nod. \"He\'ll be
coming back.\"

Li Baoping looked at her two surprise visitors, and it felt to her like
a real shame that her junior uncle wasn\'t here. Otherwise, they
would\'ve been able to have a snow fight.

Ever since she grew up, she felt like she had barely gotten to see her
junior uncle at all.

\*\*\*

Li Baoping, Pei Qian, and Cui Dongshan climbed up onto the tree on the
mountain summit of Mountain Cliff Academy one by one, looking as if they
had all climbed the same tree a million times. They sat side by side on
a branch.

Pei Qian wanted to sit in the middle, and Cui Dongshan was shoved out of
the way, while Li Baoping was happy to indulge her, so she managed to
get her way, and she was ecstatic.

Pei Qian had been telling Li Baoping about the journey she had taken
here, and she told her story very slowly, having only just finished
telling Li Baoping about the leg of the journey from Ox Horn Mountain to
Old Dragon City.

Cui Dongshan\'s fingers were interlaced behind the back of his head, and
he was swinging his legs back and forth.

Even in the darkness of the night, the capital of the Great Sui Nation
was still filled with radiant lights.

The faint breeze rustled, and the moonlight shimmered.

These were peaceful and prosperous times.

Cui Dongshan had seen far too much of this, and he didn\'t want to see
any more, so he closed his eyes.

His only hope was that his teacher would be able to return home soon.

[]{#chapter-150.xhtml}

# Chapter 632: Challenge

Sword of Coming

Chen Ping\'an paid a visit to the Sword Qi Great Wall on his own and
personally witnessed the challenge that was laid down.

Who could possibly challenge the Sword Qi Great Wall to a battle of the
sword? If the immortal sects of the Majestic World were to catch wind of
this, they would likely immediately dismiss it as an absurd joke.
However, the Savage World really had laid down a challenge to the Sword
Qi Great Wall, and it began on a dark night where the moon was almost
completely absent.

Initially, Chen Ping\'an could only see some specks of sword light
emerge on the southern battlefield. However, the specks of light quickly
increased in number, and it felt just like back when he saw all those
lotus flower lanterns rising up into the sky during his earlier travels
through the Majestic World. Eventually, there were so many specks of
light that their collective radiance outshone even that of the celestial
bodies.

Finally, a series of bonded flying swords began to race toward the Sword
Qi Great Wall, leaving trails of resplendent light behind them that
formed an incredibly spectacular river of radiance. Looking down from
the top of the city walls, one felt as if they were an immortal looking
down at the lights of the mortal world. It was truly a breathtaking
visual spectacle.

As the Hidden Official, there was no need for Chen Ping\'an to fight,
and he couldn\'t fight even if he wanted to because he had to return to
the summer palace soon.

It wasn\'t that the swordsmen of the Hidden Official\'s branch weren\'t
doing a good enough job. Instead, Chen Ping\'an simply couldn\'t bring
himself to leave them unsupervised for long. This type of near-obsessive
urge to oversee everything himself was a double-edged sword, and even if
he wanted to kick the habit, this wasn\'t the time to do it.

\"This is a challenge of unprecedented magnitude, and I doubt we\'ll
ever see anything like this again,\" Chen Ping\'an mused as he stood
atop the city walls near the thatched cottage.

\"It\'s likely true that we\'ll never see anything like this again, but
this is not exactly unprecedented,\" the old great sword immortal
disagreed with a smile. \"In the past, the swordsmen of the mortal world
once raised their swords to challenge the heavens, and in response, the
heavens rained down swords in a storm of golden light that was even more
spectacular than what you see now.

"At the time, the human camp had been led by the Paramount Sage, the Dao
Ancestor, the Buddha, and the forefathers of close to half of the
Hundred Schools of Thought. All of them were completely selfless, and
they regarded death as a badge of honor.\"

Chen Ping\'an thought back to the journey that he had embarked on with
Cui Dongshan as his only companion. On the way back, Cui Dongshan had
said many strange things to him.

\"I heard that at the time, the concept of the Three Teachings and the
Hundred Schools of Thought didn\'t even exist,\" Chen Ping\'an said.
\"All of the teachings and schools of thought were in a very rudimentary
state, and everyone, including swordsmen, Qi refiners, and even the
flood dragons, joined forces on a united front. Even the Savage World
called for a temporary ceasefire, and while they didn\'t help us, they
didn\'t hinder our efforts, either.\"

\"Indeed,\" Chen Qingdu replied with a nod as a rare look of
reminiscence appeared on his face. \"Long Jun, Guan Zhao, and I were all
present, alongside many other swordsmen of our generation who have since
already been long forgotten, and we lashed out at the heavens over and
over again.\"

Chen Ping\'an crouched down to rest a hand against the slightly cool
ground atop the city walls, then cast his gaze toward the southern
battlefield and said, \"Back then, everyone struggled for survival, and
if they didn\'t, then they would die. I\'m not downplaying your feats. I
wouldn\'t dare to do such a thing, nor is that something I want to do.
Over ten thousand years have passed since then, and I\'ve seen quite a
bit of the current world over the course of my journeys across three
continents.

"From what I\'ve seen, I daresay that the Majestic World is still good
and stable overall. You are like the old senior of a large clan. You can
clearly see all of the merits and transgressions committed by your
juniors, and you\'ve already been very lenient, but I still hope that
you won\'t be disappointed. If even you become disappointed, then the
juniors below you will have far fewer chances to realize the mistakes of
their ways and make amends.\"

Chen Qingdu remained silent.

Chen Ping\'an wanted to say something, but he couldn\'t help but
hesitate.

\"Go ahead,\" Chen Qingdu prompted with a smile. \"You\'re the Hidden
Official now, so you should have the courage to speak your mind.\"

\"I still feel like the state of the world is improving over time,\"
Chen Ping\'an said. \"Please don\'t think of the past ten thousand years
as a complete waste. The Majestic World has had peace for ten thousand
years, and during that time, everyone has developed their own goals and
aspirations, whether big or small. Even someone like me, who welcomed
death as a child, went on to become an apprentice at the dragon kiln and
began trying to earn money and live a good life.

"While the Majestic World may seem barren and hopeless to you, even the
most barren land still has soil, and as long as there\'s soil, there are
countless possibilities. Do whatever it is that you need to do, but all
that I ask is that you don\'t become disappointed and disheartened. Can
you do that for me?\"

The old great sword immortal crouched down to press a hand down onto
Chen Ping\'an\'s head, and he chuckled. \"You are still but a young man
who hasn\'t seen and experienced anywhere near enough. All of the
swordsmen my age had to crawl out of the deepest and darkest pits of
despair. The world that we came up from was far bleaker than the current
Majestic World, so there\'s nothing for me to be overly disappointed
about.

"Of course, I\'m a little disappointed, but it\'s nowhere near the
extent that you think. Over the past ten thousand years, I\'ve seen much
more hope than despair. Even if that hope doesn\'t grow on the Sword Qi
Great Wall, I can still smell its sweet fragrance from all the way in
the Majestic World.\"

Chen Ping\'an was rendered speechless for a moment, then smiled in
amusement and said, \"I never imagined you would say something like
this. It\'s very\... poetic!\"

\"I\'ll tell you a couple more interesting tidbits, but make sure you
don\'t tell anyone else too soon,\" Chen Qingdu said with a smile.

\"Please go ahead,\" Chen Ping\'an prompted with a serious expression.

However, Chen Qingdu changed his mind, and he shook his head and said,
\"I\'ll tell you later.\"

Chen Ping\'an was just about to leave when Chen Qingdu suddenly
remarked, \"You may be a swordsman now with two bonded flying swords and
a pure martial artist at the pinnacle of the seventh tier, but that\'s
still not enough.\"

\"You really shouldn\'t ask so much of me.\" Chen Ping\'an sighed in a
resigned manner. \"I\'m already doing very well among my peers. As a
martial artist, at the very least, I haven\'t completely lost sight of
Cao Ci, and as a Qi refiner of the Lower Five Tiers, I am now serving as
the Hidden Official of the Sword Qi Great Wall. I can\'t say I\'ve made
any significant contributions up to this point, but surely at least my
effort is to be commended! Maybe if I continue accumulating karma and
fortune, I can---\"

\"Don\'t even think about it,\" Chen Qingdu warned with a shake of his
head, cutting Chen Ping\'an off mid-sentence. \"You don\'t have the
makings of someone who can glean the Cultivator Trapping Tier, so don\'t
even consider trying to reach the Upper Five Tiers in one go.\"

\"Couldn\'t you have waited until I reached the fourth tier before you
told me that?\" Chen Ping\'an complained with a wry smile.

\"There\'s still one more spot to be filled for the roster of three
sword immortals; have you decided on who it should be?\" Chen Qingdu
asked.

\"I\'m struggling to make up my mind,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a
shake of his head.

\"You can\'t even figure out something this simple? What a useless
Hidden Official you are!\" Chen Qingdu scoffed with a dismissive wave.
\"Piss off back to the summer palace, and don\'t come back out until
you\'ve reached the Abode Tier and the Far Roaming Tier!\"

Chen Ping\'an stood up to depart, but before he left, he asked Chen
Qingdu\'s permission for something, and it was granted to him.

He had asked Chen Qingdu if the swordsmen of the Hidden Official\'s
branch could leave the city to battle against the demons. Chen Qingdu
told him that he didn\'t care. As long as they didn\'t shirk their
duties, they could go out and battle as they pleased.

Chen Ping\'an summoned his talismanic boat, and as he did so, he took a
glance at the nearby thatched cottage. Zuo You was still in seclusion,
recovering from his injuries. Xiao Xun hadn\'t held back at all, and if
someone like Yue Qing had been in Zuo You\'s place, they would\'ve
already perished. Even the likes of Lu Zhi and Nalan Shaowei would\'ve
suffered a drop in cultivation base from such a devastating blow.

Chen Ping\'an\'s talismanic boat had only just left the city walls when
someone drifted onto it.

\"Are you leaving?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

\"Probably sometime in the next couple of days,\" Liu Xianyang replied
with a nod. \"The coastal defenses of the Southern Whirl Continent need
to be bolstered, and there\'s a bunch of stuff that needs to be done.\"

\"Make sure to wait for me before you challenge Sun Scorch Mountain,\"
Chen Ping\'an warned. \"This is not something to be taken lightly.\"

\"I would understand your trepidation if you hadn\'t seen me in action,
but is there really a need to be so cautious about Sun Scorch
Mountain?\" Liu Xianyang asked with a puzzled expression.

\"Trust me, my caution is very much warranted,\" Chen Ping\'an insisted
with a nod.

\"Li Tuanjing alone was able to keep Sun Scorch Mountain in check for
several hundred years; why are you taking them so seriously?\" Liu
Xianyang asked.

\"The Sun Scorch Mountain from back when Li Tuanjing was still around is
completely different from the current Sun Scorch Mountain,\" Chen
Ping\'an said. \"Not only has Sun Scorch Mountain finally revealed the
power that it\'s been hiding all along, but its strength is also now
bolstered by its association with the Light Breeze City Xu Clan.

"On top of that, Sun Scorch Mountain will be claiming the majority of
the Luminous Vermilion Empire\'s Sword Dao fortune, something that even
the Dragon Spring Sword Sect wasn\'t able to accomplish because no
matter how much reverence the emperor of the Great Li Empire has for
Master Ruan, there\'s no way he could allow the Dragon Spring Sword Sect
to become the sole dominant force on the continent.

"In addition to the Luminous Vermilion Empire\'s Sword Dao fortune, Sun
Scorch Mountain will also get to claim all of the empire\'s most
talented swordsmen. Right now, Sun Scorch Mountain has already become
intertwined with the fortune of the Great Li Empire, and it\'s not to be
taken lightly. I can\'t reveal anything more to you beyond that, but
what you have to understand is that Sun Scorch Mountain is a very
important and indispensable part of the Great Li Empire\'s future
plans.\"

Liu Xianyang looked back at Chen Ping\'an with a blank expression.

\"Did I say something wrong?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

\"I think you\'ve misunderstood my intentions,\" Liu Xianyang said with
a smile. \"Who said that by challenging them, I have to succeed the
first time? I can prod their arse cheek with my sword today, then run
away before they can retaliate. The next day, I\'ll go back and stab
them in the crotch. Doesn\'t that also count as issuing a challenge? Why
do I have to aim to take them down in one go? Do you see something like
that as too shameful and beneath you now that you\'re a cultivator? You
were never like this growing up.

"Are you not familiar with how I like to do things? I may say some
outlandish stuff sometimes, but I\'d say I\'m fairly reliable when it
comes to the important stuff, wouldn\'t you agree? Whenever you do
something, you always strive to do it the right way, but does that
guarantee that what you do is right? Maybe what you think is right is
actually incorrect, but you simply don\'t realize it. Compared with you,
I\'m much less pedantic about right and wrong.

"I can handle myself, just as I can handle my enemies. You can live like
a pedant, or you can be more carefree. You can lead a life of suffering,
or you can enjoy life. You really need to learn a thing or two from me
when it comes to turning suffering into enjoyment. I\'m not saying that
you\'re wrong. If we look at things solely from the angle of right or
wrong, then you are much more correct than I am.

"However, you have to learn to slack off a little sometimes and give
yourself a chance to breathe. That\'s a useful little trick that you
won\'t be able to learn from any sagely scripture, but I\'ve already
figured it out a long time ago even without reading any books; I just
haven\'t had a chance to tell you about it. \"

This time, it was Chen Ping\'an\'s turn to stare back at Liu Xianyang in
a daze.

\"Gu Can may no longer be the little snot-nosed brat of old, but I\'m
still as smart as ever,\" Liu Xianyang chuckled.

\"I see,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a nod.

\"Make sure to remember that,\" Liu Xianyang insisted.

\"Whatever you say,\" Chen Ping\'an conceded with a smile.

The two of them sat facing each other in the talismanic boat. Life was
always full of separations.

\"Have you done it yet?\" Liu Xianyang asked after a brief silence.

Chen Ping\'an looked back at him with a puzzled expression.

Liu Xianyang took a quick glance at his surroundings to make sure that
there was no one around, then extended his two index fingers before
touching their tips to one another.

Chen Ping\'an hurriedly slapped his hands away and snarled, \"If you
want to die, then you can go die on your own! Don\'t try to get me
killed too!\"

Liu Xianyang looked back at him with a stunned expression.

\"You haven\'t even held hands yet? Are you being serious right now?\"

Chen Ping\'an was completely rooted to the spot.

\"Man, you\'re even worse off than me,\" Liu Xianyang sighed with a
sorrowful expression. \"You\'re not single anymore, but you may as well
still be single.\"

\"Come talk to me again once you\'ve found someone for yourself,\" Chen
Ping\'an said with a smile.

Liu Xianyang shook his head, then lay down in the boat and sighed.
\"Women can never look past my handsome looks to see me for who I really
am.\"

The talismanic boat stopped at the entrance of the summer palace.
According to the rules of the Hidden Official\'s branch, all outsiders
were strictly prohibited from entry. The two of them drifted down to the
ground, and Chen Ping\'an stowed his talismanic boat up his sleeve, but
Liu Xianyang didn\'t immediately leave.

He stood in front of Chen Ping\'an, helping him smooth down his collar
before patting him on the shoulder, and he said, \"Alright, I\'m going
now. Make sure to look after yourself when I\'m gone.\"

\"Same to you,\" Chen Ping\'an replied with a nod.

Liu Xianyang was just about to leave when Chen Ping\'an tossed a seal at
him with a smile and said, \"That\'s a unique seal, so make sure to keep
it safe. You might be able to sell it for an astronomical price
someday.\"

Liu Xianyang tucked the seal up his sleeve without even bothering to
look at it, then flew away into the distance, while Chen Ping\'an
remained on the spot, continuing to stare into the distant sky even
after Liu Xianyang was long gone.

The gates of the summer palace had been wide open this entire time, and
there was no gatekeeper.

Chen Ping\'an made his way into the main hall, where he was approached
by Chou Miao, who reported, \"All of the plans have already been
finalized. Observing the battlefield from afar isn\'t as good as
experiencing it for oneself, so we have decided that three people will
be sent to the top of the city walls at a time to join the battle.
We\'ll make sure that this doesn\'t get in the way of their duties.\"

\"Who\'s going to be in the first batch of three?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

Chou Miao was joined by Mi Yu and Dong Bude.

\"You two can go, but I\'ll have Deng Liang take Sword Immortal Mi\'s
place this time,\" Chen Ping\'an said with a smile. \"Make sure you
don\'t just stay there and don\'t come back. You must return after ten
days, and Sword Immortal Mi, Pang Yuanji, and Lin Junbi will take your
place. After that will be Song Gaoyuan, Cao Gun, and Xuan Can, followed
by Luo Zhenyi, Xu Ning, and Chang Taiqing. The final group of three will
consist of Gu Jianlong, Wang Xinshui, and Guo Zhujiu, and I may go with
them as well.\"

Out of the four newest members of the Hidden Official\'s branch, Chen
Ping\'an had no reservations about Chou Miao, who was a young sword
immortal that both the old great sword immortal and A\'Liang thought
very highly of.

However, he still had some doubts about Luo Zhenyi\'s trio, and that was
why he had placed them after Deng Liang and Song Gaoyuan\'s groups of
three. However, if he were to put the three of them at the very end,
after even Gu Jianlong\'s trio, then that would be excessive.
Furthermore, grouping the trio together without splitting them apart was
a minor form of compensation for them.

Hence, it made sense that Luo Zhenyi\'s trio harbored some gripes toward
him, but as long as their personal feelings didn\'t get in the way of
the big picture, then Chen Ping\'an didn\'t really care about how they
felt about him. On a personal level, Chen Ping\'an actually really
admired these swordsmen who had previously ventured into the heart of
the Savage World, but he still had to be wary of them. If Luo Zhenyi\'s
trio resented him for it, then so be it. Someone who was too eager to
please and overly concerned about being liked by others was unfit to be
the Hidden Official.

Chou Miao\'s trio left the main hall and departed from the summer palace
atop their flying swords.

Most of the swordsmen of the Hidden Official\'s branch were very young,
but possessed wisdom beyond their years, and they knew that this war
wasn\'t going to end anytime soon. At the very least, it would rage for
three to five years, and it could even last over a decade. In any case,
it was undoubtedly going to be an extremely brutal and grueling affair.

With Huang Luan at the helm, the demonic cultivators continued to throw
a vast wave of immortal treasures at the Sword Qi Great Wall, and they
were assisted by a formidable army of tens of thousands of demon
swordsmen under the leadership of the current Lotus Flower Nunnery
Master.

After these two battles, millions of demons were going to be leaving the
Savage World to embark on a march toward the Sword Qi Great Wall,
whether it be against their will or not. It was said that the road
leading to the northern battlefield was lined with piles of remains.

After enduring this challenge from the Savage World, the swordsmen on
top of the city walls would have to go into battle on the southern
battlefield.

Instead of immediately entering the main hall, Chen Ping\'an began
taking a stroll on the plaza outside.

The swordsmen of the Hidden Official\'s branch were already accustomed
to seeing him performing walking meditation in the courtyard outside. It
seemed to help him think, and whenever he thought of something, he would
issue an instruction to the swordsmen inside.

All of a sudden, Mi Yu, who was looking more and more like a door god,
asked, \"Lord Hidden Official, have you already become a swordsman?\"

\"Why do you say that?\" Chen Ping\'an asked.

\"I just had a feeling,\" Mi Yu replied.

Instead of giving a definitive answer, Chen Ping\'an smiled and said,
\"It\'s a real shame that you aren\'t a guest elder on my mountain,
Sword Immortal Mi.\"

# Chapter 633: (1): The Young Man in the Main Seat

Sword of Coming

A group of around a dozen people stepped out of the gate from the
blistering summer heat of the Sword Qi Great Wall and arrived on the
snowy Stalactite Mountain.

They had all cast illusions on themselves, and they went out in the dead
of the night to visit the Spring Banner Inn.

Both Yan Ming and Nalan Caihuan were part of this group, and they were
able to remain undetected by everyone aside from the Great Heavenly
Lord, who was observing the proceedings from afar.

Standing beside him was the old Spiritual Master holding the golden
horsetail whisk, and he asked in a quiet voice, \"This isn\'t going to
spell trouble, is it, Master?\"

The Great Heavenly Lord sneered. \"You think they would dare to cause
trouble under my watch?\"

The old Spiritual Master stroked the advanced refined flood dragon
whiskers that formed the golden threads of his horsetail whisk as he
mused, \"Pure intimidation may not be enough to get the job done.\"

The Great Heavenly Lord turned to a man standing nearby before giving
him a nod, and the latter took a glance at the Great Heavenly Lord
before responding with a nod of his own.

It seemed that the Great Heavenly Lord had come here with the sole
purpose of seeing this man, and after exchanging those nods, he turned
to depart, but before he did so, he said, \"After I go into seclusion,
you\'ll be in charge, and your job is very simple: Just don\'t do
anything.\"

The old Spiritual Master was very much taken aback to hear this, but he
still extended a Daoist salute and replied, \"As you wish, Master.\"

\"What about Uncle Master Jiang?\" the old Spiritual Master asked.

Once the Great Heavenly Lord went into seclusion, there would be no one
left on Stalactite Mountain capable of keeping the little Daoist priest
from White Jade Capital in check.

Despite his status as a True Lord, the Spiritual Master was inferior to
the little Daoist priest in both seniority and cultivation base, and
they also hailed from different Daoist branches, making it very
difficult for him to even try to reason with the little Daoist priest.

The Great Heavenly Lord turned his gaze to the old gate, where the
little Daoist priest was seated on a cushion, reading a book while
discussing the storyline with Sword Immortal Zhang Lu.

After a brief hesitation, the Great Heavenly Lord said, \"Just let him
be. He\'s already been quite well-behaved during the past few centuries
in which he\'s served as gatekeeper. If he were back home, then he
would\'ve been much more of a pain to deal with. That junior uncle of
mine adores him more than anyone else, and he always makes sure to bring
him along whenever he goes to cause trouble at the Mystery Capital
Temple.

"If it wasn\'t for the fact that Daoist Master Sun has set his sights on
him with the intent to kill, he wouldn\'t even have had to come to the
Majestic World to seek refuge.\"

\"I\'m sure Uncle Master Jiang will be granted immense fortune after
surviving that ordeal,\" the old Spiritual Master mused.

The Great Heavenly Lord went into seclusion, while the old Spiritual
Master remained standing at the railing, looking down upon the entirety
of Stalactite Mountain. Many people were aware that Stalactite Mountain
was the largest mountain seal under the heavens, but it was much less
well known that the eight attractions on the mountain and the Lone Peak
the old Spiritual Master was standing on formed an ancient formation
passed down from the Master of Three Mountains and Nine Lords. The
ultimate finished product was something akin to an ancient ascension
platform.

The old Spiritual Master was a disciple that the Great Heavenly Lord had
taken on in the Majestic World, and this was his home. However, the old
Spiritual Master wasn\'t much different from the old boatman who had
served Branch Master Lu Chen during his journey out at sea. For
cultivators, their place of residence from before they embarked on the
path of cultivation was their first home.

After they began cultivating, their place of cultivation would become
their true home. Thus, both the old Spiritual Master stationed on
Stalactite Mountain and the old boatman who was constantly drifting out
at sea held an intense desire to cultivate in the Heavenly World.

However, the Great Dao was extremely lofty, and the journey was very
long. Unless they had someone to take them there, their lackluster
cultivation bases meant that ascending to another world was nothing more
than a distant dream.

The old Spiritual Master watched the cultivators sneaking onto
Stalactite Mountain and found it very boring. His master had already
ordered him not to do anything, so he simply left. In the blink of an
eye, he appeared in the Catch and Release Pavilion, which was completely
deserted at this late hour, and in the next instant, he appeared out at
sea, having decided that he would pay a visit to the Flood Dragon
Trench.

If it weren\'t for something that Jiang Yunsheng had said to the old
Spiritual Master, he would\'ve already slain all of the True Dragon
descendants in the Flood Dragon Trench. All he would\'ve had to do was
intercept and kill all of the rainbringer flood dragons one after
another, and had he done that, his horsetail whisk would\'ve already
been elevated into a celestial tool long ago.

The old True Lord excelled in accumulating a large quantity of a certain
thing before refining it into a celestial tool, as was the case with the
flood dragon whiskers that he had refined into his horsetail whisk.

A reminiscent look appeared on the old Spiritual Master\'s face as he
stood atop the waves and thought back to a certain secret event of the
past.

Back then, the only one who was capable of convincing that sword
immortal to stand down was Lu Chen.

He was truly an unfathomable figure who stood at the top of the world,
and it was no wonder that in his eyes, all of the immortal sects of the
Majestic World were utterly insignificant.

The more the old Spiritual Master learned, the more insignificant and
inept he felt in comparison with the almighty Branch Master, and as he
dwelled on these thoughts, he entered a somewhat immersive state.

All of a sudden, the little Daoist priest turned his gaze to the railing
of the tall building sitting on the summit of the Lone Peak.

\"What\'s up?\" Sword Immortal Zhang Lu asked with a curious expression.

\"He seems to have entered a state of enlightenment similar to what\'s
described in Buddhism, but he\'s not quite there,\" the little Daoist
priest replied.

\"You\'re not going to lend him a hand?\" Zhang Lu asked with a smile.
\"You two have already known each other for several hundred years;
surely you should help him out here.\"

\"Not just anyone can help him in this situation,\" the little Daoist
priest replied with a shake of his head. \"At the very least, I
certainly don\'t possess the necessary capabilities. If I try to help
him, it\'s most likely the case that I will only end up hindering him.\"

\"Let\'s keep reading then,\" Zhang Lu encouraged. \"Whenever the
protagonists of these stories stop to rest on a riverbank at night, they
always run into a beautiful maiden stripping off her clothes to bathe in
the river.\"

However, the little Daoist priest didn\'t continue reading. Instead, he
suddenly said, \"Be careful, they haven\'t gone through this gate the
past two times.\"

\"Sentimental as ever, aren\'t you?\" Zhang Lu chuckled. \"I don\'t
think you\'re going to ever be a true believer of Daoist teachings.\"

\"I\'m issuing this warning as a matter of principle, not because I hold
any sentimental attachment to them,\" the little Daoist priest disagreed
with a shake of his head. \"Besides, those who are extremely emotional
and sincere are actually considered bright talents in Daoism. The
teachings of Daoism are broader, deeper, and more profound than you
think. You can\'t look down on Daoism as a whole just because I\'m not a
good Daoist.\"

\"Just turn the page.\" Zhang Lu yawned. \"If you don\'t keep reading,
I\'m going to fall asleep soon.\"

The little Daoist priest resumed his reading.

Not long ago, the Clay Pot intercontinental ship of the Mountain and
Water Cave had only just traveled several hundred kilometers away from
Stalactite Mountain when it suddenly received a flying sword message
from Stalactite Mountain.

The old Nascent Tier administrator on the ship had a feeling that his
ship wasn\'t the only one to receive such a message, and sure enough, it
didn\'t take long before more messenger flying swords from the other
intercontinental ships arrived in his ship\'s sword chamber. After
weighing up his options, the old Nascent Tier administrator decided to
leave the ship and return to Stalactite Mountain.

As it turned out, the other intercontinental ship administrators who had
been present at the meeting in the Ganoderma Inn had also received
flying sword messages not long after leaving Stalactite Mountain,
requesting that they return to Stalactite Mountain.

As a matter of fact, all of the intercontinental ships that had recently
been at Stalactite Mountain and hadn\'t traveled too far away had been
invited to visit Shao Yunyan\'s Spring Banner Inn.

The invitation hadn\'t come from Yan Ming, nor was it from Nalan
Caihuan. Instead, it was from the entire Sword Qi Great Wall, and that
was something that had never been seen before.

Given the peculiar nature of the invitation, everyone knew that this
wasn\'t something they could simply choose to ignore, and of course,
many of them were very curious about exactly who it was that had sent
out these invitations. Who had the right to send out these invitations
on behalf of the Sword Qi Great Wall? Was it Nalan Shaowei?

If it were him, then the administrators of the intercontinental ships
felt like they had nothing to fear. While Nalan Shaowei was undoubtedly
one of the most powerful sword immortals alive, his business acumen was
significantly lacking compared with his cultivation base.

The majority of the intercontinental ships to receive this invitation
were from the Middle Earth Divine Continent and the Pure White
Continent, and all of them chose to oblige and return to Stalactite
Mountain. Most of them arranged to meet up somewhere on the way back to
try and figure out what the Sword Qi Great Wall\'s intentions were. They
were confident that their lives weren\'t under threat; the Sword Qi
Great Wall wouldn\'t be so demented as to kill them.

The only concern was that the Sword Qi Great Wall would do something
foolish that would negatively impact everyone\'s profit margins. If they
could work out a plan to collectively stifle whatever the Sword Qi Great
Wall\'s plans were, that would undoubtedly be massively beneficial to
them.

Shao Yunyan personally greeted everyone at the entrance of the Spring
Banner Inn along with the few remaining trusted subordinates left in the
inn, and they arranged places to stay for all of the guests. The entire
time, Shao Yunyan maintained a very pleasant and approachable demeanor,
and many of the ship administrators felt extremely flattered to be
receiving such hospitality from a sword immortal of Shao Yunyan\'s
status.

Thanks to his prized gourd vine, Shao Yunyan had countless powerful
connections all over the entire Majestic World, so the Spring Banner Inn
was definitely far superior in status to the likes of the Plum Blossom
Garden and the Water Essence Palace.

Those who were able to stay in the Ape Havoc Estate on Stalactite
Mountain were all extremely wealthy, but for the most part, those who
were able to stay in the Spring Banner Inn had extremely bright futures
ahead on the path of cultivation.

The Spring Banner Inn had arranged around a dozen peaceful courtyards
for the administrators of the intercontinental ships to stay in, and
before everyone went to their respective courtyards, Shao Yunyan
encouraged them to take a rest and drink some tea before making their
way to the main hall of the Spring Banner Inn.

The Nascent Tier administrator from the Mountain and Water Cave was
called Bai Xi, and he had no idea what Shao Yunyan was plotting.
However, as soon as he entered his assigned courtyard, he spotted a
person looking at him from the main room, and his heart immediately
sank.

It was Sword Immortal Xie Zhi from the Circling Ascension Continent.

He was a vagrant cultivator through and through, and even after he
became a sword immortal, he still displayed no intention of founding a
sect or faction of his own. Instead, he preferred traveling to wherever
he pleased, and his travels ultimately took him to the Sword Qi Great
Wall.

He didn\'t have any ties to the immortal sects and factions of the
Circling Ascension Continent, and in particular, he had once openly
expressed his severe disdain for the Mountain and Water Cave. He was on
such bad terms with the patriarch of the Mountain and Water Cave that
they wouldn\'t even bother to acknowledge each other in a chance
encounter.

Inside the main room were several other intercontinental ship
administrators, all of whom were seated in tense, upright postures,
looking every bit as anxious as Bai Xi.

Similarly, in another courtyard, an intercontinental ship administrator
from the Golden Armor Continent was greeted by the sight of a woman
sitting in the main room with a sword on her back.

Her physical appearance was nothing special, but the sword on her back,
Circling Ascension, was a household name on the Golden Armor Continent
and the Circling Ascension Continent. The Circling Ascension Continent
had been named after her sword, yet she wasn\'t even a swordsman from
the Circling Ascension Continent, and as one might expect, there were
many spectacular stories behind this legendary woman.

She was the female sword immortal, Song Pin.

A highly respected poet from the Circling Ascension Continent had once
caught a glimpse of Song Pin from afar, and that became an unforgettable
memory for him. He was so deeply infatuated with Song Pin that he never
married, and the poems that he wrote about her were enough to fill
several anthologies.

The intercontinental ship administrators in the room with Song Pin all
wore concerned expressions, and the arrival of their latest comrade
didn\'t bring them any joy.

The hospitality from Shao Yunyan had left them all feeling a little
suspicious and apprehensive, and sure enough, their apprehension had
been vindicated.

\"Is that everyone?\" Song Pin asked as she opened her eyes. \"If so,
then I\'m going to propose a toast, and once we\'ve all had a drink we
can get down to business.\"

She picked up a cup that was sitting on the table beside her, then
downed the wine inside in one go.

Sword Immortal Pu He of the Flowing Dawn Continent was a tall and thin
old man with a set of rather gaunt facial features. Instead of sitting
in the main room, he was standing at the entrance of the courtyard,
watching the falling snow. Thus, the intercontinental ship
administrators could only stand in the walkway behind him to watch the
snow with him.

Pu He was once known as the sword immortal with the most unpredictable
personality on the Flowing Dawn Continent, often killing people purely
on a whim. Apparently, he had been defeated while challenging the Sword
Qi Great Wall, and since then, he had remained here to cultivate.

After all of the intercontinental ship administrators arrived, Pu He
said, \"All of you are businessmen, so I\'m sure you\'re all familiar
with buying and selling. How about you all sell me a favor? What do you
say?\"

The administrators looked back and forth at one another, and one of them
mustered up some courage before cupping his fist in a salute as he
asked, \"May I ask if you\'re asking us this question as a swordsman of
the Sword Qi Great Wall, or as a sword immortal of the Flowing Dawn
Continent?\"

Pu He took a side-eyed glance at the Nascent Tier cultivator who had
just spoken, then said, \"Leave. Tell your patriarch, Li Xun, that once
I return to the Flowing Dawn Continent, I\'ll be paying a visit to your
sect\'s ancestral hall with a few of my good friends.\"

Before the Nascent Tier cultivator had a chance to say anything else, Pu
He\'s bonded flying sword was already hovering directly in front of his
glabella, completely rooting him to the spot.

Pu He then grabbed him by the neck and casually tossed him onto the
street outside the Spring Banner Inn, following which he communicated
through his mind\'s lake, \"Your ship is called Tight Weave, right? It
doesn\'t look to be in very good condition. How about I demolish it for
you so you can get a new one? I see you have the Unpolished Jade Tier
swordsman, Leng Ran, hiding inside. I wonder if he\'ll be able to stop
me.\"

The Nascent Tier cultivator was just about to storm away in a fit of
rage, but this was too severe a threat for him to ignore.

The intercontinental ship was the lifeblood of the sect, and it was
renowned for its size and durability. Of course, significant investments
had to be made to achieve this level of size and durability, and that
was why the sect had spent an exorbitant sum to secretly hire the
Unpolished Jade Tier sword immortal, Leng Ran, to guard the ship.

However, even on the ship, the administrator should\'ve been the only
one aware of this, and the few times that Leng Ran had to defend the
ship, he made sure to cover his tracks extremely well.

The Nascent Tier cultivator could only swallow his dissatisfaction and
return to the Spring Banner Inn to apologize to Pu He.

He knew that the Sword Qi Great Wall wouldn\'t kill him or even target
him, but if Pu He so desired, he could make the entire sect\'s existence
a living hell.

[]{#chapter-152.xhtml}

# Chapter 633: (2): The Young Man in the Main Seat

Sword of Coming

Clearly, Pu He had no interest in keeping up appearances, and even
though he had asked the administrators whether they would be willing to
sell him a favor, it really was more of an order than a request.

There were only a few intercontinental ship administrators from the
Southern Whirl Continent, and they were having a much more pleasant
discussion in another courtyard with Sword Immortal Yuan Qingshu.

Unlike Pu He, Xie Zhi, and Song Pin, Yuan Qingshu had adopted a much
more amicable approach. He had invited everyone for a pleasant chat over
some wine, which he proclaimed was the most renowned Bamboo Sea Small
World wine on the Sword Qi Great Wall. At the end, he proposed that his
six direct disciples could go to the sects and factions of everyone
present to serve as guest elders. As for what he had truly gathered
everyone here to discuss, he told them that that could wait until after
they\'ve all had their fill of wine.

There were quite a few intercontinental ship administrators from the
Pure White Continent, second only to those from the Middle Earth Divine
Continent, and they were in the presence of the female sword immortal,
Xie Songhua.

Xie Songhua was a very strange sword immortal. She was born on the Pure
White Continent, yet her entire rise had taken place on the Middle Earth
Divine Continent, and she was never willing to acknowledge her Pure
White Continent roots. She proclaimed that a continent that couldn\'t
even keep the suffix of \"north\" from falling into the hands of the
Complete Reed Continent wasn\'t worthy of her acknowledgment.

Generally speaking, a foul-tempered sword immortal like her wouldn\'t
have been able to make much of a splash on the Pure White Continent.
After all, the immortal powers of the Pure White Continent were all
extremely wealthy, and none of them were afraid of any powerful
individual, even if that individual were a sword immortal.

However, it just so happened to be the case that Xie Songhua had several
close friends on the Pure White Continent who shared her fiery temper.
One of them was a female pure martial artist who liked to go to the
north to hunt demons, and she just so happened to be extremely close
with the Liu Clan of the Pure White Continent.

Xie Songhua had always displayed nothing but disdain for the swordsmen
of the Pure White Continent, and it was only after meeting Deng Liang
and the other bright prodigies from the Pure White Continent that her
attitude began to soften a little.

After everyone arrived, Xie Songhua wasted no time, cutting straight to
the chase with a very impactful opening statement. \"I have fought in
battles on the Sword Qi Great Wall so far, and I have accumulated
accolades equivalent to killing an Immortal Tier great demon.\"

This wasn\'t enough to send everyone into a frenzy, but it certainly
sufficed in terms of intimidation.

At the moment, all information was extremely closely guarded on the
Sword Qi Great Wall, but there was one thing that was very common
knowledge to just about everyone on Stalactite Mountain, and that was
that Xie Songhua had single-handedly destroyed the Great Dao foundation
of an Unpolished Jade Tier sword immortal of the Savage World. According
to the rules of the Sword Qi Great Wall, that was a contribution
equivalent to killing half an Immortal Tier great demon.

Truth be told, the businessmen of the Pure White Continent didn\'t feel
much pride in this feat. Instead, they were more interested in the
business opportunities that it presented. If any of them could recruit
Xie Songhua to become a guest elder at their sect, that would
undoubtedly be massively profitable for them.

However, no one dared to even raise the subject. Everyone knew what Xie
Songhua\'s personality was like, and if they weren\'t careful, such a
proposal could end up being the last proposal they ever made.

What was particularly unsettling to everyone was that Xie Songhua
normally had no interest in business matters whatsoever, yet she had
gathered everyone here to discuss business, and that was clearly not
good news.

Sure enough, she continued, \"I owe someone a favor, so I\'ll be
accompanying all of you on your journey back to the Pure White
Continent. He told me that everyone who does business tries to maximize
profits as much as possible, and that none of you can be faulted for
simply doing your job. He doesn\'t blame any of you, and on the
contrary, he says that he sympathizes with all of you.

"Hence, not only do none of you have anything to worry about, you are
all in for a pleasant surprise. Once I\'ve gotten a good grasp on
everyone\'s financial status, I\'ll know which sect among you is the
poorest and most desperately in need of making profits from the Sword Qi
Great Wall. Once I\'ve established which sect that is, I will personally
escort their intercontinental ship back to the Pure White Continent. If
I fail in my assignment, then I will be entirely to blame.\"

After all of the intercontinental ship administrators of the Northern
Complete Reed Continent were assembled, they were attended to by Sect
Leader Li Cai of the Duckweed Sword Lake.

Everyone immediately stood up to cup their fists in a collective salute.

If she were just a sect leader and an Unpolished Jade Tier sword
immortal, then everyone wouldn\'t have been so earnestly reverent of
her. However, the courage that she had displayed in coming to the Sword
Qi Great Wall had earned everyone\'s respect.

Li Cai returned the salute, but didn\'t sit down. Instead, she pulled
out a flagon of wine that she had prepared in advance, then declared,
\"Han Huaizi won\'t be going back, and I most likely won\'t be, either.
That\'s all I have to say. Please have a drink on me.\"

Wei Jin was the sword immortal who met with the two intercontinental
ship administrators from Old Dragon City. Instead of discussing
business, he asked them about the recent state of the Eastern Treasured
Vial Continent, and in the end, he declared, \"If I manage to reach the
Immortal Tier and don\'t die on the Sword Qi Great Wall, I will travel
to the Northern Complete Reed Continent and challenge Heavenly Lord Xie
Shi again.\"

The two administrators were already feeling rather apprehensive to begin
with, and they felt even more uneasy upon hearing this.

The Eastern Treasured Vial Continent was the smallest and most secluded
continent in the Majestic World, and Wei Jin was one of the brightest
talents to ever come out of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, so he
was held in extremely high regard.

If Wei Jin were to reach the Immortal Tier, then both the Divine Edict
Sect and the True Realm Sect would have to reconsider their position on
the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.

The Old Dragon City intercontinental ships were the least well-informed
of all of the intercontinental ships from the nine continents, yet even
they had been tipped off to the fact that Wei Jin had already reached
his Unpolished Jade Tier bottleneck.

Wei Jin had all but confirmed this himself with that declaration, and
that was why the two Old Dragon City administrators were feeling so
uneasy.

*Why is he telling us this? We\'ve never even met before! Why would he
tell us something like this?*

Wei Jin began drinking on his own, and it was still the most expensive
and most scam-adjacent wine in the shop, selling for one lesser heat
coin per flagon.

All of the sword immortals had prepared what they were going to say in
advance, so these were all calculated decisions. Otherwise, why would
Wei Jin tell a couple of intercontinental ship administrators that he
had never met before about his future plans after making a breakthrough?

While this was a calculated decision, it was indeed true that he
intended to challenge Heavenly Lord Xie Shi again.

The largest courtyard in the Spring Banner Inn was reserved for all of
the intercontinental ship administrators from the Middle Earth Divine
Continent.

Compared with the tense and uneasy atmosphere in the other courtyards,
the administrators from the Middle Earth Divine Continent were all very
composed, and there were even two Unpolished Jade Tier cultivators among
them, Wu Qiu and Tang Feiqian. Even though they were managing their
respective sect\'s intercontinental ships, they had refused the title of
administrator as it was too demeaning for cultivators of their caliber.

Among them, Wu Qiu was not only at the Unpolished Jade Tier, but also a
sword immortal, and the two immortals were seated next to each other,
chatting amicably without a care in the world.

Their composure stemmed from the fact that they came from the Middle
Earth Divine Continent, and on top of that, the representatives from the
Sword Qi Great Wall in the room with them were not someone they were
afraid of at all.

It was only the Unpolished Jade Tier Mi Yu, as opposed to the expected
Nalan Shaowei. He was joined by Sword Immortal Ku Xia of the Shaoyuan
Empire, who had very close ties to the Middle Earth Divine Continent, so
it wasn\'t really even clear which side he was on.

In the eyes of all of the intercontinental ship administrators from the
Middle Earth Divine Continent, the fact that these two had been chosen
to see them meant that they weren\'t in any danger at all.

Wu Qiu and Tang Feiqian were so relaxed that they were even in the mood
to observe Mi Yu and a female Nascent Tier cultivator in the room with a
combination of amusement and intrigue in their eyes. The female Nascent
Tier cultivator possessed exceptional cultivation aptitude, yet she had
insisted on becoming the administrator of an intercontinental ship, a
rigorous role that should\'ve never fallen upon a prodigy of her
caliber.

The reason for this was her infatuation with Mi Yu. Unfortunately, her
devotion was directed toward a womanizer with countless female admirers
and pursuers. The Middle Earth Divine Continent was teeming with bright
young prodigies, yet the cruel hand of fate had made her fall for Mi Yu.

If Mi Yu were able to leave the Sword Qi Great Wall and were willing to
become her Dao partner, then she could be considered very fortunate, but
as a sword immortal of the Sword Qi Great Wall, there was no way Mi Yu
could go to the Middle Earth Divine Continent.

Sword Immortal Ku Xia wasn\'t very good with his words, and there was no
need for him to speak, given that he had only been instructed to keep
the guests in the room company.

Wu Qiu turned to Ku Xia with a smile and asked, \"Where are Yan Ming and
Nalan Caihuan? Are they in the main hall, waiting for us to finish our
tea?\"

\"I\'m not sure,\" Ku Xia replied with a shake of his head.

Wu Qiu nodded and accepted that answer.

Even though they were both Unpolished Jade Tier sword immortals, Ku Xia
was also a junior nephew to Zhou Shenzhi, one of the top ten cultivators
of the Middle Earth Divine Continent, so he was certainly superior in
status to Wu Qiu.

Regardless of how little Zhou Shenzhi thought of his junior nephew, that
was certainly no excuse for others to look down on Ku Xia.

Ku Xia had a reputation for being easygoing and approachable, but that
only made it an even worse idea to get on his bad side.

Hence, sending Ku Xia to meet with everyone from the Middle Earth Divine
Continent could be considered a decently smart move from the Sword Qi
Great Wall.

However, once the business negotiations began, Ku Xia wasn\'t going to
be able to make any difference. After all, he was still just Ku Xia, not
Zhou Shenzhi.

Ku Xia heaved an internal sigh, knowing that all of the intercontinental
ship administrators were in for a massive headache once the star of the
show arrived. He was even of the opinion that if the young man currently
in the main hall of the Spring Banner Inn had been the one contending
against the future patriarch of the Mountain and Water Cave in the place
of Nalan Shaowei, then it would\'ve been a much more even contest. In
the past, Ku Xia had never imagined that Lin Junbi would concede himself
inferior to anyone, yet that young man had managed to accomplish such a
feat.

The female Nascent Tier cultivator was communicating with Mi Yu through
her mind\'s lake, hissing with as much venom as she could muster.
\"You\'re going to pay, Mi Yu! Even if I\'m going to be punished by my
sect, I\'m going to humiliate you! In fact, I may be able to humiliate
you without even incurring any consequences! Revenge truly is a dish
best served cold! I bet you never thought that this day would come, did
you?!\"

Mi Yu turned to her with a wistful expression, then lamented through his
mind\'s lake, \"It\'s a real shame to see what was once such a kind and
gentle girl become so bitter. I suppose I\'m to blame for that.\"

The woman had no response for this, and her expression only became more
resentful. She had so many things she wanted to say, but she was unable
to get anything out through her tightly clenched jaws.

Mi Yu also didn\'t say anything further, and he took a glance at her
before averting his gaze slightly, as if to see her out of his
peripheral vision, almost like he wanted to see her, but didn\'t dare to
look directly at her.

In the main hall of the Spring Banner Inn, a young man was leaning
against the door frame of the entrance, and there was an ancient jade
tablet hanging from his waist.

Yan Ming and Nalan Caihuan were also present, but neither of them
occupied the main seat in the room. Not only that, but they were seated
quite far back.

Nalan Caihuan was a little disgruntled by this, while Yan Ming didn\'t
really seem to care.

Earlier, she had been screwed over by the young man, and after the
event, she had gone to Nalan Shaowei to report the contents of their
discussion, only for Nalan Shaowei to stare at her as if she were an
idiot the entire time.

After learning that she had been tricked, Nalan Caihuan was so furious
that she intended to scrap everything that they had agreed upon, but
Nalan Shaowei told her that there was no need to do that, and that she
should honor the agreement, even though all of the terms had been
negotiated under false pretenses.

Shao Yunyan was standing beside the young man at the entrance, and he
didn\'t seem to be bothered at all that the young man looked as if he
had taken over the Spring Banner Inn from him.

This was the first meeting between the two, and they were having a
spirited discussion about Liu Jinglong of the Northern Complete Reed
Continent and Celestial Maiden Lu Sui of Water Scripture Mountain.

Shao Yunyan was full of praise for Liu Jinglong, proclaiming that the
latter had very good chances of becoming the first Ascension Tier sword
immortal of the Northern Complete Reed Continent.

In response, the young man praised Lu Sui for her beauty and kindness,
stating that she and Liu Jinglong were a match made in heaven. While
praising Lu Sui, the young man also paid some compliments to her master.

Shao Yunyan didn\'t care whether he was being sincere or not. Even if
the young man were only saying this to be polite, it was still quite
flattering to hear.

After chatting about his gourd vine and the wine from the Golden Millet
Blessed Land, Shao Yunyan asked, \"Is it about time we called them
over?\"

\"There\'s no hurry,\" the young man replied with a smile. \"It\'s not
every day that the sword immortals come to Stalactite Mountain, so we
can\'t let their visit go to waste. Let\'s have everyone keep them
company for a little longer.\"

The young man then cast his gaze toward the falling snow outside as he
tucked his hands up their opposite sleeves, thinking to himself that if
only all of the falling snowflakes were snowflake coins instead.

Shao Yunyan also began looking out at the snow outside, feeling a rare
moment of peace.

\"After tonight, we can negotiate the thing that you promised to the
Sword Qi Great Wall,\" the young man suddenly said. \"The terms of your
promise will remain the same, but the outcome can be different, and all
three parties can be at least somewhat satisfied.\"

\"Do you have the authority to make a decision on that?\" Shao Yunyan
asked with slightly furrowed brows.

\"If *I* don\'t even have the authority, then who does?\" the young man
asked with a smile.

Shao Yunyan was very relieved. Up to this point, he had already resolved
himself to die on Stalactite Mountain, and he took a few steps back
before cupping his fist toward the young man in a grateful salute.
